prompt:
This is a one-off Muse Code design session, not a kernel round. It writes nothing into muse-spark/. You are its lead. Do not run the muse-round skill. You coordinate a swarm of helper agents that you start yourself (subagent_spawn, subagent_wait, subagent_read_result, subagent_send_message), and you write the final design. You don't investigate or design yourself beyond reading what your helpers return and checking it.

THE TASK
Design how to fix the behaviour of the Muse agent swarm that, in two rounds, produced no real efficiency improvement while its own reports predicted gains. The approved brief at the end gives the five behaviours, the evidence, the root cause, the acceptance criteria, what must stay protected and the constraints. The deliverable is ONE coherent, implementation-ready solution design, not code.

LIMITS
- No cost or time limit. Take the time and the agents the work needs; stop when the design is tested and you judge more work won't change it, and say why.
- Up to 12 agents run at once, you included. The phases below give the least you start; split a territory, add explorers, designers or testers whenever it helps, as long as no more than 12 run at once.

RULES FOR YOU AND EVERY HELPER (tell each helper these in its prompt)
- The repository's tracked files stay as they are: change, move or delete none of them, run no git command that changes anything, and commit nothing.
- design-lab/, at the workspace root, is the swarm's own folder. It is untracked and never committed. Each agent writes only in design-lab/<agent name>/: prototypes of proposed changes (copies of skill files, role cards or tools, edited there), test scripts, and measurement results. Never edit the originals; a prototype imports or copies them.
- Testing is allowed and expected. Run the project's measurement tools, the originals or a prototype, to see what a proposed change does: bench/grader/check_candidate.py, time_candidates.py (plain or vllm), check_sizes.py, bench/micro/*.py. Write their outputs only under design-lab/. Earlier attempts to test with are in muse-spark/kernels/ and muse-spark/round-2/kernels/.
- The GPU runs one job at a time: every grader and timing tool takes the lock in bench/grader/gpu_lock.py and waits its turn; a prototype that runs GPU work takes the same lock (import gpu_lock; gpu_lock.hold("<what>")). Load a model only inside such a run. The machine has 16 GB and pages heavily; a vLLM run takes about 10-12 minutes with 5 repeats.
- Never read credentials: .env files, ~/.config/muse, or any key store. No network calls.
- Every claim about the repository cites a path and line, and every claim about performance cites the result file it comes from; mark proposals, predictions and assumptions as such.
- The workspace is the repository's muse-agent worktree, at the same commit as main (1113c2d); paths in the brief are relative to it.

PHASE 1: EXPLORATION. Start at least these four explorers at the same time, each with its territory, the brief and the rules. Each returns: the facts of its territory that bear on behaviours 1-5 (with file:line), how its territory causes or could prevent each behaviour, and anything the brief gets wrong.
1. explorer-skill: .agents/skills/muse-round/ (SKILL.md, every role card, tracking.md, CHANGELOG.md) and claude/muse-agent-brief.md. Where do the instructions create or allow each behaviour (the goal's wording, the harden loop, Ready to test, the verifier's scope, the "load no model" rule)?
2. explorer-tools: bench/grader/check_candidate.py, slots.py, time_candidates.py, gpu_lock.py, engine_table.py, bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py, breakdown.py (run_plain, run_vllm, prefill, prompt_ms), clean_vllm.py, compiled_exact.py. What an in-round end-to-end check could reuse as it is, what it would need, how long it takes, and how it could be gamed.
3. explorer-rounds: the Muse agent's own records, muse-spark/ (round 1: exploration/, implementation/, kernels/*/attempt-*/notes.md, summary.md) and muse-spark/round-2/ (the same, plus logs). Find every instance of behaviours 1-5 and any other behaviour that led to a claimed but unreal gain, with file:line.
4. explorer-findings: Claude's measurements and decisions, claude/findings/muse-round-1.md, muse-round-2.md, claude/adr/0006 to 0012, claude/GLOSSARY.md, PROVENANCE.md. What was predicted against what was measured, what each ADR already fixed, and which protected contracts a fix must keep.
Explorers may also run the existing tools to check a fact (for example, how long a check takes, or how noisy it is). Wait for all of them. If two explorers disagree on a fact, check the source yourself and record which is right.

PHASE 2: DESIGN (the implementation proposals). Start at least three designers at the same time, each with the brief, the rules, ALL FOUR explorer reports, and its own starting perspective; no designer sees another's design. Give each designer these instructions verbatim:
---
You are an independent senior software architect. Design the strongest coherent solution for the exact brief. You are responsible for the entire problem, not just your starting perspective; the perspective tells you where to begin and must not bias you into an inferior architecture.
Rules:
- Change no tracked file. Write only in design-lab/<your name>/: prototypes of your proposed changes, test scripts and results. Commit nothing, create no branches or worktrees, and call no paid or external services.
- Read the actual relevant source, callers, contracts, conventions and tests before making codebase-specific claims.
- Distinguish observed facts (with paths) from hypotheses and design decisions.
- Fix the root problem rather than a narrow symptom. Preserve unrelated, correct behavior.
- Choose one internally consistent approach; do not propose incompatible ideas as a single architecture.
- Explain effects on other modules, old data, deployment, edge cases, security, failure handling, maintenance, and future changes where they matter.
- Do not optimize for time-to-answer, diff size, code size or superficial novelty.
- Avoid unneeded abstractions and speculative scalability work.
- If an essential premise conflicts with code or is unknowable, return BLOCKED with exact evidence instead of assuming it away.
- No implementation in the repository: the design is your deliverable. Prototype and test it in design-lab/<your name>/ to see what it does, and report the commands, result files and what they showed.

Deliver:
1. Status: READY | CONDITIONAL | BLOCKED
2. Context and diagnosis: verified facts, example(s), cause and certainty.
3. Recommended design: responsibilities, important interfaces/contracts, data flow and integration points.
4. Why it solves the underlying problem and meets each acceptance criterion.
5. What remains unchanged; migration/compatibility effects if any.
6. Failure handling, data integrity, security and operational concerns if relevant.
7. Credible alternatives considered and their trade-offs.
8. Implementation handoff: dependency-ordered work, expected locations, acceptance/regression tests, monitoring and rollback if relevant.
9. Unverified assumptions, risks and decisions requiring the user.
---
Starting perspectives:
- designer-a: existing-system-first. Study established patterns and solve the problem with the smallest coherent architectural change, not necessarily the fewest lines.
- designer-b: contract-and-data-first. Begin with semantics, contracts, ownership, data shape and consistency, then choose responsibilities and integrations.
- designer-c: failure-and-evolution-first. Begin with the realistic ways the system can fail or need to change, including how a swarm could game any new check, then design a proportionate solution.
Each designer may prototype and test its own design in design-lab/<its name>/ before returning, and reports what it ran and what it saw. Wait for all of them. A designer that returns BLOCKED or an incomplete design counts as partial evidence; never fill it in yourself.

PHASE 3: TEST. For each design, start a tester (or more) to check, by running it, what the design claims; the tester works in design-lab/<its name>/. The tests include at least:
- whether the design's proposed in-round check would have caught behaviours 1-3 on round 2's real attempts (routing attempt-4, combine attempt-1, experts attempt-7 in muse-spark/round-2/kernels/), compared with what Claude measured (claude/findings/muse-round-2.md);
- how long the check takes, and how it holds up against noise (repeats) and against a swarm trying to game it;
- that the protected behaviour still holds: the grader's verdict keys, the bit-exact G2, one grader run per attempt, the GPU queue.
Each tester returns what it ran (commands), the result files and what they show.

PHASE 4: REVIEW. Start one reviewer, with the brief, the explorer reports, the test results, and the designs labelled X, Y, Z (and on) in a shuffled order, without the designers' names or perspectives. Give it these instructions verbatim:
---
You are the independent, skeptical reviewer. Read-only review. Evaluate each anonymous design against the same brief, not against its style. Check consequential factual claims against the repository code. Never claim verification you did not perform.
For each design apply gates individually as PASS / FAIL / UNKNOWN, with the evidence:
G1: Addresses true outcome and root cause (or honestly labels what is not yet proved).
G2: Fits real code, module boundaries, consumers, and existing engineering standards.
G3: Protects correct behavior, interfaces, compatibility and data integrity.
G4: Covers credible failures, concurrency, privacy/security and recovery as applicable.
G5: Feasible, implementable and testable; has meaningful acceptance/regression checks.
G6: Evidence-backed, architecturally cohesive, and proportionate; no speculative complexity.

Then identify:
- The strongest passing design and concrete reasons.
- Hidden assumptions, unexamined callers, counterexamples, migration risks and missing validation.
- Useful ideas from other designs that can fit the preferred one *without breaking its consistency*.
- Any unresolved architectural trade-off or decisive question for the user.

Do NOT produce invented rankings, numeric scores, or speed-based preferences. Do NOT automatically merge architectures. If none passes, say so plainly. Prefer concise, concrete evidence over rhetoric.
---

PHASE 5: SYNTHESIS (you). Select the strongest internally coherent design that passes the gates. Incorporate an idea from another design only if it fits that design without breaking its invariants; never average designs or glue incompatible architectures together. Recheck the result against gates G1-G6 and the brief's acceptance criteria 1-6. Have a tester run the synthesised design's key checks once more if it differs from the tested ones. If no design passes, say so plainly and name the smallest decision or evidence needed.

YOUR FINAL MESSAGE (the only output collected from this session) is the recommended design in Markdown:
1. Context: what exists, what is wrong, why it matters now.
2. What the swarm found: the facts and root causes, proof separated from suspicion, with file:line.
3. Recommended solution: components, responsibilities, the exact changes to the skill, role cards, brief and tools (what each will say or do), data flow and invariants.
4. How it behaves: a normal round and the failure cases (a gamed check, GPU queue contention, noise at 1 request, a session stopped midway, the model ignoring a rule).
5. What changes and what stays protected.
6. Why this approach: the alternatives (the other designs), the decisive trade-offs, and which ideas came from which designer.
7. Implementation handoff: dependency-ordered steps, files (and the design-lab/ prototypes to start from), and the acceptance and regression checks, including how to validate it before round 3 without a paid Muse run, and how round 3's outcome would show success.
8. Test evidence: every test run, its command, its result file under design-lab/, and what it showed.
9. Risks and decisions for surucuonur.
10. The reviewer's gate table for the three designs and for your synthesis.
Then a short list of the helpers you started, each with its role.

APPROVED BRIEF:

# Solution design brief: make the Muse agent swarm pursue real efficiency, not its proxies (v1)

## APPROVAL
- User approved this brief on 2026-11-04 (surucuonur). Decisions: the swarm may run end-to-end checks in-round through the GPU queue; Meta's Muse does the design work; from round 3 the launcher runs muse-spark-1.3-contributor with tool approvals off (ADR 0012, commit 1113c2d).
- Approved activity: one Muse Code session (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) whose lead starts its own helper agents, up to 12 at once, with no cost or time limit. Agents may prototype and test in design-lab/ (untracked, never committed) and run the measurement tools through the GPU queue. The repository's tracked files stay unchanged.

## PROBLEM AND OUTCOME
- **Current problem:** two rounds of the Muse agent swarm (round 1: Muse Spark; round 2: Muse Wonder, 63 min, ~$58) produced no kernel that is a real efficiency improvement, while the swarm's own reports predicted gains. Five behaviours, each with evidence:
  1. **Treats unmeasured costs as free.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`: "Prefill speed is not timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart from time to first token", citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`. The result: experts attempt-7 is 16–28× slower than the compiled reference at prefill sizes, and routing attempt-4 2.6–8.7× slower (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`). Prompts took 6.6–14.5× and 7–10% longer, and throughput fell by up to 83% (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §5).
  2. **Claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Expected G3 = (compiled − candidate) µs × 20 layers (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md` *Ready to test*; `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`). Round 1 predicted −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.98/+0.16/−1.76. Round 2 predicted −0.84 at each and measured −0.73/−0.74/+0.53 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`, `muse-round-2.md`).
  3. **Reasons inconsistently.** The same README says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then reports "Together (sum) −0.84 ms". Combine's −0.35 ms prediction is −0.07 to −0.09 from its own timing plus −0.27 to −0.29 borrowed from what `mx.compile` gains end to end. Measured: +1.05 ms with 32 requests.
  4. **Used the grader as a search loop (round 1).** 29 grader runs on experts for 4 counted attempts, 18 on attempt-1 with edits between (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §5). Fixed since skill v4: one run is one attempt; round 2 ran 13 for 13.
  5. **Persists with a failing design family.** All 7 experts attempts in round 2 are fused kernels that lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs per layer). The cause, too few threadgroups at 1 row, was already known from round 1. The harden loop says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" (`.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:138`), and there is no rule for changing design.
- **Root cause** (likely; supported by the evidence above): inside a round, the swarm never sees the real objective. Its feedback is a per-slot proxy, the grader's piece timing. The real measurement, Claude's G3 over whole requests, arrives only after the round. The swarm's claims are self-reported and checked by no one before the summary.
  - *verified:* the rules forbid an in-round model run: `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:152` "Load no model and start no other GPU work" and `SKILL.md:164` "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team".
  - *verified:* the goal is phrased as passing gates (`SKILL.md:20`).
  - *verified:* the verifier checks only exploration's inefficiency entries (`verifier.md`). No one checks the implementation phase's predictions, combination claims or Ready-to-test arithmetic.
  - *partly fixed:* ADR 0011 (commit `2090949`) now times the prefill (grader at 6 sizes, G3 with prompt and whole-request time, 5 repeats), so behaviour 1's specific gap is closed. The general habit, treating anything outside the measurement as free, is not addressed.
- **Intended outcome:** in round 3 and later, the swarm's statements about speed match what Claude's independent G3 then measures. It marks something ready only when it is a real improvement under the ADR 0011 rule (faster in one phase, prefill or decode, slower in neither, no whole request slower). It stops repeating a design that keeps failing at the same point.
- **Why now:** surucuonur asked how to fix "these essential problems and behaviour of these agents". The hackathon deadline is 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, about 11.5 h from 14:30 UTC on 2026-11-04. Round 3 should run with the fix.
- **Maturity:** hackathon research tool; judges read the repo, the skill and the round documents.
- **User's suggested approach:** none given. Claude has suggested an in-round end-to-end check and prediction rules; treat these as hypotheses, not constraints.

## SCOPE AND SUCCESS
- **In scope:**
  - the round skill (`.agents/skills/muse-round/`: SKILL.md, the role cards, tracking.md);
  - the brief (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md`);
  - the measurement tools the swarm may call (`bench/grader/`, `bench/micro/` entry points);
  - `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` if needed;
  - the docs that describe these (ADR, glossary, `claude/muse-swarm.md`, diagrams).
- **Out of scope:**
  - changing the model or the engine;
  - Claude's post-round measurement process, beyond what it needs to compare claims;
  - running round 3 itself;
  - Muse Code itself.
- **Observable acceptance criteria:**
  1. Every speed claim in a round's READMEs and summary is either backed by a measurement made in the round, with its run file cited, of exactly what is claimed (the slot or combination, at the end-to-end level claimed), or labelled as a prediction and shown next to the measured value.
  2. No hypothesis reaches `ready`, and no attempt goes to *Ready to test*, unless an in-round check shows it improves under ADR 0011's rule, against the unchanged model and the compiled reference.
  3. Predictions count only the candidate's own measured effect, and a combination's effect is measured as a combination.
  4. Anything the swarm did not measure is listed as unverified, never assumed free or neutral.
  5. After a stated number of failures of one design at the same size or phase for the same cause, the next attempt changes approach, or the log records why not.
  6. Claude's post-round G3 agrees with the swarm's in-round measured claims within the noise of the repeats. This is the ultimate test.
- **Quality guardrails:**
  - proportionate and simple: surucuonur rejected sandbox and guard-hook hardening before (memory `muse-isolation-simple`);
  - keep the documents readable by judges;
  - keep Muse-facing instructions in the repo.

## VERIFIED SYSTEM CONTEXT
- **Launch:** `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` (`:71` first prompt "Run the muse-round skill…", `:136` `muse exec … -c agents.execution_capacity=12`). One Muse Code session per round, in worktree `../Hackathon-muse` on branch `muse-agent`, on the Meta Model API. Round 2 ran `muse-wonder-1.0` with approvals on; from step 0 the default is `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` with approvals off.
- **The swarm** (`SKILL.md:22-38`):
  - the lead coordinates and commits, but never explores, builds or grades;
  - explorers write `exploration/territory-*.md` and `ineff-*.md`;
  - the verifier confirms or refutes inefficiencies;
  - builders write and grade one attempt each (`builder.md`);
  - boundary agents write and check a hypothesis's boundary (`boundary.md`);
  - shared docs and logs per phase (`tracking.md`), checkpoints commit them.
- **Steps** (`SKILL.md`): 0 find where you are, 1 starting point, 2 exploration, 3 the analysis, 4 implementation (open hypothesis → boundary → compete → collect → harden → close `ready`/`dropped`), 5 finish (READMEs, *Ready to test*, summary).
- **Measurement tools:**
  - **`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`:** G1/G2 bit-exact at 6 sizes; paired piece timing with a sign test; `beats_compiled`/`beats_baseline` per ADR 0011; takes the GPU lock; loads the model on every run (ADR 0010).
  - **`bench/grader/time_candidates.py`:** end-to-end check and G3.
    - Engines: `plain` (MLX) or `vllm`.
    - Variants: base, compiled-<slot>, muse-<slot>, muse-all, `--variant`.
    - G2 compares greedy tokens; G3 records decode step, prompt time (vLLM only) and wall time; `--repeats` defaults to 5; writes `g3-vllm.json`.
    - Duration: about 8.5 s per run on average in vLLM, so roughly 10–12 min per candidate with base and compiled at 4 settings × 5 repeats.
    - The plain engine has no prompt time yet (`bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py:prompt_ms`, `breakdown.run_plain`).
  - **`bench/grader/gpu_lock.py`:** one GPU job at a time; later ones wait.
- **Isolation and provenance:**
  - git hooks refuse Muse commits outside `muse-spark/`, changes to finished rounds' files, and merges;
  - `tools/provenance_check.py` audits authorship;
  - Claude merges each round, measures it independently (G3) and writes `claude/findings/muse-round-<N>.md`, which the next round reads as its starting point.
- **Round 3's starting point:** no baseline in any slot (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` *For round 3*).
- **Revision:** main at `2090949`, working tree clean apart from two uncommitted pilot files.

## PROTECTED CONTRACTS AND BEHAVIORS
- Authorship separation: the Muse agent writes only in `muse-spark/`, only the lead commits, with the Muse co-author line; Claude never commits on `muse-agent`; hooks and provenance check stay.
- Finished rounds stay frozen (tags `muse-round-1`, `muse-round-2`).
- Muse Code only, swarm design (ADR 0007), no attempt limit (ADR 0006: "limitless"), one grader run per attempt, the GPU queue.
- Grading rules of ADR 0010/0011 (bit-exact at 6 sizes, both phases, hand-off via `max_rows`); G2's token check.
- Claude's post-round independent measurement remains the authority for baselines.
- The attempt format (`spec.json` + `block-N.metal`) and the grader's JSON verdict keys (`g1`, `g2`, `beats_compiled`, `beats_baseline`, `timing_us_per_layer`, `phases_vs_compiled`).

## CONSTRAINTS AND OPERATIONAL REALITY
- **Machine:** M1 Pro, 16 GB, heavy swapping (19–20 GB swap in use); one GPU job at a time. vLLM needs `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` (now the default in `breakdown.py`) and Docker quit. 1-request vLLM timings are noisy (6–41% spread).
- **Time:** about 11.5 h to the deadline, including implementing the fix, running round 3 (~1–2 h), and Claude's measurement and findings (~1 h). The fix should be implementable and checkable in roughly 2–3 h.
- **Cost:** round 2 on Muse Wonder cost about $58; on the contributor model a round costs about $1 (round 1: $0.70). Claude never runs `start.sh` or calls the Meta API without asking.
- **Hard constraints:** the protected items above, and the deadline.
- **Preferences:** simple over airtight (no sandboxing or guard hooks); rules phrased positively for agents (writing-for-agents guidance).
- **Decided:** round 3 runs on `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, round 1's model, which ADR 0008 judged less capable than Muse Wonder, with tool approvals off. No one approves tool calls during the round, so rules must hold without a human watching. Instructions must be explicit and checkable, since a less capable model follows general advice less reliably.

## FAILURE MODES AND FUTURE CHANGES
- **Goodhart risk:** any new check becomes the next proxy. A design must say how the swarm could game it.
- **GPU queue contention:** a 10–12 min end-to-end check blocks builders' grader runs.
- **Memory:** a vLLM run inside the round competes with Muse Code's own processes and may page.
- **Noise:** at 1 request, end-to-end verdicts are mostly `same`.
- **Partial rounds:** a session can stop mid-round, and checks must leave the shared documents consistent.
- **The model can ignore instructions:** round 1 ignored "one attempt per grader run" before it became an explicit rule.
- **Future:** more slots or a different model; rounds 4+; possibly other engines.
- **Prior pitfalls:**
  - independent piece timing hid latency (fixed by ADR 0010);
  - tolerances let the tokens change (fixed by ADR 0010);
  - prefill was untimed (fixed by ADR 0011);
  - G3 with 3 repeats falsely flagged unchanged phases (fixed with 5 repeats).

## DESIGN EXPECTATIONS
- Deliver one coherent approach that fixes the root cause (the gap between the proxy and the objective, and unchecked self-reports) and covers behaviours 1–5, not one patch per symptom.
- Address whole-system effects: the GPU queue and round duration, memory, Claude's post-round role, the docs and judges.
- Cite repository evidence; distinguish verified facts from proposals.
- Specify the changes to the skill, cards, brief and tools, plus any new measurement entry point, at the level of what each says or does.
- Define how a future implementation is validated before round 3, without a paid Muse run if possible, and how round 3's own outcome would show success.
- Do not edit the repository's tracked code, data or configuration; prototypes and tests live in design-lab/.

## UNRESOLVED ASSUMPTIONS AND STOP CONDITIONS
- **Decided (surucuonur, 2026-11-04):** the swarm may run an end-to-end check itself during the round, through the GPU queue. This replaces "Load no model…" (`tracking.md:152`) and "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team" (`SKILL.md:164`) as needed. Claude's post-round G3 remains the independent authority.
- **Assumed (unanswered):** the fix must be ready for round 3 before 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, implementable and checkable in about 2–3 h.
- **Assumption:** the Muse agent follows explicit, checkable rules better than general advice (round 2 kept "one run per attempt" once it was a rule).
- **Return BLOCKED if:** the design requires breaking a protected contract, or depends on a Muse Code capability not documented here.

{"content":"# Solution design brief: make the Muse agent swarm pursue real efficiency, not its proxies (v1)

## APPROVAL
- User approved this brief on 2026-11-04 (surucuonur). Decisions: the swarm may run end-to-end checks in-round through the GPU queue; Meta's Muse does the design work; from round 3 the launcher runs muse-spark-1.3-contributor with tool approvals off (ADR 0012, commit 1113c2d).
- Approved activity: one Muse Code session (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) whose lead starts its own helper agents, up to 12 at once, with no cost or time limit. Agents may prototype and test in design-lab/ (untracked, never committed) and run the measurement tools through the GPU queue. The repository's tracked files stay unchanged.

## PROBLEM AND OUTCOME
- **Current problem:** two rounds of the Muse agent swarm (round 1: Muse Spark; round 2: Muse Wonder, 63 min, ~$58) produced no kernel that is a real efficiency improvement, while the swarm's own reports predicted gains. Five behaviours, each with evidence:
  1. **Treats unmeasured costs as free.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`: "Prefill speed is not timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart from time to first token", citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`. The result: experts attempt-7 is 16–28× slower than the compiled reference at prefill sizes, and routing attempt-4 2.6–8.7× slower (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`). Prompts took 6.6–14.5× and 7–10% longer, and throughput fell by up to 83% (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §5).
  2. **Claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Expected G3 = (compiled − candidate) µs × 20 layers (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md` *Ready to test*; `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`). Round 1 predicted −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.98/+0.16/−1.76. Round 2 predicted −0.84 at each and measured −0.73/−0.74/+0.53 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`, `muse-round-2.md`).
  3. **Reasons inconsistently.** The same README says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then reports "Together (sum) −0.84 ms". Combine's −0.35 ms prediction is −0.07 to −0.09 from its own timing plus −0.27 to −0.29 borrowed from what `mx.compile` gains end to end. Measured: +1.05 ms with 32 requests.
  4. **Used the grader as a search loop (round 1).** 29 grader runs on experts for 4 counted attempts, 18 on attempt-1 with edits between (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §5). Fixed since skill v4: one run is one attempt; round 2 ran 13 for 13.
  5. **Persists with a failing design family.** All 7 experts attempts in round 2 are fused kernels that lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs per layer). The cause, too few threadgroups at 1 row, was already known from round 1. The harden loop says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" (`.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:138`), and there is no rule for changing design.
- **Root cause** (likely; supported by the evidence above): inside a round, the swarm never sees the real objective. Its feedback is a per-slot proxy, the grader's piece timing. The real measurement, Claude's G3 over whole requests, arrives only after the round. The swarm's claims are self-reported and checked by no one before the summary.
  - *verified:* the rules forbid an in-round model run: `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:152` "Load no model and start no other GPU work" and `SKILL.md:164` "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team".
  - *verified:* the goal is phrased as passing gates (`SKILL.md:20`).
  - *verified:* the verifier checks only exploration's inefficiency entries (`verifier.md`). No one checks the implementation phase's predictions, combination claims or Ready-to-test arithmetic.
  - *partly fixed:* ADR 0011 (commit `2090949`) now times the prefill (grader at 6 sizes, G3 with prompt and whole-request time, 5 repeats), so behaviour 1's specific gap is closed. The general habit, treating anything outside the measurement as free, is not addressed.
- **Intended outcome:** in round 3 and later, the swarm's statements about speed match what Claude's independent G3 then measures. It marks something ready only when it is a real improvement under the ADR 0011 rule (faster in one phase, prefill or decode, slower in neither, no whole request slower). It stops repeating a design that keeps failing at the same point.
- **Why now:** surucuonur asked how to fix "these essential problems and behaviour of these agents". The hackathon deadline is 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, about 11.5 h from 14:30 UTC on 2026-11-04. Round 3 should run with the fix.
- **Maturity:** hackathon research tool; judges read the repo, the skill and the round documents.
- **User's suggested approach:** none given. Claude has suggested an in-round end-to-end check and prediction rules; treat these as hypotheses, not constraints.

## SCOPE AND SUCCESS
- **In scope:**
  - the round skill (`.agents/skills/muse-round/`: SKILL.md, the role cards, tracking.md);
  - the brief (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md`);
  - the measurement tools the swarm may call (`bench/grader/`, `bench/micro/` entry points);
  - `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` if needed;
  - the docs that describe these (ADR, glossary, `claude/muse-swarm.md`, diagrams).
- **Out of scope:**
  - changing the model or the engine;
  - Claude's post-round measurement process, beyond what it needs to compare claims;
  - running round 3 itself;
  - Muse Code itself.
- **Observable acceptance criteria:**
  1. Every speed claim in a round's READMEs and summary is either backed by a measurement made in the round, with its run file cited, of exactly what is claimed (the slot or combination, at the end-to-end level claimed), or labelled as a prediction and shown next to the measured value.
  2. No hypothesis reaches `ready`, and no attempt goes to *Ready to test*, unless an in-round check shows it improves under ADR 0011's rule, against the unchanged model and the compiled reference.
  3. Predictions count only the candidate's own measured effect, and a combination's effect is measured as a combination.
  4. Anything the swarm did not measure is listed as unverified, never assumed free or neutral.
  5. After a stated number of failures of one design at the same size or phase for the same cause, the next attempt changes approach, or the log records why not.
  6. Claude's post-round G3 agrees with the swarm's in-round measured claims within the noise of the repeats. This is the ultimate test.
- **Quality guardrails:**
  - proportionate and simple: surucuonur rejected sandbox and guard-hook hardening before (memory `muse-isolation-simple`);
  - keep the documents readable by judges;
  - keep Muse-facing instructions in the repo.

## VERIFIED SYSTEM CONTEXT
- **Launch:** `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` (`:71` first prompt "Run the muse-round skill…", `:136` `muse exec … -c agents.execution_capacity=12`). One Muse Code session per round, in worktree `../Hackathon-muse` on branch `muse-agent`, on the Meta Model API. Round 2 ran `muse-wonder-1.0` with approvals on; from step 0 the default is `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` with approvals off.
- **The swarm** (`SKILL.md:22-38`):
  - the lead coordinates and commits, but never explores, builds or grades;
  - explorers write `exploration/territory-*.md` and `ineff-*.md`;
  - the verifier confirms or refutes inefficiencies;
  - builders write and grade one attempt each (`builder.md`);
  - boundary agents write and check a hypothesis's boundary (`boundary.md`);
  - shared docs and logs per phase (`tracking.md`), checkpoints commit them.
- **Steps** (`SKILL.md`): 0 find where you are, 1 starting point, 2 exploration, 3 the analysis, 4 implementation (open hypothesis → boundary → compete → collect → harden → close `ready`/`dropped`), 5 finish (READMEs, *Ready to test*, summary).
- **Measurement tools:**
  - **`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`:** G1/G2 bit-exact at 6 sizes; paired piece timing with a sign test; `beats_compiled`/`beats_baseline` per ADR 0011; takes the GPU lock; loads the model on every run (ADR 0010).
  - **`bench/grader/time_candidates.py`:** end-to-end check and G3.
    - Engines: `plain` (MLX) or `vllm`.
    - Variants: base, compiled-<slot>, muse-<slot>, muse-all, `--variant`.
    - G2 compares greedy tokens; G3 records decode step, prompt time (vLLM only) and wall time; `--repeats` defaults to 5; writes `g3-vllm.json`.
    - Duration: about 8.5 s per run on average in vLLM, so roughly 10–12 min per candidate with base and compiled at 4 settings × 5 repeats.
    - The plain engine has no prompt time yet (`bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py:prompt_ms`, `breakdown.run_plain`).
  - **`bench/grader/gpu_lock.py`:** one GPU job at a time; later ones wait.
- **Isolation and provenance:**
  - git hooks refuse Muse commits outside `muse-spark/`, changes to finished rounds' files, and merges;
  - `tools/provenance_check.py` audits authorship;
  - Claude merges each round, measures it independently (G3) and writes `claude/findings/muse-round-<N>.md`, which the next round reads as its starting point.
- **Round 3's starting point:** no baseline in any slot (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` *For round 3*).
- **Revision:** main at `2090949`, working tree clean apart from two uncommitted pilot files.

## PROTECTED CONTRACTS AND BEHAVIORS
- Authorship separation: the Muse agent writes only in `muse-spark/`, only the lead commits, with the Muse co-author line; Claude never commits on `muse-agent`; hooks and provenance check stay.
- Finished rounds stay frozen (tags `muse-round-1`, `muse-round-2`).
- Muse Code only, swarm design (ADR 0007), no attempt limit (ADR 0006: "limitless"), one grader run per attempt, the GPU queue.
- Grading rules of ADR 0010/0011 (bit-exact at 6 sizes, both phases, hand-off via `max_rows`); G2's token check.
- Claude's post-round independent measurement remains the authority for baselines.
- The attempt format (`spec.json` + `block-N.metal`) and the grader's JSON verdict keys (`g1`, `g2`, `beats_compiled`, `beats_baseline`, `timing_us_per_layer`, `phases_vs_compiled`).

## CONSTRAINTS AND OPERATIONAL REALITY
- **Machine:** M1 Pro, 16 GB, heavy swapping (19–20 GB swap in use); one GPU job at a time. vLLM needs `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` (now the default in `breakdown.py`) and Docker quit. 1-request vLLM timings are noisy (6–41% spread).
- **Time:** about 11.5 h to the deadline, including implementing the fix, running round 3 (~1–2 h), and Claude's measurement and findings (~1 h). The fix should be implementable and checkable in roughly 2–3 h.
- **Cost:** round 2 on Muse Wonder cost about $58; on the contributor model a round costs about $1 (round 1: $0.70). Claude never runs `start.sh` or calls the Meta API without asking.
- **Hard constraints:** the protected items above, and the deadline.
- **Preferences:** simple over airtight (no sandboxing or guard hooks); rules phrased positively for agents (writing-for-agents guidance).
- **Decided:** round 3 runs on `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, round 1's model, which ADR 0008 judged less capable than Muse Wonder, with tool approvals off. No one approves tool calls during the round, so rules must hold without a human watching. Instructions must be explicit and checkable, since a less capable model follows general advice less reliably.

## FAILURE MODES AND FUTURE CHANGES
- **Goodhart risk:** any new check becomes the next proxy. A design must say how the swarm could game it.
- **GPU queue contention:** a 10–12 min end-to-end check blocks builders' grader runs.
- **Memory:** a vLLM run inside the round competes with Muse Code's own processes and may page.
- **Noise:** at 1 request, end-to-end verdicts are mostly `same`.
- **Partial rounds:** a session can stop mid-round, and checks must leave the shared documents consistent.
- **The model can ignore instructions:** round 1 ignored "one attempt per grader run" before it became an explicit rule.
- **Future:** more slots or a different model; rounds 4+; possibly other engines.
- **Prior pitfalls:**
  - independent piece timing hid latency (fixed by ADR 0010);
  - tolerances let the tokens change (fixed by ADR 0010);
  - prefill was untimed (fixed by ADR 0011);
  - G3 with 3 repeats falsely flagged unchanged phases (fixed with 5 repeats).

## DESIGN EXPECTATIONS
- Deliver one coherent approach that fixes the root cause (the gap between the proxy and the objective, and unchecked self-reports) and covers behaviours 1–5, not one patch per symptom.
- Address whole-system effects: the GPU queue and round duration, memory, Claude's post-round role, the docs and judges.
- Cite repository evidence; distinguish verified facts from proposals.
- Specify the changes to the skill, cards, brief and tools, plus any new measurement entry point, at the level of what each says or does.
- Define how a future implementation is validated before round 3, without a paid Muse run if possible, and how round 3's own outcome would show success.
- Do not edit the repository's tracked code, data or configuration; prototypes and tests live in design-lab/.

## UNRESOLVED ASSUMPTIONS AND STOP CONDITIONS
- **Decided (surucuonur, 2026-11-04):** the swarm may run an end-to-end check itself during the round, through the GPU queue. This replaces "Load no model…" (`tracking.md:152`) and "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team" (`SKILL.md:164`) as needed. Claude's post-round G3 remains the independent authority.
- **Assumed (unanswered):** the fix must be ready for round 3 before 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, implementable and checkable in about 2–3 h.
- **Assumption:** the Muse agent follows explicit, checkable rules better than general advice (round 2 kept "one run per attempt" once it was a rule).
- **Return BLOCKED if:** the design requires breaking a protected contract, or depends on a Muse Code capability not documented here.

1|# Explorer-skill report: what `.agents/skills/muse-round/` and `claude/muse-agent-brief.md` say that bears on behaviours 1–5
2|
3|Territory: `.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md`, `explorer.md`, `verifier.md`, `builder.md`, `boundary.md`, `tracking.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `claude/muse-agent-brief.md`. Skill version 7 (`SKILL.md:10`). Read at worktree commit 1113c2d (brief says 2090949; see §Corrections).
4|
5|No GPU work was run: every claim below is textual (file:line quotes), so no measurement result files exist for this report.
6|
7|## Territory facts (shared by all behaviours)
8|
9|- T1. The goal is phrased purely as passing gates. `SKILL.md:20`: "The goal: kernels that pass G1 and G2 and have `beats_compiled` true, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither (ADR 0011); where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline` true too; faster because they remove a cause you can name."
10|- T2. In-round model runs are forbidden twice. `tracking.md:152`: "**The grader is the only GPU job.** Run it only as a builder, through the brief's command; it waits its turn when another run has the GPU. Load no model and start no other GPU work: the machine has 16 GB and slows down sharply when memory runs short." `SKILL.md:164`: "**G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team,** who run them after merging your branch."
11|- T3. The verifier's scope is exploration only. `verifier.md:5`: "The implementation phase builds only on inefficiencies you confirmed, so every claim an inefficiency rests on is checked against its source before anyone builds on it." Its steps (`verifier.md:9-25`) only ever touch `<round>/exploration/ineff-*.md` (`verifier.md:11`: "Find open entries: `grep -l 'Status:** open' <round>/exploration/ineff-*.md`") and mark them `confirmed`/`refuted` (`verifier.md:17-19`). Nothing in the card mentions hypothesis entries, builder predictions, combination claims, or Ready to test.
12|- T4. The lead writes all unchecked summary numbers. `SKILL.md:160-161`: "you write the two READMEs, the hypothesis entries' status blocks and decisions, and `summary.md`". Ready to test (`SKILL.md:147`): "It names the attempt per slot that goes to G3, this round's, the baseline kept, or the reference, and the change you expect in G3's four workloads, in the decode step, the prompt time and the whole request, against the previous round's, with how you worked it out." No method, citation, or labelling rule constrains "how you worked it out". The close-`ready` Decision likewise "states what G3 should show" (`tracking.md:113`; `SKILL.md:140`).
13|- T5. The only cross-cutting number rule is vague. `tracking.md:153`: "**Every number has a source:** a file and line, a table (path and row), a grader verdict (attempt folder), or arithmetic shown in full." Piece arithmetic with its working shown therefore satisfies the letter of the rule.
14|- T6. The harden loop has a continue rule but no stop-or-switch rule. `SKILL.md:135-138`: pick the best attempt ("passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, has `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline`, and it is the fastest across the six sizes"), "Set the status to `hardening`, and start a builder for that attempt's next single change", "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove." `ready` (`SKILL.md:140`) requires "you can name no further change worth making". Nothing names giving up on a design family, switching approach, or counting repeated failures at the same size/phase/cause.
15|- T7. The builder self-checks its own prediction with no enforcement. `builder.md:24` requires predicted µs per layer at the six sizes "with the arithmetic"; `builder.md:30`: "If the attempt failed, or its time missed your prediction by more than 20%, find out why. Write the answer in `notes.md`, and add it to the inefficiency entry as a note." No one verifies this happened; the lead only checkpoints (`SKILL.md:38-43`).
16|- T8. One-run-one-attempt is explicit (behaviour 4's fix). `builder.md:13`: "**One grader run is one attempt.** After a run, any change, even a one-line fix, is a new attempt with its own number, built by copying the files you keep." `CHANGELOG.md:12` dates it to skill v4. `SKILL.md:15` also removes the brief's stop rule: "you decide when a slot is done. Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try."
17|- T9. Inefficiency entries must state cross-phase effects, but only as predictions. `tracking.md:103`: "**Predicted saving** if removed, in µs per decode step at 1, 8 and 32 rows and per prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows, with the arithmetic. A saving in one phase that costs the other is not one." `SKILL.md:112-114` ranks by "predicted saving" and requires "each with what removing it does to the other phase, and whether a hand-off (`max_rows`) keeps that phase unchanged".
18|- T10. The brief's own end-to-end language is descriptive, not an in-round procedure. `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:213`: "It is a guide; G3 decides." `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:215`: "Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch." `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:11` states the both-phases rule ("faster in one, and no slower in the other"), and `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:173` documents `max_rows` ("The hand-off is graded like the rest: bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes").
19|- T11. Explorers predict savings the verifier confirms only against cited sources. `explorer.md:18`: "write an inefficiency entry with its cost arithmetic and predicted saving"; `verifier.md:12-15` checks claims by "open the cited file at the cited lines; find the cited table row; redo the arithmetic". A prediction whose arithmetic is internally consistent and whose inputs are cited therefore passes, even if the inputs don't transfer end to end.
20|
21|## Behaviour 1: treats unmeasured costs as free
22|
23|Facts bearing on it: T1, T2, T5, T9, T10.
24|
25|Where the instructions create or allow it. The goal (T1, `SKILL.md:20`) defines success entirely in grader verdicts, so anything the grader does not time is definitionally irrelevant to passing. The in-round measurement ban (T2, `tracking.md:152`, `SKILL.md:164`) makes it impossible to check anything the grader omits, so "free apart from time to first token" style reasoning is the only available move for unmeasured costs. The cross-phase guard (`tracking.md:103`, `SKILL.md:114`) asks for a prediction ("what removing it does to the other phase"), not a measurement, and the number rule (`tracking.md:153`) accepts shown arithmetic as a source. Nothing says "list what you did not measure" or "never assume an unmeasured cost is zero/neutral".
26|
27|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes the general habit structurally: gate-defined goal + no in-round end-to-end measurement + arithmetic-accepted-as-source. It could prevent the specific prefill instance only indirectly (v7 times prefill via `beats_compiled`, `CHANGELOG.md:9`), but the general habit has no rule against it. Proposal (not a finding): a "list unverified costs; never assume free/neutral" rule would plug the gap the brief's acceptance criterion 4 names.
28|
29|## Behaviour 2: claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic
30|
31|Facts bearing on it: T2, T4, T5, T7, T10.
32|
33|Where the instructions create or allow it. Ready to test (`SKILL.md:147`, quoted in T4) *requires* the lead to state "the change you expect in G3's four workloads" while T2 forbids running anything that measures G3 in-round — so the expected change can only be piece arithmetic (e.g. × 20 layers). No rule constrains the method ("with how you worked it out" is free-form), no rule requires labelling it a prediction, and T3/T4 leave no checker: the verifier never sees implementation documents. The brief reinforces the hand-off model (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:215`, T10). `tracking.md:153` blesses the arithmetic as sourced.
34|
35|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes it directly: it demands an end-to-end number and simultaneously forbids the only measurement that could produce one. Prevention would need either an in-round end-to-end check (the brief's decided direction) or a prediction rule (measure what you claim; label the rest) — neither exists in this territory today.
36|
37|## Behaviour 3: reasons inconsistently (non-composition admitted, then summed; borrowed compile gains)
38|
39|Facts bearing on it: T4, T5, T7, T11.
40|
41|Where the instructions allow it. No rule in the territory says a combination's effect must be measured as a combination, or that a prediction may count only the candidate's own measured effect. The builder records per-attempt six-size timings (`builder.md:29`) and self-explains >20% misses (`builder.md:30`), but combining two slots' savings, or borrowing `mx.compile`'s end-to-end gain into one slot's prediction, violates no stated rule: the verifier's remit ends at exploration (T3), the lead's Ready-to-test arithmetic is unchecked (T4), and shown arithmetic counts as sourced (T5). The "faster because they remove a cause you can name" clause (`SKILL.md:20`) asks for a causal story, not arithmetic discipline.
42|
43|Cause vs prevention. The territory allows rather than mandates this: it is silent on combination arithmetic, so inconsistent reasoning passes every gate. Prevention needs an explicit prediction rule (brief's acceptance criterion 3); the closest existing hooks are `builder.md:30` (could be extended to combinations) and `tracking.md:153` (could require measured-not-borrowed inputs).
44|
45|## Behaviour 4: used the grader as a search loop (round 1)
46|
47|Facts bearing on it: T8.
48|
49|Where the instructions created it, and the fix. Pre-v4 skill had no one-run-one-attempt rule, and the brief's attempt model ("Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed", `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:14`) assumed a single agent grading its own work, so repeated grade-edit-grade cycles fit the letter of the instructions. Skill v4 added the explicit rule (`builder.md:13`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`), and the brief's stop rule was simultaneously voided (`SKILL.md:15`, `builder.md:13`: "the brief's *When a slot stops* rule no longer applies"). The fix works by making each run a countable, committed attempt ("Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try", `SKILL.md:15`).
50|
51|Cause vs prevention. This is the territory's one demonstrated self-correction: an explicit, checkable rule ("any change, even a one-line fix, is a new attempt") replaced a violated norm. It supports the brief's assumption that explicit checkable rules work on this swarm. Residual gap (proposal, not finding): nothing stops a builder from running the grader, then abandoning the attempt folder uncommitted — the lead commits "the attempt folder" at collect (`SKILL.md:133`), so an unreturned attempt could still hide a run; the history shows every *returned* try.
52|
53|## Behaviour 5: persists with a failing design family
54|
55|Facts bearing on it: T1, T6, T9.
56|
57|Where the instructions create or allow it. The harden loop (`SKILL.md:135-138`) only ever says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" — a skilled agent can always name one more cause, so the loop has no failure counter and no exit to a different design. `ready` (`SKILL.md:140`) requires only gate passage plus "no further change worth making", judged by the same lead running the loop. "Faster because they remove a cause you can name" (`SKILL.md:20`) rewards cause-naming, which is exactly what kept the fused-kernel family alive. The compete step (`SKILL.md:131`) diversifies directions once ("Give each a different direction"), but harden then single-threads on "the best attempt" (`SKILL.md:136`), so early convergence to one family is structural. No rule says "after N failures at the same size/phase for the same cause, change approach or log why not".
58|
59|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes it: single-threaded hill-climbing on a nameable-cause loop with no design-switch rule. The starting-point machinery (`SKILL.md:64-76`, step 1: "what keeps a starting point from passing G2, and where the attempt still spends its time") surfaces the repeated failure in prose but attaches no consequence. Prevention needs the brief's acceptance criterion 5 as an explicit rule, e.g. in the harden step.
60|
61|## Corrections: what the brief gets wrong about this territory
62|
63|1. Stale revision. Brief `design-lab/brief.md:72` says "main at `2090949`", but the session worktree is at 1113c2d (per the task; `SKILL.md:20` and `CHANGELOG.md:9` already contain the ADR 0012 contributor-model text, which postdates 2090949). Correction: brief §"Revision" predates commit 1113c2d.
64|2. Stale skill-version reference inside the territory (not a brief error, but the brief's citations assume v7 consistency): `SKILL.md:80` step 2.1 says "its version line (v1, with skill version 6)" while `SKILL.md:10` declares "**Skill version 7**". One of the two is stale; a round following step 2.1 literally would stamp the wrong skill version.
65|3. Imprecise swarm citation (minor). Brief `:50` cites "`SKILL.md:22-38`" for the swarm table; the role table itself is `SKILL.md:24-30`, helper-start shape `SKILL.md:32-34`, tracking pointer `SKILL.md:36`, and checkpoints `SKILL.md:38-43`. The range covers it but the checkpoint procedure runs past line 38 (to 43).
66|4. All behaviour-1–5 citations to this territory verified correct: harden-loop quote (`SKILL.md:138`), "Load no model…" (`tracking.md:152`), "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team" (`SKILL.md:164`), goal-as-gates (`SKILL.md:20`), verifier scope (`verifier.md`), one-run-one-attempt fix in v4 (`builder.md:13`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`). No wording errors found in these quotes.
67|
68|## Pre-existing hooks a fix could reuse (all verified above)
69|
70|- `tracking.md:153` (number-source rule) — extend to require measured inputs and unverified-lists.
71|- `SKILL.md:147` (Ready to test) + `tracking.md:113` (Decision "states what G3 should show") — attach prediction-labelling and method rules.
72|- `builder.md:30` (20% miss rule) — extend to combinations and borrowed gains.
73|- `SKILL.md:135-140` (harden/ready) — add failure-count design-switch rule.
74|- `verifier.md` — extend remit, or add a second checker for implementation arithmetic.
75|- `CHANGELOG.md:12` pattern — behaviour 4 shows explicit checkable rules get followed.

354|  (`muse-spark/exploration/README.md:74-83`,
355|  `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/README.md:156+`), the `ineff-runs-3`
356|  refutation (`muse-spark/exploration/README.md:68`), attempt-3's lever
357|  refutation (B5-e), the dropped hyp-1 with an explicitly unclaimed
358|  prediction (`hyp-1-experts-exact.md:493`), and the interaction carried
359|  as a constraint (`README.md:13`) all show builders recording
360|  anti-evidence. Behaviour 1/2/3 persist not because counter-evidence is
361|  suppressed but because no record slot forces the Ready-to-test/summary
362|  arithmetic to answer it.
363|- **Per behaviour:**
364|  1. Caused by the boundary template's can't-see list being a *deferral*
365|     list ("runs after merging", B1-c/g) with no "unverified, do not
366|     assume" slot; the same boundary files that price prefill at zero
367|     could instead record it as unverified — the vocabulary already
368|     exists ("unmeasured", used 10+ times in exploration).
369|  2. Caused by Decision/README/summary templates requiring a G3 number
370|     computable only from piece data; preventable by a schema that
371|     requires the run file and level of each claimed number (the records
372|     already cite run files for piece timings, e.g. README `:9` tables).
373|  3. Caused by caveats living in prose while numbers live in tables: the
374|     "not assumed to compose" sentence (`:13`) and the sum (`:36`) are 23
375|     lines apart with no cell linking them. A table column ("composes?
376|     unmeasured") would have forced the conflict into the open.
377|  4. Round-1 cause visible in records: attempt folders double as scratch
378|     space (v1–v15 "same attempt folder", B4-a–c) and the log records
379|     grades without numbering rule; fixed in round 2 by the
380|     one-run-one-attempt practice (B4-g) — evidence that an explicit,
381|     checkable record rule holds.
382|  5. Caused by the builder-section template ending in "Next: one change"
383|     plus Decisions judging "no further single change": the loop can only
384|     terminate a *change*, never a *family*. B5-b shows the family-level
385|     judgment happens — but only in the summary, after the attempts are
386|     spent. A per-hypothesis "attempts at this failure point" counter in
387|     the log/README would move it in-round.
388|
389|## Corrections: what the brief gets wrong about this territory
390|
391|- **C1. Round-1 experts grader runs: 28, not 29.** Bash invocations of
392|  `check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-N` in session
393|  `01a1a345`: attempt-1: 18, attempt-2: 3, attempt-3: 6, attempt-4: 1 =
394|  28 (round total 33 for 8 attempts; combine attempt-2 accounts for the
395|  other multi-run case with 2). "18 on attempt-1, with edits between"
396|  matches exactly (notes.md v1–v15 + re-grade). The one-run gap may be a
397|  quoted-but-unrun command or a lock-stopped retry counted elsewhere;
398|  from this territory's transcripts the executed count is 28.
399|- **C2. "All 7 experts attempts … lose at 1 row" overstates twice.**
400|  Attempt-6 never launched (G1 fail: "Thread group size (512) is greater
401|  than the maximum allowed (448)",
402|  `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:360-365`), so
403|  six attempts have 1-row timings. And attempts 2–3 are two-kernel
404|  splits (`:205-212`, `:231-241`) — "fused" only in the per-op sense,
405|  not single-kernel. The ranges check out: candidates 92.1–109.5,
406|  compiled 73.1–86.9 (README `:9`).
407|- **C3. Behaviour-2's formula and round-1 totals.** "(compiled −
408|  candidate)" is round 2's formula (README `:29`); round 1 used
409|  "(reference − candidate)" with the *eager* reference
410|  (`muse-spark/implementation/README.md:27,35`: "(64.3−50.0)" where 64.3
411|  is eager, 65.3 compiled). Round-1 records also never state cross-slot
412|  totals; "−0.54/−1.81/−5.72" occur in-territory only as quotations of
413|  `claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` (B2-k cites). The brief's "Round 1
414|  predicted −0.54…" is Claude's sum of the swarm's per-slot numbers,
415|  not a sentence the swarm wrote.
416|- **C4. No `logs/` directory in round 2.** The delegated task's "plus
417|  logs" does not exist as a directory; each phase keeps one `log.md`
418|  (`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/log.md`,
419|  `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/log.md`), same as round 1.
420|- **C5. "Too few threadgroups … already known from round 1" needs
421|  dating.** Round 1's recorded cause was 1-row occupancy
422|  (`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-1-fused-experts.md:103-108`); the "4
423|  threadgroups" framing is round 2's `ineff-baseline-experts-2`
424|  (chained timing, unavailable in round 1). Moreover round-2 attempt-3
425|  refuted group-count as the lever past 4 groups (B5-e) — the records'
426|  own later finding, which the brief's phrasing predates.
427|- **C6. Trivia: combine's borrowed offsets are −0.26…−0.29, not
428|  "−0.27…−0.29".**
429|  `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:29`: routing compiled
430|  −0.220/−0.183/−0.157, combine compiled −0.288/−0.260/−0.272.
431|- **C7. Stale revision line (brief-internal).** Brief §APPROVAL cites
432|  commit 1113c2d (ADR 0012) while "Revision: main at `2090949`" two
433|  sections later; the worktree is at 1113c2d (`git log --oneline -1`,
434|  read-only). Not about my territory's content, flagged once.
435|- **Confirmed verbatim:** the B1-a quote and `:150-151` cite; "Together
436|  (sum) −0.84" (`README.md:36`); "per-slot wins are not assumed to
437|  compose" (`:13`); summary `:8`; round-2 "13 for 13" (transcript +
438|  log); round-2 duration 63.4 min (transcript `01a1a48b` first→last;
439|  the "~$58" cost is not verifiable from this territory — no prices).
440|- **Not verifiable from this territory** (post-round artifacts outside
441|  `muse-spark/`): experts "16–28×" / routing "2.6–8.7×" prefill
442|  slowdowns, combine "+1.05 ms with 32 requests", prompt-length and
443|  throughput effects. No statement for or against.
444|
445|## Appendix: grader-count method (reproducible)
446|
447|```bash
448|# bash tool calls only (edit_file calls that merely quote the command excluded)
449|python3 -c "
450|import json, re, glob
451|from collections import Counter
452|c = Counter()
453|for f in sorted(glob.glob('muse-spark/transcripts/*.jsonl')):
454|    sess = f.split('/')[-1][:8]
455|    for line in open(f):
456|        if 'check_candidate' not in line: continue
457|        d = json.loads(line)
458|        if d.get('event') != 'assistant_tool_calls_committed': continue
459|        for tc in d.get('tool_calls', []):
460|            if tc.get('name') != 'bash': continue
461|            for x in re.findall(r'check_candidate\.py\s+(muse-spark/(?:round-2/)?kernels/[a-z-]+/attempt-\d+)', tc.get('args','')):
462|                c[(sess,x)] += 1
463|for k in sorted(c): print(c[k], k)
464|"
465|# Result: 01a1a345 → experts 18/3/6/1, routing 1/1, combine 1/2 (33 total);
466|# 01a1a48b → 1 per attempt × 13 (13 total).
467|```
468|
469|Caveat: this counts executed bash tool calls, not completed grader
470|verdicts; a call stopped by the GPU lock would still count. No such
471|stop is recorded in either implementation log, and every round-2 call
472|has its matching "graded" log line, so executed ≈ completed here.
473|*[analysis]* on the caveat sentence.

results.text:
Read text file `design-lab/explorer-tools/report.md`.
1|# explorer-tools report: measurement tools territory
2|
3|Scope: `bench/grader/check_candidate.py`, `slots.py`, `time_candidates.py`,
4|`gpu_lock.py`, `engine_table.py`, `bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py`,
5|`breakdown.py` (`run_plain`, `run_vllm`, `prefill`, `prompt_ms`),
6|`clean_vllm.py`, `compiled_exact.py`. Read `design-lab/brief.md` first.
7|No tracked file changed; all outputs below are in `design-lab/explorer-tools/`.
8|
9|Own measurements (commands in §8): `help-check_candidate.txt`,
10|`help-time_candidates.txt`, `grade-routing-a4.json` (+`.stderr`),
11|`grade-experts-a7.json` (+`.stderr`), `plain-probe*/`, `vllm-duration-estimate.txt`.
12|
13|## 1. Territory facts
14|
15|### 1.1 check_candidate.py — the per-slot grader
16|
17|- CLI: `attempt slot [--out FILE] [--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER ...]`
18|  (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:280-291`). No `--repeats`, `--sizes`,
19|  `--tokens` flags: the protocol is fixed in code, unlike `time_candidates.py`.
20|  Verified: `help-check_candidate.txt`.
21|- Takes the GPU lock first (`check_candidate.py:293`), then loads the model on
22|  every run (`check_candidate.py:304` via `slots.load_model`).
23|- Sizes (6): decode rows 1/8/32 from saved inputs (`check_candidate.py:50,307`),
24|  prefill rows 127/1016/2048 captured live from a real prefill
25|  (`check_candidate.py:308-311`, `slots.py:214-221`).
26|- G2: every output bit-identical to the reference at all 6 sizes × 20 layers
27|  (`check_candidate.py:312-343`). Timing runs only if G2 passes
28|  (`check_candidate.py:344`).
29|- Timing: 20 layers chained so each call waits for the previous
30|  (`check_candidate.py:191-208`); candidate vs compiled (vs baseline) in
31|  rotating paired repeats, REPEATS=30, WINS_NEEDED=22, one-sided sign test
32|  p<0.01 (`check_candidate.py:52-57,223-244`). The `reference` (uncompiled)
33|  column is an unpaired median for display only (`check_candidate.py:211-220,359`).
34|- Verdict per bar: `beats_*` = faster at every size of one phase, slower at
35|  none of the other (`check_candidate.py:247-263`).
36|- For `routing+combine`, per-repeat times are summed across parts before
37|  comparing (`check_candidate.py:365`): one part's win can be masked by the
38|  other's loss inside a single verdict.
39|- Any exception (bad spec, failed Metal build, shape error) is reported as G1
40|  with exit code 0 (`check_candidate.py:378-383`): a wrapper must read the JSON,
41|  not the exit code.
42|- `--baseline` accepts any folder; the tool does not enforce "previous round's
43|  final attempt" (`check_candidate.py:74-88`). It must merely cover the slot's
44|  parts.
45|- `max_rows` hand-off (`slots.py:327-337`): above `max_rows` rows the compiled
46|  reference runs instead of the kernels. With `max_rows=32`, all prefill sizes
47|  compare compiled-vs-compiled ("same"), so `beats_compiled` needs only decode
48|  wins. Sanctioned by ADR 0011, but it makes prefill a non-event by delegation.
49|- Duration measured: routing attempt-4 (G2 pass): 12.7 s wall
50|  (`grade-routing-a4.json`); experts attempt-7 (G2 pass): 4 m 57 s wall
51|  (`grade-experts-a7.json`). Range spans ~13 s to ~5 min per run depending on
52|  slot. GPU-bound (user+sys ≪ real).
53|
54|### 1.2 time_candidates.py — end-to-end check and G3
55|
56|- Engines `plain` (MLX in-process) or `vllm` (`time_candidates.py:202`).
57|- Variants are built positionally: `base`, per-slot `compiled-<slot>` and
58|  `muse-<slot>`, plus `compiled-all`/`muse-all` only when >1 attempt is passed
59|  (`time_candidates.py:111-132`). `--variant NAME:...` adds extras outside
60|  `muse-all`; `compiled` as a folder means that slot's compiled reference
61|  (`time_candidates.py:100-109`).
62|- Swapping is a runtime class-attribute patch of `MoE.__call__` in every layer
63|  (`time_candidates.py:134-135`, `slots.make_moe_call`, `slots.py:97-119`).
64|  Positional attempts must not share parts (`time_candidates.py:221-223`);
65|  `--variant` extras are not checked for overlap.
66|- G2 end-to-end: greedy tokens over 24 generated tokens at 1 and 32 requests
67|  must equal base's — `TOKENS=24` (`time_candidates.py:51,138-160`) for plain,
68|  `max_tokens=24` (`repeat_fixes.py:187`) for vLLM. Kernel counts are also
69|  recorded (`repeat_fixes.py:137-144`). **There is no pass/fail gate on token
70|  exactness**: `exact` is logged per check and G3 ignores it
71|  (`time_candidates.py:168-197` reads only `kind=="run"` records).
72|- Timing loop `repeat_fixes.time_variants` (`repeat_fixes.py:285-359`):
73|  `--repeats` (default 5), `--settings` (default `1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024`),
74|  `--tokens` (default 256 output tokens). Plan shuffled with fixed seeds
75|  (`repeat_fixes.py:299-303`). Each run records decode-step period
76|  (`breakdown.summarize`), wall time, and `prompt_ms()`.
77|- G3 verdict (`time_candidates.py:163-197`) is computed **only for vLLM**
78|  (`time_candidates.py:260-261`) and written to `g3-vllm.json`. Each `muse-*`
79|  variant is judged against `base` and its `compiled-*` counterpart: one phase
80|  (decode or prompt) faster in every setting, neither phase nor any request
81|  slower; faster/slower = non-overlapping min–max ranges over repeats.
82|- Fragility: G3 judges every variant whose name starts with `muse-`
83|  (`time_candidates.py:177`) and looks up a bar named `compiled-<suffix>`. A
84|  `--variant muse-foo:...` (no `compiled-foo` runs) makes `ranges()` empty and
85|  `min()` raises — G3 crashes. Conversely a `--variant` not starting with
86|  `muse-` is timed but never judged.
87|- `--tokens` below 9 crashes with `RuntimeError: no steady decode steps`
88|  (`breakdown.py:508-510`, `summarize` needs interior steps after SKIP=5):
89|  verified, `plain-probe.stderr`. So the gaming floor for `--tokens` is 9, at
90|  which wall ≈ prompt + 8 steps.
91|- KV cache size depends on the chosen settings: 1 GiB if any prompt >128 else
92|  512 MiB (`time_candidates.py:250`). Different `--settings` choices are therefore run under different memory
93|  pressure and are not strictly comparable.
94|- Duration from the current-format log
95|  `results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/muse-vllm.jsonl` (8 variants × 4
96|  settings × 3 repeats, 256 tokens): per-setting wall medians 1x128: 1.5 s,
97|  8x128: 3.9 s, 32x128: 8.6 s, 32x1024: 17.0 s (mean 37.6 s — heavy paging
98|  outliers); overall mean 13.6 s/run. See `vllm-duration-estimate.txt`.
99|  Extrapolated single-slot G3 call (3 variants: base, compiled-X, muse-X):
100|  60 runs ≈ 13–14 min of run wall at 5 repeats, plus checks and model load
101|  (prediction from that log, not a fresh run). A 3-slot call builds 9 variants
102|  (base + 3×compiled + 3×muse + both -all) ≈ 3× that. Checks cost 12
103|  vLLM generations (24 tokens each) per variant set plus one graph export.
104|- Plain probe: 3 variants × 1 setting × 1 repeat × 32 tokens + full checks ran
105|  in 10.5 s (`plain-probe32/`). Checks dominate at small scale. Plain full-G3
106|  shape (60 runs × 256 tokens) was not measured; per-run decode work is the
107|  same model, so expect the same order as vLLM minus vLLM overhead
108|  (assumption, unmeasured).
109|
110|### 1.3 What plain lacks
111|
112|- `prompt_ms()` measures first-forward to first step with no prefill tokens
113|  left (`repeat_fixes.py:277-282`), but `run_plain` records steps only for the
114|  decode loop (`breakdown.py:468-484`); the prefill runs outside any step.
115|  Result: plain `prompt_ms` is exactly `0.0` on every run — verified in
116|  `plain-probe32/muse-plain.jsonl` (all three runs `prompt_ms= 0.0`).
117|- No G3 verdict is ever written for plain (`time_candidates.py:260-261`):
118|  verified, `plain-probe32/` contains only `muse-plain.jsonl`.
119|- Plain prefill chunks prompts at PREFILL_TOKENS=2048 (`breakdown.py:87,453-465`),
120|  mirroring vLLM's 2048-token budget, and `wall_ms` does include the prefill
121|  (timed around the whole run, `repeat_fixes.py:309-311`). So plain has
122|  decode + wall, a zero prompt, and no verdict.
123|- Single-repeat noise anecdote from the probe: `muse-routing` had the fastest
124|  step period (4.42 ms) but the slowest wall (250.9 ms vs base 208.9 ms) —
125|  ordering by one repeat's wall disagrees with ordering by period.
126|
127|### 1.4 gpu_lock.py
128|
129|- Exclusive `flock` on `/tmp/mobilemoe-gpu.lock`, shared across checkouts; waits
130|  forever with a stderr notice naming the holder; OS releases on process end
131|  (`gpu_lock.py:18-32`). No timeout, no queue fairness beyond kernel order.
132|- The lock is purely voluntary: it works only if every GPU user calls `hold()`.
133|  Holders: `check_candidate.py:293`, `time_candidates.py:224`,
134|  `check_sizes.py:38`, `slots.py:371` (capture), `compiled_exact.py:36`,
135|  `clean_vllm.py:78`, `chain_timing.py:34`. **Non-holders:
136|  `breakdown.py` and `repeat_fixes.py` never import `gpu_lock`** (verified by
137|  grep over `bench/`, §8) — a swarm agent running those entry points directly
138|  bypasses the queue and distorts a concurrent run's timings.
139|- Attack surfaces (by code reading): a process that never calls `hold()`
140|  bypasses; a process that calls `hold()` then sleeps holds the GPU hostage
141|  indefinitely; deleting `/tmp/mobilemoe-gpu.lock` silently breaks mutual
142|  exclusion for newcomers (new inode); holder string is self-reported.
143|
144|### 1.5 Adjacent tools
145|
146|- `check_sizes.py`: G2 checks at 25 in-between row counts (2..1500) to catch
147|  row-count branching (`check_sizes.py:26-27,45-57`). Takes the lock. Not part
148|  of the grader; the swarm never runs it in-round (skill matter, not tool).
149|- `compiled_exact.py`: verifies the `max_rows` hand-off target (compiled
150|  reference) is bit-exact at the 6 G2 sizes (`compiled_exact.py:1-9,35-54`).
151|  Takes the lock.
152|- `clean_vllm.py`: outside-view vLLM timing (no hooks) in 3 layouts
153|  (`clean_vllm.py:1-22`); prompt = 1-token run, step = (256-run − 1-run)/255.
154|  Takes the lock. Shows an alternative prompt/decode split that needs no hooks.
155|- `engine_table.py`: renders `muse-<engine>.jsonl` into `versions.csv` /
156|  `correctness.csv` (`engine_table.py:37-97`). Tolerates missing `prompt_ms`
157|  (`engine_table.py:63`). Pure reader, no lock needed.
158|
159|## 2. Behaviours 1–5: how the territory causes or could prevent each
160|
161|1. **Unmeasured costs as free.** Cause: the grader's piece timing never sees
162|   request-level effects by construction; worse, the plain engine reports
163|   `prompt_ms = 0.0` always (§1.3) — an in-round plain check literally prices
164|   the prefill at zero. `max_rows` lets prefill be "same by delegation" (§1.1).
165|   Prevent: G3's rule (faster in one phase, slower in none, no request slower,
166|   `time_candidates.py:187-194`) already encodes "nothing is free" across
167|   decode/prompt/request — if the swarm must run it and cite `g3-vllm.json`.
168|2. **Piece arithmetic.** Cause: both tools hand out medians that invite
169|   subtraction — `timing_us_per_layer` per-size medians
170|   (`check_candidate.py:367-374`) and the printed
171|   `(med-base ms, %)` summary (`repeat_fixes.py:335-359`, seen live in the
172|   probe). Neither tool computes a piece's end-to-end effect. Prevent: an
173|   in-round `time_candidates.py vllm` run measures the whole request directly,
174|   making the arithmetic unnecessary; the design must require citing it.
175|3. **Inconsistent reasoning.** Cause: two different "compiled" baselines exist —
176|   per-part `mx.compile(ref)` in piece timing (`check_candidate.py:360`) vs
177|   whole-MoE `compiled-<slot>` end to end (`time_candidates.py:119-122`) — so
178|   "what mx.compile gains" is ambiguous, inviting borrowed gains. Also
179|   `muse-all`/`compiled-all` exist only with >1 positional attempt
180|   (`time_candidates.py:125-127`); a single-slot invocation never measures a
181|   combination, leaving "Together (sum)" as the only available number.
182|   Prevent: require passing all submitted slots positionally in one call so
183|   `muse-all` is measured as a combination.
184|4. **Grader as search loop.** Cause/enabler: the tool allows unlimited runs and
185|   prints a rich per-size gradient every run; one-run-one-attempt is a skill
186|   rule the tool cannot see (no attempt registry, no run counting, `--out`
187|   arbitrary, exit 0 even on G1 failure). The tool cannot prevent this; only
188|   the skill plus post-hoc log audit can. Note the queue makes each extra run
189|   cost everyone time (§1.4).
190|5. **Failing design family.** The tool provides the per-size signal
191|   (`timing[size].vs_compiled`, e.g. slower at rows 1 in both my grade files)
192|   but no cross-attempt memory: each run is stateless JSON. Cause data (e.g.
193|   too few threadgroups) is not measurable by any tool here. Prevention is
194|   skill-level (aggregate verdicts across attempts); proposal: none in-tool
195|   beyond citing the existing per-size verdicts.
196|
197|## 3. In-round end-to-end check: reuse, needs, duration, gaming
198|
199|- **Reuse as-is:** `time_candidates.py vllm <out> SLOT=FOLDER...` with defaults
200|  (4 G3 settings, 5 repeats, 256 tokens) plus the `g3()` verdict in
201|  `g3-vllm.json` — the rule already matches ADR 0011. `engine_table.py` renders
202|  it for judges. `gpu_lock.hold()` is already inside.
203|- **Needs (gaps in the tool):** (a) pin the invocation — `--repeats`,
204|  `--settings`, `--tokens` are free flags; (b) require all submitted slots
205|  positionally so `muse-all` exists; (c) forbid/ignore `--variant` names
206|  starting with `muse-` (crashes G3) and note non-`muse-` names escape judgment;
207|  (d) token exactness is recorded but never gated — a wrong-tokens variant can
208|  still pass G3; the check must require `exact` in the log; (e) plain engine
209|  must not count as the check (zero prompt, no verdict).
210|- **Duration:** single-slot vLLM G3 ≈ 13–14 min run wall at 5 repeats
211|  (extrapolated, `vllm-duration-estimate.txt`); 3-slot ≈ 3×. Grader: ~13 s
212|  (routing) to ~5 min (experts) per run (§1.1). Plain probe: 10.5 s for the
213|  minimal shape (§1.3). All GPU work serialises on the lock.
214|- **Gaming catalogue:**
215|  - `--repeats 1`: min–max ranges collapse to points; non-overlap (spurious
216|    faster AND slower) becomes near-certain. Undetectable from the verdict
217|    alone — repeats are logged per record (`rep` field) so audit the log.
218|  - `--settings` subset (e.g. only `32x128`): shrinks the "every setting"
219|    burden; non-G3 settings also change KV bytes (§1.2), breaking
220|    comparability with Claude's G3.
221|  - `--tokens` down to 9: wall ≈ prompt + 8 steps; below 9 the tool crashes
222|    (§1.2). Changes the decode/prompt weight silently.
223|  - `--variant myname:...`: timed but never judged (§1.2) — free numbers to
224|    quote. `--variant muse-x:...`: crashes G3 (§1.2).
225|  - Single-slot calls: no `muse-all`; combination claims stay arithmetic (§2.3).
226|  - Plain engine: zero prompt time, no verdict file; quotable medians that look
227|    like end-to-end numbers (§1.3).
228|  - Quoting medians/ranges selectively from the jsonl instead of the verdict.
229|  - check_candidate: `--baseline` points at any folder (pick a slow one);
230|    `max_rows=32` makes prefill "same" without doing prefill work (§1.1);
231|    in-between row counts are untested by the grader (`check_sizes.py` is
232|    separate, §1.5); unlimited re-runs (§2.4).
