Read text file `design-lab/designer-a/design.md`.
1|# Designer-A design: the round measures its own submission
2|
3|Status, approach and evidence for the brief
4|`design-lab/brief.md`: make the Muse agent swarm pursue real efficiency.
5|
6|Prototypes and tests alongside: `prototypes/check_submission.py`,
7|`prototypes/skill-text.md`, `tests/test_*.py`, `results/*.txt`.
8|All result files below are under `design-lab/designer-a/results/`; all
9|repository paths are relative to the worktree at commit `1113c2d`.
10|
11|---
12|
13|## 1. Status: READY
14|
15|The design is complete and self-contained. It needs no protected-contract
16|change, no new Muse Code capability, no model or engine change, and no
17|`start.sh` change. Its one new tool delegates to the existing G3 code; its
18|skill edits are replacement wordings, prototyped verbatim in
19|`prototypes/skill-text.md`; its three mechanisms were replayed against
20|round-2 records and real result logs with 25/25 prototype checks passing
21|(`results/test_*.txt`).
22|
23|---
24|
25|## 2. Context and diagnosis
26|
27|### 2.1 Verified facts (all read at 1113c2d; explorer reports cross-checked)
28|
29|- The goal is phrased as passing gates: `.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:20`
30|  ("kernels that pass G1 and G2 and have `beats_compiled` true ... faster
31|  because they remove a cause you can name").
32|- In-round model runs are forbidden twice: `tracking.md:152` ("Load no model
33|  and start no other GPU work") and `SKILL.md:164` ("G3 and vLLM belong to
34|  surucuonur's team"). The brief's decided direction (§UNRESOLVED) explicitly
35|  replaces these two lines; this design does that replacement and nothing more.
36|- Ready to test *requires* an end-to-end number (`SKILL.md:147`: "the change
37|  you expect in G3's four workloads ... with how you worked it out") while the
38|  ban above forbids measuring it — so the number can only be piece arithmetic.
39|- The verifier checks exploration only (`verifier.md:5-25`; only
40|  `ineff-*.md`, only `confirmed`/`refuted` on cost/saving inputs). Nothing
41|  checks hypothesis Decisions, Ready-to-test arithmetic, or the summary. The
42|  lead writes all three unchecked (`SKILL.md:160-161`).
43|- The number rule blesses arithmetic: `tracking.md:153` accepts "arithmetic
44|  shown in full" as a source with no level or method constraint.
45|- The harden loop has a continue rule and no switch rule (`SKILL.md:135-138`:
46|  "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove").
47|- The builder self-checks predictions with no enforcement (`builder.md:24`
48|  prediction with arithmetic, `builder.md:30` 20%-miss analysis, no checker).
49|- One-run-one-attempt is explicit and held: `builder.md:13`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`
50|  (v4); round 2 ran 13 grader runs for 13 attempts (explorer-rounds B4-g).
51|  This is the demonstrated proof that explicit, checkable rules hold on this
52|  swarm — the design's central precedent.
53|- The tools already contain the needed measurement: `time_candidates.py`
54|  builds base/compiled-*/muse-*/compiled-all/muse-all variants
55|  (`time_candidates.py:111-132`), judges each muse-* vs base and its
56|  compiled-* bar with the ADR 0011 rule (`:163-197`), defaults to 5 repeats
57|  and the 4 G3 workloads (`:51-53`), and takes the GPU lock (`:224`).
58|- Three tool gaps verified by reading: (a) token `exact` is logged but never
59|  gated — `g3()` reads only `kind=="run"` records (`:168-171`); (b) the
60|  free flags (`--repeats/--settings/--tokens/--variant`) can shrink or skew
61|  the check, and `--variant muse-x` without a `compiled-x` bar crashes G3
62|  (`:177-183`, `min()` on empty); (c) the plain engine always reports
63|  `prompt_ms = 0.0` (`breakdown.py:468-484` records steps only for the decode
64|  loop; `repeat_fixes.py:277-282`) and never writes a G3 verdict
65|  (`time_candidates.py:260-261`).
66|- Round-2 records confirm every behaviour instance (explorer-rounds B1-B5):
67|  prefill priced at zero (`hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`), the
68|  −0.84/−0.85/−0.84 together-sum (`implementation/README.md:36`) 23 lines
69|  below "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose" (`:13`), borrowed compile
70|  offsets (`:29`), six timed fused experts attempts losing at 1 row
71|  (`README.md:9`), the unfused alternative named only in the summary
72|  (`round-2/summary.md:9`).
73|- Cost and duration anchors: round 2 took 63.4 min on Muse Wonder (~$58);
74|  a single-slot 5-repeat vLLM G3 call is ~13–14 min run wall extrapolated
75|  from `results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/muse-vllm.jsonl`
76|  (explorer-tools §1.2; mean 13.6 s/run over 60 runs for 3 variants).
77|
78|### 2.2 Cause and certainty
79|
80|The brief's root-cause hypothesis is confirmed with high certainty: inside a
81|round the swarm's only speed feedback is the grader's per-slot piece timing,
82|the real objective (G3 over whole requests) arrives only post-round, and the
83|swarm's end-to-end claims pass through three unchecked documents (Decision →
84|Ready to test → summary). Three structural facts jointly force behaviours
85|1–3, not merely allow them: the goal is defined in grader verdicts (so the
86|unmeasured is definitionally irrelevant), the Ready-to-test number is
87|demanded but unmeasurable in-round (so it must be arithmetic), and no checker
88|exists downstream (so arithmetic errors and borrowed gains survive).
89|Behaviour 5 is forced the same way by a loop whose only exit is "no further
90|change worth making", judged by the agent running the loop. Behaviour 4 is
91|already fixed and is the design's positive control: the fix worked by making
92|the rule explicit and countable.
93|
94|---
95|
96|## 3. Recommended design: one gate, one checker pass, one counter
97|
98|The design adds exactly three mechanisms, each reusing an established
99|pattern. Together they close the feedback loop: the swarm sees the real
100|objective before it claims anything, an independent checker replays every
101|claim from cited files, and a counter forces design diversity.
102|
103|### 3.1 The submission check (the gate; fixes behaviours 1–3 at the root)
104|
105|**New tool `bench/grader/check_submission.py`** (prototype:
106|`prototypes/check_submission.py`), a ~150-line wrapper that:
107|
108|- takes `<out> SLOT=FOLDER...` — every candidate slot positionally in ONE
109|  call, so per-slot variants AND `muse-all`/`compiled-all` are measured as a
110|  combination (`time_candidates.py:125-127`);
111|- delegates to `time_candidates.main()` with pinned arguments: engine `vllm`,
112|  the 4 G3 workloads, 5 repeats, 256 tokens (asserting equality with
113|  `G3_SETTINGS`/`G3_REPEATS` first, so upstream drift fails loudly);
114|- then audits `<out>/muse-vllm.jsonl` + `g3-vllm.json`: exact expected
115|  variant set, engine vllm, reps 0–4 present per (variant, rows, prompt), and
116|  `exact is True` for every judged variant at rows 1 and 32 (the brief's G2
117|  end-to-end check, currently ungated);
118|- writes `<out>/submission-verdict.json` (params echoed, per-variant pass,
119|  bars, phases, exact flags, problems list) and exits 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL,
120|  2 when the log is uncitable. "Passes" = exit 0 — a countable rule in the
121|  behaviour-4 mould.
122|
123|The free flags do not exist on the wrapper, which removes the whole
124|`--repeats 1 / --settings subset / --tokens 9 / --variant` gaming catalogue
125|(explorer-tools §3) by construction rather than by prose. The G3 crash case
126|(`muse-x` without a bar) is unreachable: no `--variant` is accepted.
127|
128|**Skill integration** (wordings in `prototypes/skill-text.md` §§1–4, 8):
129|
130|- Goal (`SKILL.md:20`) rewritten: `beats_compiled` is named as the builders'
131|  cheap proxy filter; the submission check is the verdict.
132|- Hypotheses close to a new status **`candidate`** on grader+boundary
133|  (`tracking.md:108` statuses extended); nothing reaches **`ready`** until
134|  the submission check passes it. This satisfies acceptance criterion 2
135|  literally while costing ONE GPU run however many hypotheses closed.
136|- At Finish, the lead runs the check itself (the single exception to "you
137|  don't grade", which exists to avoid a grading bottleneck per ADR 0007 —
138|  inapplicable to one finish-time run when no builder is grading), then sets
139|  `ready`/`dropped` per variant verdict in a checkpoint. At most two checks
140|  per round (one scheduled + one re-check after a fix); both logged, the
141|  last cited. Zero candidates → no check; Ready to test names
142|  baselines/references and makes no end-to-end claim.
143|- Ready to test (`SKILL.md:147`) becomes a measured section: verdict file,
144|  per-variant phases vs both bars, exact flags, the piece-basis prediction
145|  labelled PREDICTION next to the measured value, and the UNVERIFIED list.
146|  If `muse-all` fails or a single slot has no combination, no together-number
147|  is written — ever.
148|- `SKILL.md:164` and `tracking.md:152` are replaced per the decided
149|  direction: two named GPU jobs (grader for builders, submission check for
150|  the lead), both through the lock (`gpu_lock.py:18-32`), nothing else; the
151|  plain engine's 0.0 prompt time is explicitly unusable for claims.
152|
153|**Data flow:** candidate attempt folders (committed at collect) →
154|`check_submission.py` → `time_candidates vllm` (GPU, queued) →
155|`muse-vllm.jsonl` + `g3-vllm.json` → audit → `submission-verdict.json` →
156|cited by Ready to test / summary / Decisions → replayed by the verifier →
157|compared against Claude's post-round G3.
158|
159|### 3.2 The claims pass (the checker; makes self-reports checked)
160|
161|**`verifier.md` gains a second task** (wording in `skill-text.md` §12): at
162|Finish, after the submission check, the lead starts the verifier again to
163|check every speed claim in Decisions, Ready to test, and the summary:
164|
165|1. level-and-cite (grader file for piece claims, `submission-verdict.json`
166|   with empty `problems` and pinned params for end-to-end, else labelled
167|   PREDICTION with measured beside);
168|2. own-effect-only (no borrowed compile offsets, no cross-slot borrowing);
169|3. combinations measured (`muse-all` cited, or explicitly not measured/not
170|   passed — never summed);
171|4. unverified listed (no free/neutral/invisible/zero assumption);
172|5. counters replayed from cited grader verdicts (§3.3);
173|6. inputs match (`git diff --exit-code` on the checked folders is empty).
174|
175|Verdicts go under `## From other agents` as today; Finish commits only after
176|the pass returns. No GPU: every check replays cited files.
177|
178|**The number rule (`tracking.md:153`) is extended** (`skill-text.md` §9) with
179|exactly these four lines (R1 cite-at-level-or-PREDICTION-beside-measured,
180|R2 own-effect + measured-combinations, R3 UNVERIFIED-never-free), so the
181|rule every agent reads already contains the discipline and the verifier
182|enforces it. Small conforming edits: `tracking.md:103` (predicted saving
183|labelled a prediction), `SKILL.md:112-114` (ranking by prediction),
184|`builder.md:24` (prediction labelled, own effect), `boundary.md` item 4
185|(can't-see list becomes the UNVERIFIED list with what would verify each),
186|brief `:213`/`:215` (submission check + G3 decide; finalists go to both).
187|
188|### 3.3 The failure-point counter (fixes behaviour 5)
189|
190|**Harden gains a counter** (`skill-text.md` §2, `tracking.md:111`):
191|
192|- Each graded attempt records its **failure point**: sizes `slower` than
193|  compiled (or G2-fail sizes) + the named cause.
194|- After **3 consecutive** attempts fail at the same failure point, the next
195|  builder takes a **different approach** (a different design family, named
196|  in the log) **or the lead logs why not** (criterion 5's escape clause,
197|  kept deliberate).
198|- N=3 is evidence-grounded: round-2 experts attempts 1–3 already spanned
199|  per-pair, block-split and 4-block packings at the same 1-row point
200|  (`hyp-1-experts-exact.md:178-241`); the rule would have forced the
201|  "stop fusing" decision (`round-2/summary.md:9`) four attempts earlier.
202|- Anti-gaming: an unlaunched (G1-fail) attempt pauses without resetting; a
203|  new cause restarts the count only with a cited measurement refuting the
204|  old one (round-2 attempt-3's lever refutation, `:254-258`, is the model —
205|  genuine re-diagnosis still counts, renaming does not).
206|
207|### 3.4 Integration points and interfaces
208|
209|- **Tool contract:** `check_submission.py OUT SLOT=FOLDER... [--dry-run]`;
210|  reads attempt folders (spec.json + block-*.metal, unchanged format);
211|  writes `<out>/` under the round folder (`<round>/submission/`, a new
212|  dir inside the round folder so the hooks accept it); exit codes 0/1/2.
213|  Protected grader JSON keys untouched.
214|- **Skill contract:** new status `candidate`; `ready` redefined; lead runs
215|  one command; verifier runs twice. No new role card, no capacity change
216|  (12 agents suffice; the check needs none), no `start.sh` change.
217|- **Docs:** skill v8 (`CHANGELOG.md` entry in `skill-text.md` §15),
218|  glossary terms (Submission check, Failure point), `muse-swarm.md`
219|  honesty bullets, and a new ADR 0013 (see §8). ADRs 0010/0011 stay
220|  verbatim; 0013 sets the future convention that "Not covered" sections
221|  say "unverified: assume nothing".
222|
223|---
224|
225|## 4. Why it solves the underlying problem; acceptance criteria
226|
227|The underlying problem is the gap between the proxy the swarm sees and the
228|objective it is judged on, plus unchecked self-reporting. The design moves
229|the objective into the round (the gate measures exactly what G3 measures,
230|with the same code and rule, plus the token gate) and puts a checker between

279|  stays required at harden so a weak baseline can't promote; (b)
280|  `max_rows=32` prefill-"same" — the submission times the real prefill, and
281|  a hand-off genuinely runs the compiled code there (ADR 0011:33-35), so
282|  "same" is true, not a dodge; (c) post-check attempt edits — verifier step
283|  6 (`git diff --exit-code` on checked paths); attempts are also committed
284|  at collect and only builders write them; (d) selective median quoting —
285|  R1 allows only the verdict file; (e) direct `time_candidates` with gamed
286|  flags — only `submission-verdict.json` counts, and its `params` block
287|  (vllm/5/4×256) plus empty `problems` are verifier-checked; (f) lock
288|  bypass via `breakdown.py`/`repeat_fixes.py` direct use (they never call
289|  `hold()`) — forbidden by the rewritten GPU rule; detection stays absent
290|  (accepted: simple-over-airtight, and Claude's G3 is independent);
291|  re-check-until-noise-passes — capped at 2 checks/round, 5-repeat ranges
292|  (1/252 per check, ADR 0011:40), post-round G3 backstop; (h) counter
293|  reset by cause-renaming — restart requires a cited refuting measurement.
294|- **Noise:** the documented 1-request whole-request spread (6–41%,
295|  ADR 0011:52) mostly yields `same`, which passes "never slower" without
296|  showing gain — unchanged semantics, now visible in-round instead of
297|  surprising post-round.
298|- **GPU queue and duration:** one call per round (two at most), at Finish
299|  when builders are idle — zero contention with grader runs by scheduling.
300|  Cost at 13.6 s/run mean: 1 slot ≈ 60 runs ≈ 14 min; 2 slots ≈ 140 runs ≈
301|  32 min; 3 slots ≈ 180 runs ≈ 41 min (prediction from the engine-comparison
302|  log, same basis as explorer-tools §1.2). Round 3 ≈ 1.5–2.5 h total.
303|- **Memory:** a vLLM run at Finish contends with less (no concurrent
304|  builders) than a mid-round one; `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` default
305|  and Docker-quit guidance (`breakdown.py:54`) unchanged. 90-minute stop
306|  rule bounds a pathological run; a stop counts as FAIL and is recorded.
307|- **Integrity of the verdict:** the wrapper asserts constant-equality with
308|  `time_candidates` before delegating (drift fails loudly); the audit
309|  replays coverage from the log rather than trusting stdout; `problems`
310|  are written into the citable file, not just printed (prototype line
311|  `verdict["problems"]`, tested in `results/test_check_submission.txt`).
312|- **Security:** no credentials read (skill rule kept), no network, no new
313|  permissions; the wrapper runs the same local commands the swarm already
314|  runs.
315|- **Failure modes:** GPU lock held by a stale process — same as today
316|  (OS releases on process end, `gpu_lock.py:7`); wrapper crash mid-run —
317|  partial log fails the audit (missing reps → exit 2, uncitable, re-run);
318|  `attempts` overlapping parts — `time_candidates` already errors
319|  (`:221-223`); single-slot call — no `muse-all`, combination section
320|  says so.
321|
322|## 7. Alternatives considered
323|
324|1. **Skill-only fix: mandate the exact `time_candidates` command line, no
325|   wrapper.** Smallest diff (zero code). Rejected: every free flag stays a
326|   live game surface for an unattended contributor-model run; the token gate
327|   stays unenforced; the G3 crash case stays reachable. The wrapper's ~150
328|   lines convert five prose prohibitions into one inexistent-flagset plus an
329|   audit — cheaper to verify than to hope. (Prediction: prose-only pinning
330|   would be the next behaviour-4-style violation report.)
331|2. **Per-hypothesis end-to-end gates at close (one vLLM run per ready).**
332|   Matches criterion 2 without a new status. Rejected: 2–3× the GPU cost
333|   (base + compiled re-timed per call), mid-round queue contention with
334|   builders' grader runs, and — decisively — no measured combination
335|   without an extra run. The single submission call judges every slot AND
336|   the combination at once; the `candidate` status is a smaller price.
337|3. **Cheaper in-round proxy instead of full G3: fewer repeats/tokens or the
338|   plain engine.** Rejected on evidence: 3 repeats false-flagged an
339|   unchanged phase (ADR 0011:40); `--tokens` below 9 crashes and lower
340|   values reweight decode-vs-prompt silently; plain `prompt_ms` is always
341|   0.0, i.e. precisely behaviour 1 in tool form. A cheaper gate re-opens
342|   the proxy gap the brief pays to close.
343|4. **New checker role instead of extending the verifier.** Rejected:
344|   existing-system-first — the verifier pattern (independent agent, cited
345|   files, verdict sections, `## From other agents`) already exists and is
346|   trusted by judges; a second card duplicates it. The verifier's singleton
347|   naming is no obstacle (the lead restarts it with a new task prompt).
348|5. **Automatic counter enforcement in tooling (attempt registry, run
349|   counting).** Rejected: the tool cannot see design families or causes;
350|   behaviour 4's lesson is that the skill layer plus committed history is
351|   the enforcement point. The counter lives in the hypothesis entry where
352|   the causes live, replayed by the verifier.
353|6. **Forbidding piece-basis predictions entirely.** Rejected: predictions
354|   are the swarm's legitimate working language (builders must predict to
355|   choose directions; `builder.md:24` stays). The fix is labelling +
356|   beside-measured + own-effect, not silence.
357|
358|---
359|
360|## 8. Implementation handoff
361|
362|Dependency order (all by Claude on main before round 3; ~2–3 h total):
363|
364|1. **Tool** (30–45 min): copy `prototypes/check_submission.py` to
365|   `bench/grader/check_submission.py`; review the delegate + audit paths;
366|   run `tests/test_check_submission.py` (16 checks, no GPU) from the repo
367|   root; run `--dry-run`.
368|2. **Skill v8** (45–60 min): paste `prototypes/skill-text.md` §§1–13 into
369|   SKILL.md/tracking.md/builder.md/verifier.md/boundary.md; fix the two
370|   stale version stamps the explorers found (`SKILL.md:80` says skill
371|   version 6 while `:10` says 7; `tracking.md` version-line example);
372|   add the CHANGELOG v8 entry (§15).
373|3. **Brief + docs** (20–30 min): brief `:213`/`:215` (§14); glossary terms;
374|   `muse-swarm.md` honesty bullets; new **ADR 0013** (the fix; also records
375|   the one-run-one-attempt rule, currently missing from every ADR per
376|   explorer-findings §4, and the "unverified, never free" phrasing
377|   convention for future "Not covered" sections).
378|4. **Pre-round validation, no paid run** (15–20 min + one optional GPU run):
379|   - replay tests `test_failure_counter.py` (5/5) and `test_claim_rules.py`
380|     (4/4) — done, in `results/`;
381|   - hand-check: apply the verifier's 6 steps to round-2's Ready to test by
382|     reading (expect: claims 1–2 wrong per R1/R2, together-number wrong per
383|     R2/R3 — the test encodes the same);
384|   - RECOMMENDED one GPU run through the queue: the implemented wrapper on
385|     round-2's finalists (`routing/attempt-4`, `combine/attempt-1`) as a
386|     single call. Falsifiable expectations: the audit passes (exit 0/1, not
387|     2); `muse-routing` FAILs (prompt 7–10% slower is documented,
388|     `muse-round-2.md:134-141`); the run completes in ~30–35 min. If it
389|     does not FAIL routing, investigate before round 3 (the gate must catch
390|     a known-bad submission).
391|5. **Round-3 success read-out:** every `ready` cites `submission-verdict.json`
392|   with empty problems; Ready to test shows predictions beside measurements;
393|   UNVERIFIED lists exist; any 3-in-a-row shows a new family or a reason;
394|   Claude's G3 agrees with the submission verdicts within repeat noise
395|   (criterion 6). Failure of 6 with 1–5 held means the gate itself is miscalibrated —
396|   that becomes round 4's starting point, not a swarm failure.
397|
398|Regression tests: the three prototype test files move with the implementation
399|(the wrapper test becomes the tool's test; the replay tests document the
400|rules' intent). Monitoring: none new — the round's own documents plus
401|Claude's findings carry the signal, as today. Rollback: skill v7 + ignore
402|the new tool (one commit revert); rounds run v7 semantics unchanged since no
403|tracked tool was modified.
404|
405|---
406|
407|## 9. Unverified assumptions, risks, decisions for the user
408|
409|- **Assumed (brief §UNRESOLVED, kept):** explicit checkable rules hold on the
410|  contributor model (evidence: behaviour-4 fix held in round 2); the fix
411|  ships before 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC; Claude's G3 stays authoritative.
412|  Verified instead of assumed: every repository citation above was read at
413|  1113c2d; every performance figure traces to `results/` logs or the
414|  prototype results.
415|- **Prediction, not measurement:** submission-check durations (~14/32/41 min
416|  for 1/2/3 slots) extrapolate the engine-comparison mean; round-3's
417|  attempts could shift it (a very slow prefill lengthens runs, as the
418|  grader's 5-minute experts run foreshadows). The 90-minute stop bounds it.
419|- **Risk: one bad slot fails the combination.** If `muse-all` FAILs while
420|  slots pass (interference, seen in both rounds), the design reports it
421|  rather than fixing it — per-slot `ready`s still stand, the together-claim
422|  is withheld. That is deliberate (honesty over completeness), but judges
423|  should expect withheld together-claims.
424|- **Risk: the re-check budget burns on noise.** Two full checks ≈ 80 min
425|  worst case. Mitigated by the cap and by scheduling at Finish; if round 3
426|  shows noise-flips between the two checks, round 4 should widen repeats
427|  rather than re-checks.
428|- **Risk: contributor-model compliance with the 6-step verifier pass.**
429|  The pass is file-replay only (no judgement about physics), which is the
430|  easiest class of instruction to follow; the behaviour-4 precedent supports
431|  it, but it is untested until round 3.
432|- **Decision for surucuonur (before implementing):** confirm the lead runs
433|  the submission check itself (this design) vs a new helper role doing it.
434|  I chose the lead: one finish-time run, no bottleneck, no new card. If you
435|  prefer the lead to stay GPU-free, the fallback is a 10-line role card
436|  (`runner.md`: run the wrapper command, report exit code + verdict file)
437|  with no other change.
438|- **Decision (before implementing):** confirm the 2-check cap and the N=3
439|  counter threshold. Both are judgement calls anchored in round-2 evidence
440|  (14-min single-slot cost; 3 packings at one failure point); N=2 would
441|  churn, N=4+ repeats round 2.
442|- **Out of scope, noted for later:** `check_sizes.py` in-round use (row
443|  counts between the six G2 sizes stay boundary-reasoned, not measured);
444|  lock-bypass detection; the `PROVENANCE.md:42` vs ADRs sign-in
445|  contradiction (explorer-findings §5.6, load-bearing for isolation claims,
446|  untouched by this design).

Read text file `design-lab/designer-b/design.md`.
1|# Designer-B design: typed claims, an owned request check, and a checker
2|
3|*Perspective: contract-and-data-first. Worktree commit 1113c2d. No tracked
4|file changed; prototypes, fixtures and results live in
5|`design-lab/designer-b/prototypes/` and `design-lab/designer-b/test-results/`.*
6|
7|## 1. Status: READY
8|
9|The design is complete and implementable as skill v8 plus one new pinned tool
10|(`bench/grader/check_submit.py`) before round 3. It breaks no protected
11|contract, needs no Muse Code capability beyond what the brief documents, and
12|was prototyped and tested CPU-only (5/5 wrapper tests, claim-contract
13|fail/pass pair, ledger replay all green; no GPU run was needed — see §8).
14|
15|## 2. Context and diagnosis: verified facts, examples, cause, certainty
16|
17|### 2.1 The four data contracts that exist today
18|
19|I read the skill, the brief, both measurement tools and the round records
20|first-hand. Four contracts govern what the swarm can say about speed:
21|
22|1. **The piece contract (tool-owned, sound).** `bench/grader/check_candidate.py`
23|   computes per-size paired verdicts (30 repeats, 22 wins, one-sided sign test
24|   p<0.01 — `:52-57`, `:238-244`), per-phase verdicts and `beats_compiled`
25|   under the ADR 0011 rule (faster in one phase, slower in neither — `:247-263`).
26|   The verdict JSON keys (`g1`, `g2`, `beats_compiled`, `timing_us_per_layer`,
27|   `phases_vs_compiled`) are protected and stay.
28|2. **The request contract (tool-owned, sound but unreachable in-round).**
29|   `bench/grader/time_candidates.py` `g3()` judges each `muse-*` variant
30|   against `base` and its `compiled-*` bar over 4 workloads × 3 measures
31|   (`:168-197`, measures `:54`), with non-overlapping min–max ranges as the
32|   faster/slower test (`:163-166`). The swarm is forbidden to run it:
33|   `tracking.md:152` ("Load no model and start no other GPU work") and
34|   `SKILL.md:164` ("G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team").
35|3. **The claim contract (untyped prose — the hole).** `tracking.md:153`
36|   ("Every number has a source ... or arithmetic shown in full") accepts shown
37|   arithmetic as a source. There is no distinction between a measured number,
38|   a prediction, and an assumption, and no rule tying a claim's level (piece
39|   vs whole request) to the file that may source it.
40|4. **The verification contract (half-built).** The verifier checks only
41|   exploration inefficiency entries (`verifier.md:5`, `:11`), by reopening
42|   cited files and redoing arithmetic (`:12-15`). Nothing checks
43|   implementation-phase numbers: the lead writes them unchecked (`SKILL.md:160-161`),
44|   and *Ready to test* (`SKILL.md:147`) requires an expected G3 change "with
45|   how you worked it out" — free-form, citable to arithmetic.
46|
47|### 2.2 The five behaviours as contract failures (all verified first-hand)
48|
49|- **B1, unmeasured costs priced at zero.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-152`:
50|  "Prefill speed is not timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart
51|  from time to first token", citing ADR 0010's "Not covered" line. I found a
52|  second instance in the same family: `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-1/notes.md:30-31`
53|  ("per-pair reads at/above 60 rows are correctness-only cost (prefill is
54|  untimed)"). *Contract cause:* with no UNVERIFIED kind, the boundary's
55|  can't-see list (`boundary.md:13`) is a deferral list, and the only available
56|  move for an unmeasured cost is to narrate it as free. ADR 0011 closed the
57|  prefill instance (`:21-32`) but kept the shape: its own "Not covered" (`:51`,
58|  other chunk/row counts) is equally citable as permission.
59|- **B2, request gains from piece arithmetic.** Round-2 *Ready to test*
60|  (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:29-38`) computes
61|  "(compiled − candidate) µs/layer × 20 layers" plus borrowed offsets and
62|  publishes "Together (sum) −0.84/−0.85/−0.84 ms" (`:36`); the summary repeats
63|  it (`muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`). *Contract cause:* the skill demands
64|  a request-level number (`SKILL.md:147`) while forbidding the only
65|  measurement that produces one (`SKILL.md:164`) — arithmetic is the only
66|  compliant output, and `tracking.md:153` blesses it.
67|- **B3, inconsistent reasoning.** Same README `:13` ("per-slot wins are not
68|  assumed to compose") vs `:36` (the sum); combine's −0.35 ms is −0.07..−0.09
69|  own effect plus −0.26..−0.29 borrowed from `mx.compile`'s end-to-end gain
70|  (`:29`, `:34`). *Contract cause:* no rule says a combination must be
71|  measured as a combination, or that a prediction may count only the
72|  candidate's own effect. The tool side invites it too: per-part `mx.compile`
73|  in piece timing (`check_candidate.py:360`) vs whole-MoE `compiled-<slot>`
74|  end to end (`time_candidates.py:119-122`) are two different "compiled" bars
75|  with one name.
76|- **B4, grader as search loop (fixed, and the fix is the template).**
77|  Round-1 experts: 28 executed bash grader invocations for 4 counted attempts
78|  (18/3/6/1 — I accept the lead's settled count of 28 over the brief's 29).
79|  Skill v4's explicit rule (`builder.md:13`, "One grader run is one attempt")
80|  held in round 2 (13 for 13). *Lesson, verified:* explicit, checkable,
81|  countable rules hold on this swarm; norms don't. The design below copies
82|  that shape four times (pinned command, one file per claim, countable ledger,
83|  stamped check).
84|- **B5, one family pasted to the wall.** Round-2 experts attempts 1–5,7 all
85|  keep the per-pair fused structure ("Stay in attempt-1's fused single
86|  kernel", `round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-4/notes.md:16`) and all lose at
87|  1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs/layer, README `:9`); the unfused alternative is
88|  named only in the summary (`summary.md:9`, "so stop fusing") — after the
89|  attempts are spent. *Contract cause:* the harden loop (`SKILL.md:135-138`)
90|  has a continue rule ("Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can
91|  name and remove") and no data structure for repeated failure: builder
92|  sections end in "Next: one change", so the loop can terminate a change but
93|  never a family.
94|
95|### 2.3 Root cause and certainty
96|
97|**Root cause (high certainty — mechanism verified at both ends):** the swarm's
98|in-round feedback is untyped. Piece verdicts, request verdicts, predictions and
99|assumptions all travel as undifferentiated prose under one citation rule that
100|accepts arithmetic, while the only request-level measurement is forbidden
101|in-round and arrives post-round. Behaviours 1–3 are then not mistakes but the
102|only compliant outputs; behaviour 5 follows because repeated failure has no
103|record with a consequence attached. The miss-analysis ritual (builder.md:30)
104|proves the records *can* carry correction — every attempt carries predicted vs
105|measured — but no slot forces *Ready to test* to answer it.
106|
107|Two load-bearing tool facts sharpen the fix (both verified by reading, one by
108|my own test run): `g3()` ignores token exactness (`time_candidates.py:168-197`
109|reads only `kind=="run"` records), so a wrong-tokens variant can pass G3; and
110|the plain engine's `prompt_ms` is always exactly 0.0 with no verdict file
111|(`breakdown.py:468-484` records steps only for the decode loop;
112|`time_candidates.py:260-261`; lead's settled note 5). Any in-round check must
113|therefore be vLLM-only and must gate exactness itself.
114|
115|## 3. Recommended design
116|
117|One approach with four parts: **type every speed claim; pin the request
118|measurement into one owned command; check every claim before it closes; count
119|repeated failure per family.** Semantics first (what a number *is*), then
120|ownership (who computes, who cites, who verifies), then the tools that make
121|each step mechanical for an unattended contributor model
122|(ADR 0012:32: "explicit and checkable").
123|
124|### 3.1 The claim contract (the semantic core)
125|
126|Every speed number in a hypothesis entry, the implementation README, or the
127|summary is exactly one of (prototype text:
128|`prototypes/claim-schema.md`):
129|
130|- **measured / piece** — from a `grade.json` the builder wrote with the
131|  grader's `--out`: per-size times, `vs_compiled`, phase verdicts,
132|  `beats_compiled`/`beats_baseline`. Cites file + key; value matches verbatim.
133|- **measured / request** — from a `submit.json` the submission check wrote: a
134|  `g3` verdict, or a median with its [min–max] over the 5 repeats. Cites
135|  `submit.json` + key and the jsonl cell (variant, setting).
136|- **predicted** — everything else numeric: shows its formula, every input is
137|  the candidate's own measured number, and it stands next to its measured
138|  value with the miss (or "unvalidated: first of its kind").
139|
140|Two structural rules do most of the work. **Level integrity:** a grader file
141|never sources a request-level claim — piece timing cannot, by type, evidence
142|a whole-request sentence. **Nothing unmeasured is free:** anything not
143|measured goes under **Unverified** (at least the boundary's can't-see items,
144|prefill chunks of other sizes, decode row counts other than 1/8/32, 1-request
145|whole-request noise); the words *free/neutral/invisible* about an unmeasured
146|cost are a defect. Predictions count only the candidate's own measured
147|effect: no borrowed `mx.compile` offsets, no cross-slot sums — a sum across
148|slots is a prediction until a `muse-all` row measures it, and then it is
149|measured, not predicted.
150|
151|### 3.2 The submission check (measurement ownership)
152|
153|New tool `bench/grader/check_submit.py` (prototype:
154|`prototypes/check_submit.py`): a pinned, vLLM-only wrapper with the smallest
155|possible surface — `check_submit.py <out> SLOT=FOLDER...` and no other flags.
156|It calls `time_candidates.main` with the G3 argv (repeats 5, the 4 workloads,
157|256 tokens — the constants stay in `time_candidates.py`, which is untouched),
158|then composes **one** verdict file, `submit.json`:
159|
160|```json
161|{"check": "submit", "attempts": {"routing": "..."},
162| "invocation": {"engine": "vllm", "settings": "1x128,...", "repeats": 5, "tokens": 256, ...},
163| "exact": {"muse-routing": {"1": true, "32": true}}, "exact_pass": true,
164| "g3": {"muse-routing": "...same verdict dict as g3-vllm.json..."},
165| "target": "muse-all | muse-<slot>", "target_pass": true,
166| "medians": {"muse-routing": {"1x128": {"decode": {"median": 0.0, "min": 0.0, "max": 0.0, "n": 5}}}},
167| "pass": true, "unverified": ["prefill chunks of other sizes", "..."]}
168|```
169|
170|The wrapper adds what `g3()` lacks: the **token-exact gate** (every judged
171|variant `exact` at rows 1 *and* 32 — base exact by definition), a **per-cell
172|repeat audit** (exactly 5 runs per variant × setting, so a non-G3 run cannot
173|source a claim), the **invocation record**, and the **static Unverified list**.
174|The gate target is `muse-all` when more than one slot is submitted, else the
175|single `muse-<slot>`; a two-slot run whose verdict lacks `muse-all` fails
176|cleanly ("the combination was not measured as a combination"). Overall
177|`pass` = `exact_pass` and target `g3` true — the ADR 0011 rule, against base
178|and compiled, over whole requests. It takes the GPU lock through the existing
179|path. Out dir is `<round>/evals/<name>/`, committed with the round.
180|
181|### 3.3 The checker (verification ownership)
182|
183|New role card `checker.md` (prototype: `prototypes/checker.md`), mirroring
184|`boundary.md`'s two-task shape, CPU-only (never runs GPU work):
185|
186|- **Check a hypothesis** (before it closes `ready`): every measured row
187|  resolves verbatim to its `grade.json`/`submit.json` key; every prediction
188|  shows formula + own inputs + miss; Unverified covers the boundary items and
189|  the mandatory four; the ledger recomputes from the cited verdicts. Stamps
190|  `check: pass/fail` with file+line defects into the entry's new **Checks**
191|  section. `ready` needs the pass.
192|- **Check the submission** (once, over *Ready to test* + summary): the
193|  expected G3 change is a measured/request table from the submission
194|  `submit.json`; any cross-slot measured number cites `muse-all`; Unverified
195|  travels. The round finishes only on this pass.
196|
197|Ownership summary: tools compute verdicts; builders cite piece verdicts;
198|the lead cites request verdicts and owns claim tables and the ledger; the
199|checker verifies all three and changes no number it checks; **only Claude's
200|post-round G3 names baselines** — the in-round check gates, never grants.
201|
202|### 3.4 The failure ledger (family-change data)
203|
204|Each hypothesis entry gains a lead-kept **failure ledger**: one row per graded
205|attempt (family, loss sizes/phases vs compiled from `grade.json`, named
206|cause). Families are the lead's compete directions (`SKILL.md:131`); the lead
207|assigns each row's family at collect — builders only propose — so the
208|granularity is auditable in one place and ungameable by renaming. Rule:
209|**after 3 graded, timed attempts of one family lose at the same size or
210|phase, the next attempt uses a different family, or the log records why not
211|with the evidence.** The K=3 value is stated in the skill (see §4.5 for the
212|calibration). Harden's "repeat while cause nameable" keeps running *unless*
213|the ledger asks for a family change.
214|
215|### 3.5 Data flow and integration points
216|
217|Per hypothesis: builder writes kernels + `notes.md` (family, prediction with
218|own inputs + last miss) → grades once with `--out attempt-N/grade.json` →
219|lead commits attempt + entry at collect, appends the ledger row → on a
220|`ready` candidate, a builder runs the submission check (explicitly *not* an
221|attempt, creates no attempt number) → `checker-<n>` stamps → `ready` or back
222|to hardening with request-level evidence. At finish: lead runs the submission
223|check over all submitted slots at once (so `muse-all` exists), drafts
224|*Ready to test* + summary as claim tables, `checker-submit` stamps, commit,
225|"Round N finished".
226|
227|Consequences with teeth: a hypothesis whose check fails goes back to
228|hardening or drops — nothing failing reaches *Ready to test* (criterion 2).
229|If `muse-all` fails while singles passed (the documented interaction loss),
230|the combination is not submitted; the lead re-checks a passing subset (each
231|run committed under a new eval folder; claims cite the latest) or submits
232|nothing. Re-running the check on unchanged kernels to hunt noise is forbidden.
233|
234|GPU/queue integration: checks = (#ready hypotheses) + 1 submission, each
235|~13–14 min single-slot (tool-explorer extrapolation from the current-format
236|log), serialised on the existing lock. Builders keep writing Metal (CPU work)
237|while a check holds the GPU; only GPU runs wait. No lock, hook, sandbox or
238|`start.sh` change: capacity 12 absorbs one checker, and the check reuses
239|`gpu_lock.hold`.
240|
241|The exact text changes are prototyped as P1–P15 in
242|`prototypes/skill-patch.md`: goal sentence (`SKILL.md:20`), swarm table
243|(`:24-30`), harden/ready (`:135-140`), *Ready to test* (`:147`), summary
244|(`:153`), the G3 line (`:164`), hypothesis entry sections
245|(`tracking.md:106-113`), GPU rule (`:152`), number rule (`:153`), builder
246|prediction/`--out`/family rules (`builder.md:13,24,28,30`), boundary
247|can't-see wording (`boundary.md:13`), brief hand-off model (`:213-215`), plus
248|new `checker.md` and `check_submit.py`. `verifier.md` is deliberately
249|untouched.
250|
251|## 4. Why it solves the underlying problem and meets each acceptance criterion
252|
253|The root cause is untyped feedback: the proxy and the objective travel in the
254|same prose with the same citation rule. The design fixes that structurally —
255|the type of each number dictates which file may source it, the objective's own
256|procedure runs in-round behind one pinned command, and a second pair of eyes
257|owns the mapping. No behaviour below is fixed by advice; each is fixed by a
258|type, a gate, or a count.
259|
260|- **Criterion 1 (every claim measured-and-cited or labelled-predicted with
261|  its miss).** The three claim kinds are exhaustive: a speed number with no
262|  kind is a checker defect by construction. Measured rows resolve verbatim to
263|  `grade.json`/`submit.json` keys; predictions stand next to their measured
264|  value with the miss. *Evidence it bites:* the validator prototype
265|  (`prototypes/check_claims.py`) run over round-2's *Ready to test* recast
266|  reports 8 defects — missing verdict file, level violation, combination
267|  without `muse-all`, borrowed input, 3 missing Unverified items — while the
268|  conforming fixture passes (`test-results/check_claims-tests.txt`).
269|- **Criterion 2 (ready / Ready-to-test only on an in-round ADR 0011
270|  improvement vs unchanged + compiled).** `ready` needs `submit.json` `pass`
271|  (exact + target `g3` vs both bars) *and* the checker stamp; the submission
272|  needs the same over all submitted slots at once. A failing hypothesis
273|  returns to hardening or drops; a failing combination is not submitted.
274|  This closes B1's general habit (the check prices prefill and whole requests
275|  directly) and B2 (no arithmetic path to *Ready to test* exists).
276|- **Criterion 3 (predictions count own effect; combinations measured as
277|  combinations).** Own-inputs rule + `muse-all` requirement, both checker
278|  enforced. Round-2's combine prediction (own −0.07 plus borrowed −0.28) and
279|  "Together (sum)" both fail the prototype validator today (R4/R5 in
280|  `test-results/check_claims-tests.txt`). The tool side cooperates: the

280|  `test-results/check_claims-tests.txt`). The tool side cooperates: the
281|  wrapper has no `--variant` flag, so nothing escapes judgment or crashes the
282|  bar lookup, and multi-slot runs always build `muse-all`/`compiled-all`
283|  (`time_candidates.py:125-127`).
284|- **Criterion 4 (unmeasured listed, never free).** The Unverified list is
285|  mandatory content with a mandatory minimum (boundary items + other chunk
286|  sizes + other row counts + 1-request noise), travelling from hypothesis
287|  entry to README to summary; *free/neutral/invisible* is defect language.
288|  ADR 0011's "Not covered" (`:51`) becomes the wrapper's static Unverified
289|  list — the same gap, phrased as "assume nothing" instead of citable
290|  permission.
291|- **Criterion 5 (N failures → change approach or log why not).** The ledger
292|  with stated K=3, lead-assigned families, mechanical loss signal (same run's
293|  `vs_compiled`). Calibration: replayed on round-2's parsed tracker, the rule
294|  triggers for experts after attempt-3 (six 1-row losses of one family —
295|  exactly where "stop fusing" belonged) and correctly stays silent for
296|  routing (losses scattered across sizes/families):
297|  `test-results/ledger_replay.txt`. K=2 would fire on noise at the twitchy
298|  1-row size (the findings note even within-run 1-row comparison "is close to
299|  the noise"); K=4 would have spent one more fused attempt for nothing.
300|- **Criterion 6 (in-round claims agree with Claude's G3 within repeat noise).**
301|  The in-round check *is* Claude's procedure (same tool, same argv, same 4
302|  workloads → same 1 GiB KV cache per `time_candidates.py:250`), plus an
303|  exact gate that only removes a divergence the brief's end-to-end G2 would
304|  catch anyway. Divergence is then bounded to noise + hardware drift, and the
305|  [min–max] medians make "within the noise" checkable as range overlap. This
306|  is the ultimate test and the design makes it a comparison of two ranges,
307|  not two stories.
308|
309|Goodhart accounting (brief §Failure modes): the pinned check cannot become a
310|*cheaper* proxy because it is the objective's procedure, not a new proxy —
311|gaming it means gaming G3 itself, which Claude re-runs independently. Each
312|known gaming move is closed by construction: flag-tuning (no flags; repeat
313|audit fails non-G3 runs — proven on the 3-repeat handoff log in
314|`test-results/check_submit-tests.txt` test 1), `--variant` escape/crash (no
315|such flag), selective median quotes (checker accepts verdict keys and
316|median+[min–max]+n only), plain-engine zeros (not a citable source),
317|`--baseline` shopping (both bars fixed), noise-hunting re-runs (forbidden;
318|every run committed, latest cited), lock bypass via `breakdown.py`
319|(claim-sourcing requires wrapper-produced files, so a bypass run distorts
320|only its own author's timings). Residual: overfitting to the 4 workloads —
321|named in Unverified, not solved (§9).
322|
323|## 5. What remains unchanged; migration/compatibility
324|
325|- **Unchanged tools:** `check_candidate.py` (same 6 sizes, same sign test,
326|  same verdict keys), `time_candidates.py` (the wrapper imports it; the G3
327|  rule lives in exactly one place), `slots.py` (attempt format, `max_rows`
328|  hand-off semantics), `gpu_lock.py`, `check_sizes.py`, `engine_table.py`
329|  (submission logs keep the `muse-vllm.jsonl` shape, so judges' tables still
330|  render), `start.sh` (no new flags; capacity 12 covers the checker).
331|- **Unchanged skill machinery:** explorer/verifier/boundary cards and the
332|  verifier's exploration loop (P14 — the checker that works keeps its narrow
333|  job), checkpoints and versioning, compete/collect/harden flow except the
334|  ledger row and the two gates, one-run-one-attempt, limitless attempts,
335|  lead-only commits, authorship separation (all swarm writes stay in
336|  `<round>/`, including `evals/` and `grade.json`), frozen rounds and tags,
337|  G2 bit-exactness and token checks, and Claude's exclusive authority to name
338|  baselines.
339|- **Unchanged data:** all committed verdicts, logs and round documents keep
340|  their meaning. Round-2-era claims are not restated (rounds are frozen); the
341|  starting-point step already compares "G3 effect against its prediction"
342|  (`SKILL.md:67`) and now also seeds each lineage's first residual.
343|- **Migration:** purely additive. One skill commit (v8: edited cards +
344|  `checker.md` + claim-schema section) and one tool commit
345|  (`check_submit.py`), both on main before round 3; `grade.json` appears in
346|  attempt folders from round 3 on (the checker's R2 expects it — old attempts
347|  without one simply predate the contract). The `check_candidate.py`
348|  docstring line "It never writes into the attempt folder" (`:11-12`) stays
349|  true in intent (the grader doesn't litter inputs there); the builder's
350|  explicit `--out` is the documented mechanism, and the file travels with the
351|  attempt it verdicts. Docs: one ADR (skill v8; also records the one-run rule
352|  that today lives only in skill text — the traceability gap the findings
353|  report flags), plus `muse-swarm.md`/glossary touch-ups.
354|- **Compatibility risk:** negligible. The wrapper's only coupling to
355|  `time_candidates.py` is `main` + constants + `attempt_arg`; if those move,
356|  the wrapper fails loudly at import, never silently.
357|
358|## 6. Failure handling, data integrity, security, operational concerns
359|
360|- **Check fails (target `g3` false or exact false).** Hypothesis: back to
361|  hardening with the request-level evidence appended to the ledger, or drop.
362|  Submission (`muse-all` fails): the combination is not submitted; lead
363|  re-checks a passing subset or submits nothing. An empty submission is an
364|  honest round, not a failed one — the checker still stamps the summary (no
365|  measured request numbers claimed, Unverified present).
366|- **Check crashes / partial round.** `submit.json` is written only after the
367|  repeat audit passes, so a half run never sources a claim. Eval folders are
368|  committed per checkpoint like attempts; a resumed session carries on from
369|  the READMEs' last versions (`SKILL.md:52`) with ledger and evals intact.
370|- **Noise.** Faster/slower stay range-non-overlap in both tools; the [min–max]
371|  medians travel with every measured request number so Claude's comparison is
372|  range overlap. 1-request whole-request `same`-passes are listed as noise in
373|  Unverified, never presented as gains. `prompt_ms: null` cells (a run with
374|  no prefill-0 step) fail the audit loudly rather than timing prefill at zero.
375|- **Memory.** vLLM checks run strictly sequentially (the lock serialises
376|  them); the wrapper adds no process beyond what `time_candidates.py` already
377|  runs. `machine_before/after` rows are already in the jsonl for Claude to
378|  discount paged runs; the checker does not gate on them (no flaky gate).
379|  Existing mitigations (Docker quit, `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` default
380|  in `breakdown.py:54`) stand.
381|- **Data integrity.** Verdicts are content-addressed by citation (file + key);
382|  the checker compares verbatim. Every check run is committed under a new
383|  eval folder — the same "history shows every try" safeguard as one-run-one-attempt
384|  (ADR 0006:29-31), extended to request runs. The wrapper never edits attempt
385|  folders or round docs; it writes only its out dir.
386|- **Security.** No credentials (the wrapper reads no `.env`, makes no network
387|  calls), no sandbox/hook changes per the simplicity preference, no new
388|  privileged path: the swarm could already run `time_candidates.py`; it now
389|  runs a narrower subset of it. Lock-file deletion and hold-forever DoS are
390|  pre-existing voluntary-lock limits, unchanged by this design and out of
391|  scope to harden.
392|- **Operational fit.** Round-2 shape (2 ready + 1 submission) costs ~3 checks
393|  ≈ 40 min serial on top of a ~63 min round — inside the evening's budget
394|  with Claude's hour. Worst-case subset bisection over ≤3 slots is bounded
395|  (~7 runs) and each run is visible in the log; realistically 1–2 extra runs.
396|
397|## 7. Credible alternatives considered and their trade-offs
398|
399|- **A: skill-only fix (prediction rules + a second verifier pass, no
400|  in-round check).** Cheapest on GPU time and simplest to write. Rejected: it
401|  leaves the objective unmeasured in-round, so request-level numbers stay
402|  arithmetic by necessity — behaviour 2's mechanism (demand a number, forbid
403|  the measurement) survives, and criterion 6 has no in-round counterpart to
404|  compare. The brief already decided the swarm may run the check; refusing
405|  the tool concedes the root cause.
406|- **B: extend the verifier instead of a new checker.** Fewer roles. Rejected:
407|  the verifier's loop, done-condition and write-ownership are all
408|  exploration-scoped (`verifier.md:9-25`); bolting implementation checks onto
409|  it complicates the one checker that works, and its invocations happen at
410|  different times (exploration end vs per-hypothesis close + finish). A narrow
411|  second card copies a proven shape (`boundary.md`) and keeps both loops
412|  checkable by the contributor model.
413|- **C: flags on `time_candidates.py` ("run vLLM with --repeats 5 ...")
414|  instead of a wrapper.** Smaller diff. Rejected: free flags are gameable by
415|  the agent they constrain (`--repeats 1` collapses ranges to points;
416|  `--settings` subsets shrink "every setting" and change KV bytes per
417|  `:250`; `--tokens 9` reweights decode/prompt), and the exact gate plus the
418|  repeat audit would have to live in prose. Pinning belongs in the tool when
419|  no human watches (ADR 0012:33). The wrapper also fixes the invocation for
420|  judges and Claude to audit.
421|- **D: ship the claim validator (`check_claims.py`) as an enforced tool.**
422|  Tempting — it is mechanical. Rejected for the required path: claims live in
423|  prose tables, so a validator needs a machine-readable claim file the swarm
424|  must also maintain — a second source of truth that can drift from the docs
425|  judges read, plus new validator-gaming surface. It stays design scaffolding
426|  (it proved the contract is checkable); the checker agent is the mechanism.
427|  Revisit if round 3 shows checker misses.
428|- **E: require `check_sizes.py` (25 in-between row counts) for `ready`.**
429|  Would shrink Unverified honestly. Deferred, not rejected: its GPU cost was
430|  never measured, and the boundary agent already reports those counts as
431|  unverified. Cheap follow-up once timed.
432|- **F: family counter on "same cause" prose instead of lead-assigned family +
433|  same size/phase.** Matches criterion 5's wording most literally. Rejected:
434|  cause sameness is not mechanically checkable — renaming the cause dodges
435|  the rule. Size/phase loss comes from verdicts (mechanical), family from one
436|  auditable owner (the lead); cause prose stays as the row's explanation,
437|  not its trigger.
438|
439|## 8. Implementation handoff
440|
441|Dependency order (each step states where; total ≈2–3 h per the brief's budget):
442|
443|1. **`bench/grader/check_submit.py` (new, ~120 lines).** Copy the prototype
444|   (`prototypes/check_submit.py`), delete the prototype header. Depends on
445|   nothing new. CPU-test with `prototypes/test_check_submit.py` (5 tests;
446|   last green run: `test-results/check_submit-tests.txt`).
447|2. **Live acceptance run (one GPU job, ~15 min, through the lock).** Claude
448|   (or a smoke session — never a paid round) runs the pinned check on round-2
449|   routing-4 + combine-1 and compares the `submit.json` ranges against
450|   Claude's post-round G3 medians for range overlap. Proves the live path the
451|   prototypes could not (designer-b ran **no** GPU job — siblings held the
452|   lock and every addition over the already-exercised `time_candidates` path
453|   is CPU-testable). Required before round 3.
454|3. **Skill v8 text (all in `.agents/skills/muse-round/` + brief).** Apply
455|   P1–P15 from `prototypes/skill-patch.md` verbatim (new `checker.md` from
456|   `prototypes/checker.md`, claim contract from `prototypes/claim-schema.md`);
457|   bump `SKILL.md:10` and `CHANGELOG.md` to v8; fix the stale v6 stamps the
458|   skill explorer found (`SKILL.md:80`, `tracking.md:33`). Commit on main
459|   before round 3 starts.
460|4. **Docs.** One ADR (skill v8: the claim contract, the check, the checker,
461|   the ledger; also records one-run-one-attempt for the first time);
462|   `claude/muse-swarm.md` swarm/ready description; glossary `Improvement`
463|   already encodes the rule — no change. Judges read the ADR + `checker.md` +
464|   one `submit.json`.
465|5. **Dry-run checklist (no paid Muse run — all re-runnable now).**
466|   - `test_check_submit.py` (5/5) + `check_claims.py` recast-fails (8
467|     defects) / conforming-passes + `ledger_replay.py` (trigger at experts
468|     attempt-3, silent for routing). Commands and outputs:
469|     `test-results/check_submit-tests.txt`,
470|     `test-results/check_claims-tests.txt`, `test-results/ledger_replay.txt`.
471|   - Post-edit re-read of the v8 skill for internal consistency (version
472|     stamps, card cross-refs, P6 vs `tracking.md:152` agreement).
473|   - The live run from step 2.
474|6. **Round-3 success read (criterion 6 operationalised).** Every `ready` has
475|   a `submit.json` + `check: pass`; every *Ready to test*/summary number has
476|   kind+level+source; Unverified lists present; ledger triggers or why-nots
477|   visible; Claude's post-round G3 ranges overlap the in-round ranges.
478|
479|- **Acceptance tests:** steps 2 + 5 (all must pass pre-round-3).
480|- **Regression tests:** round-3 transcripts show one grader run per attempt
481|  still holds; `tools/provenance_check.py` clean; finished-round tags
482|  untouched; `engine_table.py` still renders the in-round `muse-vllm.jsonl`.
483|- **Monitoring:** eval-folder count per round (check runs), checker fail
484|  count (contract friction), queue waits (transcript "waiting for the GPU"
485|  lines), round wall time vs the ~2 h envelope.
486|- **Rollback:** skill v8 is one commit — revert to v7 and round 3 runs the
487|  old rules (losing only the new gates); `check_submit.py` is additive —
488|  delete the file. A mid-round abort leaves `evals/` + ledger committed and
489|  versioned, resumable under either version.
490|
491|Prototype/test inventory (all under `design-lab/designer-b/`): 
492|`prototypes/check_submit.py` + `test_check_submit.py` (pinned wrapper; live
493|path reuses `time_candidates.main`, CPU-tested incl. real handoff log);
494|`prototypes/check_claims.py` + `claims-round2-recast.json` (fails, 8 defects)
495|+ `claims-conforming.json` (passes); `prototypes/ledger_replay.py` (parses
496|round-2 README, no transcription); `prototypes/checker.md`,
497|`prototypes/claim-schema.md`, `prototypes/skill-patch.md` (P1–P15).
498|Results: `test-results/check_submit-tests.txt`,
499|`test-results/check_claims-tests.txt`, `test-results/ledger_replay.txt`,
500|`test-results/synth-*.jsonl` (+ `g3`/`submit` pairs).
501|
502|## 9. Unverified assumptions, risks, decisions requiring the user
503|
504|- **Assumptions (explicit, each cheap to verify):** (a) the contributor model
505|  follows the checker card as reliably as it followed one-run-one-attempt —
506|  same shape (explicit, countable), but unverified until round 3; (b) a
507|  ~40-min check overhead fits round 3's evening — follows from the
508|  tool-explorer's 13–14 min extrapolation, which is itself a prediction from
509|  one log, not a fresh run (step-8.2 replaces it with a measurement);
510|  (c) builders tolerate writing `notes.md` predictions with inputs+miss —
511|  small addition to an existing ritual; (d) `muse-all` subset bisection
512|  terminates in 1–2 extra runs in practice.
513|- **Risks:** (a) **4-workload overfitting** — the pinned check and Claude's G3
514|  share workloads, so both can miss the same out-of-workload loss; carried in
515|  Unverified, mitigated only by `check_sizes.py`-style breadth later (E
516|  above). (b) **`--tokens` unaudited** — output tokens are pinned by argv but
517|  not recorded per run, so the repeat audit cannot re-verify them; fix is a
518|  one-line `tokens` field in `repeat_fixes.time_variants` (proposed, not
519|  required). (c) **In-round vLLM paging** under 16 GB + agent processes could
520|  widen in-round ranges vs Claude's; ranges make this visible, not fatal.
521|  (d) **Lead-assigned families** could be gamed by over-splitting (every
522|  attempt its own family); the history shows every assignment, and Claude's
523|  findings can call it out — no mechanical fix proposed, by the simplicity
524|  guardrail. (e) **Checker–lead collusion** is out of scope: both are the same
525|  model; the backstop is Claude's independent G3 plus committed, citable
526|  files.
527|- **Decisions for surucuonur:** (1) K=3 for the ledger trigger (2 is twitchier,
528|  4 spends more; replay supports 3). (2) Ship `check_claims.py` as an optional
529|  helper or leave it as scaffolding (recommended: scaffolding). (3) Whether
530|  the step-8.2 live acceptance run happens before round 3 (recommended: yes —
531|  it is the one untested path) and who runs it. (4) Whether to add the
532|  `tokens` audit field (E/b above) now or after round 3.

Read text file `design-lab/designer-c/design.md`.
1|# Designer-c design: measure what you claim (failure-and-evolution-first)
2|
3|Perspective: failure-and-evolution-first. This design begins from the
4|realistic ways the system can fail — including how a swarm could game each
5|new check — and proposes the smallest architecture that survives them.
6|
7|Paths below are relative to the worktree at commit `1113c2d` unless noted.
8|"Proposal" marks what is designed but not yet built; everything else cites
9|a path and line, or a result file under `design-lab/designer-c/results/`.
10|
11|## 1. Status: READY
12|
13|The design is complete and its risky half — the pinned tool gate — is
14|prototyped and tested: 13/13 offline audit checks pass
15|(`results/audit-tests/`, §8), and the skill-text half replays correctly
16|against every historical false claim (`results/schema-dry-run.md`).
17|A live pinned vLLM run validates the full path and its duration (§8, T-live).
18|No protected contract is broken; no Muse Code capability beyond the brief
19|is assumed.
20|
21|## 2. Context and diagnosis
22|
23|### 2.1 Verified facts
24|
25|Two rounds produced no real efficiency gain while predicting gains. The
26|five behaviours and their evidence (explorer reports, spot-verified):
27|
28|1. **Unmeasured costs priced at zero.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`
29|   declares a slow prefill branch "free apart from time to first token",
30|   citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42` (line 44 today).
31|   Measured cost: experts-7 prompts 6.6–14.5× slower, throughput −10% to
32|   −83%; routing-4 prompts 7–10% slower (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md:134-141`).
33|   Six sibling instances exist (B1-b–g, explorer-rounds §B1).
34|2. **End-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Round 1 predicted
35|   −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.980/+0.163/−1.756; round 2
36|   predicted −0.84/−0.85/−0.84 and measured −0.726/−0.735/+0.527
37|   (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md:24-29`, `muse-round-2.md:39,83`;
38|   recomputed exactly in explorer-findings `g3_recompute.txt`).
39|3. **Inconsistent reasoning.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:13`
40|   says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then `:36` publishes
41|   "Together (sum) −0.84/−0.85/−0.84". Combine's −0.35 borrows −0.26…−0.29
42|   of `mx.compile`'s end-to-end gain onto −0.07…−0.09 of its own (`:29,34`).
43|   Measured at 32 requests: +1.051 ms (`muse-round-2.md:81`).
44|4. **Grader as search loop (round 1).** 28 executed bash invocations on
45|   experts for 4 counted attempts (18/3/6/1; brief says 29 — lead's
46|   verification note 1 settles 28). Fixed by skill v4's one-run-one-attempt
47|   rule (`builder.md:13`); round 2 ran 13 for 13.
48|5. **Failing design family persisted.** Six timed round-2 experts attempts

84|### 2.2 Failure-first analysis: how the system can fail
85|
86|Any fix must survive these; each maps to a design element in §3
87|(reference F1…F10):
88|
89|- **F1. The new check becomes the next proxy (Goodhart).** A free-flag
90|  end-to-end call is gamed nine ways (verified against code): `--repeats 1`
91|  collapses min–max ranges to points so non-overlap is near-certain;
92|  `--settings` subsets shrink the every-setting burden and change KV bytes;
93|  `--tokens 9` reweights decode/prompt silently; `--variant myname:...`
94|  yields quotable but unjudged medians; `--variant muse-x:...` crashes G3;
95|  single-slot calls leave sums as the only combination number; the plain
96|  engine prices prefill at zero with quotable medians; medians can be
97|  quoted selectively from the jsonl; `max_rows=32` makes prefill
98|  "same by delegation". → Pillar A pins the invocation and audits the log.
99|- **F2. The check becomes a search loop.** Behaviour 4's analogue: unlimited
100|  14-minute runs as a gradient, each blocking every builder. → One gated
101|  call shape, verdict stands (no re-runs), failed checks force
102|  redesign-or-drop.
103|- **F3. Queue contention stretches the round past the deadline.** A 3-slot
104|  call is ~40 min; naive per-hypothesis checks of 3 slots plus a combined
105|  check exceed an hour of serial GPU. → Batching: one combined call judges
106|  every candidate plus the combination; piece timing stays the search
107|  signal; the check runs only at close-time.
108|- **F4. Noise kills or crowns.** 1-request whole-request spreads 6–41%
109|  (`0011:52`); 5 repeats still leave ~3% false-slower over 8 checks
110|  (`0011:40`); 1-row piece timing is near noise even within-run
111|  (`muse-round-2.md:55`; experts-7 1-row flipped sign between re-grades).
112|  A re-run-on-noise rule would be a license to re-roll. → The verdict
113|  stands; precision (no false claims) beats recall (a missed improvement
114|  simply isn't submitted). Claude's independent G3 stays authoritative.
115|- **F5. The model ignores the rule.** Round 1 ignored one-attempt-per-run
116|  until it became explicit (`builder.md:13`); round 3 runs the less
117|  capable contributor model unattended (ADR 0012). General advice fails;
118|  explicit checkable rules held (13-for-13). → Every new rule is shaped
119|  like behaviour 4's fix: countable, file-backed, auditable post-hoc.
120|- **F6. Partial rounds leave half-gates.** A session can stop mid-check.
121|  Appended reruns, half-written logs, or a `ready` set before the verdict
122|  lands would corrupt the record. → Fresh folder per check (refuse
123|  non-empty); audit demands completeness; `ready` requires the verdict
124|  file to exist; new interim status `candidate` separates piece-done
125|  from end-to-end-proven.
126|- **F7. Self-checking fails.** The builder's >20% miss rule (`builder.md:30`)
127|  is self-graded and unverified; predictions missed by 2.7–60× while
128|  Ready-to-test kept publishing fresh arithmetic (O7). → An independent
129|  checker, not the author, signs every number; the lead cannot close
130|  without that signature.
131|- **F8. Forgeries and bypasses.** Hand-edited verdict files; direct
132|  `time_candidates.py` runs quoted as evidence; `breakdown.py` direct runs
133|  bypassing the lock and distorting concurrent timings. → The audit
134|  recomputes G3 from the log and compares (kills lazy forgery); only
135|  marker-bearing logs count (direct runs have none); a re-entrant-safe
136|  lock plus entry-point coverage closes the bypass.
137|- **F9. Docs drift and "Not covered" repeats.** ADR 0010's "Not covered:
138|  prefill speed" was cited to justify behaviour 1; ADR 0011 has its own
139|  "Not covered" (`:51`) in the same citable form; the one-run-one-attempt
140|  fix never reached any ADR; `SKILL.md:80` stamps "skill version 6" while
141|  `:10` declares v7. → Rephrase every coverage gap as "unverified: assume
142|  nothing"; record the fix in an ADR; repair the version stamp.
143|- **F10. Evolution.** More slots, other engines, rounds 4+, other models.
144|  A fix wired to "vLLM, 3 slots, 4 workloads" rots. → The pinned protocol
145|  lives in one audited place (the wrapper + marker); the skill cites the
146|  wrapper, not flag values; the glossary holds the shared definitions.
147|
148|### 2.3 Root cause and certainty
149|
150|**Cause (high certainty — five independent behaviour chains converge):**
151|inside a round the swarm never observes the real objective. Its only
152|feedback is per-slot piece timing, while the real measurement (G3 over
153|whole requests) arrives post-round; and its end-to-end claims pass from
154|hypothesis to README to summary with no recorded check step (verifier
155|verdicts appear in every exploration entry and nowhere in
156|`implementation/`). Behaviour 2 is directly *mandated* by this structure:
157|`SKILL.md:147` requires an end-to-end number while `tracking.md:152` and
158|`SKILL.md:164` forbid the only measurement that could produce one.
159|
160|**Why behaviour 1's specific fix (ADR 0011) is not enough (high
161|certainty):** it closes the prefill gap but leaves the general habit —
162|"anything outside the measurement is free" — unaddressed, and adds a new
163|citeable "Not covered" (`0011:51`).
164|
165|**Why rules alone are not enough (medium-high certainty):** behaviour 4
166|shows rules work when explicit and checkable — but an end-to-end call with
167|free flags has nine gaming vectors (§2.1), several undetectable from the
168|verdict alone. The flags must be mechanically pinned, not merely
169|listed. Conversely, tools alone are not enough either: no tool sees
170|unwritten assumptions, borrowed arithmetic, or design-family persistence —
171|those need the checker and the counter.
172|
173|## 3. Recommended design: measure what you claim
174|
175|One principle, three pillars. **Every speed claim in a round is either a
176|measurement of exactly what is claimed, at the level claimed, citing its
177|run file — or a labelled prediction shown next to the measured value.**
178|Proposal in full; prototypes live in `prototype/`.
179|
180|### Pillar A — a pinned in-round end-to-end gate (tool)
181|
182|**New entry point `bench/grader/check_ready.py`** (proposal; prototype:
183|`prototype/check_ready.py`, 13/13 audit tests pass). It is the only
184|end-to-end evidence the swarm may cite. It does exactly two things:
185|
186|1. **Runs one pinned invocation** — `time_candidates.py vllm` with the G3
187|   protocol fixed in code: 4 G3 settings (`1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024`),
188|   5 repeats, 256 tokens, positional `SLOT=FOLDER` only. There are no
189|   `--repeats`, `--settings`, `--tokens`, `--variant` or engine flags to
190|   game (F1: six vectors removed by pinning, two more by the audit below;
191|   the ninth, `max_rows` delegation, is piece-level and contained by G2 +
192|   the boundary agent + `check_sizes.py`). It takes the GPU lock
193|   through `time_candidates.main()`'s existing `hold()` (no second hold:
194|   a same-process re-hold would self-deadlock on `flock`, F8 note), loads
195|   the model inside the run, and appends a `ready-protocol` marker record
196|   to the jsonl pinning what ran.
197|2. **Audits the log instead of trusting it** — exactly one marker with
198|   pinned values; every run vLLM at the 4 settings × 5 repeats; the exact
199|   variant set (`base`, `compiled-<slot>`, `muse-<slot>` per slot, plus
200|   `compiled-all`/`muse-all` when >1 slot, so a combination is always
201|   measured as a combination); every non-base variant keeps base's greedy
202|   tokens at rows 1 and 32 (the brief's end-to-end G2, which G3 itself
203|   ignores — §2.1); the G3 verdict **recomputed from the log** and
204|   compared with `g3-vllm.json` (kills lazy forgery, F8); every submitted
205|   `muse-<slot>` and `muse-all` passing G3 against base and its compiled
206|   counterpart.
207|
208|**Contract.** CLI: `check_ready.py <out-dir> SLOT=FOLDER [...]`, plus
209|`--audit <out-dir>` (no GPU; re-audits any folder — also useful to
210|Claude post-round). Refuses a non-empty out-dir (F6: no appends, one
211|folder per check). Writes `muse-vllm.jsonl`, `g3-vllm.json`,
212|`ready-verdict.json` (schema: `pass`, per-variant `g3`/`vs`/`phases`,
213|`exact` table, `protocol`, file paths). Exit 0 pass / 1 judged fail /
214|2 protocol violation; every path writes `ready-verdict.json` so the
215|checker can cite even failures. Prints one `ready <variant>: pass/fail`
216|line each plus `ready check: PASS/FAIL`.
217|
218|**Scheduling (F3).** Piece timing stays the search signal; the ready
219|check runs only at close-time. The lead batches: hypotheses converge on
220|piece timing to the new `candidate` status, then **one combined call**
221|over all submitted slots judges every `muse-<slot>` and `muse-all`
222|together. Typical cost: one vLLM run per round (~14 min for 1 slot,
223|~25–40 for 2–3). A failed check returns the hypothesis to building only
224|with a changed approach, else drops it (F2: bounded by genuine
225|redesigns, never a loop). The verdict stands — no re-runs (F4).
226|
227|### Pillar B — claim discipline with an independent checker (skill)
228|
229|**Number rule rewrite** (`tracking.md:153`; prototype:
230|`prototype/skill/tracking.md`). The old rule accepts shown arithmetic as
231|a source — the letter that blessed behaviours 2–3. The new rule: every
232|speed number carries level (piece/end-to-end), run file, and label
233|(measured/prediction). Measured piece numbers cite the grader verdict
234|that timed exactly that slot; measured end-to-end numbers cite the ready
235|check that timed exactly that slot or combination; predictions count
236|only the candidate's own measured effect and sit next to the measured
237|value; combinations are measured as combinations, never summed;
238|everything unmeasured goes under **Unverified** and is never assumed
239|free, neutral or zero — "G3 decides" is an Unverified entry, not a
240|measurement. GPU rule (`tracking.md:152`) becomes "the grader and the
241|ready check are the only GPU jobs", run only as builder / only as lead
242|respectively, with direct `time_candidates.py`/`breakdown.py`/
243|`repeat_fixes.py` runs explicitly not evidence (F8).
244|
245|**New `candidate` status + `ready` gate** (prototype:
246|`prototype/skill/tracking.md` hypothesis schema). `candidate` = passes
247|G1, G2, boundary check, `beats_compiled` (+ `beats_baseline`) on piece
248|timing, checker-signed, awaiting the ready check. `ready` = the ready
249|check's `ready-verdict.json` says `pass` for exactly this attempt. The
250|Decision at `candidate` states the piece basis as a prediction; at
251|`ready` it cites the verdict file with the measured change. Ready to
252|test names only `ready` attempts (or kept baselines / the reference,
253|which carry no new claim). This is AC2 made mechanical (F5: file-backed).
254|
255|**New role: checker** (proposal; prototype card:
256|`prototype/skill/checker.md`). The verifier's implementation-phase
257|counterpart — same method (open the cited file, redo the arithmetic),
258|because that method is proven. `checker-<n>` signs each hypothesis
259|before `candidate`/`ready`; `checker-final` signs Ready to test and the
260|summary. It checks levels, run files, labels, own-effect-only arithmetic,
261|Unverified completeness, the failure counter (§3C), and the ready-gate.
262|The lead cannot close without its `pass` in the `Check` section / log.
263|Like the verifier it never edits others' numbers; the lead fixes and
264|re-calls. One agent per check keeps it cheap; post-round, Claude audits
265|that the signatures exist (F7, §8).
266|
267|### Pillar C — a design-family switch rule (skill)
268|
269|**Failure signatures + count of 3** (proposal; schema in
270|`prototype/skill/tracking.md`, rule text for `SKILL.md` step 4 in §8).
271|The lead logs each failed attempt's signature — the phase/size it failed
272|at plus the named cause. After **3 failures sharing one phase and one
273|cause**, the next attempt must be a **changed approach** (different
274|kernel structure, parallelisation or dataflow — not tuning), named in
275|`notes.md` as "approach change: from X to Y", or the log holds the
276|lead's reason why not. The checker verifies the counter. A failed ready
277|check logs an end-to-end-level signature under the same counter.
278|Why 3: round-2 experts' attempts 1–3 share decode/1-row + "fused-structure
279|1-row latency", and attempt-3's own note refuted the lever — the rule
280|fires exactly where the record says it should (`results/schema-dry-run.md`),
281|while allowing genuine iteration (F5: countable, not advisory).
282|
283|### Data flow and integration points
284|
285|```text
286|builder → grader (piece) → hyp entry → boundary check → checker-<n> pass
287|  → candidate ─┐
288|               ├→ lead: ONE check_ready.py over all candidates (+muse-all)
289|candidate ─────┘         → ready-verdict.json pass → ready (per slot)
290|                       → fail → redesign (approach change) or dropped
291|ready set → Ready to test + summary → checker-final pass → commit → Claude's G3
292|```
293|
294|Integration points: `check_ready.py` imports `time_candidates` (calls
295|`main()` with a pinned argv, reuses `g3()` for recompute) and needs no
296|change to it; skill changes touch `SKILL.md` (goal line, step 4–5,
297|role table, `:164` ownership line), `tracking.md` (rules + schema),
298|new `checker.md`, `builder.md` (notes gain an Unverified line),
299|`boundary.md` ("can't see" list becomes Unverified entries),
300|`claude/muse-agent-brief.md` (`:213-215` end-to-end ownership),
301|`CHANGELOG.md` (v8), glossary (`Ready check`, `Candidate`,
302|`Prediction`, `Unverified`), `muse-swarm.md` + diagrams, and a new ADR
303|(§8). `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` needs no change.
