390|## 6. Failure handling, data integrity, security, operations
391|
392|**Failure handling (in-round).** Every failure has a defined landing
393|state, and every landing state is a committed document, so a partial
394|round resumes cleanly from step 0's "carry on from its READMEs":
395|- ready check fails → hypothesis back to `building` (approach change
396|  required) or `dropped`; the verdict file is cited either way.
397|- ready check crashes mid-run (OOM, killed) → folder holds a partial
398|  log with no marker; audit reports protocol violation; hypothesis
399|  stays `candidate`; the lead re-runs into a fresh folder (a crash is
400|  not a verdict, so "verdict stands" does not apply — the distinction
401|  is file-backed: no `ready-verdict.json`, no verdict).
402|- checker finds defects → lead fixes the numbers, re-calls the checker;
403|  close is blocked until `pass`.
404|- counter hits 3 with no approach change and no logged reason →
405|  checker defect; close blocked.
406|- GPU lock contention → runs queue (existing behaviour); builders keep
407|  waiting per `builder.md:28`. The lead schedules the ready check when
408|  few builders are active (end of implementation) and starts no new
409|  helpers until it lands, to bound swap pressure on 16 GB.
410|- swap/OOM during vLLM → same as any vLLM run today (Docker quit,
411|  `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` default in `breakdown.py:54`); no new
412|  mitigation, and the crash path above keeps the record consistent.
413|
414|**Data integrity.** One folder per check, never appended (tool-refused);
415|audit demands exact settings/repeats/variants/marker; G3 recomputed
416|from the log and compared (forgery of `g3-vllm.json` alone is caught —
417|verified `results/audit-tests/game-forged-g3`). Residual: a fully
418|hand-fabricated jsonl (60+ coherent runs + checks) would pass the
419|audit. Contained, not closed: fabrication at that scale must also match
420|Claude's independent post-round G3 (AC6), which it cannot predict;
421|transcripts show whether `check_ready.py` actually ran. This matches
422|the brief's "simple over airtight" guardrail — proportionate, stated.
423|
424|**How the swarm could still game it (Goodhart audit, F1/F10).**
425|1. Tune to the 4 G3 workloads (e.g. `max_rows` edges placed just
426|   outside them). Contained: G2 still tests 6 sizes; the boundary agent
427|   checks off-size rows; `check_sizes.py` exists for Claude's audit.
428|2. Pick attempt folders that flatter (e.g. a weak `--baseline`) — the
429|   ready check has no `--baseline` flag; bars are fixed (base + compiled).
430|3. Time-of-day gaming (run when the machine is quiet). Inherent to all
431|   timing here; paired repeats (piece) and shuffled repeats (G3) bound it.
432|4. Quote piece medians as end-to-end. Killed by the level+label rule +
433|   checker + marker requirement.
434|5. Skip the checker (lead closes without calling it). The signature is
435|   file-backed and Claude's post-round audit checks presence (§8, M3);
436|   transcripts record helper starts. A lead that forges a signature is
437|   visible in the same audit. Residual accepted (see §9).
438|6. Three failures, cosmetic "approach change" (rename, not redesign).
439|   The checker judges the notes' from-X-to-Y statement; weak but
440|   auditable. AC5's "or log why not" already concedes this boundary.
441|
442|**Security.** No new surface: no network, no credentials (rule stands),
443|no sandbox change, no hook change. The wrapper runs the same local
444|binaries the swarm already runs. The marker is provenance, not trust —
445|Claude's independent measurement stays the authority.
446|
447|**Operations.** Round duration grows by typically one vLLM run
448|(§3A: ~14 min/1 slot, ~25–40/2–3; measured live in §8 T-live) plus
449|checker agents (minutes, no GPU). Cost stays ~$1/round (contributor
450|model). Memory: schedule the check late; the lead pauses new helper
451|starts while it runs. Monitoring: §8 M1–M4.
452|
453|## 7. Credible alternatives considered and their trade-offs
454|
455|1. **Skill rules only (no tool change).** "Run `time_candidates.py vllm`
456|   with these exact flags." Rejected: nine gaming vectors (§2.1), and
457|   the contributor model follows explicit rules but cannot self-police
458|   flag discipline against its own incentive to show gains. Behaviour 4
459|   cuts the other way — but that rule was countable post-hoc (runs ==
460|   attempts), while flag values evaporate unless audited. The wrapper
461|   makes the protocol countable.
462|2. **Pin by editing `time_candidates.py` (remove flags / add a `--g3`
463|   mode).** Rejected: it changes Claude's own measurement path (risk to
464|   the authority), and any flag the script accepts stays available to
465|   the swarm. The additive wrapper leaves the authority untouched (§5).
466|3. **Plain-engine in-round check (fast: seconds, not minutes).**
467|   Rejected: plain `prompt_ms` is always 0.0 and writes no verdict
468|   (§2.1) — it would re-legalise behaviour 1 (prefill priced at zero)
469|   as the official gate. Speed is the attraction; wrongness is
470|   disqualifying. (If plain ever gains real prompt timing + verdict,
471|   the wrapper can pin it as a pre-gate — evolution path, F10.)
472|4. **Extend the verifier instead of adding a checker.** Rejected
473|   narrowly: the verifier is exploration-scoped and returns before
474|   implementation (`verifier.md:25`); re-tasking it mid-round muddies
475|   its proven remit and its Done condition. A sibling card with the
476|   same method reuses what works without touching it. If agent count
477|   ever binds, merging the cards is a safe refactor (same method).
478|5. **Hard attempt/family cap (e.g. "drop after 3 failures", no escape).**
479|   Rejected: AC5 explicitly allows "or the log records why not", and a
480|   hard cap risks killing a slow-converging real improvement (round-2
481|   routing improved across 4 attempts). The approach-change rule bounds
482|   cost while preserving the escape hatch, file-backed.
483|6. **Re-run-on-noise tiebreak (allow one repeat on marginal `slower`).**
484|   Rejected (F4): any re-roll rule is a license to re-roll, and "marginal"
485|   needs a threshold that becomes the next proxy. Precision beats recall
486|   here; a noise-killed candidate is merely unsubmitted, while a
487|   noise-crowned one corrupts the baseline chain.
488|7. **Full provenance (signed logs, trusted timestamps, sandboxing).**
489|   Rejected per the brief's guardrails (surucuonur rejected sandbox/hook
490|   hardening; "simple over airtight"). The recompute-and-compare +
491|   independent-G3 pairing gives two independent observations of the same
492|   protocol, which is the proportionate integrity story.
493|
494|## 8. Implementation handoff
495|
496|Dependency-ordered work (proposal; fits the 2–3 h budget — the prototypes
497|are the first drafts):
498|
499|1. **`bench/grader/check_ready.py`** (new, ~200 lines). Move
500|   `prototype/check_ready.py` (adjust `WORKTREE` import path to the
501|   `HERE`-relative form the other grader scripts use). Owner: Claude.
502|2. **Skill v8 text.** `tracking.md` ← `prototype/skill/tracking.md`
503|   (rules + schema); new `checker.md` ← `prototype/skill/checker.md`;
504|   `SKILL.md`: role table + helper-start shape gain the checker;
505|   step 4 gains `candidate` + the ready-check call + failure-counter rule
506|   ("After 3 failures sharing one phase and one cause, the next attempt
507|   changes approach, named in notes.md, or the log records why not");
508|   step 5 Ready-to-test/summary gain the citation schema; `:20` goal
509|   gains "and a ready check shows it improves end to end"; `:164`
510|   becomes "Claude's post-round G3 stays the authority; your ready
511|   check predicts it"; fix `:80` "skill version 6" → 8. `builder.md`:
512|   notes gain an Unverified line. `boundary.md`: "can't see" list
513|   becomes Unverified entries. `CHANGELOG.md`: v8 row.
514|3. **Brief + docs.** `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:213-215`: the swarm
515|   runs the ready check in-round; Claude's G3 stays authoritative.
516|   Glossary: `Ready check`, `Candidate`, `Prediction`, `Unverified`.
517|   `muse-swarm.md` §§ Implementation / What-keeps-it-honest + the
518|   implementation diagram page gain checker + ready check. New ADR
519|   (next number): the fix, and — closing the traceability gap (§2.2
520|   F9) — record one-run-one-attempt with its round-1 evidence.
521|   Rephrase `0011:51` "Not covered" as "unverified: assume nothing"
522|   (amendment note, same pattern as `0010:9-10`).
523|4. **Validate without a paid Muse run (acceptance tests):**
524|   - T-audit: `tests/test_audit.py` — 13/13 pass (done; rerun after the
525|     move). Covers pinned-protocol acceptance, every end-to-end gaming
526|     vector's representative (repeats, settings, tokens/exactness,
527|     plain engine, variant extras, missing muse-all, missing marker),
528|     forged-g3 detection, and old-log rejection.
529|     Command: `.venv/bin/python design-lab/designer-c/tests/test_audit.py`
530|     (no GPU). Result: `results/audit-tests/` (13 case folders each
531|     with log + g3 + ready-verdict files). Two further manual probes
532|     (no GPU): a partial mid-run log copied out of T-live audits as
533|     protocol violation exit 2 with no verdict (`crash-partial` —
534|     the §6 crash path); a non-empty out-dir is refused with exit 2
535|     before touching the GPU (F6).
536|   - T-schema: `results/schema-dry-run.md` (done) — every historical
537|     false claim rejected with an allowed form; counter fires at the
538|     right attempt. Rerun mentally against final v8 text.
539|   - T-live: one real pinned run (see result below). Proves the GPU
540|     path, the lock hand-off, and the duration on this machine.
541|   - T-docs: checklist — each AC1–6 maps to a skill sentence + (where
542|     mechanical) an audit assertion; each F1–F10 maps to §3/§6 text.
543|5. **Round-3 success read-out (no extra instrumentation):** AC6 —
544|   Claude's G3 agrees with each cited `ready-verdict.json` within
545|   repeat-noise; plus (a) every `ready` cites a passing verdict file,
546|   (b) every Ready-to-test/summary number carries level+file+label,
547|   (c) checker `pass` lines exist for every close, (d) any 3-shared
548|   failure shows an approach change or logged reason. (a)–(d) are
549|   checkable by grep.
550|6. **Optional hardening (deferrable past round 3):** `gpu_lock.hold()`
551|   idempotency + `__main__` coverage; `g3()` no-bar guard (§5).
552|7. **Monitoring (M1–M4, all post-round, no new infra):** M1 ready-check
553|   count and wall time per round (GPU cost); M2 in-round vs post-round
554|   G3 deltas per slot (AC6 trend); M3 missing-checker-signature audit;
555|   M4 counter firings and approach-change outcomes (does switching pay?).
556|8. **Rollback:** delete `check_ready.py`, revert skill/brief/docs to v7
557|   (single commit each); round 4 runs v7. Old data unaffected (§5).
558|
559|**T-live result (live pinned run, GPU):** PASS as a test — the gate works
560|end to end and reproduces the known-correct verdict. Command:
561|`.venv/bin/python design-lab/designer-c/prototype/check_ready.py design-lab/designer-c/results/ready-routing-a4 routing=muse-spark/round-2/kernels/routing/attempt-4`
562|(single slot, 3 variants × 4 settings × 5 repeats = 60 runs).
563|Result files: `results/ready-routing-a4/` (`muse-vllm.jsonl` 60 runs +
564|6 checks + marker, `g3-vllm.json`, `ready-verdict.json`).
565|- **Verdict:** judged FAIL, exit 1, zero protocol problems:
566|  `muse-routing` fails G3 vs both bars — prompt `slower` at 8x128,
567|  32x128 and 32x1024, one request `slower` at 32x1024, decode
568|  `not slower`; token exactness true for both non-base variants.
569|  This reproduces ADR 0011's demotion of routing-4 ("fails G3 on
570|  prompt time at 8 and 32 requests", `0011:46`) from inside the round —
571|  the AC6 premise validated on historical data: the in-round gate and
572|  the post-round authority agree at verdict level.
573|- **Duration:** 9 min 9 s end to end (folder birth → verdict file),
574|  7.7 min of it run wall — under the 13–14 min extrapolation (§2.1),
575|  which included heavier paging outliers. Per-setting wall medians
576|  (1.5/3.9/8.6/16.9 s) match the explorer-tools estimates to the decimal.
577|- **Noise note (inputs to D4):** decode-step deltas vs base
578|  (−0.440/−0.281/−0.458 ms at 1/8/32×128) agree in sign with Claude's
579|  post-round round-2 figures (−0.474/−0.434/−0.537) but drift ~0.1–0.2 ms
580|  across sessions — larger than the within-session repeat spread
581|  (~0.06 ms). Verdict-level agreement is exact; median-level comparison
582|  across sessions needs a tolerance of a few tenths of a ms.
583|  The 1x128 decode comparison also landed exactly on the boundary
584|  (muse max 5.465 = base min 5.465 → `same`, blocking a `faster`
585|  phase) — a live example of why the verdict-stands rule (§7.6)
586|  exists instead of a tiebreak.
587|
588|## 9. Unverified assumptions, risks, decisions requiring the user
589|
590|**Unverified assumptions:**
591|- A1. One combined vLLM run per round fits round 3's time budget
592|  alongside builders' grader runs (prediction: +14–40 min serial GPU;
593|  T-live measures the 1-slot case; multi-slot is extrapolated, §2.1).
594|- A2. The contributor model follows the new explicit rules as it
595|  followed one-run-one-attempt (brief's own assumption; first tested
596|  in round 3).
597|- A3. In-round and post-round G3 agree within noise (same protocol,
598|  same machine class, different time/swap state). Partly validated:
599|  T-live reproduces the post-round verdict exactly, but decode medians
600|  drift ~0.1–0.2 ms across sessions (see T-live noise note); AC6 in
601|  round 3 measures this on fresh candidates.
602|- A4. `muse-all` from one combined call is the combination claim that
603|  matters (interactions beyond the submitted set stay Unverified).
604|
605|**Risks (residual, accepted with containment):**
606|- R1. Full-log fabrication (§6) — contained by independent G3 +
607|  transcripts; accepted per simplicity guardrail.
608|- R2. Skipped/forged checker signature (§6 gaming-5) — detected by
609|  post-round audit M3, not prevented; accepted (prevention needs hooks,
610|  rejected).
611|- R3. Noise-killed real improvements (F4) — accepted as precision
612|  over recall; visible in M2/M4 if systematic.
613|- R4. Ready-check failure late in the round leaves no time to redesign —
614|  mitigated by piece pre-gating (most failures land cheaply) and by
615|  scheduling the check as soon as candidates exist, not at the deadline.
616|- R5. 16 GB swap during the vLLM run slows the swarm's own processes —
617|  mitigated by late scheduling + paused helper starts (§6).
618|
619|**Decisions requiring the user (surucuonur):**
620|- D1. Count of 3 for the family-switch rule (2 is twitchier, 4 burns
621|  more; 3 matches the round-2 evidence point).
622|- D2. Verdict-stands with no noise tiebreak (§7.6) — confirm precision
623|  over recall.
624|- D3. Whether to include the §5/§8-step-6 lock/idempotency hardening in
625|  the round-3 commit or defer it.
626|- D4. (For Claude, post-round 3:) if AC6 shows a systematic in-round vs
627|  post-round offset, whether to investigate machine state or accept a
628|  documented tolerance.
629|
630|---
631|*Prototypes/tests/results alongside:* `prototype/check_ready.py`,
632|`prototype/skill/tracking.md`, `prototype/skill/verifier.md` (unmodified
633|copy, kept for reference), `prototype/skill/checker.md`,
634|`tests/test_audit.py`, `results/audit-tests/` (13 cases),
635|`results/schema-dry-run.md`, `results/ready-routing-a4/` (T-live).

Read text file `design-lab/reviewer/review.md`.
1|# Independent review: designs X, Y, Z against the brief
2|
3|Reviewer: independent, read-only. Read order followed: `design-lab/brief.md`,
4|the four explorer reports, then `design-lab/review/design-{X,Y,Z}/design.md`
5|+ `test-report.md` + prototype/result files. Never opened `design-lab/designer-*/`
6|or `design-lab/tester-*/`. No GPU work, no model load, no tracked file changed
7|(`git status` shows only `?? design-lab/`), no network, no credentials.
8|CPU-only verification: targeted reads and greps of repo code cited below.
9|
10|All three designs agree on the core architecture the brief points at: a pinned
11|in-round end-to-end gate (wrapper over `bench/grader/time_candidates.py` vLLM +
12|G3 path) with a token-exactness gate, claim discipline (measure-at-level or
13|label prediction, own-effect-only, combinations measured, Unverified lists),
14|an independent checker, and a K=3 failure counter. All three were prototyped
15|and independently live-tested on GPU against round-2's known-bad attempts, and
16|all three live checks returned FAIL verdicts matching Claude's post-round G3.
17|The differences are in gate placement, audit strictness, checker shape,
18|counter trigger, and GPU cost — and one of those differences is decisive.
19|
20|## Per-design gate table
21|
22|| Gate | X | Y | Z |
23||---|---|---|---|
24|| G1 root cause | PASS | PASS | PASS |
25|| G2 fits code/boundaries | PASS | PASS | PASS |
26|| G3 protects behavior/integrity | FAIL | FAIL | PASS |
27|| G4 failures/concurrency/recovery | PASS | PASS | PASS |
28|| G5 feasible/testable | PASS | PASS | PASS |
29|| G6 cohesive/proportionate | PASS | PASS | PASS |
30|
31|### Design X — typed claims, owned request check, checker
32|
33|- G1 PASS. Names the root cause as untyped feedback (piece verdicts, request
34|  verdicts, predictions, assumptions all prose under `tracking.md:153`) plus
35|  the forbidden in-round measurement (`tracking.md:152`, `SKILL.md:164`).
36|  Each behaviour is traced to a contract failure with verified cites. The fix
37|  (claim types + pinned check + checker + ledger) addresses the gap, not
38|  symptoms. Evidence: design §2–§4; live FAIL on experts-7 matches Claude
39|  (test-report §1: prompt 7.5–14.8× slower, decode mixed, `pass=false`).
40|- G2 PASS. Additive only: new `bench/grader/check_submit.py` importing
41|  `time_candidates` (same pattern as existing scripts), new `checker.md`,
42|  skill v8 patches P1–P15 quoting current text at 1113c2d (spot-verified:
43|  `SKILL.md:20`, `:135-140`, `:147`, `:164`, `tracking.md:152-153`,
44|  `builder.md:13,24,28,30`, `boundary.md:13` all quoted verbatim). Keeps the
45|  lead GPU-free, fitting `SKILL.md:32`. One wart: P10 writes `grade.json`
46|  into the attempt folder, contradicting `check_candidate.py:11-12` ("It never
47|  writes into the attempt folder"). Mechanically safe — `load()` at
48|  `check_candidate.py:64-71` reads only `spec.json` + `block-*.metal` — but
49|  the docstring needs updating at implementation time.
50|- G3 FAIL. `compose_submit` copies the `g3` verdict dict into `submit.json`
51|  without recomputing any range from the jsonl
52|  (`prototypes/check_submit.py:153-157`, verified by reading). Tester-X's G4
53|  (hand-edited `g3-vllm.json` claiming pass over a failing log) exits through
54|  with `pass=true`, and the checker card compares `submit.json` verbatim
55|  (`checker.md` steps 1–4) with no jsonl cross-check, so the forgery
56|  propagates to `ready`. This is a demonstrated data-integrity hole in the
57|  load-bearing evidence mechanism. Everything else in G3 holds (protected
58|  keys, formats, lock path, one-run rule — tester-X §5, all confirmed).
59|- G4 PASS. Covers check-fail landing states (back to hardening or drop;
60|  failing `muse-all` blocks the combination, subset re-check), crash/partial
61|  (no `submit.json`, no claim), noise (ranges travel; 1-request `same` as
62|  noise), memory (sequential vLLM, existing mitigations), committed-history
63|  integrity. Locks/DoS correctly left as pre-existing limits.
64|- G5 PASS. Implemented as prototype; 5/5 wrapper tests, claim fail/pass pair
65|  (8 defects vs pass), ledger replay — all rerun byte-identical by tester-X
66|  (§2). Live acceptance done by the tester (17.4 min active). Regression and
67|  rollback specified. GPU-budget risk noted below, but feasible.
68|- G6 PASS. Cohesive "type every claim" story; the claim validator is
69|  deliberately kept as scaffolding, not shipped (alt D rejected with reasons).
70|  No speculative machinery. The two-tier check (per-hypothesis + submission)
71|  is the costliest shape of the three — see risks.
72|
73|### Design Y — the round measures its own submission
74|
75|- G1 PASS. Confirms the brief's root cause at high certainty with the same
76|  verified structural facts, and closes it with one gate + one checker pass +
77|  one counter. Live 2-slot check FAILs routing (prompt), combine (decode at
78|  32), and `muse-all`, matching Claude sign-for-sign and reason-for-reason
79|  (test-report §1). This is the only live multi-slot run of any design —
80|  the combination-measurement path at the heart of B2/B3 is proven live here
81|  and only here.
82|- G2 PASS. Minimal footprint: one wrapper, no new role card (verifier gains a
83|  second task), `candidate` status, v8 text pasted verbatim. Two warts.
84|  (1) The lead runs the GPU check, deviating from `SKILL.md:32` ("You don't
85|  explore, build or grade yourself"). This is skill convention, not a
86|  protected contract, and the design justifies it (ADR 0007 bottleneck
87|  rationale inapplicable to one Finish-time run) and asks the user to confirm
88|  (design §9) — acceptable, flagged. (2) The prototype's import,
89|  `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("bench/grader").resolve()))`
90|  (`prototypes/check_submission.py:162`), is cwd-dependent; existing scripts
91|  use file-relative `HERE` (`time_candidates.py:40-41`). Must be fixed when
92|  moved into `bench/grader/`.
93|- G3 FAIL. Same hole as X: `audit()` replays coverage (variants, engine,
94|  reps, exact) but takes the timing verdict purely from `g3.get(name)` pass
95|  flags (`prototypes/check_submission.py:120-141`, verified by reading).
96|  Tester-Y's G4 (forged `g3-vllm.json` pass over a 10×-slower jsonl) exits 0.
97|  This directly weakens the design's §6 claim that "the audit replays coverage
98|  from the log rather than trusting stdout" — coverage yes, verdict no.
99|  Rest of G3 holds (tester-Y §5, all contracts verified intact).
100|- G4 PASS. Best explicit gaming catalogue with per-game mitigations (weak
101|  baseline, `max_rows`, post-check edits, median quoting, direct runs,
102|  noise re-rolls capped at 2 checks, cause-renaming). Lock bypass forbidden
103|  but undetected — stated and accepted per simplicity guardrail. Noise
104|  semantics preserved from ADR 0011.
105|- G5 PASS. 25/25 prototype checks rerun byte-identical (tester-Y §2); live
106|  2-slot run 20:49, no queue wait; falsifiable pre-round expectations stated
107|  and met. Cheapest GPU shape (≤2 checks, at Finish, zero builder contention).
108|- G6 PASS. The most minimal of the three: one gate, one extended role, one
109|  counter. Alternatives 1–6 each rejected with evidence. Proportionate.
110|
111|### Design Z — measure what you claim
112|
113|- G1 PASS. Same confirmed root cause, plus the clearest statement of why ADR
114|  0011 alone is insufficient (new citable "Not covered" at `0011:51`) and why
115|  neither rules-alone nor tools-alone suffices. Failure-first F1–F10 analysis
116|  maps each failure to a design element. Two live FAIL agreements: designer's
117|  T-live on routing-4 (prompt slower → FAIL, reproducing ADR 0011's demotion)
118|  and tester-Z's live run on combine-1 (+0.964 ms vs Claude's +1.051 ms at 32
119|  requests, same verdict).
120|- G2 PASS. Additive wrapper + new checker card + `candidate` status, all
121|  prototyped. Same lead-runs-GPU deviation as Y (`prototype/skill/tracking.md:155`),
122|  with the same justification burden. Marker record appended to the jsonl is
123|  safe for consumers: `engine_table.py:42-43` filters `kind=="run"`/`"check"`,
124|  so the `ready-protocol` marker is ignored (verified by reading). No tracked
125|  tool edited. The §5/§8-step-6 hardenings that would touch `gpu_lock.py` /
126|  `g3()` are explicitly separable and deferred — correctly, since §7.2
127|  rejects editing Claude's measurement path.
128|- G3 PASS. The audit recomputes G3 from the log via `tc.g3()` and compares
129|  per judged variant (`prototype/check_ready.py:168-179`, verified by reading);
130|  tester-Z's forged-g3 fixture exits 2 with "differs from log recompute".
131|  Exact variant-set, engine, settings, reps-0..4, and token-exactness checks
132|  all demonstrated across 13/13 audit fixtures (rerun from copy by tester-Z).
133|  Fresh-folder refusal and crash-vs-verdict distinction (`ready-verdict.json`
134|  absent = no verdict) are the best partial-round story. Warts, none
135|  FAIL-worthy: (a) `run()` passes no `--repeats/--settings/--tokens` to
136|  `tc.main()` (lines 207–210), relying on upstream defaults — settings/repeats
137|  drift would burn a GPU run then fail audit, and tokens drift would pass
138|  silently since the marker is self-written (see risks); (b) the exact gate
139|  covers `compiled-*` variants too (line 149), slightly over-strict — a
140|  non-exact compiled reference (never observed) would fail the candidate;
141|  (c) `prompt_ms: null` (possible per `repeat_fixes.py:277-282`) would crash
142|  `g3()` recompute with a traceback rather than a clean exit 2 — shared with
143|  X and Y, who also lack a null check.
144|- G4 PASS. Strongest failure analysis of the three (F1–F10 + Goodhart audit
145|  with six residual games, each contained-or-accepted). Verdict-stands with a
146|  file-backed crash exception; fabrication contained by independent G3 +
147|  transcripts and explicitly accepted per simplicity. Noise: verdict-level
148|  agreement validated live; median drift (~0.1–0.2 ms) honestly reported with
149|  the tester's qualifier that within-session spread is setting-dependent
150|  (up to ~0.6 ms at 1×128/32×128).
151|- G5 PASS. 13/13 audit tests, schema dry-run over all five historical claim
152|  families, live T-live (9:09 single-slot), tester live run, post-round
153|  monitors M1–M4, rollback by deletion. Implementable in the 2–3 h budget
154|  from the prototypes.
155|- G6 PASS. One principle, three pillars, each load-bearing; full-provenance
156|  and re-roll tiebreaks explicitly rejected per guardrails. The marker is
157|  small and evidenced (old logs rejected: `real-round2`, `real-engine-comparison`
158|  fixtures). No speculative complexity.
159|
160|## Verdict: Z is the strongest passing design
161|
162|Z is the only design that passes all six gates. The deciding difference is
163|tool-evidence integrity: X and Y both fail G3 on a demonstrated forgery hole
164|(hand-edited `g3-vllm.json` sails through), while Z's recompute-and-compare
165|closes it in a few lines — within the simplicity budget, proven by test.
166|Beyond that, concrete reasons to prefer Z:
167|
168|1. Strongest audit: recompute, exact variant-set/engine/settings/reps checks,
169|   token gate, fresh-folder refusal, exit 0/1/2 semantics, plus `--audit` for
170|   CPU-only re-checks (also useful to Claude post-round). 13/13 fixtures,
171|   independently rerun.
172|2. Best failure handling: the crash-vs-verdict distinction (no
173|   `ready-verdict.json` = no verdict = re-run allowed; judged FAIL = stands)
174|   is the only file-backed answer to partial rounds, and the F1–F10 analysis
175|   is the most thorough Goodhart accounting.
176|3. Batched cost shape: one combined call judges every slot plus `muse-all`
177|   (no per-hypothesis mid-round GPU jobs competing with builders, unlike X),
178|   while piece timing stays the search signal.
179|4. Per-hypothesis checking at close time plus a finish check (unlike Y's
180|   Finish-only pass), so Decision errors surface before the deadline rush.
181|5. Honest residuals: fabrication, skipped signatures, noise-killed
182|   candidates, and the untested-until-round-3 compliance assumption are all
183|   stated with containment, not buried.
184|
185|Caveat: Z's combination path is proven only on synthetic logs (`pass-2slot`,
186|`game-noall`); Y is the only design with a live multi-slot `muse-all` run.
187|The implementation should therefore include a live multi-slot acceptance run
188|before round 3 (routing-4 + combine-1, ~21 min measured by tester-Y) — cheap,
189|and it closes Z's one evidence gap with Y's evidence.
190|
191|## Hidden assumptions, counterexamples, and risks
192|
193|Shared by all three (must be understood before round 3):
194|
195|- No live PASS exists. Every live run in this session failed the candidate
196|  (X: experts-7, Y: routing+combine+all, Z: routing-4, tester-Z: combine-1).
197|  The gate's pass path at live scale is exercised only synthetically. AC6
198|  agreement on a passing submission is therefore prediction, not measurement.
199|  Mitigation: the pre-round-3 multi-slot acceptance run above, plus defining
200|  AC6 operationally now (range overlap per X, or verdict agreement per Y/Z —
201|  cross-session median drift is ~0.1–0.2 ms per Z's T-live and tester-Z §4,
202|  so median-equality is the wrong bar).
203|- Checker compliance is untested until round 3. All three admit this
204|  (X §9-a, Y §9, Z A2). The behaviour-4 precedent (explicit countable rules
205|  held 13-for-13) is the entire basis. Nothing can pre-validate it without a
206|  paid run; M3-style post-round signature audits (Z §8) should be committed to.
207|- `--tokens` is unaudited in every design. `time_variants`
208|  (`bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py:305-325`, record fields verified by reading)
209|  writes no token count into run records, so a `--tokens 9` log is
210|  indistinguishable from `--tokens 256` in the jsonl. In-round impact is
211|  limited (all wrappers pin the live argv), but a directly-run gamed log
212|  passes every audit. Only X names this with a fix (one-line `tokens` field,
213|  §9-b). Z's "tokens9 caught" fixture tests an honestly-marked log only — a
214|  direct `--tokens 9` run plus one forged marker line appended by shell would
215|  pass Z's audit. All three should adopt the `tokens` field or explicitly
216|  defer it.
217|- `prompt_ms: null` crashes, not clean failure, in all three (X claims
218|  "fails the audit loudly", §6 — the prototype has no null check; Y and Z
219|  make no claim). Rare (needs a run with no prefill-0 step), but the live
220|  path would traceback instead of writing a citable verdict.
221|
222|Design X:
223|
224|- Per-hypothesis checks + subset bisection is the most expensive shape:
225|  round-2 shape ≈ 2 singles + 1 double ≈ 40–55 min serial plus queue waits
226|  (tester-X waited 28.7 min behind one sibling run), all mid-round against
227|  builders' grader runs. Worst-case bisection (~7 runs) approaches 2 h.
228|  Least margin under the deadline.
229|- The ledger replay assumes its own trigger: families are hand-assigned in
230|  the replay script (`ledger_replay.py:66-75`), and the loss signal is median
231|  comparison while production uses the stricter sign-test `vs_compiled` —
232|  so production triggers less readily than the replay suggests. Lead
233|  over-splitting (every attempt its own family) games it; X admits this
234|  (§9-d) with no mechanical fix.
235|- FAIL verdicts exit 0 (tester-X §1 observation). Consistent with the
236|  file-based contract, but any lead/helpers checking exit codes misread fail
237|  as success. Y's and Z's 0/1/2 convention is strictly better.
238|- The repeat audit counts runs per cell (`check_submit.py:79-94`) rather than
239|  requiring reps 0..4, and ignores extra variants — strictly weaker than Y/Z.
240|- Builder-recall mechanics ("the lead may recall you", skill-patch P11) are
241|  unspecified in Muse Code terms (respawn? new prompt?). Minor.
242|
243|Design Y:
244|
245|- The Finish-only verifier pass concentrates all claim-checking and any
246|  attempt-fix + re-check cycle at the deadline. A request-level failure
247|  discovered at Finish leaves one capped re-check; after that, "whatever
248|  passed" stands. Cheapest when things pass, most time-pressured when they
249|  fail.
250|- Verifier step 6 (`git diff --exit-code` on checked paths) misses untracked
251|  files — a post-check added file is invisible to it. `git status
252|  --porcelain` is the correct mechanism (tester-Y's G5 tested only a tracked
253|  edit). One-line fix.
254|- Piece-claim provenance is unspecified: no `--out`/`grade.json` rule
255|  anywhere in the skill text, so "cites its grader verdict file" (skill-text
256|  §9) points at prose pastes in `notes.md`, not a machine-checkable file.
257|  Transplant X's `--out` rule.
258|- The counter's consecutiveness + cause-identity lets alternating failure
259|  points evade it (fail@1, fail@8, fail@1, … never reaches 3-in-a-row), and
260|  the test hard-codes transcribed causes (`test_failure_counter.py:17-30`).
261|  The cited-refuting-measurement restart rule is the best anti-rename hook of
262|  the three, but it is verifier-judged, not mechanical.
263|- Split single-slot calls each pass the audit (tester-Y G6) — combination
264|  coverage rests on one-call prose + verifier step 3, as designed and stated.
265|  Accepted residual, correctly labelled.
266|
267|Design Z:
268|
269|- `run()` omits all pinning flags, trusting upstream defaults
270|  (`prototype/check_ready.py:207-210`). Today defaults match (verified:
271|  `--tokens` 256 at `time_candidates.py:213`, `G3_SETTINGS`, `G3_REPEATS`),
272|  but settings/repeats drift would burn a GPU run before failing audit, and
273|  tokens drift would pass silently. Transplant X/Y's explicit-argv pinning
274|  plus Y's drift asserts. Trivial fix, should be in the implementation.
275|- The counter is the weakest of the three: "3 failures sharing one phase and
276|  one cause" with no anti-renaming provision, and the dry-run assumes attempts
277|  1–3 share one cause ("fused-structure 1-row latency") although the
278|  historical notes differentiated causes per attempt (attempt-3 refuted the
279|  lever). A lead that re-diagnoses each attempt never triggers it. Transplant
280|  Y's restart-requires-cited-measurement rule or X's family+size/phase
281|  mechanics.
282|- Small tension: R4 says schedule the check "as soon as candidates exist"
283|  while §3A batches one call over all candidates — early-closing hypotheses
284|  either wait (late failure discovery, Z's own R4) or cost extra runs.
285|  Needs one sentence in the implementation.
286|
287|Evidence-hygiene notes (test reports, not designs):
288|
289|- Tester-X §5's "minor defect" (`phases_vs_compiled` misspelling) is a false
290|  positive: I byte-compared all three strings — the real key from
291|  `grade-phases-routing-attempt-4.json`, `checker.md:24`, and `design.md:27`
292|  are identical (`phases_vs_compiled`, matching `check_candidate.py:377`).
293|  No fix needed.
294|- Tester-X's "28 vs 29" and tester-Y/Z's verdict matches were verified
295|  first-hand by the testers and are consistent with the explorer reports;
296|  the run-result evidence (exits, verdicts, timings) stands independently of
297|  the one false-positive reading above.
298|
299|## Transplantable ideas (into Z, without breaking its consistency)
300|
301|1. From Y: explicit-argv pinning + `G3_SETTINGS`/`G3_REPEATS` drift asserts
302|   (fixes Z's defaults reliance; same wrapper, same audit).
303|2. From Y: counter restart requires a cited refuting measurement (fixes Z's
304|   cause-renaming gap; one sentence in the counter rule + one checker bullet).
305|3. From X: `--out grade.json` piece-provenance rule (gives Z's checker a
306|   machine-checkable file for piece claims; safe per `load()`; update the
307|   `check_candidate.py:11-12` docstring line at the same time).
308|4. From X: medians + [min–max] + n embedded in the verdict file (makes AC6
309|   range-overlap comparison direct from the cited file instead of re-reading
310|   the jsonl; additive schema field).
311|5. From Y: the 2-check cap as backstop wording (Z's redesign-gated re-checks
312|   are already bounded in spirit; a cap makes the GPU budget committable).
313|6. From X or Y test suites: the repeat/subset/plain-engine gaming fixtures
314|   (Z's 13 already cover these; keep the union).
315|
316|NOT transplantable: X's per-hypothesis mid-round checks (breaks Z's batching
317|and cost story); Y's Finish-only single verifier pass (breaks Z's
318|close-time checking); Z's marker into X/Y without their audit rewrite (the
319|marker alone adds nothing — Z's recompute is the load-bearing part, and that
320|transplants only as a pair).
321|
322|## Open trade-offs and decisive questions for surucuonur
323|
324|1. Who runs the check — lead (Y/Z) or builder (X)? Y/Z deviate from
325|   `SKILL.md:32` ("You don't grade yourself"); X preserves it at the cost of
326|   mid-round contention and recall mechanics. One decision, before writing v8.
327|2. Batched-only gating (Y/Z) vs per-hypothesis request feedback (X)? Batching
328|   is 2–3× cheaper and contention-free; X buys earlier request-level evidence
329|   per hypothesis. Given piece timing already filters losers cheaply, I
330|   recommend batched — but it means a piece-passing, request-failing
331|   hypothesis is discovered late (Z's R4). Confirm the risk appetite.

text:
# Fix the swarm: measure what you claim (solution design)

**Outcome:** the swarm gets a pinned in-round end-to-end gate (same G3 protocol Claude runs), claim discipline enforced by an independent checker, and a failure counter that forces design change. Recommended: implement designer-c's *"measure what you claim"* design with five small transplants from the other two designs. The synthesized tool gate is prototyped and proven live: it FAILs round-2's known-bad submission exactly as Claude's post-round G3 did.

Why stop here: three independent designs converged on the same core architecture; their one decisive difference (audit integrity) was settled by live test, not opinion; the synthesized gate re-tested green (13/13 + 8/8 + live 2-slot FAIL). The two remaining unknowns — checker compliance on the contributor model, and the gate's live PASS path — cannot be resolved without round 3 itself.

---

## 1. Context: what exists, what is wrong, why it matters now

**What exists.** One Muse Code session per round runs the swarm in `.agents/skills/muse-round/` (skill v7): a lead coordinates, explorers map inefficiencies, a verifier checks them, builders write and grade one attempt each, boundary agents check hypothesis boundaries. Builders' only speed feedback is `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` (per-slot piece timing). After the merge, Claude measures whole requests with `bench/grader/time_candidates.py` (G3) and writes `claude/findings/muse-round-<N>.md`, which seeds the next round.

**What is wrong.** Two rounds produced no real efficiency gain while predicting gains, via five behaviours (brief §Problem, all verified by the explorers): (1) unmeasured costs priced at zero; (2) end-to-end gains claimed from piece arithmetic; (3) inconsistent reasoning (non-composition admitted, then summed; borrowed `mx.compile` offsets); (4) grader used as a search loop in round 1 (fixed by skill v4, held in round 2); (5) persistence with a fused-kernel family that loses at 1 row. Structural root: inside a round the swarm never observes the real objective, and its end-to-end claims pass Decision → Ready-to-test → summary with no checker.

**Why now.** Round 3 should run with the fix before the 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC deadline, on the less capable contributor model with approvals off — so the fix must be explicit, checkable rules plus a mechanically pinned measurement, not advice and not airtight sandboxing (rejected per guardrail).

---

## 2. What the swarm found: facts and root causes

Proof (measured or read verbatim) first, then suspicion.

**Verified structural facts (skill territory):**

- Goal phrased as passing gates: [.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:20).
- In-round model runs doubly forbidden: [tracking.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:152) ("Load no model and start no other GPU work") and [SKILL.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:164) ("G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team").
- Ready-to-test *demands* an end-to-end number ("the change you expect in G3's four workloads… with how you worked it out", [SKILL.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:147)) while the ban forbids measuring it — so behaviour 2 is the only compliant output, not a mistake.
- Verifier checks exploration only ([verifier.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/verifier.md:5)); verifier verdicts appear in every exploration entry and nowhere in `implementation/`; the lead writes Decisions, READMEs and summary unchecked ([SKILL.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:160)).
- Shown arithmetic counts as sourced ([tracking.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:153)); harden loop has a continue rule and no switch rule ([SKILL.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:138)); builder self-checks predictions with no enforcement ([builder.md](/Users/oner/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/builder.md:30)); one-run-one-attempt explicit since v4 ([builder.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/builder.md:13)) and held 13-for-13 in round 2 — the positive control that explicit countable rules hold.

**Verified tool facts:**

- `time_candidates.py` G3 is vLLM-only ([time_candidates.py](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/bench/grader/time_candidates.py:260)); plain `prompt_ms` is always exactly `0.0` (measured in `design-lab/explorer-tools/plain-probe32/`) — a plain-engine gate would re-legalise behaviour 1 as the official check.
- G3 ignores token exactness (`g3()` reads only `kind=="run"` records, [time_candidates.py](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/bench/grader/time_candidates.py:168)) — any in-round check must gate exactness itself.
- Free flags are nine gaming vectors (verified by reading + probes): `--repeats 1` collapses ranges, `--settings` subsets shrink "every setting" and change KV bytes ([time_candidates.py](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/bench/grader/time_candidates.py:250)), `--tokens 9` reweights silently (below 9 crashes), `--variant` escapes judgment or crashes G3, single-slot calls never measure combinations, plain medians look end-to-end.
- GPU lock is voluntary: `breakdown.py`/`repeat_fixes.py` never call `hold()`; no timeout; deleting the lock file silently breaks exclusion ([gpu_lock.py](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/bench/grader/gpu_lock.py:18)).
- Durations measured: grader 12.7 s (routing) to 4 m 57 s (experts) per run; single-slot vLLM G3 ≈ 9–14 min; 2-slot ≈ 21 min (both measured live this session).

**Verified round/finding facts:**

- Behaviour 1: 8 instances incl. the brief's anchor (`hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`), combine's twin (`hyp-3-combine-exact.md:59`), routing's deferral (`hyp-2-routing-exact.md:81`), all citing ADR 0010's "Not covered: prefill speed" (:42 at round-2 time, verified via `git show 4033cae:`).
- Behaviour 2/3: "Together (sum) −0.84/−0.85/−0.84" ([README.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:36)) 23 lines below "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose" (:13); combine's −0.35 = own −0.07…−0.09 + borrowed −0.26…−0.29 (:29, :34). Predictions vs measured recomputed exactly from raw consoles (round 1: −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 vs +0.980/+0.163/−1.756; round 2: −0.84/−0.85/−0.84 vs −0.726/−0.735/+0.527).
- Behaviour 4: 28 executed bash grader invocations on round-1 experts (18/3/6/1) — lead-verified; the documented "29" is off by one, design-neutral.
- Behaviour 5: six timed round-2 experts attempts lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs/layer; attempt-6 never launched — G1 fail); attempt-3's own note refuted group-count as the lever (`hyp-1-experts-exact.md:254-258`); the unfused alternative was named only in the summary.
- ADR 0011 closed the prefill instance but added its own citable "Not covered" (:51); the one-run-one-attempt fix lives in no ADR (traceability gap); `PROVENANCE.md:42` contradicts ADRs 0006/0008/0012 on round-2 sign-in (flagged, untouched by this design).

**Suspicion (labelled as such):** the three-together interaction loss (+2.8 ms at 8 requests in plain MLX) is unexplained in both rounds; cross-session median drift (~0.1–0.2 ms) exceeds within-session spread at some settings, so verdict-level agreement is the right bar, not median equality.

**Brief corrections found:** "main at 2090949" is stale (worktree at 1113c2d); round-2 prediction is −0.84/−0.85/−0.84 not "−0.84 at each"; "6–41% spread" is whole-request time at 1 request specifically; no `logs/` directory (one `log.md` per phase); round-1 formula was (eager-reference − candidate), round 2 (compiled − candidate).

---

## 3. Recommended solution

Base: designer-c's *"measure what you claim"* (reviewer's only all-PASS design), plus reviewer-approved transplants. One principle: **every speed claim is either a measurement of exactly what is claimed, at the level claimed, citing its run file — or a labelled prediction shown next to the measured value.**

### Pillar A — pinned in-round end-to-end gate (tool)

**New `bench/grader/check_ready.py`** (implement from [design-lab/synthesis/check_gate.py](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/synthesis/check_gate.py), rename on move; exact diff vs C's prototype in [gate.diff](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/synthesis/gate.diff)). The only end-to-end evidence the swarm may cite. CLI: `check_ready.py <out-dir> SLOT=FOLDER [...]` plus `--audit <out-dir>` (no GPU; re-audits any folder — also useful to Claude post-round).

- **Runs one pinned invocation**: `time_candidates.py vllm` with the G3 protocol fixed in code — 4 G3 settings, 5 repeats, 256 tokens, positional slots only. No engine/repeat/setting/token/variant flags exist. Explicit argv + drift asserts against `G3_SETTINGS`/`G3_REPEATS`/argparse defaults fail loudly CPU-side before any GPU work (transplant from designer-a).
- **Appends a `ready-protocol` marker** to the jsonl (safe: `engine_table.py:42-43` filters to run/check records). Refuses a non-empty out-dir (one folder per check, never appended).
- **Audits the log instead of trusting it**: exactly one marker with pinned values; every run vLLM at 4 settings × 5 reps (reps 0–4); exact variant set (`base`, `compiled-<slot>`, `muse-<slot>` per slot, plus `compiled-all`/`muse-all` when >1 slot); every non-base variant keeps base's greedy tokens at rows 1 and 32; **G3 recomputed from the log via `tc.g3()` and compared per judged variant** (kills lazy forgery — the decisive differentiator); null measured values → clean protocol violation, never a traceback.
- **Writes `ready-verdict.json` on every path** (`pass`, per-variant g3/vs/phases, exact table, protocol, file paths, plus transplanted `medians` with median/min/max/n per variant/setting/measure from designer-b). Exit 0 pass / 1 judged fail / 2 protocol violation. Prints one `ready <variant>: pass/fail` line each.

### Pillar B — claim discipline with an independent checker (skill)

- **Number-rule rewrite** ([tracking.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:153), start from [designer-c prototype tracking.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/designer-c/prototype/skill/tracking.md)): every speed number carries level (piece/end-to-end), run file, and label (measured/prediction). Measured piece numbers cite the grader verdict that timed exactly that slot (builders write it with `--out attempt-N/grade.json` — transplant from designer-b; update the `check_candidate.py:11-12` docstring line at the same time). Measured end-to-end numbers cite the ready check that timed exactly that slot or combination. Predictions count only the candidate's own measured effect and sit next to the measured value. Combinations are measured as combinations, never summed. Everything unmeasured goes under **Unverified** — never assumed free, neutral, or zero; "G3 decides" is an Unverified entry, not a measurement.
- **GPU rule rewrite** ([tracking.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:152)): the grader (builders only) and the ready check (lead only) are the only GPU jobs, both through the lock; direct `time_candidates.py`/`breakdown.py`/`repeat_fixes.py` runs are explicitly not evidence.
- **New `candidate` status + `ready` gate**: `candidate` = passes G1, G2, boundary check, `beats_compiled` (+`beats_baseline`) on piece timing, checker-signed, awaiting the ready check. `ready` = a `ready-verdict.json` says `pass` for exactly this attempt. Ready-to-test names only `ready` attempts (or kept baselines/the reference, which carry no new claim) and shows the verdict file, per-variant phases vs both bars, exact flags, the piece-basis prediction labelled PREDICTION beside measured, and the UNVERIFIED list.
- **New `checker.md` role** (start from [designer-c prototype checker.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/designer-c/prototype/skill/checker.md)): the verifier's implementation-phase counterpart, same proven method (open the cited file, redo the arithmetic). `checker-<n>` signs each hypothesis before `candidate`/`ready`; `checker-final` signs Ready-to-test and the summary. Checks levels, run files, labels, own-effect-only arithmetic, Unverified completeness, the failure counter, and the ready gate. The lead cannot close without its `pass`; the checker never edits others' numbers.
- **Goal line** ([SKILL.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:20)) gains "and a ready check shows it improves end to end"; `:164` becomes "Claude's post-round G3 stays the authority; your ready check predicts it"; brief `:213`/`:215` updated to the new ownership. Skill v8.

### Pillar C — design-family switch rule (skill)

The lead logs each failed attempt's failure signature (phase/size + named cause). **After 3 failures sharing one phase and one cause, the next attempt changes approach** (different kernel structure/parallelisation/dataflow, named in `notes.md` as "approach change: from X to Y") **or the log records why not.** Anti-rename (transplant from designer-a): a new cause restarts the count only with a cited measurement refuting the old one. A failed ready check logs an end-to-end-level signature under the same counter. The checker verifies the count. (Replay evidence: fires after round-2 experts attempt-3, stays silent for routing.)

### Scheduling, data flow, invariants

- Piece timing stays the search signal; hypotheses converge to `candidate` on piece timing; then **one combined call** over all submitted slots judges every `muse-<slot>` and `muse-all` together. Run it **as soon as the candidate set is stable** (not at the deadline) — one sentence resolving the early-vs-batch tension. At most **2 checks per round** (one scheduled + one re-check; transplant from designer-a as a committable GPU budget).
- Verdict stands — no re-runs on noise. File-backed crash exception: no `ready-verdict.json` = no verdict = re-run into a fresh folder allowed; judged FAIL = stands.
- Flow: builder → grader (piece) → hyp entry → boundary check → checker pass → `candidate` → lead: ONE `check_ready.py` over all candidates → `ready-verdict.json` pass → `ready` per slot (fail → approach-change redesign or drop) → Ready-to-test + summary → checker-final pass → commit → Claude's G3.
- Invariants: (1) only `ready-verdict.json` evidences end-to-end claims; (2) `ready` ⇔ passing verdict file exists for exactly this attempt; (3) `muse-all` measured whenever >1 slot submitted; (4) Unverified listed, never zero; (5) every close carries a checker `pass`.

---

## 4. How it behaves

**A normal round.** Builders compete on piece timing as today, writing `grade.json` per attempt. The lead keeps the failure ledger at collect. Hypotheses reaching `candidate` get checker-signed. Once candidates settle, the lead runs one `check_ready.py` call (e.g. 2 slots ≈ 21 min, builders idle or writing Metal), sets `ready`/`dropped` per variant verdict in a checkpoint, drafts Ready-to-test as measured tables with predictions beside measured plus Unverified, gets `checker-final`'s pass, commits. Claude's post-round G3 then compares against cited verdict files.

**Failure cases:**

- *Gamed check.* Forged `g3-vllm.json` → exit 2 ("differs from log recompute"), tested. 3-repeat/settings-subset/plain-engine/no-marker/missing-`muse-all` logs → exit 2, tested (13/13 + extras). `--tokens 9` via direct run + forged marker → PASSES audit (known gap: token count is not in run records; decision §9). Full-log fabrication → passes audit but cannot match Claude's independent G3; transcripts show whether the wrapper ran. Split single-slot calls → each passes alone; combination coverage rests on the one-call rule + checker (stated residual).
- *GPU queue contention.* One batched call per round at low-builder activity; builders' grader runs queue normally. Measured: a 2-slot run took 20:41 with no wait; a queued run waited 28.7 min behind a sibling and still completed. The 2-check cap bounds worst case.
- *Noise at 1 request.* 1-request whole-request spreads up to ~27% measured; verdicts there are mostly `same`, which passes "never slower" without showing gain — now visible in-round instead of surprising post-round. Verdict-stands (no tiebreak): precision over recall; a noise-killed candidate is merely unsubmitted. AC6 bar must be verdict agreement / range overlap, not median equality (cross-session drift ~0.1–0.2 ms).
- *Session stopped midway.* Every landing state is a committed document: `candidate` with no check resumes (step 0 carries on); partial log has no marker → exit 2, hypothesis stays `candidate`, re-run into a fresh folder; `ready` requires the verdict file to exist.
- *Model ignores a rule.* All new rules are behaviour-4-shaped (countable, file-backed, post-hoc auditable): exit codes, cited verdict files, checker `pass` lines greppable post-round (M3 audit). The checker card itself is the unremovable residual — untestable until round 3.

---

## 5. What changes and what stays protected

**Changes:** one new tool file `bench/grader/check_ready.py`; skill v8 (`SKILL.md` goal/step 4–5/role table/`:164`, `tracking.md` rules + hypothesis schema, new `checker.md`, `builder.md` Unverified line + `--out` rule, `boundary.md` can't-see → Unverified, `CHANGELOG.md` v8 row, fix the stale v6 stamp at `SKILL.md:80`); brief `:213`/`:215`; glossary (`Ready check`, `Candidate`, `Prediction`, `Unverified`); `muse-swarm.md` + diagram; new ADR (also records one-run-one-attempt for the first time, sets "unverified: assume nothing" convention, amends 0011:51 the way 0010:9-10 was amended); one-line `--tokens` audit field in `repeat_fixes.py` only if surucuonur approves (§9).

**Protected (all verified holding in tests):** authorship separation, frozen rounds/tags, Muse-Code-only swarm shape (one added role), no attempt limit, one-grader-run-per-attempt, GPU queue mechanism, ADR 0010/0011 grading rules, G2 token check, Claude's post-round authority, attempt format, grader JSON keys. No tracked tool edited (wrapper only imports); `start.sh`, model, engine untouched. Old data stays valid (past logs lack markers → audit reports non-ready-check evidence, tested). Rollback: delete the tool, revert skill/brief/docs to v7.

---

## 6. Why this approach

All three independent designs converged on the same core (pinned in-round G3-protocol gate + claim discipline + checker + K=3 counter) — that convergence is itself evidence. They differed in audit strictness, checker shape, counter trigger, and GPU cost:

- **Designer-a** (existing-system-first; review label Y): `check_submission.py` + `candidate` status + verifier-gains-second-pass (no new role) + failure-point counter. Minimal footprint; cheapest GPU shape; the only live multi-slot run (20:49, exit 1, all FAIL matching Claude). Fails G3: audit trusts `g3-vllm.json` pass flags — forged verdict exits 0 (demonstrated by tester-a G4). Finish-only checking also concentrates risk at the deadline.
- **Designer-b** (contract-and-data-first; review label X): typed claim contract + `check_submit.py` → single `submit.json` + new checker + failure ledger with lead-assigned families. Strongest semantics; per-hypothesis + submission two-tier checks. Fails G3: same forgery hole (demonstrated by tester-b G4); most expensive GPU shape (~40–55 min + contention); FAIL exits 0 (exit-code readers misread fail as success).
- **Designer-c** (failure-and-evolution-first; review label Z): `check_ready.py` with marker + recompute-and-compare + fresh-folder refusal + crash-vs-verdict distinction + new checker + signature counter. Passes all six gates. Proven live twice (designer's T-live routing-4 FAIL in 9:09; tester's combine-1 FAIL, +0.964 vs Claude's +1.051 ms). Weaknesses (all fixed in synthesis): trusted upstream defaults, weakest counter (no anti-rename), no piece-provenance file, no embedded medians, prose-only re-check bound, null crash.

**Decisive trade-off:** evidence integrity of the load-bearing gate. A and B left a demonstrated hole where a hand-edited verdict file sails through; C closes it in a few lines via recompute-and-compare, within the simplicity budget, proven by test. Everything else was transplantable *into* C without breaking its invariants: explicit-argv pinning + drift asserts (from A), counter-restart-requires-cited-measurement (from A), 2-check cap (from A), `--out grade.json` provenance (from B), medians+[min–max]+n in verdict (from B), null guard (reviewer). NOT transplanted: B's mid-round per-hypothesis checks (breaks batching/cost), A's Finish-only single pass (breaks close-time checking).

---

## 7. Implementation handoff

Dependency-ordered (Claude on main before round 3; ≈2–3 h):

1. **Tool** (30–45 min): move [check_gate.py](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/synthesis/check_gate.py) to `bench/grader/check_ready.py` (rename; fix the `WORKTREE` parents-depth line per `gate.diff` note to the `HERE`-relative form); review delegate + audit paths.
2. **Skill v8** (45–60 min): apply §3B/§3C starting from [designer-c tracking.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/designer-c/prototype/skill/tracking.md) and [checker.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/designer-c/prototype/skill/checker.md), plus the transplanted sentences (argv pinning is tool-side; counter anti-rename; `--out grade.json`; 2-check cap; "run as soon as candidates settle"); fix `SKILL.md:80` stale v6 stamp; CHANGELOG v8 row.
3. **Brief + docs** (20–30 min): brief `:213`/`:215`; glossary; `muse-swarm.md` + diagram; new ADR (fix + one-run-one-attempt record + "unverified" convention + 0011:51 amendment note).
4. **Validate without a paid Muse run** (CPU minutes + one optional GPU run):
   - Rerun `test_audit.py` 13/13 and `probe_newpaths.py` 8/8 from `design-lab/synthesis/` (no GPU).
   - Hand-check: apply the checker's steps to round-2's Ready-to-test by reading (expect: per-slot numbers fail level/own-effect rules, together-sum fails combination rule).
   - RECOMMENDED one GPU run through the queue: implemented `check_ready.py` on round-2's finalists (routing-4 + combine-1). Falsifiable expectations: exit 1 (not 2); all three FAIL with routing-on-prompt/combine-on-decode-at-32 reasons; ~21 min. If routing does not FAIL, investigate before round 3.
5. **Round-3 success read-out (checkable by grep + G3):** every `ready` cites a passing `ready-verdict.json`; every Ready-to-test/summary number carries level+file+label; checker `pass` lines exist for every close; any 3-shared-failure shows an approach change or logged reason; Claude's G3 agrees with in-round verdicts (verdict agreement + range overlap per the §9-defined tolerance). If 1–5 hold but 6 fails, the gate is miscalibrated — that becomes round 4's starting point, not a swarm failure.
6. **Regression/monitors/rollback:** transcripts show one-run-per-attempt still holds; `provenance_check.py` clean; tags untouched; `engine_table.py` still renders in-round jsonl. Monitors M1–M4: check count + wall time/round; in-round vs post-round deltas; missing-signature audit; counter firings and switch outcomes. Rollback: delete tool + revert v8 commit.

---

## 8. Test evidence

Every run below was executed; commands and files are cited. Tracked tree untouched throughout (`git status` → only `?? design-lab/` before and after every GPU run).

**Phase 1 (explorers):**

Fixed grader protocol vs free G3 flags.

B: 5/5 wrapper + claim recast (8 defects) / conforming (pass) + ledger replay ([test-results/](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/designer-b/test-results/)). C: 13/13 audit + schema dry-run + **live T-live** `check_ready.py … routing=…/routing/attempt-4` → [ready-routing-a4/](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/designer-c/results/ready-routing-a4/), 9:09, exit 1, prompt-slower FAIL reproducing ADR 0011's demotion.

**Phase 3 (testers):**

- Tester-a: live `check_submission.py catch routing=…/attempt-4 combine=…/attempt-1` → [catch/](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/tester-a/catch/), 20:49, exit 1, routing/combine/muse-all FAIL matching Claude sign-for-sign and reason-for-reason. ---

## 9. Risks and decisions for surucuonur

**Decisions (before implementing):**

1. **K=3 and verdict-stands (no noise tiebreak)?** All three designs converge on K=3 from round-2 evidence; precision-over-recall should be an explicit yes/no.
2. **Who runs the check — lead (recommended) or a helper?** Lead deviates from `SKILL.md:32` ("you don't grade yourself") but costs no new card and no contention; fallback is a 10-line `runner.md` with no other change.
3. **Define AC6 operationally now:** verdict agreement, or range overlap with what tolerance? Cross-session drift (~0.1–0.2 ms) exceeds within-session spread at some settings — without a number, "agrees within noise" is not checkable.
4. **One-line `tokens` audit field in `repeat_fixes.py` now or after round 3?** Additive field, no behaviour change, but touches Claude's path. Without it, a direct `--tokens 9` run + forged marker passes the audit.
5. **Confirm the 2-check cap** (committable GPU budget) and **batched-only gating** (2–3× cheaper; a piece-passing/request-failing hypothesis surfaces late — accepted?).
6. **Accept checker compliance as the unremovable residual**, with the M3 post-round signature audit as backstop. No design can prove contributor-model compliance before round 3.

**Risks (residual, accepted with containment):** full-log fabrication (contained by independent G3 + transcripts); skipped/forged checker signature (detected post-round, not prevented — prevention needs hooks, rejected); noise-killed real improvements (precision over recall); 4-workload overfitting shared by in- and post-round G3 (carried in Unverified); 16 GB swap during vLLM (late scheduling + paused helper starts); no live PASS exists anywhere — the gate's pass path at live scale is exercised only synthetically, so AC6 on a passing submission is prediction until round 3. Out of scope, noted: `check_sizes.py` in-round use, lock-bypass detection, `PROVENANCE.md:42` contradiction.

---

## 10. Gate tables

**Reviewer (blind: X=designer-b, Y=designer-a, Z=designer-c; full text in [review.md](/Users/onur/Desktop/Github/Hackathon-muse/design-lab/reviewer/review.md)):**

| Gate | X (designer-b) | Y (designer-a) | Z (designer-c) |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 root cause | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| G2 fits code | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| G3 integrity | **FAIL** (forged g3 sails through) | **FAIL** (forged g3 exits 0) | PASS (recompute-and-compare) |
| G4 failures/recovery | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| G5 feasible/testable | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| G6 cohesive/proportionate | PASS | PASS | PASS |

Strongest: **Z** — only all-PASS; deciding difference is tool-evidence integrity, plus best failure handling (crash-vs-verdict), batched cost, close-time checking, honest residuals. Caveat: Z's combination path was synthetic-only → closed by the synthesis live 2-slot run (§8).

**Lead's recheck of the synthesis (Z + transplants 1–5 + null guard):**

| Gate | Synthesis | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | PASS | Same root-cause closure; live 2-slot FAIL reproduces Claude's verdicts |
| G2 | PASS | Additive; explicit argv; medians additive; grade.json safe per `load()` |
| G3 | PASS | Recompute closes forgery (tested); null → clean exit 2 (tested) |
| G4 | PASS | F1–F10 + cap + crash distinction; tokens gap disclosed as decision |
| G5 | PASS | Prototype + 13/13 + 8/8 + live run; pre-round validation specified |
| G6 | PASS | Each transplant fixes a demonstrated gap; no new machinery |

Acceptance criteria: AC1 (level+file+label + checker), AC2 (`ready` ⇔ passing verdict vs both bars), AC3 (own-effect + measured `muse-all`), AC4 (Unverified, never free), AC5 (3-shared-failures + anti-rename + escape hatch), AC6 (same protocol in-round; verdict agreement validated live on FAILs, PASS path pending round 3).

---

**Helpers started (11):** explorer-skill (skill/brief instructions), explorer-tools (measurement tools + gaming surface), explorer-rounds (round records, behaviour instances), explorer-findings (predictions vs measured, ADRs, contracts) · designer-a (existing-system-first), designer-b (contract-and-data-first), designer-c (failure-and-evolution-first) · tester-a/b/c (independent live test of each design) · reviewer (blind G1–G6 review) · synthesis-tester (synthesized gate confirmation run).
