results.text:
Read text file `design-lab/brief.md`.
1|# Solution design brief: make the Muse agent swarm pursue real efficiency, not its proxies (v1)
2|
3|## APPROVAL
4|- User approved this brief on 2026-11-04 (surucuonur). Decisions: the swarm may run end-to-end checks in-round through the GPU queue; Meta's Muse does the design work; from round 3 the launcher runs muse-spark-1.3-contributor with tool approvals off (ADR 0012, commit 1113c2d).
5|- Approved activity: one Muse Code session (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) whose lead starts its own helper agents, up to 12 at once, with no cost or time limit. Agents may prototype and test in design-lab/ (untracked, never committed) and run the measurement tools through the GPU queue. The repository's tracked files stay unchanged.
6|
7|## PROBLEM AND OUTCOME
8|- **Current problem:** two rounds of the Muse agent swarm (round 1: Muse Spark; round 2: Muse Wonder, 63 min, ~$58) produced no kernel that is a real efficiency improvement, while the swarm's own reports predicted gains. Five behaviours, each with evidence:
9|  1. **Treats unmeasured costs as free.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`: "Prefill speed is not timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart from time to first token", citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`. The result: experts attempt-7 is 16–28× slower than the compiled reference at prefill sizes, and routing attempt-4 2.6–8.7× slower (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`). Prompts took 6.6–14.5× and 7–10% longer, and throughput fell by up to 83% (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §5).
10|  2. **Claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Expected G3 = (compiled − candidate) µs × 20 layers (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md` *Ready to test*; `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`). Round 1 predicted −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.98/+0.16/−1.76. Round 2 predicted −0.84 at each and measured −0.73/−0.74/+0.53 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`, `muse-round-2.md`).
11|  3. **Reasons inconsistently.** The same README says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then reports "Together (sum) −0.84 ms". Combine's −0.35 ms prediction is −0.07 to −0.09 from its own timing plus −0.27 to −0.29 borrowed from what `mx.compile` gains end to end. Measured: +1.05 ms with 32 requests.
12|  4. **Used the grader as a search loop (round 1).** 29 grader runs on experts for 4 counted attempts, 18 on attempt-1 with edits between (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §5). Fixed since skill v4: one run is one attempt; round 2 ran 13 for 13.
13|  5. **Persists with a failing design family.** All 7 experts attempts in round 2 are fused kernels that lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs per layer). The cause, too few threadgroups at 1 row, was already known from round 1. The harden loop says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" (`.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:138`), and there is no rule for changing design.
14|- **Root cause** (likely; supported by the evidence above): inside a round, the swarm never sees the real objective. Its feedback is a per-slot proxy, the grader's piece timing. The real measurement, Claude's G3 over whole requests, arrives only after the round. The swarm's claims are self-reported and checked by no one before the summary.
15|  - *verified:* the rules forbid an in-round model run: `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:152` "Load no model and start no other GPU work" and `SKILL.md:164` "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team".
16|  - *verified:* the goal is phrased as passing gates (`SKILL.md:20`).
17|  - *verified:* the verifier checks only exploration's inefficiency entries (`verifier.md`). No one checks the implementation phase's predictions, combination claims or Ready-to-test arithmetic.
18|  - *partly fixed:* ADR 0011 (commit `2090949`) now times the prefill (grader at 6 sizes, G3 with prompt and whole-request time, 5 repeats), so behaviour 1's specific gap is closed. The general habit, treating anything outside the measurement as free, is not addressed.
19|- **Intended outcome:** in round 3 and later, the swarm's statements about speed match what Claude's independent G3 then measures. It marks something ready only when it is a real improvement under the ADR 0011 rule (faster in one phase, prefill or decode, slower in neither, no whole request slower). It stops repeating a design that keeps failing at the same point.
20|- **Why now:** surucuonur asked how to fix "these essential problems and behaviour of these agents". The hackathon deadline is 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, about 11.5 h from 14:30 UTC on 2026-11-04. Round 3 should run with the fix.
21|- **Maturity:** hackathon research tool; judges read the repo, the skill and the round documents.
22|- **User's suggested approach:** none given. Claude has suggested an in-round end-to-end check and prediction rules; treat these as hypotheses, not constraints.
23|
24|## SCOPE AND SUCCESS
25|- **In scope:**
26|  - the round skill (`.agents/skills/muse-round/`: SKILL.md, the role cards, tracking.md);
27|  - the brief (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md`);
28|  - the measurement tools the swarm may call (`bench/grader/`, `bench/micro/` entry points);
29|  - `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` if needed;
30|  - the docs that describe these (ADR, glossary, `claude/muse-swarm.md`, diagrams).
31|- **Out of scope:**
32|  - changing the model or the engine;
33|  - Claude's post-round measurement process, beyond what it needs to compare claims;
34|  - running round 3 itself;
35|  - Muse Code itself.
36|- **Observable acceptance criteria:**
37|  1. Every speed claim in a round's READMEs and summary is either backed by a measurement made in the round, with its run file cited, of exactly what is claimed (the slot or combination, at the end-to-end level claimed), or labelled as a prediction and shown next to the measured value.
38|  2. No hypothesis reaches `ready`, and no attempt goes to *Ready to test*, unless an in-round check shows it improves under ADR 0011's rule, against the unchanged model and the compiled reference.
39|  3. Predictions count only the candidate's own measured effect, and a combination's effect is measured as a combination.
40|  4. Anything the swarm did not measure is listed as unverified, never assumed free or neutral.
41|  5. After a stated number of failures of one design at the same size or phase for the same cause, the next attempt changes approach, or the log records why not.
42|  6. Claude's post-round G3 agrees with the swarm's in-round measured claims within the noise of the repeats. This is the ultimate test.
43|- **Quality guardrails:**
44|  - proportionate and simple: surucuonur rejected sandbox and guard-hook hardening before (memory `muse-isolation-simple`);
45|  - keep the documents readable by judges;
46|  - keep Muse-facing instructions in the repo.
47|
48|## VERIFIED SYSTEM CONTEXT
49|- **Launch:** `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` (`:71` first prompt "Run the muse-round skill…", `:136` `muse exec … -c agents.execution_capacity=12`). One Muse Code session per round, in worktree `../Hackathon-muse` on branch `muse-agent`, on the Meta Model API. Round 2 ran `muse-wonder-1.0` with approvals on; from step 0 the default is `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` with approvals off.
50|- **The swarm** (`SKILL.md:22-38`):
51|  - the lead coordinates and commits, but never explores, builds or grades;
52|  - explorers write `exploration/territory-*.md` and `ineff-*.md`;
53|  - the verifier confirms or refutes inefficiencies;
54|  - builders write and grade one attempt each (`builder.md`);
55|  - boundary agents write and check a hypothesis's boundary (`boundary.md`);
56|  - shared docs and logs per phase (`tracking.md`), checkpoints commit them.
57|- **Steps** (`SKILL.md`): 0 find where you are, 1 starting point, 2 exploration, 3 the analysis, 4 implementation (open hypothesis → boundary → compete → collect → harden → close `ready`/`dropped`), 5 finish (READMEs, *Ready to test*, summary).
58|- **Measurement tools:**
59|  - **`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`:** G1/G2 bit-exact at 6 sizes; paired piece timing with a sign test; `beats_compiled`/`beats_baseline` per ADR 0011; takes the GPU lock; loads the model on every run (ADR 0010).
60|  - **`bench/grader/time_candidates.py`:** end-to-end check and G3.
61|    - Engines: `plain` (MLX) or `vllm`.
62|    - Variants: base, compiled-<slot>, muse-<slot>, muse-all, `--variant`.
63|    - G2 compares greedy tokens; G3 records decode step, prompt time (vLLM only) and wall time; `--repeats` defaults to 5; writes `g3-vllm.json`.
64|    - Duration: about 8.5 s per run on average in vLLM, so roughly 10–12 min per candidate with base and compiled at 4 settings × 5 repeats.
65|    - The plain engine has no prompt time yet (`bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py:prompt_ms`, `breakdown.run_plain`).
66|  - **`bench/grader/gpu_lock.py`:** one GPU job at a time; later ones wait.
67|- **Isolation and provenance:**
68|  - git hooks refuse Muse commits outside `muse-spark/`, changes to finished rounds' files, and merges;
69|  - `tools/provenance_check.py` audits authorship;
70|  - Claude merges each round, measures it independently (G3) and writes `claude/findings/muse-round-<N>.md`, which the next round reads as its starting point.
71|- **Round 3's starting point:** no baseline in any slot (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` *For round 3*).
72|- **Revision:** main at `2090949`, working tree clean apart from two uncommitted pilot files.
73|
74|## PROTECTED CONTRACTS AND BEHAVIORS
75|- Authorship separation: the Muse agent writes only in `muse-spark/`, only the lead commits, with the Muse co-author line; Claude never commits on `muse-agent`; hooks and provenance check stay.
76|- Finished rounds stay frozen (tags `muse-round-1`, `muse-round-2`).
77|- Muse Code only, swarm design (ADR 0007), no attempt limit (ADR 0006: "limitless"), one grader run per attempt, the GPU queue.
78|- Grading rules of ADR 0010/0011 (bit-exact at 6 sizes, both phases, hand-off via `max_rows`); G2's token check.
79|- Claude's post-round independent measurement remains the authority for baselines.
80|- The attempt format (`spec.json` + `block-N.metal`) and the grader's JSON verdict keys (`g1`, `g2`, `beats_compiled`, `beats_baseline`, `timing_us_per_layer`, `phases_vs_compiled`).
81|
82|## CONSTRAINTS AND OPERATIONAL REALITY
83|- **Machine:** M1 Pro, 16 GB, heavy swapping (19–20 GB swap in use); one GPU job at a time. vLLM needs `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` (now the default in `breakdown.py`) and Docker quit. 1-request vLLM timings are noisy (6–41% spread).
84|- **Time:** about 11.5 h to the deadline, including implementing the fix, running round 3 (~1–2 h), and Claude's measurement and findings (~1 h). The fix should be implementable and checkable in roughly 2–3 h.
85|- **Cost:** round 2 on Muse Wonder cost about $58; on the contributor model a round costs about $1 (round 1: $0.70). Claude never runs `start.sh` or calls the Meta API without asking.
86|- **Hard constraints:** the protected items above, and the deadline.
87|- **Preferences:** simple over airtight (no sandboxing or guard hooks); rules phrased positively for agents (writing-for-agents guidance).
88|- **Decided:** round 3 runs on `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, round 1's model, which ADR 0008 judged less capable than Muse Wonder, with tool approvals off. No one approves tool calls during the round, so rules must hold without a human watching. Instructions must be explicit and checkable, since a less capable model follows general advice less reliably.
89|
90|## FAILURE MODES AND FUTURE CHANGES
91|- **Goodhart risk:** any new check becomes the next proxy. A design must say how the swarm could game it.
92|- **GPU queue contention:** a 10–12 min end-to-end check blocks builders' grader runs.
93|- **Memory:** a vLLM run inside the round competes with Muse Code's own processes and may page.
94|- **Noise:** at 1 request, end-to-end verdicts are mostly `same`.
95|- **Partial rounds:** a session can stop mid-round, and checks must leave the shared documents consistent.
96|- **The model can ignore instructions:** round 1 ignored "one attempt per grader run" before it became an explicit rule.
97|- **Future:** more slots or a different model; rounds 4+; possibly other engines.
98|- **Prior pitfalls:**
99|  - independent piece timing hid latency (fixed by ADR 0010);
100|  - tolerances let the tokens change (fixed by ADR 0010);
101|  - prefill was untimed (fixed by ADR 0011);
102|  - G3 with 3 repeats falsely flagged unchanged phases (fixed with 5 repeats).
103|
104|## DESIGN EXPECTATIONS
105|- Deliver one coherent approach that fixes the root cause (the gap between the proxy and the objective, and unchecked self-reports) and covers behaviours 1–5, not one patch per symptom.
106|- Address whole-system effects: the GPU queue and round duration, memory, Claude's post-round role, the docs and judges.
107|- Cite repository evidence; distinguish verified facts from proposals.
108|- Specify the changes to the skill, cards, brief and tools, plus any new measurement entry point, at the level of what each says or does.
109|- Define how a future implementation is validated before round 3, without a paid Muse run if possible, and how round 3's own outcome would show success.
110|- Do not edit the repository's tracked code, data or configuration; prototypes and tests live in design-lab/.
111|
112|## UNRESOLVED ASSUMPTIONS AND STOP CONDITIONS
113|- **Decided (surucuonur, 2026-11-04):** the swarm may run an end-to-end check itself during the round, through the GPU queue. This replaces "Load no model…" (`tracking.md:152`) and "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team" (`SKILL.md:164`) as needed. Claude's post-round G3 remains the independent authority.
114|- **Assumed (unanswered):** the fix must be ready for round 3 before 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, implementable and checkable in about 2–3 h.
115|- **Assumption:** the Muse agent follows explicit, checkable rules better than general advice (round 2 kept "one run per attempt" once it was a rule).
116|- **Return BLOCKED if:** the design requires breaking a protected contract, or depends on a Muse Code capability not documented here.

1|---
2|name: muse-round
3|description: Run one round of the Muse agent on the MobileMoE-S kernels as a swarm. Explorers map the code and measurements into a shared analysis; then competing builders write and grade fused Metal kernels for the top inefficiencies. From round 2 on, the round starts from the previous rounds' results and must beat their best attempts. Both phases are tracked in shared documents.
4|---
5|
6|# One round of the Muse agent: a swarm explores, then builds
7|
8|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed on main and tagged `muse-code-era` before the first Muse Code session; each later version is committed before the round that uses it. [Who made what](../../../PROVENANCE.md).*
9|
10|**Skill version 7.** This file, the role cards and tracking.md are versioned together; [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) lists every version. Each round records the version it ran (see *Versions* in tracking.md).
11|
12|You are the **lead** of a Muse Code session in your own worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. The first prompt names the Meta model you run as, the name your commit subjects start with, and the co-author line every commit ends with. `claude/muse-agent-brief.md` fixes the task, the slots, the tools and limits, the grader command and the pass criteria (G1, G2). Four ADRs change it in five ways:
13|
14|1. **Harness** ([ADR 0006](../../../claude/adr/0006-muse-spark-in-muse-code.md)). You are a Muse Code session, not a Claude Code one. Muse Code adds no trailer, so you write the first prompt's co-author line on every commit yourself (see *Commits*).
15|2. **No attempt limit and no stop rule** (ADR 0006). The brief's *When a slot stops* no longer applies: you decide when a slot is done. Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try.
16|3. **A swarm** ([ADR 0007](../../../claude/adr/0007-muse-spark-swarm.md)). Helpers explore and build; you coordinate and commit.
17|4. **Files** (ADR 0007, [ADR 0009](../../../claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md)). Each round writes in its own **round folder**: round 1 at the top of `muse-spark/`, round N from 2 on in `muse-spark/round-<N>/`. It holds `exploration/` and `implementation/`, the round's shared documents, which replace `strategy.md`; `kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<M>/`; and `summary.md`. tracking.md writes it `<round>/`.
18|5. **Rounds build on each other** (ADR 0009). A finished round's files are frozen: read them and cite them, and the hooks refuse any change to them. From round 2 on, a slot may have a **baseline**: the best attempt so far that passes the current G2 and that Claude's G3 accepted: against the unchanged model and the compiled reference, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A new attempt must beat it in the same grader run. A slot without one has a **starting point** instead: an earlier attempt to build from, which Claude's measurement names, with what kept it from being a baseline.
19|
20|The rest of the brief stands. The goal: kernels that pass G1 and G2 and have `beats_compiled` true, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither (ADR 0011); where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline` true too; faster because they remove a cause you can name. A faster decode step bought with a slower prefill is no improvement. An attempt built for decode sizes may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference with `max_rows` (the brief's launch spec). The Muse agent was Muse Spark in round 1 and Muse Wonder in round 2 ([ADR 0008](../../../claude/adr/0008-muse-wonder.md)), and is Muse Spark's contributor model again from round 3 ([ADR 0012](../../../claude/adr/0012-muse-spark-contributor-unattended.md)); the first prompt names the model you run as, and documents from earlier rounds say the model of their round. No one approves your tool calls during the round, so the rules here are yours to keep.
21|
22|## The swarm
23|
24|| Role | Name | Task | Card |
25||---|---|---|---|
26|| **Lead** (you) | | Start the helpers, keep the two READMEs, settle clashes, commit | this file |
27|| **Explorer** | `explorer-<territory>` | Map one territory into entries, and find where it loses time | [explorer.md](explorer.md) |
28|| **Verifier** | `verifier` | Check every inefficiency against its sources | [verifier.md](verifier.md) |
29|| **Builder** | `builder-<n>-<letter>` | Write and grade one solution for one hypothesis: one attempt | [builder.md](builder.md) |
30|| **Boundary agent** | `boundary-<n>` | Write what a hypothesis's solution must keep identical, and check passing attempts against it | [boundary.md](boundary.md) |
31|
32|You don't explore, build or grade yourself. Start each helper with a prompt of this shape:
33|
34|> You are `<name>`, a `<role>` in round `<N>`'s swarm; this round writes in `<round folder>`. Read `.agents/skills/muse-round/<card>` and `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md`, then: `<task>`.
35|
36|[tracking.md](tracking.md) describes the shared documents (the two phase folders, their READMEs, entries and logs) and the rules every agent keeps. Read it before starting anyone. Up to 12 agents run at once, you included.
37|
38|**A checkpoint** is what you do each time a helper returns, and whenever the log shows something to settle:
39|1. **Read the log.** Read the phase log since your last checkpoint.
40|2. **Settle clashes.** When two entries describe one cause, keep the fuller one and set the other's status to `superseded by <entry>`. When two helpers work on one item, redirect one of them (`subagent_send_message`). Log what you decided.
41|3. **Refresh the tracker.** Update the phase README's tracker table, and raise the version of each hypothesis entry that changed.
42|4. **Raise the version.** Raise the phase README to its next version, and add its line to `## Versions`, naming the entries that changed and their versions (see *Versions* in tracking.md).
43|5. **Commit** the phase folder, plus any attempt that came back, as that version (see *Commits*).
44|
45|## The round
46|
47|### 0. Find where you are
48|
49|- Run `git log --oneline main -1`, then `git tag --list -n1 'muse-round-*'`, which lists the finished rounds. **This round** is one more than the highest; with none, it is round 1. Its folder is `muse-spark/round-<N>/` (round 1: `muse-spark/`).
50|- `git log --oneline --grep '^Muse ' muse-code-era..HEAD` lists the Muse agent's commits of every round.
51|- **From round 2 on,** read Claude's measurement of the previous round, `claude/findings/muse-round-<N-1>.md`. It has the G3 results and names each slot's baseline or starting point. If it is missing, stop and reply "Claude's measurement of round <N-1> is missing": this round builds on it.
52|- If this round's folder already exists, a session stopped partway: carry on from its READMEs' last versions.
53|- Read the brief.
54|
55|**Done** when you can name the round number and its folder, and from round 2 on each slot's baseline or starting point and the latest G3 results.
56|
57|### 1. The starting point (from round 2 on)
58|
59|This is the round's plan, built on what the earlier rounds learned. Read:
60|- the previous rounds' final exploration and implementation READMEs and `summary.md`;
61|- the `notes.md` of each baseline or starting-point attempt;
62|- Claude's measurement.
63|
64|Then write the opening of this round's `exploration/README.md` (set up as in step 2.1), a section **Starting point**:
65|- **Per slot:**
66|  - the baseline, or the starting point where there is none, and its piece timing;
67|  - its G3 effect, and how that compares with what was predicted, with the reason where Claude's measurement gives one;
68|  - what keeps a starting point from passing G2, and where the attempt still spends its time.

70|  - the confirmed inefficiencies not yet built or not fully removed, ranked by predicted saving against the baselines, or the reference where a slot has none;
71|  - the slots not yet tried, for example `routing+combine`;
72|  - the recommendations outside the slots.
73|- **Refuted claims,** which no one chases again.
74|- **Territories** this round opens (step 2.2), each with the line of this section that reopens it.
75|
76|Commit it as exploration v1. **Done** when every slot has its baseline or starting point and every territory has its reason.
77|
78|### 2. Exploration
79|
80|1. **Set up the folder.** Write `<round>/exploration/README.md` with a heading, its version line (v1, with skill version 6), the tracker (one row per territory) and `## Versions`, and an empty `log.md`.
81|2. **Start the explorers and the verifier,** all at once.
82|   - **Round 1** starts with these territories:
83|
84|     | Territory | Covers |
85|     |---|---|
86|     | `model` | `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py`: the decoder layer, `MoE.__call__` and everything around the slots |
87|     | `switch-layers` | `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py`: the routed experts' path, `gather_qmm`, the sort from 16 rows |
88|     | `quantized-kernels` | `quantized.h` and `quantized_utils.h` in `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mlx/include/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/`: the `affine_gather_*` kernels behind `gather_qmm` |
89|     | `other-kernels` | the other Metal kernels in the same folder that the routing and combine slots launch: sort, softmax, reductions, elementwise, copies |
90|     | `vllm-metal` | `third_party/vllm-metal/vllm_metal/`: how the engine runs a decode step and a prefill chunk around the model |
91|     | `grader` | `bench/grader/`: the slot interface, what G1, G2 and the piece timing measure, and so the boundary every solution keeps |
92|     | `findings` | `claude/findings/` and `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/` |
93|     | `runs` | `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/`, `2026-10-29-baseline/` and `2026-10-30-micro/` |
94|
95|   - **From round 2 on,** the starting point lists the territories:
96|     - `baseline-<slot>` for each slot: its baseline's kernels and `spec.json`, which are now the code in the slot, or its starting point's. Map them with the checklist, and find where they still lose time and, for a starting point, why it fails G2;
97|     - `g3`: Claude's measurement of the previous round, where the end-to-end change differs from the piece timing, and why;
98|     - of round 1's territories, only those the starting point reopens. An explorer starts from that territory's earlier entries and writes only what is new.
99|3. **Refocus as costs show up.** When an entry shows that one file holds most of a territory's cost, split it off as a territory of its own, with its own explorer. Merge or close a territory that turns out to hold nothing, and add one when an inefficiency points somewhere no one covers. Log each change and update the tracker.
100|4. **Checkpoint** each time a helper returns.
101|
102|**Done** when every territory entry is `done`, the verifier has returned, and every inefficiency is `confirmed`, `refuted` or `superseded`.
103|
104|### 3. The analysis
105|
106|Write the final `<round>/exploration/README.md`. It is the round's report on the code, for this round's builders and for future improvements:
107|
108|- **Tracker:** the final table.
109|- **Starting point** (from round 2 on), as written in step 1, with any correction exploration made.
110|- **Context:** the decode step and the prefill, the MoE block and its slots, and what the measurements say about where the time goes in each.
111|- **Territory map:** how the territories feed each other. For each territory: what it receives, what it passes on, and its measured cost.
112|- **Inefficiencies, ranked:**
113|  - the confirmed ones inside the slots, ranked by predicted saving as a share of the decode step, averaged over 1, 8 and 32 rows, or of the prefill chunk, averaged over 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows; from round 2 on, the saving is against the baseline where the slot has one;
114|  - each with what removing it does to the other phase, and whether a hand-off (`max_rows`) keeps that phase unchanged;
115|  - each with its cost, kind and entry;
116|  - Claude's findings marked as Claude's, earlier rounds' entries linked as theirs, and this round's own reading marked as yours.
117|- **Recommendations:** the confirmed inefficiencies outside the slots, with their evidence. They're for surucuonur's team.
118|- **Refuted claims,** in one line each, so no one chases them again.
119|- **Files read:** links to each territory entry's list.
120|
121|Commit it. **Done** when every ranked item links a confirmed entry and every number in the README has its source.
122|
123|### 4. Implementation
124|
125|Take the ranked inefficiencies in order, at most two at a time, in different slots so their attempts never touch. Write `<round>/implementation/README.md` with a heading, its version line, the tracker and `## Versions`, and an empty `log.md`. For each hypothesis:
126|
127|1. **Open the hypothesis.** Write `<round>/implementation/hyp-<n>-<slug>.md`, with status `boundary`, the inefficiency, the slot and, from round 2 on, the slot's baseline folder or `none`. Add its tracker row and log it.
128|2. **Draw its boundary.** Start `boundary-<n>` to write the boundary, and wait for it.
129|3. **Compete.**
130|   - Set the status to `building`.
131|   - Start 2 or 3 builders, `builder-<n>-a`, `-b` and `-c`. Give each a different direction drawn from the analysis: for example, fusing kernels, reading each weight byte once, or a different threadgroup shape. From round 2 on, a direction may start from the baseline's or starting point's kernels, or from scratch.
132|4. **Collect.** Each time a builder returns:
133|   - checkpoint, committing its attempt folder with the hypothesis entry, the README and the log;
134|   - if the attempt passed G2, start `boundary-<n>` to check it.
135|5. **Harden.**
136|   - Pick the best attempt: it passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, has `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline`, and it is the fastest across the six sizes.

143|Then open the next-ranked inefficiency. **Done** when no confirmed inefficiency is left that you judge will pay. Write why in the implementation README.
144|
145|### 5. Finish
146|
147|1. **The implementation README:** the final tracker, one paragraph per hypothesis, and a **Ready to test** section. It names the attempt per slot that goes to G3, this round's, the baseline kept, or the reference, and the change you expect in G3's four workloads, in the decode step, the prompt time and the whole request, against the previous round's, with how you worked it out.
148|2. **The exploration README:** add *What building taught*, the analysis corrected by what the attempts showed.
149|3. **`<round>/summary.md`:** a `## Round N` section with:
150|   - the model, the skill version this round ran, and the final versions of both READMEs;
151|   - the final attempt per slot;
152|   - the number of graded attempts per slot, this round and over all rounds;
153|   - the expected G3 change;
154|   - what you'd try next;
155|   - your recommendations outside the slots.

157|
158|## Your own rules
159|
160|- **Writes:**
161|  - you write the two READMEs, the hypothesis entries' status blocks and decisions, and `summary.md`;
162|  - every helper writes only what its card names;
163|  - all of it stays in this round's folder.
164|- **G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team,** who run them after merging your branch.
165|- **The rules every agent keeps** are in tracking.md.
166|
167|## Commits
168|
169|You are the only agent that commits. Commit only on `muse-agent`.
170|- **What to add:** this round's phase folders that exist so far (only `exploration` until implementation starts) and the attempt folders that came back. An attempt another builder is still writing waits for its own commit. An entry that is mid-edit is committed as it stands, and finished in a later commit.
171|- **The message:**
172|  - every subject starts with the name the first prompt gives you, then a colon;
173|  - a checkpoint's subject is `<name>: <phase> v<N>: <what changed>`, the version it records;
174|  - every message ends with the first prompt's co-author line, exactly.
175|
176|For example, in round 2 as Muse Wonder:
177|
178|```bash
179|git add muse-spark/round-2/exploration muse-spark/round-2/implementation muse-spark/round-2/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<M>
180|git commit -m "Muse Wonder: implementation v4: experts attempt 3 graded, beats baseline" \
181|  -m "Co-Authored-By: Muse Wonder (Meta Model API) <muse-wonder@meta-model-api.invalid>"
182|```

1|# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write faster MobileMoE-S kernels, for decoding and prompt processing
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|You are a Claude Code session powered by Meta's Muse Spark, working in your own git worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. This brief fixes your task, what you may change, where your work goes and how it is judged. It does not change during your session.
6|
7|## The task
8|
9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.
10|
11|A request goes through two phases: **prompt processing** (the prefill), which runs its whole prompt through the model, and **decoding**, one step per generated token. An improvement must hold in both: faster in one, and no slower in the other ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A kernel that speeds up the decode step but slows the prefill is not an improvement.
12|
13|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
14|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
15|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.
16|
17|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
18|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
19|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
20|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
21|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
22|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
23|
24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
29|
30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
50|
51|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
52|
53|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
54||---|---|---|---|
55|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
56|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
57|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
58|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
59|
60|Reference:
61|
62|```python
63|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
64|```
65|
66|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
67|
68|### `routing+combine`
69|
70|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
71|
72|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
73|
74|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
75||---|---|---|---|
76|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
77|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
78|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
79|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
80|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
81|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
82|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
83|
84|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
85|
86|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
87|
88|```python
89|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
90|```
91|
92|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
93|
94|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
95|
96|## Tools and limits
97|
98|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.
99|- **The grader runs no Python of yours.** It reads your launch spec as data and compiles only your Metal.
100|- **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes, longer for an attempt much slower than the reference at the prefill sizes; stop one that runs past 15.
101|- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.
102|
103|## Rules of this session
104|
105|These keep your work apart from everyone else's. Git hooks and an audit script enforce them, and a commit that breaks them is refused.
106|
107|- **Write only inside `muse-spark/`.** Never change `bench/`, `claude/`, `results/`, `tools/`, `third_party/`, or any other file. A copy of the grader you edit is never used.
108|- **Commit only on `muse-agent`,** with the co-author trailer your settings add: `Co-Authored-By: Muse Spark (Meta Model API) <muse-spark@meta-model-api.invalid>`. Start each subject with `Muse Spark:`. No other co-author.
109|- **Never push, merge, rebase, change git config, or skip hooks.**
110|- **Don't read `.env`** or any credentials file.
111|- One commit per attempt, after you've run the grader on it, so the history shows every attempt in order.
112|
113|## Your files
114|
115|```
116|muse-spark/
117|  strategy.md                                your choice and design, ending with the targets JSON
118|  kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/
119|    block-0.metal, block-1.metal, ...        Metal kernel bodies (and headers), numbered from 0
120|    spec.json                                the launch spec
121|    notes.md                                 optional: what you tried and why
122|  summary.md                                 your final attempt per slot
123|```
124|
125|`<slot-folder>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing-combine` or `experts`. Grade an attempt with:
126|
127|```bash
128|.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N> <slot>
129|```
130|
131|where `<slot>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing+combine` or `experts`.
132|
133|**The targets JSON** at the end of `strategy.md`:
134|
135|```json
136|{
137|  "targets": [
138|    {"slot": "routing+combine", "why": "...", "expected_saving_ms": {"rows_1": 0.0, "rows_32": 0.0}, "design": "..."}
139|  ]
140|}
141|```
142|
143|List one or two targets, in the order you work on them.
144|
145|**The launch spec** (`spec.json`):
146|
147|```json
148|{
149|  "kernels": [
150|    {
151|      "name": "fused_routing",
152|      "source_block": 0,
153|      "header_block": null,
154|      "inputs": ["x", "w_router", "bias"],
155|      "outputs": [
156|        {"name": "inds", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "uint32"},
157|        {"name": "weights", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "float32"}
158|      ],
159|      "grid": ["rows*32", 1, 1],
160|      "threadgroup": [32, 1, 1],
161|      "template": {"T": "bfloat16"},
162|      "init_value": null,
163|      "atomic_outputs": false
164|    }
165|  ],
166|  "slot_outputs": {"inds": "inds", "weights": "weights"}
167|}
168|```
169|
170|- **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
171|- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
172|- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
173|- **`max_rows`** (optional, an integer of at least 1): inputs with more rows than this skip your kernels and run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. Use it to keep prefill-sized inputs on MLX's own code when your kernels are built for decode sizes; MLX switches its own experts kernel at 60 rows. The hand-off is graded like the rest: bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes.
174|- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot, `max_rows` included: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
175|- **Shape and grid entries** are integers, or products of integers and the names `rows`, `D`, `E`, `K` and `H`, such as `"rows*32"`. Nothing else is evaluated.
176|- **dtypes** are `float32`, `bfloat16`, `float16`, `uint32` or `int32`.
177|- **Template values** are one of those dtypes, an integer or a boolean.
178|- **`grid`** counts threads, not threadgroups, as in `mx.fast.metal_kernel`.
179|
180|## How each attempt is judged
181|
182|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only. From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.
183|
184|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
185|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
186|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
187|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
188|
189|   At every size:
190|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
191|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
192|
193|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
194|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
195|3. **G3, faster, in vLLM.** Each workload runs 5 times in shuffled order: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts, 256 generated tokens each. Three times are measured per run:
196|   - the **decode step**, the median period between steady steps;
197|   - the **prompt time**, until every prompt was processed;
198|   - the **whole request**, from sending the requests to the last token.
199|
200|   Against both the original model and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code, the attempt passes when the decode step or the prompt time is faster in every workload, neither is slower in any, and no whole request is slower. Faster and slower mean that the ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
201|
202|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
203|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
204|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
205|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same` or `slower`); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.
206|
207|**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
208|- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
209|- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
210|- **Per phase:** decode (1, 8, 32 rows) and prefill (127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) are each `faster` when every size is, `slower` when any size is, and `not slower` otherwise.
211|- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
212|
213|It is a guide; G3 decides.
214|
215|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and has `beats_compiled` true, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

tool_calls.args:
{"content":"# Explorer-skill report: what `.agents/skills/muse-round/` and `claude/muse-agent-brief.md` say that bears on behaviours 1–5

Territory: `.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md`, `explorer.md`, `verifier.md`, `builder.md`, `boundary.md`, `tracking.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `claude/muse-agent-brief.md`. Skill version 7 (`SKILL.md:10`). Read at worktree commit 1113c2d (brief says 2090949; see §Corrections).

No GPU work was run: every claim below is textual (file:line quotes), so no measurement result files exist for this report.

## Territory facts (shared by all behaviours)

- T1. The goal is phrased purely as passing gates. `SKILL.md:20`: "The goal: kernels that pass G1 and G2 and have `beats_compiled` true, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither (ADR 0011); where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline` true too; faster because they remove a cause you can name."
- T2. In-round model runs are forbidden twice. `tracking.md:152`: "**The grader is the only GPU job.** Run it only as a builder, through the brief's command; it waits its turn when another run has the GPU. Load no model and start no other GPU work: the machine has 16 GB and slows down sharply when memory runs short." `SKILL.md:164`: "**G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team,** who run them after merging your branch."
- T3. The verifier's scope is exploration only. `verifier.md:5`: "The implementation phase builds only on inefficiencies you confirmed, so every claim an inefficiency rests on is checked against its source before anyone builds on it." Its steps (`verifier.md:9-25`) only ever touch `<round>/exploration/ineff-*.md` (`verifier.md:11`: "Find open entries: `grep -l 'Status:** open' <round>/exploration/ineff-*.md`") and mark them `confirmed`/`refuted` (`verifier.md:17-19`). Nothing in the card mentions hypothesis entries, builder predictions, combination claims, or Ready to test.
- T4. The lead writes all unchecked summary numbers. `SKILL.md:160-161`: "you write the two READMEs, the hypothesis entries' status blocks and decisions, and `summary.md`". Ready to test (`SKILL.md:147`): "It names the attempt per slot that goes to G3, this round's, the baseline kept, or the reference, and the change you expect in G3's four workloads, in the decode step, the prompt time and the whole request, against the previous round's, with how you worked it out." No method, citation, or labelling rule constrains "how you worked it out". The close-`ready` Decision likewise "states what G3 should show" (`tracking.md:113`; `SKILL.md:140`).
- T5. The only cross-cutting number rule is vague. `tracking.md:153`: "**Every number has a source:** a file and line, a table (path and row), a grader verdict (attempt folder), or arithmetic shown in full." Piece arithmetic with its working shown therefore satisfies the letter of the rule.
- T6. The harden loop has a continue rule but no stop-or-switch rule. `SKILL.md:135-138`: pick the best attempt ("passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, has `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline`, and it is the fastest across the six sizes"), "Set the status to `hardening`, and start a builder for that attempt's next single change", "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove." `ready` (`SKILL.md:140`) requires "you can name no further change worth making". Nothing names giving up on a design family, switching approach, or counting repeated failures at the same size/phase/cause.
- T7. The builder self-checks its own prediction with no enforcement. `builder.md:24` requires predicted µs per layer at the six sizes "with the arithmetic"; `builder.md:30`: "If the attempt failed, or its time missed your prediction by more than 20%, find out why. Write the answer in `notes.md`, and add it to the inefficiency entry as a note." No one verifies this happened; the lead only checkpoints (`SKILL.md:38-43`).
- T8. One-run-one-attempt is explicit (behaviour 4's fix). `builder.md:13`: "**One grader run is one attempt.** After a run, any change, even a one-line fix, is a new attempt with its own number, built by copying the files you keep." `CHANGELOG.md:12` dates it to skill v4. `SKILL.md:15` also removes the brief's stop rule: "you decide when a slot is done. Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try."
- T9. Inefficiency entries must state cross-phase effects, but only as predictions. `tracking.md:103`: "**Predicted saving** if removed, in µs per decode step at 1, 8 and 32 rows and per prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows, with the arithmetic. A saving in one phase that costs the other is not one." `SKILL.md:112-114` ranks by "predicted saving" and requires "each with what removing it does to the other phase, and whether a hand-off (`max_rows`) keeps that phase unchanged".
- T10. The brief's own end-to-end language is descriptive, not an in-round procedure. `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:213`: "It is a guide; G3 decides." `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:215`: "Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch." `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:11` states the both-phases rule ("faster in one, and no slower in the other"), and `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:173` documents `max_rows` ("The hand-off is graded like the rest: bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes").
- T11. Explorers predict savings the verifier confirms only against cited sources. `explorer.md:18`: "write an inefficiency entry with its cost arithmetic and predicted saving"; `verifier.md:12-15` checks claims by "open the cited file at the cited lines; find the cited table row; redo the arithmetic". A prediction whose arithmetic is internally consistent and whose inputs are cited therefore passes, even if the inputs don't transfer end to end.

## Behaviour 1: treats unmeasured costs as free

Facts bearing on it: T1, T2, T5, T9, T10.

Where the instructions create or allow it. The goal (T1, `SKILL.md:20`) defines success entirely in grader verdicts, so anything the grader does not time is definitionally irrelevant to passing. The in-round measurement ban (T2, `tracking.md:152`, `SKILL.md:164`) makes it impossible to check anything the grader omits, so "free apart from time to first token" style reasoning is the only available move for unmeasured costs. The cross-phase guard (`tracking.md:103`, `SKILL.md:114`) asks for a prediction ("what removing it does to the other phase"), not a measurement, and the number rule (`tracking.md:153`) accepts shown arithmetic as a source. Nothing says "list what you did not measure" or "never assume an unmeasured cost is zero/neutral".

Cause vs prevention. The territory causes the general habit structurally: gate-defined goal + no in-round end-to-end measurement + arithmetic-accepted-as-source. It could prevent the specific prefill instance only indirectly (v7 times prefill via `beats_compiled`, `CHANGELOG.md:9`), but the general habit has no rule against it. Proposal (not a finding): a "list unverified costs; never assume free/neutral" rule would plug the gap the brief's acceptance criterion 4 names.

## Behaviour 2: claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic

Facts bearing on it: T2, T4, T5, T7, T10.

Where the instructions create or allow it. Ready to test (`SKILL.md:147`, quoted in T4) *requires* the lead to state "the change you expect in G3's four workloads" while T2 forbids running anything that measures G3 in-round — so the expected change can only be piece arithmetic (e.g. × 20 layers). No rule constrains the method ("with how you worked it out" is free-form), no rule requires labelling it a prediction, and T3/T4 leave no checker: the verifier never sees implementation documents. The brief reinforces the hand-off model (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:215`, T10). `tracking.md:153` blesses the arithmetic as sourced.

Cause vs prevention. The territory causes it directly: it demands an end-to-end number and simultaneously forbids the only measurement that could produce one. Prevention would need either an in-round end-to-end check (the brief's decided direction) or a prediction rule (measure what you claim; label the rest) — neither exists in this territory today.

## Behaviour 3: reasons inconsistently (non-composition admitted, then summed; borrowed compile gains)

Facts bearing on it: T4, T5, T7, T11.

Where the instructions allow it. No rule in the territory says a combination's effect must be measured as a combination, or that a prediction may count only the candidate's own measured effect. The builder records per-attempt six-size timings (`builder.md:29`) and self-explains >20% misses (`builder.md:30`), but combining two slots' savings, or borrowing `mx.compile`'s end-to-end gain into one slot's prediction, violates no stated rule: the verifier's remit ends at exploration (T3), the lead's Ready-to-test arithmetic is unchecked (T4), and shown arithmetic counts as sourced (T5). The "faster because they remove a cause you can name" clause (`SKILL.md:20`) asks for a causal story, not arithmetic discipline.

Cause vs prevention. The territory allows rather than mandates this: it is silent on combination arithmetic, so inconsistent reasoning passes every gate. Prevention needs an explicit prediction rule (brief's acceptance criterion 3); the closest existing hooks are `builder.md:30` (could be extended to combinations) and `tracking.md:153` (could require measured-not-borrowed inputs).

## Behaviour 4: used the grader as a search loop (round 1)

Facts bearing on it: T8.

Where the instructions created it, and the fix. Pre-v4 skill had no one-run-one-attempt rule, and the brief's attempt model ("Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed", `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:14`) assumed a single agent grading its own work, so repeated grade-edit-grade cycles fit the letter of the instructions. Skill v4 added the explicit rule (`builder.md:13`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`), and the brief's stop rule was simultaneously voided (`SKILL.md:15`, `builder.md:13`: "the brief's *When a slot stops* rule no longer applies"). The fix works by making each run a countable, committed attempt ("Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try", `SKILL.md:15`).

Cause vs prevention. This is the territory's one demonstrated self-correction: an explicit, checkable rule ("any change, even a one-line fix, is a new attempt") replaced a violated norm. It supports the brief's assumption that explicit checkable rules work on this swarm. Residual gap (proposal, not finding): nothing stops a builder from running the grader, then abandoning the attempt folder uncommitted — the lead commits "the attempt folder" at collect (`SKILL.md:133`), so an unreturned attempt could still hide a run; the history shows every *returned* try.

## Behaviour 5: persists with a failing design family

Facts bearing on it: T1, T6, T9.

Where the instructions create or allow it. The harden loop (`SKILL.md:135-138`) only ever says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" — a skilled agent can always name one more cause, so the loop has no failure counter and no exit to a different design. `ready` (`SKILL.md:140`) requires only gate passage plus "no further change worth making", judged by the same lead running the loop. "Faster because they remove a cause you can name" (`SKILL.md:20`) rewards cause-naming, which is exactly what kept the fused-kernel family alive. The compete step (`SKILL.md:131`) diversifies directions once ("Give each a different direction"), but harden then single-threads on "the best attempt" (`SKILL.md:136`), so early convergence to one family is structural. No rule says "after N failures at the same size/phase for the same cause, change approach or log why not".

Cause vs prevention. The territory causes it: single-threaded hill-climbing on a nameable-cause loop with no design-switch rule. The starting-point machinery (`SKILL.md:64-76`, step 1: "what keeps a starting point from passing G2, and where the attempt still spends its time") surfaces the repeated failure in prose but attaches no consequence. Prevention needs the brief's acceptance criterion 5 as an explicit rule, e.g. in the harden step.

## Corrections: what the brief gets wrong about this territory

1. Stale revision. Brief `design-lab/brief.md:72` says "main at `2090949`", but the session worktree is at 1113c2d (per the task; `SKILL.md:20` and `CHANGELOG.md:9` already contain the ADR 0012 contributor-model text, which postdates 2090949). Correction: brief §"Revision" predates commit 1113c2d.
2. Stale skill-version reference inside the territory (not a brief error, but the brief's citations assume v7 consistency): `SKILL.md:80` step 2.1 says "its version line (v1, with skill version 6)" while `SKILL.md:10` declares "**Skill version 7**". One of the two is stale; a round following step 2.1 literally would stamp the wrong skill version.
3. Imprecise swarm citation (minor). Brief `:50` cites "`SKILL.md:22-38`" for the swarm table; the role table itself is `SKILL.md:24-30`, helper-start shape `SKILL.md:32-34`, tracking pointer `SKILL.md:36`, and checkpoints `SKILL.md:38-43`. The range covers it but the checkpoint procedure runs past line 38 (to 43).
4. All behaviour-1–5 citations to this territory verified correct: harden-loop quote (`SKILL.md:138`), "Load no model…" (`tracking.md:152`), "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team" (`SKILL.md:164`), goal-as-gates (`SKILL.md:20`), verifier scope (`verifier.md`), one-run-one-attempt fix in v4 (`builder.md:13`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`). No wording errors found in these quotes.

## Pre-existing hooks a fix could reuse (all verified above)

- `tracking.md:153` (number-source rule) — extend to require measured inputs and unverified-lists.
- `SKILL.md:147` (Ready to test) + `tracking.md:113` (Decision "states what G3 should show") — attach prediction-labelling and method rules.
- `builder.md:30` (20% miss rule) — extend to combinations and borrowed gains.
- `SKILL.md:135-140` (harden/ready) — add failure-count design-switch rule.

1|# Solution design brief: make the Muse agent swarm pursue real efficiency, not its proxies (v1)
2|
3|## APPROVAL
4|- User approved this brief on 2026-11-04 (surucuonur). Decisions: the swarm may run end-to-end checks in-round through the GPU queue; Meta's Muse does the design work; from round 3 the launcher runs muse-spark-1.3-contributor with tool approvals off (ADR 0012, commit 1113c2d).
5|- Approved activity: one Muse Code session (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) whose lead starts its own helper agents, up to 12 at once, with no cost or time limit. Agents may prototype and test in design-lab/ (untracked, never committed) and run the measurement tools through the GPU queue. The repository's tracked files stay unchanged.
6|
7|## PROBLEM AND OUTCOME
8|- **Current problem:** two rounds of the Muse agent swarm (round 1: Muse Spark; round 2: Muse Wonder, 63 min, ~$58) produced no kernel that is a real efficiency improvement, while the swarm's own reports predicted gains. Five behaviours, each with evidence:
9|  1. **Treats unmeasured costs as free.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`: "Prefill speed is not timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart from time to first token", citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`. The result: experts attempt-7 is 16–28× slower than the compiled reference at prefill sizes, and routing attempt-4 2.6–8.7× slower (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`). Prompts took 6.6–14.5× and 7–10% longer, and throughput fell by up to 83% (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §5).
10|  2. **Claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Expected G3 = (compiled − candidate) µs × 20 layers (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md` *Ready to test*; `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`). Round 1 predicted −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.98/+0.16/−1.76. Round 2 predicted −0.84 at each and measured −0.73/−0.74/+0.53 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`, `muse-round-2.md`).
11|  3. **Reasons inconsistently.** The same README says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then reports "Together (sum) −0.84 ms". Combine's −0.35 ms prediction is −0.07 to −0.09 from its own timing plus −0.27 to −0.29 borrowed from what `mx.compile` gains end to end. Measured: +1.05 ms with 32 requests.
12|  4. **Used the grader as a search loop (round 1).** 29 grader runs on experts for 4 counted attempts, 18 on attempt-1 with edits between (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §5). Fixed since skill v4: one run is one attempt; round 2 ran 13 for 13.
13|  5. **Persists with a failing design family.** All 7 experts attempts in round 2 are fused kernels that lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs per layer). The cause, too few threadgroups at 1 row, was already known from round 1. The harden loop says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" (`.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:138`), and there is no rule for changing design.
14|- **Root cause** (likely; supported by the evidence above): inside a round, the swarm never sees the real objective. Its feedback is a per-slot proxy, the grader's piece timing. The real measurement, Claude's G3 over whole requests, arrives only after the round. The swarm's claims are self-reported and checked by no one before the summary.
15|  - *verified:* the rules forbid an in-round model run: `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:152` "Load no model and start no other GPU work" and `SKILL.md:164` "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team".
16|  - *verified:* the goal is phrased as passing gates (`SKILL.md:20`).
17|  - *verified:* the verifier checks only exploration's inefficiency entries (`verifier.md`). No one checks the implementation phase's predictions, combination claims or Ready-to-test arithmetic.
18|  - *partly fixed:* ADR 0011 (commit `2090949`) now times the prefill (grader at 6 sizes, G3 with prompt and whole-request time, 5 repeats), so behaviour 1's specific gap is closed. The general habit, treating anything outside the measurement as free, is not addressed.
19|- **Intended outcome:** in round 3 and later, the swarm's statements about speed match what Claude's independent G3 then measures. It marks something ready only when it is a real improvement under the ADR 0011 rule (faster in one phase, prefill or decode, slower in neither, no whole request slower). It stops repeating a design that keeps failing at the same point.
20|- **Why now:** surucuonur asked how to fix "these essential problems and behaviour of these agents". The hackathon deadline is 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, about 11.5 h from 14:30 UTC on 2026-11-04. Round 3 should run with the fix.
21|- **Maturity:** hackathon research tool; judges read the repo, the skill and the round documents.
22|- **User's suggested approach:** none given. Claude has suggested an in-round end-to-end check and prediction rules; treat these as hypotheses, not constraints.
23|
24|## SCOPE AND SUCCESS
25|- **In scope:**
26|  - the round skill (`.agents/skills/muse-round/`: SKILL.md, the role cards, tracking.md);
27|  - the brief (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md`);
28|  - the measurement tools the swarm may call (`bench/grader/`, `bench/micro/` entry points);
29|  - `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` if needed;
30|  - the docs that describe these (ADR, glossary, `claude/muse-swarm.md`, diagrams).
31|- **Out of scope:**
32|  - changing the model or the engine;
33|  - Claude's post-round measurement process, beyond what it needs to compare claims;
34|  - running round 3 itself;
35|  - Muse Code itself.
36|- **Observable acceptance criteria:**
37|  1. Every speed claim in a round's READMEs and summary is either backed by a measurement made in the round, with its run file cited, of exactly what is claimed (the slot or combination, at the end-to-end level claimed), or labelled as a prediction and shown next to the measured value.
38|  2. No hypothesis reaches `ready`, and no attempt goes to *Ready to test*, unless an in-round check shows it improves under ADR 0011's rule, against the unchanged model and the compiled reference.
39|  3. Predictions count only the candidate's own measured effect, and a combination's effect is measured as a combination.
40|  4. Anything the swarm did not measure is listed as unverified, never assumed free or neutral.
41|  5. After a stated number of failures of one design at the same size or phase for the same cause, the next attempt changes approach, or the log records why not.
42|  6. Claude's post-round G3 agrees with the swarm's in-round measured claims within the noise of the repeats. This is the ultimate test.
43|- **Quality guardrails:**
44|  - proportionate and simple: surucuonur rejected sandbox and guard-hook hardening before (memory `muse-isolation-simple`);
45|  - keep the documents readable by judges;
46|  - keep Muse-facing instructions in the repo.
47|
48|## VERIFIED SYSTEM CONTEXT
49|- **Launch:** `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` (`:71` first prompt "Run the muse-round skill…", `:136` `muse exec … -c agents.execution_capacity=12`). One Muse Code session per round, in worktree `../Hackathon-muse` on branch `muse-agent`, on the Meta Model API. Round 2 ran `muse-wonder-1.0` with approvals on; from step 0 the default is `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` with approvals off.
50|- **The swarm** (`SKILL.md:22-38`):
51|  - the lead coordinates and commits, but never explores, builds or grades;
52|  - explorers write `exploration/territory-*.md` and `ineff-*.md`;
53|  - the verifier confirms or refutes inefficiencies;
54|  - builders write and grade one attempt each (`builder.md`);
55|  - boundary agents write and check a hypothesis's boundary (`boundary.md`);
56|  - shared docs and logs per phase (`tracking.md`), checkpoints commit them.
57|- **Steps** (`SKILL.md`): 0 find where you are, 1 starting point, 2 exploration, 3 the analysis, 4 implementation (open hypothesis → boundary → compete → collect → harden → close `ready`/`dropped`), 5 finish (READMEs, *Ready to test*, summary).
58|- **Measurement tools:**
59|  - **`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`:** G1/G2 bit-exact at 6 sizes; paired piece timing with a sign test; `beats_compiled`/`beats_baseline` per ADR 0011; takes the GPU lock; loads the model on every run (ADR 0010).
60|  - **`bench/grader/time_candidates.py`:** end-to-end check and G3.
61|    - Engines: `plain` (MLX) or `vllm`.
62|    - Variants: base, compiled-<slot>, muse-<slot>, muse-all, `--variant`.
63|    - G2 compares greedy tokens; G3 records decode step, prompt time (vLLM only) and wall time; `--repeats` defaults to 5; writes `g3-vllm.json`.
64|    - Duration: about 8.5 s per run on average in vLLM, so roughly 10–12 min per candidate with base and compiled at 4 settings × 5 repeats.
65|    - The plain engine has no prompt time yet (`bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py:prompt_ms`, `breakdown.run_plain`).
66|  - **`bench/grader/gpu_lock.py`:** one GPU job at a time; later ones wait.
67|- **Isolation and provenance:**
68|  - git hooks refuse Muse commits outside `muse-spark/`, changes to finished rounds' files, and merges;
69|  - `tools/provenance_check.py` audits authorship;
70|  - Claude merges each round, measures it independently (G3) and writes `claude/findings/muse-round-<N>.md`, which the next round reads as its starting point.
71|- **Round 3's starting point:** no baseline in any slot (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` *For round 3*).
72|- **Revision:** main at `2090949`, working tree clean apart from two uncommitted pilot files.
73|
74|## PROTECTED CONTRACTS AND BEHAVIORS
75|- Authorship separation: the Muse agent writes only in `muse-spark/`, only the lead commits, with the Muse co-author line; Claude never commits on `muse-agent`; hooks and provenance check stay.
76|- Finished rounds stay frozen (tags `muse-round-1`, `muse-round-2`).
77|- Muse Code only, swarm design (ADR 0007), no attempt limit (ADR 0006: "limitless"), one grader run per attempt, the GPU queue.
78|- Grading rules of ADR 0010/0011 (bit-exact at 6 sizes, both phases, hand-off via `max_rows`); G2's token check.
79|- Claude's post-round independent measurement remains the authority for baselines.
80|- The attempt format (`spec.json` + `block-N.metal`) and the grader's JSON verdict keys (`g1`, `g2`, `beats_compiled`, `beats_baseline`, `timing_us_per_layer`, `phases_vs_compiled`).
81|
82|## CONSTRAINTS AND OPERATIONAL REALITY
83|- **Machine:** M1 Pro, 16 GB, heavy swapping (19–20 GB swap in use); one GPU job at a time. vLLM needs `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` (now the default in `breakdown.py`) and Docker quit. 1-request vLLM timings are noisy (6–41% spread).
84|- **Time:** about 11.5 h to the deadline, including implementing the fix, running round 3 (~1–2 h), and Claude's measurement and findings (~1 h). The fix should be implementable and checkable in roughly 2–3 h.
85|- **Cost:** round 2 on Muse Wonder cost about $58; on the contributor model a round costs about $1 (round 1: $0.70). Claude never runs `start.sh` or calls the Meta API without asking.
86|- **Hard constraints:** the protected items above, and the deadline.
87|- **Preferences:** simple over airtight (no sandboxing or guard hooks); rules phrased positively for agents (writing-for-agents guidance).
88|- **Decided:** round 3 runs on `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, round 1's model, which ADR 0008 judged less capable than Muse Wonder, with tool approvals off. No one approves tool calls during the round, so rules must hold without a human watching. Instructions must be explicit and checkable, since a less capable model follows general advice less reliably.
89|
90|## FAILURE MODES AND FUTURE CHANGES
91|- **Goodhart risk:** any new check becomes the next proxy. A design must say how the swarm could game it.
92|- **GPU queue contention:** a 10–12 min end-to-end check blocks builders' grader runs.
93|- **Memory:** a vLLM run inside the round competes with Muse Code's own processes and may page.
94|- **Noise:** at 1 request, end-to-end verdicts are mostly `same`.
95|- **Partial rounds:** a session can stop mid-round, and checks must leave the shared documents consistent.
96|- **The model can ignore instructions:** round 1 ignored "one attempt per grader run" before it became an explicit rule.
97|- **Future:** more slots or a different model; rounds 4+; possibly other engines.
98|- **Prior pitfalls:**
99|  - independent piece timing hid latency (fixed by ADR 0010);
100|  - tolerances let the tokens change (fixed by ADR 0010);
101|  - prefill was untimed (fixed by ADR 0011);
102|  - G3 with 3 repeats falsely flagged unchanged phases (fixed with 5 repeats).
103|
104|## DESIGN EXPECTATIONS
105|- Deliver one coherent approach that fixes the root cause (the gap between the proxy and the objective, and unchecked self-reports) and covers behaviours 1–5, not one patch per symptom.
106|- Address whole-system effects: the GPU queue and round duration, memory, Claude's post-round role, the docs and judges.
107|- Cite repository evidence; distinguish verified facts from proposals.
108|- Specify the changes to the skill, cards, brief and tools, plus any new measurement entry point, at the level of what each says or does.
109|- Define how a future implementation is validated before round 3, without a paid Muse run if possible, and how round 3's own outcome would show success.
110|- Do not edit the repository's tracked code, data or configuration; prototypes and tests live in design-lab/.
111|
112|## UNRESOLVED ASSUMPTIONS AND STOP CONDITIONS
113|- **Decided (surucuonur, 2026-11-04):** the swarm may run an end-to-end check itself during the round, through the GPU queue. This replaces "Load no model…" (`tracking.md:152`) and "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team" (`SKILL.md:164`) as needed. Claude's post-round G3 remains the independent authority.
114|- **Assumed (unanswered):** the fix must be ready for round 3 before 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, implementable and checkable in about 2–3 h.
115|- **Assumption:** the Muse agent follows explicit, checkable rules better than general advice (round 2 kept "one run per attempt" once it was a rule).
116|- **Return BLOCKED if:** the design requires breaking a protected contract, or depends on a Muse Code capability not documented here.

1|"""Grade one kernel attempt: compile it, test it on captured inputs, time it.
2|
3|The independent grader for the Muse agent's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|G2 tests it on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step
5|(1, 8 and 32 rows), and on every layer's inputs in a prefill, recorded as
6|it runs (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows): every output must be identical to the
7|reference's, bit for bit, since only then are the model's tokens identical
8|(claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md). The timing runs at the same six
9|sizes and chains the 20 layers, so each call waits for the one before, as in
10|the model. The grader prints its verdict as JSON, and writes it to --out when
11|given. It never writes into the attempt folder, which holds only the Muse
12|agent's files.
13|
14|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt folder> <slot> [--out FILE]
15|      [--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER ...]
16|
17|The candidate and the compiled reference are timed in alternating repeats, so
18|drift in the GPU's clocks reaches both alike. At each size the candidate is
19|"faster" when it wins at least WINS_NEEDED of the REPEATS paired repeats (a
20|one-sided sign test at p < 0.01), "slower" when it loses that many, and
21|"same" otherwise; the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5% between
22|medians, so comparing medians alone would pass on noise. `beats_compiled`
23|needs both phases, decode and prefill: faster at every size of one, slower
24|at none of the other (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md).
25|
26|--baseline times an earlier, already graded attempt in the same run and adds
27|`beats_baseline`, judged the same way. From round 2 on, the bar is the
28|previous round's final attempt for the slot
29|(claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md). FOLDER alone is an attempt
30|for the same slot. For routing+combine, give either one routing+combine
31|attempt or `routing=FOLDER` and `combine=FOLDER`.

91|def ulp_bf16(r):
92|    """bfloat16's unit in the last place at |r|, floored at |r| = 0.001 (brief, G2)."""
93|    exp = np.floor(np.log2(np.maximum(np.abs(r), 1e-3)))

97|def differences(g, r):
98|    """Elements of *g* that aren't *r*'s bit for bit, and the largest gap in units
99|    in the last place (floored at |r| = 0.001); "at" is the flat index of it."""
100|    differ = (g != r) & ~(np.isnan(g) & np.isnan(r))
101|    out = {"differ": int(differ.sum()), "max_ulp": 0.0}
102|    if out["differ"]:
103|        with np.errstate(over="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
104|            over = np.nan_to_num(np.abs(g - r) / ulp_bf16(r), nan=1e9, posinf=1e9)
105|        out |= {"max_ulp": float(min(over.max(), 1e9)), "at": int(over.argmax())}

191|def chained(fn, layers, names):
192|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
193|
194|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
195|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
196|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
197|    """
198|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
199|    outs = []
200|    for layer in layers:
201|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
202|        if outs:
203|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
204|        out = fn(**args)
205|        if isinstance(out, dict):
206|            out = list(out.values())
207|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
208|    return outs

211|def timed(fn, layers, names):
212|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
213|    for _ in range(3):
214|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
215|    times = []
216|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
217|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
218|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
219|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
220|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)
