| routing + experts-7 | −10.0% (6.63×) | −37.5% (14.50×) | −48.0% (12.50×) | −82.5% (13.09×) |
| all three with experts-7 | −10.7% (6.75×) | −43.0% (14.33×) | −53.7% (14.37×) | −83.3% (13.66×) |

Grader re-grade under ADR 0011 rules (per-layer multiples of the compiled
reference; `muse-round-2.md:160-168`, from
`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json` — recomputed,
all match):

| Slot | Decode 1/8/32 | Prefill 127/1016/2048 | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| routing attempt-4 | 0.76/0.84/0.84 faster | 2.60/5.87/8.65 slower | `beats_compiled` false |
| combine attempt-1 | 0.86/0.85/0.93 faster | 0.95/0.83/0.52 faster | `beats_compiled` true |
| experts attempt-7 | 1.17/0.69/0.65, slower at 1 row | 15.84/27.67/20.06 slower | `beats_compiled` false |

Note the 1-row instability this exposes: experts attempt-7 at 1 row was
*faster* than compiled (140.7 vs 143.5 µs) in the main re-grade
(`muse-round-2.md:53`, `grade-experts.json`) but *slower* (92.1 vs 78.6 µs,
1 win of 30) in the phases re-grade (`grade-phases-experts-attempt-7.json`).
The findings already flag that at 1 row "even [the within-run comparison] is
close to the noise" (`muse-round-2.md:55`).

Interference (both rounds): every *pair* of kernels comes within 0.5 ms of
its parts' sum, but all three together with 8 requests miss by 2.8 ms in
plain MLX (`muse-round-2.md:125-127`, from
`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2-pairs/console-plain.txt`); round 1
did the same (+0.88 vs −1.95 ms, `muse-round-1.md:106-109`). Unexplained in
both rounds (`muse-round-2.md:127`: "It is not explained").

Grader-run counts: round 1 ran the grader 29 times for experts' 4 counted
attempts (18 on attempt-1, with edits between nearly every run), 2 for
routing, 3 for combine (`muse-round-1.md:127-132`, from
`muse-spark/transcripts/`). Round 2 ran exactly 13 for 13
(`muse-round-2.md:43`, `:150-153`).

---

## 2. What each ADR (0006–0012) already fixed

- **0006 — Muse Spark works in Muse Code, with helpers and no attempt limit**
  (`claude/adr/0006-muse-spark-in-muse-code.md`). Fixed: Anthropic's system
  prompt/tool definitions going to Meta on the training tier (`:20-21`);
  personal-skills leakage only partly — the first smoke test still leaked
  surucuonur's global instructions + 43 personal-skill descriptions, fixed by
  giving `muse` its own home folder (`:40`, `:58`). Established, still
  standing: no attempt limit / no stop rule, "limitless inside" with full
  commit history + attempt counts as the safeguard (`:29-31`, `:64`);
  lead-only commits with enforced co-author trailer (`:28`); writes only in
  `muse-spark/` (`:38`); GPU lock (`:43`, then exit-on-busy); transcript
  evidence + audit (`:44-48`); Claude's independent re-grading and G3 (`:49`).
  Its round design (helpers/drafts/diagnosis) was replaced by 0007 (`:9`).
- **0007 — the round is a swarm** (`claude/adr/0007-muse-spark-swarm.md`).
  Fixed: the lead as grading bottleneck — builders grade, and `gpu_lock.py`
  now waits instead of exiting (`:77`); concurrent-edit clobbering —
  lead-only READMEs, append-only logs (`:50-54`); untracked phases —
  versioned shared docs with per-checkpoint commits (`:58-70`). Set the
  still-current structure: 8 starter territories, verifier, 2–3 competing
  builders per hypothesis, harden-until-it-passes (`:24-45`). Unchanged by
  later ADRs (`:9`).
- **0008 — Muse Wonder from round 2** (`claude/adr/0008-muse-wonder.md`).
  Fixed (attempted): capability — "Meta's most capable model" at `max`
  effort to "see improved results" (`:11`, `:19`). What it actually bought:
  exactness in every slot (`muse-round-2.md:153`) at ~$58 vs round 1's ~$0.70
  (`:35`; `muse-round-2.md:150-151`). Standing parts: per-model co-author
  naming via `tools/provenance.py` (`:26-30`), "the Muse agent" as the
  model-neutral name (`:30`). Model choice superseded by 0012 (`:9`).
- **0009 — rounds build on each other** (`claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md`).
  Fixed: round 2 overwriting round 1's documents — per-round folders
  (`:17`); post-hoc changes — frozen finished rounds via tag + pre-commit
  hook + audit re-check (`:18-21`); a bar round 1 already passed — the
  baseline must be beaten in the same run (`:34`); median-comparison noise
  (5% self-difference; 15–19/30 self-wins) — paired sign test, 22/30 at
  p<0.01 (`:35-36`); context loss — starting point from Claude's report,
  round stops if the report is missing (`:22-27`). Note: this ADR describes
  skill v4 (`:13`) but does **not** state the "one grader run is one
  attempt" rule — that fix is recorded only in `muse-round-1.md:132`,
  the glossary's Attempt definition (`GLOSSARY.md:194-195`), and the skill
  text itself (skill explorer's territory).
- **0010 — bit-exact at every size, chained timing**
  (`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md`). Fixed all three round-1 grader
  gaps (`:11-16`): untested prefill sizes (experts differed in 62% of
  outputs there, `:13`); tolerance-allowed token flips (routing weights
  within 1e-5 changed 7–9 of 32 sequences, `:14`); overlapped timing hiding
  a 22–25% slowdown (`:15`, `:32-33`). Result: no round-1 attempt passes the
  new G2 (`:40`; `muse-round-1.md:142-150`). **Caused behaviour 1's opening:**
  its Consequences say "Not covered: prefill speed. G3 times decode steps
  only, so a kernel slower at prefill sizes would go unnoticed, apart from
  the time to first token" (`:44`; line **42** at round-2 time, before the
  ADR 0011 amendment note at `:9-10` shifted it — verified via
  `git show 4033cae:...`). Round 2's hyp-1 cites exactly that line to
  justify a slow prefill branch (see §4, behaviour 1).
- **0011 — improvement must hold in both phases; `max_rows` hand-off**
  (`claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md`). Fixed behaviour 1's specific
  gap: piece timing at all six sizes (`:21`), paired sign test at every size
  replacing median comparison everywhere (`:22-26`), per-phase verdicts with
  `beats_compiled` = faster in one phase, slower in neither (`:27-32`),
  G3 over 4 workloads × 5 repeats with decode-step, prompt and whole-request
  times (`:36-41`), and the `max_rows` hand-off to the compiled reference
  (`:33-35`, verified bit-exact in
  `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`). Also fixed 3-repeat false
  flags: a no-op hand-off copy came out `slower` by 0.5% under 3 repeats;
  5 repeats cut the per-check chance to 1/252 (`:40`). Consequences:
  routing attempt-4 demoted to starting point, round 3 has no baseline
  (`:46`); stricter decode verdicts (`:50`); 1-request whole-request G3
  mostly `same` on noise (`:52`). **Residual:** "Not covered: prefill chunks
  of other sizes, and decode steps with other row counts" (`:51`) — the same
  citeable-gap pattern as 0010's (proposal: phrase as unverified, never free).
- **0012 — contributor model, approvals off from round 3**
  (`claude/adr/0012-muse-spark-contributor-unattended.md`). Fixed: cost
  ($58 → ~$1/round, `:31`); need for a human at the terminal (`:11`).
  New constraints it imposes on the design: the model is the less capable
  round-1 one, so "the skill's instructions must be explicit and checkable"
  (`:32`); no one watches tool calls, with hooks + audit + skill write-rules
  as what still holds (`:33-35`); Claude's own tooling may refuse to start
  such sessions — surucuonur starts them (`:36`).

---

Note the dual meaning: the *grader gate* G2 is bit-exact slot outputs (0010 `:27-31`); the *brief's* G2 is identical greedy tokens end to end (0010 `:14`, `muse-round-1.md:54`). ---

## 4. How this territory causes or could prevent each behaviour

### Behaviour 1 — treats unmeasured costs as free
- **Caused by territory, directly.** ADR 0010's "Not covered: prefill speed…
  would go unnoticed, apart from the time to first token" (0010 `:44`, `:42`
  at round-2 time — verified via `git show 4033cae:`) was cited by
  `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151` to
  declare a slow-but-exact prefill branch "free apart from time to first
  token". The swarm's wording echoes the ADR's. The measurement design made
  the claim true at the time: G2 checked prefill-size *outputs* while G3
  timed decode steps only (0010 `:44`; `muse-round-2.md:146`).
- **Measured cost** (§1 tables): experts-7 prompts 6.6–14.5× slower,
  throughput −10% to −83%; routing-4 prompts 7–10% slower, −3.5% at
  32×1024 (`muse-round-2.md:134-146`).
- **Prevented in the specific case** by 0011 (both-phase rule, G3 prompt +
  whole-request times, hand-off). **Not prevented in general:** 0011 has its
  own "Not covered" (`:51`, other chunk/row counts) in the same citeable
  form, and the territory contains no rule that unmeasured = unverified.
  (Proposal: rephrase every "Not covered" as "unverified: assume nothing";
  this matches brief acceptance criterion 4.)

### Behaviour 2 — end-to-end claims from piece arithmetic
- **Caused structurally by territory.** The design gives the swarm only
  per-slot piece timing in-round; the real objective (G3 over whole
  requests) arrives post-round via Claude (0006 `:42`, `:49`;
  `muse-swarm.md:133`). Nothing in the ADRs defines a valid in-round
  prediction formula, and 0011's G3 rule (faster-in-one/slower-in-neither
  vs *two* bars over 4 workloads, `:41`) has no in-round counterpart.
- **Territory documents the failure twice:** round 1's parts-vs-whole miss
  (`muse-round-1.md:106-109`) and round 2's pairs-add-up/triples-don't
  (`muse-round-2.md:125-127`), plus combine's 1.05 ms G3 loss exceeding its
  whole grader-measured kernel time — "the cost doesn't come from the
  kernel's own work as the grader runs it" (`muse-round-2.md:108`).
- **Partially addressed:** 0009's sign test (`:35-36`) and 0011's extension
  of it (`:22-26`) fixed *noise* in piece comparisons, not *composition*.
  The existing prevention channel is the starting point's "G3 effect against
  its prediction" per slot (0009 `:27`; `muse-swarm.md:103-104`), which
  carries the lesson forward but doesn't check new claims.

### Behaviour 3 — inconsistent reasoning (non-composing sums, borrowed offsets)
- **Documented in territory:** `muse-round-2.md:154` records the missed
  combine (−0.35 ms) and 32-request predictions; `:108` gives the
  unexplained gap. The findings don't dissect the README's internal
  contradiction (rounds explorer's job).
- **Territory already contains a per-attempt version of the fix:**
  `muse-swarm.md:88` — "if the attempt failed or missed its prediction by
  more than 20%, [the builder] finds out why and adds the answer to the
  analysis." No equivalent rule covers Ready-to-test arithmetic or summary
  claims, and the boundary agent's checks are about ungraded row counts /
  races, not about prediction arithmetic (`muse-swarm.md:89`). (Proposal:
  extend the existing >20% rule to every Ready-to-test/summary number.)

### Behaviour 4 — the grader as a search loop (round 1)
- **Documented in territory:** 29 experts runs for 4 attempts, 18 on
  attempt-1 with edits between (`muse-round-1.md:127-132`).
- **Fixed and verified held:** "Skill version 4 made 'one grader run is one
  attempt' a rule" (`muse-round-1.md:132`); round 2 ran 13 for 13
  (`muse-round-2.md:43`, `:152`); the glossary now defines Attempt as "One
  grader run" (`GLOSSARY.md:194-195`).
- **Traceability gap (prevention risk):** no ADR records this fix — 0009
  describes skill v4 without mentioning it. A future reader of the ADRs
  alone would not know the rule exists or why. (Proposal: record it in the
  next ADR touching the skill.)

### Behaviour 5 — persisting with a failing design family
- **Cause known since round 1, in territory:** one threadgroup of 256
  threads per (row, expert) pair → 4 threadgroups at 1 row, "too few to fill
  the GPU" ("occupancy starvation", `muse-round-1.md:123`); chained 133 vs
  80 µs/layer (`:118-121`). Round 1's findings set "The experts kernel at
  1 row" as explicit round-2 homework (`muse-round-1.md:164`).
- **Still unsolved after round 2, in territory:** "every fused design in
  round 2" lost at 1 row, 92–110 vs 73–87 µs/layer
  (`muse-round-2.md:171`), which re-sets the same homework and suggests
  "copying the reference's unfused structure exactly for small row counts".
- **Territory documents but doesn't prevent:** the ADRs contain no
  change-approach rule; the starting-point mechanism (0009 `:22-27`) carried
  the diagnosis forward twice without forcing a design change. Note the
  brief's "All 7 experts attempts … are fused kernels" goes slightly beyond
  what this territory states ("every fused design", `muse-round-2.md:171`;
  whether all 7 were fused is in the rounds explorer's territory).

---

## 5. What the brief gets wrong (or imprecise) about this territory

1. **Round 2's prediction was −0.84/−0.85/−0.84, not "−0.84 at each"**
   (brief §Problem behaviour 2). The −0.85 at 8 requests is in
   `muse-round-2.md:90` and `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`. Minor.
2. **"Main at 2090949" is stale** (brief §Verified system context,
   "Revision"). HEAD here is `1113c2d` (ADR 0012); `2090949` (ADR 0011) is
   its parent — verified via `git log`. The brief itself cites `1113c2d`
   for ADR 0012 in §Approval, so the two lines contradict each other.
   Likewise "working tree clean apart from two uncommitted pilot files"
   does not describe this worktree (`git status` shows only untracked
   `design-lab/`).
3. **"All 7 experts attempts in round 2 are fused kernels"** (behaviour 5)
   exceeds this territory's evidence: `muse-round-2.md:171` says "every
   *fused* design in round 2" lost at 1 row. Defer the "all 7" to the rounds
   explorer; if any attempt-7-family member was unfused, rephrase to
   "every fused design".
4. **"1-request vLLM timings are noisy (6–41% spread)"** (brief §Constraints)
   over-generalises: the documented 6–41% figure is specifically the
   *whole-request time* repeats' spread at 1 request (`0011:52`). Decode-step
   spreads at 1 request are much tighter (e.g. base 5.320–5.452 in round 1,
   `muse-round-1.md:82`).
5. **"G3 with 3 repeats falsely flagged unchanged phases"** (brief §Prior
   pitfalls) is slightly loose: the documented incident is a single false
   `slower` on *prompt time* at 32×1024 for a no-op hand-off copy, 0.5%
   with ranges 16 ms apart (`0011:40`). "Phases" plural and "unchanged"
   are fine as shorthand; the precise case is one workload's prompt time.
6. **Not a brief error, but a territory-internal contradiction the designers
   should know:** `PROVENANCE.md:42` says "from round 2 the session signs in
   to surucuonur's Muse Code subscription, and the launcher passes no key at
   all" — this contradicts 0008 `:17` (round 2 uses the pay-as-you-go API
   key, `MUSE_AUTH=key`), 0012 `:10` ("still signs in with the API key"),
   and 0006 `:41`. The ADRs agree with each other; the PROVENANCE sentence
   does not match them. The brief does not repeat the claim, so no brief
   correction is needed — but the sentence is load-bearing for isolation
   claims and should be fixed or confirmed.
7. **Non-issues checked (brief is right):** experts-7 "16–28×" (exact:
   15.84/27.67/20.06, `grade-phases-experts-attempt-7.json`); routing-4
   "2.6–8.7×" (exact: 2.60/5.87/8.65); round-1 predicted/measured
   −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 vs +0.98/+0.16/−1.76 (exact: +0.980/+0.163/−1.756);
   combine "+1.05 ms with 32 requests" (exact: +1.051 vLLM,
   `muse-round-2.md:81`); hyp-1's `:42` citation of ADR 0010 (exact at
   round-2 time — the line is `:44` today only because 0011's amendment
   note shifted it); "no baseline in any slot" (`muse-round-2.md:168`);
   round costs/times ($58/63 min round 2, $0.70 round 1); both tags exist.

---

## 6. Glossary and swarm-doc notes for designers

- `GLOSSARY.md:139-141` (`Improvement`), `:143-145` (`Hand-off`),
  `:147-149` (`Baseline` of a slot), `:194-195` (`Attempt`) already encode
  the 0011 rule, the hand-off, the baseline definition and the one-run rule
  in one citable place — the design can cite these instead of redefining.
- `muse-swarm.md` describes skill v7 (`:7`, `:32`) while rounds ran v3

  explorer's to verify.
- `muse-swarm.md:88` (the >20% prediction-miss rule) is the closest existing
  prevention for behaviours 2–3 and should be extended rather than
  reinvented.

1|# Solution design brief: make the Muse agent swarm pursue real efficiency, not its proxies (v1)
2|
3|## APPROVAL
4|- User approved this brief on 2026-11-04 (surucuonur). Decisions: the swarm may run end-to-end checks in-round through the GPU queue; Meta's Muse does the design work; from round 3 the launcher runs muse-spark-1.3-contributor with tool approvals off (ADR 0012, commit 1113c2d).
5|- Approved activity: one Muse Code session (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) whose lead starts its own helper agents, up to 12 at once, with no cost or time limit. Agents may prototype and test in design-lab/ (untracked, never committed) and run the measurement tools through the GPU queue. The repository's tracked files stay unchanged.
6|
7|## PROBLEM AND OUTCOME
8|- **Current problem:** two rounds of the Muse agent swarm (round 1: Muse Spark; round 2: Muse Wonder, 63 min, ~$58) produced no kernel that is a real efficiency improvement, while the swarm's own reports predicted gains. Five behaviours, each with evidence:
9|  1. **Treats unmeasured costs as free.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`: "Prefill speed is not timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart from time to first token", citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`. The result: experts attempt-7 is 16–28× slower than the compiled reference at prefill sizes, and routing attempt-4 2.6–8.7× slower (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`). Prompts took 6.6–14.5× and 7–10% longer, and throughput fell by up to 83% (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §5).
10|  2. **Claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Expected G3 = (compiled − candidate) µs × 20 layers (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md` *Ready to test*; `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`). Round 1 predicted −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.98/+0.16/−1.76. Round 2 predicted −0.84 at each and measured −0.73/−0.74/+0.53 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`, `muse-round-2.md`).
11|  3. **Reasons inconsistently.** The same README says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then reports "Together (sum) −0.84 ms". Combine's −0.35 ms prediction is −0.07 to −0.09 from its own timing plus −0.27 to −0.29 borrowed from what `mx.compile` gains end to end. Measured: +1.05 ms with 32 requests.
12|  4. **Used the grader as a search loop (round 1).** 29 grader runs on experts for 4 counted attempts, 18 on attempt-1 with edits between (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §5). Fixed since skill v4: one run is one attempt; round 2 ran 13 for 13.
13|  5. **Persists with a failing design family.** All 7 experts attempts in round 2 are fused kernels that lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs per layer). The cause, too few threadgroups at 1 row, was already known from round 1. The harden loop says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" (`.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:138`), and there is no rule for changing design.
14|- **Root cause** (likely; supported by the evidence above): inside a round, the swarm never sees the real objective. Its feedback is a per-slot proxy, the grader's piece timing. The real measurement, Claude's G3 over whole requests, arrives only after the round. The swarm's claims are self-reported and checked by no one before the summary.
15|  - *verified:* the rules forbid an in-round model run: `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:152` "Load no model and start no other GPU work" and `SKILL.md:164` "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team".
16|  - *verified:* the goal is phrased as passing gates (`SKILL.md:20`).
17|  - *verified:* the verifier checks only exploration's inefficiency entries (`verifier.md`). No one checks the implementation phase's predictions, combination claims or Ready-to-test arithmetic.
18|  - *partly fixed:* ADR 0011 (commit `2090949`) now times the prefill (grader at 6 sizes, G3 with prompt and whole-request time, 5 repeats), so behaviour 1's specific gap is closed. The general habit, treating anything outside the measurement as free, is not addressed.
19|- **Intended outcome:** in round 3 and later, the swarm's statements about speed match what Claude's independent G3 then measures. 21|## Behaviour 1: treats unmeasured costs as free
22|
23|Facts bearing on it: T1, T2, T5, T9, T10.
24|
25|Where the instructions create or allow it. The goal (T1, `SKILL.md:20`) defines success entirely in grader verdicts, so anything the grader does not time is definitionally irrelevant to passing. The in-round measurement ban (T2, `tracking.md:152`, `SKILL.md:164`) makes it impossible to check anything the grader omits, so "free apart from time to first token" style reasoning is the only available move for unmeasured costs. The cross-phase guard (`tracking.md:103`, `SKILL.md:114`) asks for a prediction ("what removing it does to the other phase"), not a measurement, and the number rule (`tracking.md:153`) accepts shown arithmetic as a source. Nothing says "list what you did not measure" or "never assume an unmeasured cost is zero/neutral".
26|
27|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes the general habit structurally: gate-defined goal + no in-round end-to-end measurement + arithmetic-accepted-as-source. It could prevent the specific prefill instance only indirectly (v7 times prefill via `beats_compiled`, `CHANGELOG.md:9`), but the general habit has no rule against it. Proposal (not a finding): a "list unverified costs; never assume free/neutral" rule would plug the gap the brief's acceptance criterion 4 names.
28|
29|## Behaviour 2: claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic
30|
31|Facts bearing on it: T2, T4, T5, T7, T10.
32|
33|Where the instructions create or allow it. Ready to test (`SKILL.md:147`, quoted in T4) *requires* the lead to state "the change you expect in G3's four workloads" while T2 forbids running anything that measures G3 in-round — so the expected change can only be piece arithmetic (e.g. × 20 layers). No rule constrains the method ("with how you worked it out" is free-form), no rule requires labelling it a prediction, and T3/T4 leave no checker: the verifier never sees implementation documents. The brief reinforces the hand-off model (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:215`, T10). `tracking.md:153` blesses the arithmetic as sourced.
34|
35|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes it directly: it demands an end-to-end number and simultaneously forbids the only measurement that could produce one. Prevention would need either an in-round end-to-end check (the brief's decided direction) or a prediction rule (measure what you claim; label the rest) — neither exists in this territory today.
36|
37|## Behaviour 3: reasons inconsistently (non-composition admitted, then summed; borrowed compile gains)
38|
39|Facts bearing on it: T4, T5, T7, T11.
40|
41|Where the instructions allow it. No rule in the territory says a combination's effect must be measured as a combination, or that a prediction may count only the candidate's own measured effect. The builder records per-attempt six-size timings (`builder.md:29`) and self-explains >20% misses (`builder.md:30`), but combining two slots' savings, or borrowing `mx.compile`'s end-to-end gain into one slot's prediction, violates no stated rule: the verifier's remit ends at exploration (T3), the lead's Ready-to-test arithmetic is unchecked (T4), and shown arithmetic counts as sourced (T5). The "faster because they remove a cause you can name" clause (`SKILL.md:20`) asks for a causal story, not arithmetic discipline.
42|
43|Cause vs prevention. The territory allows rather than mandates this: it is silent on combination arithmetic, so inconsistent reasoning passes every gate. Prevention needs an explicit prediction rule (brief's acceptance criterion 3); the closest existing hooks are `builder.md:30` (could be extended to combinations) and `tracking.md:153` (could require measured-not-borrowed inputs).

46|
47|Facts bearing on it: T8.
48|

Pre-v4 skill had no one-run-one-attempt rule, and the brief's attempt model ("Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed", `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:14`) assumed a single agent grading its own work, so repeated grade-edit-grade cycles fit the letter of the instructions. 159|## 2. Behaviours 1–5: how the territory causes or could prevent each
160|
161|1. **Unmeasured costs as free.** Cause: the grader's piece timing never sees
162|   request-level effects by construction; worse, the plain engine reports
163|   `prompt_ms = 0.0` always (§1.3) — an in-round plain check literally prices
164|   the prefill at zero. `max_rows` lets prefill be "same by delegation" (§1.1).
165|   Prevent: G3's rule (faster in one phase, slower in none, no request slower,
166|   `time_candidates.py:187-194`) already encodes "nothing is free" across
167|   decode/prompt/request — if the swarm must run it and cite `g3-vllm.json`.
168|2. **Piece arithmetic.** Cause: both tools hand out medians that invite
169|   subtraction — `timing_us_per_layer` per-size medians
170|   (`check_candidate.py:367-374`) and the printed
171|   `(med-base ms, %)` summary (`repeat_fixes.py:335-359`, seen live in the
172|   probe). Neither tool computes a piece's end-to-end effect. Prevent: an
173|   in-round `time_candidates.py vllm` run measures the whole request directly,
174|   making the arithmetic unnecessary; the design must require citing it.
175|3. **Inconsistent reasoning.** Cause: two different "compiled" baselines exist —
176|   per-part `mx.compile(ref)` in piece timing (`check_candidate.py:360`) vs
177|   whole-MoE `compiled-<slot>` end to end (`time_candidates.py:119-122`) — so
178|   "what mx.compile gains" is ambiguous, inviting borrowed gains. Also
179|   `muse-all`/`compiled-all` exist only with >1 positional attempt
180|   (`time_candidates.py:125-127`); a single-slot invocation never measures a
181|   combination, leaving "Together (sum)" as the only available number.
182|   Prevent: require passing all submitted slots positionally in one call so
183|   `muse-all` is measured as a combination.
184|4. **Grader as search loop.** Cause/enabler: the tool allows unlimited runs and
185|   prints a rich per-size gradient every run; one-run-one-attempt is a skill
186|   rule the tool cannot see (no attempt registry, no run counting, `--out`
187|   arbitrary, exit 0 even on G1 failure). The tool cannot prevent this; only
188|   the skill plus post-hoc log audit can. Note the queue makes each extra run
189|   cost everyone time (§1.4).
190|5. **Failing design family.** The tool provides the per-size signal
191|   (`timing[size].vs_compiled`, e.g. slower at rows 1 in both my grade files)
192|   but no cross-attempt memory: each run is stateless JSON. Cause data (e.g.
193|   too few threadgroups) is not measurable by any tool here. Prevention is
194|   skill-level (aggregate verdicts across attempts); proposal: none in-tool
195|   beyond citing the existing per-size verdicts.
196|

198|
199|- **Reuse as-is:** `time_candidates.py vllm <out> SLOT=FOLDER...` with defaults
200|  (4 G3 settings, 5 repeats, 256 tokens) plus the `g3()` verdict in
201|  `g3-vllm.json` — the rule already matches ADR 0011. `engine_table.py` renders
202|  it for judges. `gpu_lock.hold()` is already inside.
203|- **Needs (gaps in the tool):** (a) pin the invocation — `--repeats`,
204|  `--settings`, `--tokens` are free flags; (b) require all submitted slots
205|  positionally so `muse-all` exists; (c) forbid/ignore `--variant` names
206|  starting with `muse-` (crashes G3) and note non-`muse-` names escape judgment;
207|  (d) token exactness is recorded but never gated — a wrong-tokens variant can
208|  still pass G3; the check must require `exact` in the log; (e) plain engine
209|  must not count as the check (zero prompt, no verdict).
210|- **Duration:** single-slot vLLM G3 ≈ 13–14 min run wall at 5 repeats
211|  (extrapolated, `vllm-duration-estimate.txt`); 3-slot ≈ 3×. Grader: ~13 s
212|  (routing) to ~5 min (experts) per run (§1.1). Plain probe: 10.5 s for the

215|  - `--repeats 1`: min–max ranges collapse to points; non-overlap (spurious

223|  - `--variant myname:...`: timed but never judged (§1.2) — free numbers to

225|  - Single-slot calls: no `muse-all`; combination claims stay arithmetic (§2.3).
226|  - Plain engine: zero prompt time, no verdict file; quotable medians that look
227|    like end-to-end numbers (§1.3).
228|  - Quoting medians/ranges selectively from the jsonl instead of the verdict.
229|  - check_candidate: `--baseline` points at any folder (pick a slow one);
230|    `max_rows=32` makes prefill "same" without doing prefill work (§1.1);
231|    in-between row counts are untested by the grader (`check_sizes.py` is
232|    separate, §1.5); unlimited re-runs (§2.4).
233|  - Lock: bypass by not calling `hold()` (all of `breakdown.py` /

227|## 4. How this territory causes or could prevent each behaviour
228|
229|### Behaviour 1 — treats unmeasured costs as free
230|- **Caused by territory, directly.** ADR 0010's "Not covered: prefill speed…
231|  would go unnoticed, apart from the time to first token" (0010 `:44`, `:42`
232|  at round-2 time — verified via `git show 4033cae:`) was cited by
233|  `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151` to
234|  declare a slow-but-exact prefill branch "free apart from time to first
235|  token". The swarm's wording echoes the ADR's. The measurement design made
236|  the claim true at the time: G2 checked prefill-size *outputs* while G3
237|  timed decode steps only (0010 `:44`; `muse-round-2.md:146`).
238|- **Measured cost** (§1 tables): experts-7 prompts 6.6–14.5× slower,
239|  throughput −10% to −83%; routing-4 prompts 7–10% slower, −3.5% at
240|  32×1024 (`muse-round-2.md:134-146`).
241|- **Prevented in the specific case** by 0011 (both-phase rule, G3 prompt +
242|  whole-request times, hand-off). **Not prevented in general:** 0011 has its
243|  own "Not covered" (`:51`, other chunk/row counts) in the same citeable
244|  form, and the territory contains no rule that unmeasured = unverified.
245|  (Proposal: rephrase every "Not covered" as "unverified: assume nothing";
246|  this matches brief acceptance criterion 4.)
247|
248|### Behaviour 2 — end-to-end claims from piece arithmetic
249|- **Caused structurally by territory.** The design gives the swarm only
250|  per-slot piece timing in-round; the real objective (G3 over whole
251|  requests) arrives post-round via Claude (0006 `:42`, `:49`;
252|  `muse-swarm.md:133`). Nothing in the ADRs defines a valid in-round
253|  prediction formula, and 0011's G3 rule (faster-in-one/slower-in-neither
254|  vs *two* bars over 4 workloads, `:41`) has no in-round counterpart.
255|- **Territory documents the failure twice:** round 1's parts-vs-whole miss
256|  (`muse-round-1.md:106-109`) and round 2's pairs-add-up/triples-don't
257|  (`muse-round-2.md:125-127`), plus combine's 1.05 ms G3 loss exceeding its
258|  whole grader-measured kernel time — "the cost doesn't come from the
259|  kernel's own work as the grader runs it" (`muse-round-2.md:108`).
260|- **Partially addressed:** 0009's sign test (`:35-36`) and 0011's extension
261|  of it (`:22-26`) fixed *noise* in piece comparisons, not *composition*.
262|  The existing prevention channel is the starting point's "G3 effect against
263|  its prediction" per slot (0009 `:27`; `muse-swarm.md:103-104`), which
264|  carries the lesson forward but doesn't check new claims.
265|
266|### Behaviour 3 — inconsistent reasoning (non-composing sums, borrowed offsets)

268|  combine (−0.35 ms) and 32-request predictions; `:108` gives the
269|  unexplained gap. The findings don't dissect the README's internal
270|  contradiction (rounds explorer's job).
271|- **Territory already contains a per-attempt version of the fix:**
272|  `muse-swarm.md:88` — "if the attempt failed or missed its prediction by

274|  analysis." No equivalent rule covers Ready-to-test arithmetic or summary
275|  claims, and the boundary agent's checks are about ungraded row counts /
276|  races, not about prediction arithmetic (`muse-swarm.md:89`). (Proposal:
277|  extend the existing >20% rule to every Ready-to-test/summary number.)

1|"""Grade one kernel attempt: compile it, test it on captured inputs, time it.
2|
3|The independent grader for the Muse agent's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|G2 tests it on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step
5|(1, 8 and 32 rows), and on every layer's inputs in a prefill, recorded as
6|it runs (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows): every output must be identical to the
7|reference's, bit for bit, since only then are the model's tokens identical
8|(claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md). The timing runs at the same six
9|sizes and chains the 20 layers, so each call waits for the one before, as in
10|the model. The grader prints its verdict as JSON, and writes it to --out when
11|given. It never writes into the attempt folder, which holds only the Muse
12|agent's files.
13|
14|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt folder> <slot> [--out FILE]
15|      [--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER ...]
16|
17|The candidate and the compiled reference are timed in alternating repeats, so
18|drift in the GPU's clocks reaches both alike. At each size the candidate is
19|"faster" when it wins at least WINS_NEEDED of the REPEATS paired repeats (a
20|one-sided sign test at p < 0.01), "slower" when it loses that many, and
21|"same" otherwise; the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5% between
22|medians, so comparing medians alone would pass on noise. `beats_compiled`
23|needs both phases, decode and prefill: faster at every size of one, slower
24|at none of the other (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md).
25|
26|--baseline times an earlier, already graded attempt in the same run and adds
27|`beats_baseline`, judged the same way. From round 2 on, the bar is the
28|previous round's final attempt for the slot
29|(claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md). FOLDER alone is an attempt
30|for the same slot. For routing+combine, give either one routing+combine
31|attempt or `routing=FOLDER` and `combine=FOLDER`.
32|"""

91|def ulp_bf16(r):

97|def differences(g, r):

100|    differ = (g != r) & ~(np.isnan(g) & np.isnan(r))
101|    out = {"differ": int(differ.sum()), "max_ulp": 0.0}
102|    if out["differ"]:

104|            over = np.nan_to_num(np.abs(g - r) / ulp_bf16(r), nan=1e9, posinf=1e9)
105|        out |= {"max_ulp": float(min(over.max(), 1e9)), "at": int(over.argmax())}

186|def link(a, prev):
187|    """*a* unchanged, computed after *prev*: one small fused kernel."""
188|    return a + (prev.reshape(-1)[:1] * 0).astype(a.dtype)

191|def chained(fn, layers, names):
192|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
193|
194|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
195|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
196|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
197|    """
198|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
199|    outs = []
200|    for layer in layers:
201|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
202|        if outs:
203|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
204|        out = fn(**args)
205|        if isinstance(out, dict):
206|            out = list(out.values())
207|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
208|    return outs

211|def timed(fn, layers, names):
212|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
213|    for _ in range(3):
214|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
215|    times = []
216|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
217|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
218|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
219|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
220|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)

223|def paired_times(fns, layers, names):
224|    """Per-repeat µs per layer of each function, in rotating order within each repeat."""
225|    calls = [lambda f=f: mx.eval(chained(f, layers, names)) for f in fns]
226|    for _ in range(3):
227|        for call in calls:
228|            call()
229|    times = [[] for _ in fns]
230|    for i in range(REPEATS):
231|        for j in [(i + k) % len(fns) for k in range(len(fns))]:
232|            t0 = time.perf_counter()
233|            calls[j]()
234|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)
235|    return times

238|def compare(wins):
239|    """One size's verdict from the candidate's wins in REPEATS paired repeats."""
240|    if wins >= WINS_NEEDED:
241|        return "faster"
242|    if REPEATS - wins >= WINS_NEEDED:
243|        return "slower"
244|    return "same"

247|def judge(verdicts):
248|    """Each phase's verdict from its sizes' verdicts, and whether the candidate
249|    beats the bar: faster at every size of one phase, slower at no size of the other.
250|
251|    A phase is "faster" when every size is, "slower" when any size is, and
252|    "not slower" otherwise.
253|    """
254|    phases = {}
255|    for phase, prefix in PHASES.items():
256|        sizes = [v for size, v in verdicts.items() if size.startswith(prefix)]
257|        phases[phase] = (
258|            "faster" if all(v == "faster" for v in sizes)
259|            else "slower" if "slower" in sizes
260|            else "not slower"
261|        )
262|    beats = "faster" in phases.values() and "slower" not in phases.values()
263|    return phases, beats

24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
29|
30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
50|
51|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
52|
53|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
54||---|---|---|---|
55|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
56|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
57|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
58|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
59|
60|Reference:
61|
62|```python
63|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
64|```
65|
66|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
67|
68|### `routing+combine`
69|
70|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
71|
72|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
73|
74|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
75||---|---|---|---|
76|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
77|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
78|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
79|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
80|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
81|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
82|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
83|
84|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
85|
86|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
87|
88|```python
89|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
90|```
91|
92|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
93|
94|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
95|
96|## Tools and limits
97|
98|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.
99|- **The grader runs no Python of yours.** It reads your launch spec as data and compiles only your Metal.
100|- **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes, longer for an attempt much slower than the reference at the prefill sizes; stop one that runs past 15.
101|- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.
102|
103|## Rules of this session
104|
105|These keep your work apart from everyone else's. Git hooks and an audit script enforce them, and a commit that breaks them is refused.
106|
107|- **Write only inside `muse-spark/`.** Never change `bench/`, `claude/`, `results/`, `tools/`, `third_party/`, or any other file. A copy of the grader you edit is never used.
108|- **Commit only on `muse-agent`,** with the co-author trailer your settings add: `Co-Authored-By: Muse Spark (Meta Model API) <muse-spark@meta-model-api.invalid>`. Start each subject with `Muse Spark:`. No other co-author.
109|- **Never push, merge, rebase, change git config, or skip hooks.**
110|- **Don't read `.env`** or any credentials file.
111|- One commit per attempt, after you've run the grader on it, so the history shows every attempt in order.
112|
113|## Your files
114|
115|```
116|muse-spark/
117|  strategy.md                                your choice and design, ending with the targets JSON
118|  kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/
119|    block-0.metal, block-1.metal, ...        Metal kernel bodies (and headers), numbered from 0
120|    spec.json                                the launch spec
121|    notes.md                                 optional: what you tried and why
122|  summary.md                                 your final attempt per slot
123|```
124|
125|`<slot-folder>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing-combine` or `experts`. Grade an attempt with:
126|
127|```bash
128|.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N> <slot>
129|```
130|
131|where `<slot>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing+combine` or `experts`.
132|
133|**The targets JSON** at the end of `strategy.md`:
134|
135|```json
136|{
137|  "targets": [
138|    {"slot": "routing+combine", "why": "...", "expected_saving_ms": {"rows_1": 0.0, "rows_32": 0.0}, "design": "..."}
139|  ]
140|}
141|```
142|
143|List one or two targets, in the order you work on them.
144|
145|**The launch spec** (`spec.json`):
146|
147|```json
148|{
149|  "kernels": [
150|    {
151|      "name": "fused_routing",
152|      "source_block": 0,
153|      "header_block": null,
154|      "inputs": ["x", "w_router", "bias"],
155|      "outputs": [
156|        {"name": "inds", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "uint32"},
157|        {"name": "weights", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "float32"}
158|      ],
159|      "grid": ["rows*32", 1, 1],
160|      "threadgroup": [32, 1, 1],
161|      "template": {"T": "bfloat16"},
162|      "init_value": null,
163|      "atomic_outputs": false
164|    }
165|  ],
166|  "slot_outputs": {"inds": "inds", "weights": "weights"}
167|}
168|```
169|
170|- **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
171|- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
172|- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
173|- **`max_rows`** (optional, an integer of at least 1): inputs with more rows than this skip your kernels and run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. Use it to keep prefill-sized inputs on MLX's own code when your kernels are built for decode sizes; MLX switches its own experts kernel at 60 rows. The hand-off is graded like the rest: bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes.
174|- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot, `max_rows` included: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
175|- **Shape and grid entries** are integers, or products of integers and the names `rows`, `D`, `E`, `K` and `H`, such as `"rows*32"`. Nothing else is evaluated.
176|- **dtypes** are `float32`, `bfloat16`, `float16`, `uint32` or `int32`.
177|- **Template values** are one of those dtypes, an integer or a boolean.
178|- **`grid`** counts threads, not threadgroups, as in `mx.fast.metal_kernel`.
179|
180|## How each attempt is judged
181|
182|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only. From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.
183|
184|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
185|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
186|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
187|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
188|
189|   At every size:
190|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
191|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
192|
193|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
194|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
195|3. **G3, faster, in vLLM.** Each workload runs 5 times in shuffled order: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts, 256 generated tokens each. Three times are measured per run:
196|   - the **decode step**, the median period between steady steps;
197|   - the **prompt time**, until every prompt was processed;
198|   - the **whole request**, from sending the requests to the last token.
199|
200|   Against both the original model and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code, the attempt passes when the decode step or the prompt time is faster in every workload, neither is slower in any, and no whole request is slower. Faster and slower mean that the ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
201|
202|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
203|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
204|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
205|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same` or `slower`); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.
206|
207|**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
208|- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
209|- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
210|- **Per phase:** decode (1, 8, 32 rows) and prefill (127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) are each `faster` when every size is, `slower` when any size is, and `not slower` otherwise.
211|- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
212|
213|It is a guide; G3 decides.
214|
215|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and has `beats_compiled` true, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

1|"""One GPU job at a time: the exclusive lock every grader entry point takes.
2|
3|Muse Spark's builder agents and Claude run these scripts on the same M1 Pro
4|GPU, and two runs at once distort each other's timings. A run that finds the
5|GPU busy says so and waits its turn, so runs queue and never overlap. The lock
6|file is in /tmp, so the main checkout and the Muse Spark worktree share it, and
7|the operating system releases it when the process ends, however it ends.
8|"""
9|
10|import fcntl
11|import os
12|import sys
13|
14|LOCK = "/tmp/mobilemoe-gpu.lock"
15|_held = []  # keeps the locked file open for the life of the process
16|
17|
18|def hold(job):
19|    """Take the GPU for this process, waiting while another run has it."""
20|    f = open(LOCK, "a+")
21|    try:
22|        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
23|    except BlockingIOError:
24|        f.seek(0)
25|        holder = f.read().strip() or "another run"
26|        print(f"{job}: waiting for the GPU ({holder})", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
27|        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
28|    f.seek(0)
29|    f.truncate()
30|    f.write(f"pid {os.getpid()}: {job}\n")
31|    f.flush()
32|    _held.append(f)

211|
212|            MetalModelRunner._submit_paged_forward_outputs = submit
213|            try:
214|                bd.REC.reset(rows)
215|                res = llm.generate(prompts, params, use_tqdm=False)
216|                bd.REC.end_step()

221|        for name in variants.names[1:]:

228|def divergence(got, want):
229|    """How many sequences' greedy tokens differ, and the first step where any does."""
230|    first = [
231|        next((i for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(g, w)) if a != b), None)
232|        for g, w in zip(got, want)
233|    ]
234|    differ = [f for f in first if f is not None]
235|    return {"rows_differ": len(differ), "first_differ_step": min(differ, default=None)}

277|def prompt_ms():
278|    """The last run's time from its first forward pass to its first one with no
279|    prompt tokens left: until every prompt was processed (vLLM's steps only)."""
280|    steps = [m for m, _ in bd.REC.steps if "t" in m]
281|    done = next((m["t"] for m in steps if m.get("prefill") == 0), None)

285|def time_variants(engine, variants, checks, run, log, settings=SETTINGS, repeats=REPEATS):
286|    """Log the checks, then time every variant at *settings* (rows, prompt tokens)
287|    in *repeats* shuffled repeats. Each run also records its wall time and prompt_ms()."""

292|            )

296|                flush=True,
297|            )

299|    plan = []

301|        block = [(v, r, p) for v in variants.names for r, p in settings]
302|        random.Random(100 + rep).shuffle(block)
303|        plan += [(rep, *b) for b in block]

307|        bd.REC.reset(rows)
308|        before = bd.machine()
309|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
310|        run(rows, prompt, rows * 10000 + prompt)

321|            prompt=prompt,
322|            rep=rep,

324|            machine_after=bd.machine(),

330|            f"{record['period_median_ms']:7.3f} ms/step",
331|            flush=True,
332|        )

336|    runs = [json.loads(line) for line in log.read_text().splitlines()]
337|    for rows, prompt in settings:

339|        for name in variants.names:

341|                r["period_median_ms"]
342|                for r in runs
343|                if r["kind"] == "run"
344|                and r["variant"] == name
345|                and r["rows"] == rows
346|                and r["prompt"] == prompt

356|            print(

5|# From round 3, an improvement must hold in both phases, decode and prefill, and an attempt may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference
6|
7|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
8|
9|**The change.** Claude's comparison of every engine version over whole requests ([findings](../findings/muse-round-2.md), section 5) found that the grader and G3 timed only the decode step. They never timed the prefill, the phase in which a request's whole prompt runs through the model:
10|- **Experts attempt-7** looked like round 2's largest gain, a 19% shorter decode step at 32 requests. It processed prompts 6.6 to 14.5 times slower and cut throughput by 10% to 83%.
11|- **Routing attempt-4,** round 2's only baseline, processed prompts 7% to 10% slower. At 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts it cost 3.5% of throughput.
12|
13|The Muse agent never saw either effect: its piece timing ran decode sizes only, and G3 measured the decode step only.
14|
15|On 2026-11-04 surucuonur set the rule: "The improvement should be in the two phases of it: decode and prefill. Then, we can consider it as an improvement." surucuonur chose:
16|- **faster in one phase, slower in neither;**
17|- **the hand-off:** an attempt may leave prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference. This replaces the part of [ADR 0010](0010-exact-at-every-size.md) that required the kernels to run in every call.
18|
19|## How it works
20|
21|- **The piece timing runs at the six G2 sizes** (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`): decode at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. The layers are still chained.
22|- **The verdict at each size comes from paired repeats.** The candidate and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times, and so does the baseline when one is given.
23|  - The candidate is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, a one-sided sign test at p < 0.01.
24|  - It is `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise.
25|
26|  This replaces the comparison of medians for the decode sizes too, since the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
27|- **The verdict per phase:**
28|  - a phase is `faster` when every one of its sizes is;
29|  - it is `slower` when any size is;
30|  - otherwise it is `not slower`.
31|
32|  `beats_compiled`, and `beats_baseline` against a baseline, are true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
33|- **The hand-off** (`max_rows` in `spec.json`, `bench/grader/slots.py`). Inputs with more rows than `max_rows` run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. G2 still checks every size.
34|  - On 2026-11-04 the compiled reference of each slot was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes (`bench/micro/compiled_exact.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`).
35|  - Above `max_rows` a hand-off runs the compiled reference itself, so it times `same` as the bar there, never better.
36|- **G3** (`bench/grader/time_candidates.py`, which writes `g3-vllm.json`):
37|  - **Workloads:** 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts.
38|  - **Measurements per run:** the decode step period, the prompt time and the whole-request time, over 5 shuffled repeats, up from 3.
39|  - **Faster and slower:** the two ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
40|  - **Why 5 repeats:** with 3 each, two identical engines' ranges miss each other by chance 1 time in 20 per direction. "Never slower" checks a phase 8 times (4 workloads, 2 bars), so a phase that changed nothing would fail about a third of the time. The first run under these rules showed it. A copy of experts attempt-7 with a hand-off at 59 rows came out `slower` on prompt time at 32 × 1,024, by 0.5% with ranges 16 ms apart, although above 59 rows it runs the compiled reference, whose own range overlapped the unchanged engine's (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`). With 5 repeats the chance is 1 in 252 per check, about 3% over 8.
41|  - **The pass rule:** against both the original model and the compiled reference, the decode step or the prompt time must be faster in every workload, neither may be slower in any, and no whole request may be slower.
42|- **The unchanged engine is vLLM's own.** The original model in G3 runs with Claude's step hooks, and with vLLM's engine inside the script's process. On 2026-11-04, alternating runs found it within −0.2% to +1.9% of vLLM with neither, inside the spread between repeats in every workload (`bench/micro/clean_vllm.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-clean-vllm/`).
43|
44|## Consequences
45|
46|- **Round 3 starts with no baseline.** Routing attempt-4 is `slower` at all three prefill sizes, 2.6 to 8.7 times the compiled reference's time. It fails G3 on prompt time at 8 and 32 requests. It becomes a starting point, so round 3's bar in every slot is the compiled reference.
47|- **A decode kernel no longer has to win at prefill sizes,** only to hand them off or not lose there. The attempt chooses the row count, so the boundary agent checks that the hand-off sits on the right side of 60 rows for the experts slot.
48|- **At prefill sizes, a slot with a hand-off is MLX's code, not the Muse agent's.** The claim for such an attempt is "faster decode, unchanged prefill".
49|- **Grader runs and G3 take longer.** Every attempt is now timed at three more sizes. G3 runs 5 repeats instead of 3, and its 32 × 1,024 workload adds at least 16 s per variant per repeat.
50|- **The decode verdict is stricter.** An attempt whose median beat the compiled reference by noise is now `same`.
51|- **Not covered:** prefill chunks of other sizes, and decode steps with other row counts. The boundary agent reports them; G3's four workloads are the end-to-end check.
52|- **At 1 request the whole-request time is noisy.** On 2026-11-04 its repeats spread 6% to 41%, so G3 there mostly says `same`, which passes the "never slower" test without showing a gain.
53|
54|## Considered options
55|
56|- **Faster in both phases.** The higher bar. A decode kernel would also have to beat MLX's large matrix kernels at 2,048 rows, which is not where the decode step loses its time. Not chosen.
57|- **Whole-request throughput alone.** Simple, but it lets a slower phase be traded for a faster one. surucuonur ruled that out.
58|- **Hand off to the uncompiled reference.** The prefill could then come out `slower` than the compiled reference wherever compiling helps; at 127 rows, routing's compiled reference takes 87 µs per layer against 102 µs uncompiled.
59|- **Keep the kernels in every call** (ADR 0010). The kernels could still branch on the row count inside themselves, but they couldn't use MLX's large-size kernels. surucuonur chose the hand-off.

83|4. **Builders compete.** Two or three builders each take a different direction from the analysis, for example fusing kernels, reading each weight byte once, or a different threadgroup shape. Each builder:
84|   1. claims the next attempt number with `mkdir`, which fails if another builder took it first;

89|5. **Commit and check.** When a builder returns, the lead commits its attempt as the next implementation version. The boundary agent then checks every attempt that passed G2 for what the grader can't see: other row counts, threadgroup memory read before it is written, and results that depend on thread timing.

91|   - **Harden:** if the best attempt still has a cause that can be named and removed, a builder makes its next single change.

99|## Rounds build on each other
100|
101|From round 2 on, a round starts where the earlier ones stopped ([ADR 0009](adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md)).
102|- **Finished rounds are frozen.** After a round's transcripts are committed, Claude tags its last commit `muse-round-<N>` (round 1: `muse-round-1`). The hooks then refuse any change to that round's files, and new files anywhere but the current round's folder and the transcripts.
103|- **The starting point.** The lead first reads the earlier rounds' final documents, the best attempts' notes and Claude's G3 report on the previous round. It writes the plan at the top of the round's exploration README:
104|  - per slot, the best attempt so far that passes G2 and that Claude's G3 accepted, the **baseline**, or where there is none, the attempt to start from; and how its G3 effect compared with its prediction;
105|  - what is left to build;

109|  Without Claude's report the round stops.
110|- **The baseline is the bar.** Where a slot has one, a new attempt must beat it in the same grader run (`check_candidate.py --baseline`). The two are timed in alternating repeats at the six sizes. At each size the attempt is faster when it wins at least 22 of 30, and slower when it loses 22; it must be faster at every size of one phase and slower at none of the other. A slot that nothing beats keeps its baseline for G3. A slot without one is measured against the compiled reference, as in round 1.

112|## Shared documents and versions
113|
114|Each phase folder, `<round>/exploration/` and `<round>/implementation/`, holds three kinds of document:
115|
116|| Document | Written by | Holds |
117||---|---|---|
118|| `README.md` | the lead only | the version line, the tracker table, the phase's analysis or report, and `## Versions`, its changelog |
119|| entries (`territory-*`, `ineff-*`, `hyp-*`) | the owner; others add notes under `## From other agents` | a status block (owner, status, version, updated, next) and the content |
120|| `log.md` | every agent, appending one line per event | time, agent, and what happened |
121|
122|Every version is raised by a single writer, so no number is taken twice:
123|- **Phase versions.** Each checkpoint raises the README's version and is exactly one commit, whose subject names it: `<name>: exploration v5: …`, for example `Muse Wonder: exploration v5: …` in round 2. `git diff` between two version commits shows what changed.
124|- **Entry versions** are raised by the entry's owner, by the verifier with its verdict, or by the lead for hypothesis entries.
125|- **The skill's own version** is in its header and its [changelog](../.agents/skills/muse-round/CHANGELOG.md), and each round records the version it ran.
126|
127|## What keeps it honest
128|
129|- **Placement.** The Muse agent writes only in its round's folder in `muse-spark/`, on `muse-agent`, and only the lead commits, always with its model's co-author. A finished round's files can't change. The git hooks refuse anything else, and [tools/provenance_check.py](../tools/provenance_check.py) re-checks the whole history.
130|- **Sources.** Every number in the shared documents has a source: a file and line, a table row, a grader verdict, or arithmetic shown in full.

{"content":""""The round's submission check: one pinned end-to-end run, judged like G3.

PROTOTYPE for design-lab/designer-a (design: "one gate"). Proposed real
location: bench/grader/check_submission.py. It changes no tracked file; it
delegates the GPU work to bench/grader/time_candidates.py with pinned
arguments, then audits the log and the G3 verdict.

  python check_submission.py <out dir> <SLOT=FOLDER>... [--dry-run]

What it pins (the G3 rule of claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:36-41):
engine vllm, 4 workloads (1x128, 8x128, 32x128, 32x1024), 5 repeats,
256 tokens, every submitted slot passed positionally in one call so
muse-all is measured as a combination, no --variant extras.

What it adds over calling time_candidates.py directly:
- the free flags (--repeats, --settings, --tokens, --variant) do not exist,
  so the run cannot be shrunk or widened by accident or design;
- the end-to-end token check (exact greedy tokens at 1 and 32 requests,
  the brief's G2) becomes a gate: time_candidates.py logs `exact` but
  never judges it (time_candidates.py:168-197 reads only kind=="run");
- the audit replays the log: every expected (variant, rows, prompt, rep)
  run present, engine vllm, then every judged muse-* variant's g3 pass.

It writes <out>/submission-verdict.json (the file the swarm cites) and:
- exit 0 with PASS lines: every judged variant passes vs base and its
  compiled-* bar, with exact tokens;
- exit 1: a variant fails (verdict FAIL, still written);
- exit 2: usage error or the log is incomplete (never cite it).

The GPU lock is taken by time_candidates.py (time_candidates.py:224);
--dry-run prints the pinned command and touches nothing.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Pinned G3 shape. Must equal time_candidates.G3_SETTINGS / G3_REPEATS and
# the --tokens default; main() asserts that before delegating, so drift fails
# loudly instead of silently running a different check.
EXPECTED_SETTINGS = ((1, 128), (8, 128), (32, 128), (32, 1024))
EXPECTED_REPEATS = 5
EXPECTED_TOKENS = 256


def expected_variants(slots):
    """Variant names one pinned call builds (time_candidates.py:111-132)."""
    names = ["base"]
    for slot in slots:
        names += [f"compiled-{slot}", f"muse-{slot}"]
    if len(slots) > 1:
        names += ["compiled-all", "muse-all"]
    return names


def judged_variants(slots):
    """Variants the verdict must pass: each muse-<slot>, plus muse-all."""
    names = [f"muse-{s}" for s in slots]
    if len(slots) > 1:
        names.append("muse-all")
    return names


def audit(out, slots):
    """Replay <out>/muse-vllm.jsonl + g3-vllm.json. Returns (verdict, problems).

    verdict: {"pass": bool, "variants": {name: {...}}, "params": {...}}.
    problems: lines explaining why the log cannot be cited (empty when citable).
    """
    problems = []
    log = out / "muse-vllm.jsonl"
    g3file = out / "g3-vllm.json"
    if not log.exists():
        return None, [f"missing {log}"]
    if not g3file.exists():
        return None, [f"missing {g3file} (no G3 verdict: not a vllm run?)"]
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in log.read_text().splitlines()]
    runs = [r for r in records if r.get("kind") == "run"]
    checks = [r for r in records if r.get("kind") == "check"]

    want = expected_variants(slots)
    got = sorted({r["variant"] for r in runs})
    if got != sorted(want):
        problems.append(f"variants {got}, want {want}")
    for r in runs:
        if r.get("engine") != "vllm":
            problems.append(f"run {r.get('variant')} rep {r.get('rep')}: engine {r.get('engine')!r}, want 'vllm'")
            break
    for name in want:
        for rows, prompt in EXPECTED_SETTINGS:
            reps = sorted(
                r["rep"]
                for r in runs
                if (r["variant"], r["rows"], r["prompt"]) == (name, rows, prompt)
            )
            if reps != list(range(EXPECTED_REPEATS)):
                problems.append(
                    f"{name} {rows}x{prompt}: reps {reps}, want 0..{EXPECTED_REPEATS - 1}"
                )

    exact = {}
    for name in judged_variants(slots):
        for rows in (1, 32):
            recs = [
                c for c in checks
                if (c["variant"], c["rows"]) == (name, rows)
            ]
            if len(recs) != 1:
                problems.append(f"check {name} rows {rows}: {len(recs)} records, want 1")
                exact[(name, rows)] = False
            else:
                exact[(name, rows)] = recs[0].get("exact") is True
                if not exact[(name, rows)]:
                    problems.append(
                        f"check {name} rows {rows}: exact is {recs[0].get('exact')!r}, "
                        f"want True ({recs[0].get('rows_differ')} sequences differ)"
                    )

    g3 = json.loads(g3file.read_text())
    verdict = {"params": {
        "engine": "vllm", "repeats": EXPECTED_REPEATS, "tokens": EXPECTED_TOKENS,
        "settings": [f"{r}x{p}" for r, p in EXPECTED_SETTINGS],
        "slots": list(slots),
    }, "variants": {}}
    allpass = not problems
    for name in judged_variants(slots):
        v = g3.get(name, {})
        bars = {b: v.get(b, {}) for b in ("base", "compiled-" + name.removeprefix("muse-"))}
        ok = v.get("g3") is True and all(b.get("pass") is True for b in bars.values())
        verdict["variants"][name] = {
            "pass": ok and all(exact.get((name, r), False) for r in (1, 32)),
            "g3": v.get("g3"),
            "bars": {b: bars[b].get("pass") for b in bars},
            "phases": {b: bars[b].get("phases") for b in bars},
            "exact_1": exact.get((name, 1)), "exact_32": exact.get((name, 32)),
        }
        allpass = allpass and verdict["variants"][name]["pass"]
    verdict["pass"] = allpass
    return verdict, problems


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("out", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("attempts", nargs="+", metavar="SLOT=FOLDER")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    slots = [a.partition("=")[0] for a in args.attempts]
    if any(not s or "=" not in a for s, a in zip(slots, args.attempts)):
        ap.error("give SLOT=FOLDER per submitted slot")

    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    cmd = (
        f"{here}/check_submission.py {args.out} " + " ".join(args.attempts)
        if here.name != "grader"
        else None
    )
    if args.dry_run:
        print("pinned run: time_candidates.py vllm"
              f" {args.out} {' '.join(args.attempts)}"
              f" --repeats {EXPECTED_REPEATS} --tokens {EXPECTED_TOKENS}"
              " --settings " + ",".join(f"{r}x{p}" for r, p in EXPECTED_SETTINGS))
        print("judged:", " ".join(judged_variants(slots)))
        return 0

    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("bench/grader").resolve()))
    import time_candidates as tc

    assert tc.G3_SETTINGS == ",".join(f"{r}x{p}" for r, p in EXPECTED_SETTINGS), \
        f"G3_SETTINGS drifted: {tc.G3_SETTINGS}"
    assert tc.G3_REPEATS == EXPECTED_REPEATS, f"G3_REPEATS drifted: {tc.G3_REPEATS}"
    sys.argv = ["time_candidates.py", "vllm", str(args.out), *args.attempts,
                "--repeats", str(EXPECTED_REPEATS), "--tokens", str(EXPECTED_TOKENS),
                "--settings", tc.G3_SETTINGS]
    tc.main()
    verdict, problems = audit(args.out, slots)
    (args.out / "submission-verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(verdict, indent=1) + "\n")
    for line in problems:
        print(f"UNCITABLE: {line}")
    for name, v in verdict["variants"].items():
        print(f"{'PASS' if v['pass'] else 'FAIL'} {name}"
              f" g3={v['g3']} bars={v['bars']} exact={v['exact_1']}/{v['exact_32']}")
    if problems:
        return 2
    return 0 if verdict["pass"] else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

{"content":""""Tests for prototypes/check_submission.py. No GPU: audit + CLI only."""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

PROTO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "prototypes"
sys.path.insert(0, str(PROTO))
import check_submission as cs

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent.parent


def make_log(d, slots, reps=5, exact=True, g3pass=True):
    """A synthetic pinned run: jsonl + g3 file in d. Returns d."""
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with (d / "muse-vllm.jsonl").open("w") as f:
        for name in cs.expected_variants(slots):
            for rows in (1, 32):
                rec = {"kind": "check", "variant": name, "rows": rows, "kernels": 900}
                if name != "base":
                    rec |= {"exact": exact, "rows_differ": 0 if exact else 3,
                            "first_differ_step": None if exact else 0}
                f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
        for name in cs.expected_variants(slots):
            for rows, prompt in cs.EXPECTED_SETTINGS:
                for rep in range(reps):
                    f.write(json.dumps({
                        "kind": "run", "engine": "vllm", "variant": name,
                        "rows": rows, "prompt": prompt, "rep": rep,
                        "period_median_ms": 5.0, "prompt_ms": 10.0, "wall_ms": 100.0,
                    }) + "\n")
    g3 = {}
    for name in cs.judged_variants(slots):
        bar = "compiled-" + name.removeprefix("muse-")
        ph = {"decode": "faster", "prompt": "not slower", "request": "not slower"}
        g3[name] = {"base": {"pass": g3pass, "phases": ph},
                    bar: {"pass": g3pass, "phases": ph}, "g3": g3pass}
    (d / "g3-vllm.json").write_text(json.dumps(g3))
    return d


results = []
def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    results.append(("PASS" if cond else "FAIL") + f" {name} {detail}")
    assert cond, name


# 1. dry run prints the pinned command, touches nothing
p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, PROTO / "check_submission.py", "OUT",
                    "routing=A", "combine=B", "--dry-run"],
                   capture_output=True, text=True)
check("dry-run exit 0", p.returncode == 0, p.stderr.strip())
check("dry-run pins vllm/5/256/4-settings",
      all(s in p.stdout for s in ("vllm", "--repeats 5", "--tokens 256",
                                  "1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024")), p.stdout.strip())
check("dry-run judges muse-all", "muse-all" in p.stdout, p.stdout.strip())

# 2. gaming flags do not exist
for flag in ("--repeats", "--settings", "--tokens", "--variant"):
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, PROTO / "check_submission.py", "OUT",
                        "routing=A", flag, "1"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    check(f"{flag} rejected", p.returncode == 2, p.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1][:80])

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
    # 3. synthetic PASS: 2 slots -> all judged pass, exact, full coverage
    d = make_log(Path(t) / "pass", ["routing", "combine"])
    v, probs = cs.audit(d, ["routing", "combine"])
    check("fixture pass", v["pass"] and not probs, str(probs))
    check("fixture judges 3", sorted(v["variants"]) == ["muse-all", "muse-combine", "muse-routing"])

    # 4. one variant fails G3 -> overall fail, still citable
    d = make_log(Path(t) / "fail", ["routing"], g3pass=False)
    v, probs = cs.audit(d, ["routing"])
    check("g3-fail verdict", v["pass"] is False and not probs, str(probs))

    # 5. inexact tokens -> fail with problem (the brief's G2 as a gate)
    d = make_log(Path(t) / "inexact", ["routing"], exact=False)
    v, probs = cs.audit(d, ["routing"])
    check("inexact fails", v["pass"] is False and any("exact" in p for p in probs), str(probs[:1]))

    # 6. short repeats -> uncitable (catches --repeats 1 style runs)
    d = make_log(Path(t) / "short", ["routing"], reps=1)
    v, probs = cs.audit(d, ["routing"])
    check("1-repeat uncitable", probs and "reps [0]" in probs[0], str(probs[:1]))

# 7. real round-2 log: 3 repeats x 3 settings, no g3 file -> uncitable, parsed fine
v, probs = cs.audit(ROOT / "results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2", ["routing", "combine"])
check("round-2 log uncitable (no g3 file)", v is None and "g3-vllm.json" in probs[0], str(probs))

# 8. real handoff log: parses, exact seen, but 3 != 5 repeats -> uncitable
v, probs = cs.audit(ROOT / "results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check", ["experts"])
check("handoff log parsed", v is not None and v["variants"]["muse-experts"]["exact_1"] is True)
check("handoff uncitable on repeats", any("reps [0, 1, 2]" in p for p in probs), str(probs[:1]))
check("handoff verdict preserved", v["variants"]["muse-experts"]["g3"] is False)

print("\n".join(results))
print(f"\n{sum(r.startswith('PASS') for r in results)}/{len(results)} passed")
","path":"design-lab/designer-a/tests/test_check_submission.py"}
