{"content":""""The harden failure-point counter, replayed on round-2 records (no GPU).

Rule (proposed): a hypothesis entry records each graded attempt's failure
point = the sizes where vs_compiled is "slower" (or the G2-fail sizes) plus
the named cause. After 3 consecutive attempts fail at the SAME failure point,
the next builder takes a different approach (a different design family, named
in the log), or the lead logs why not.

Data below is quoted from muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:9
(1-row chained candidate vs compiled) and hyp-1-experts-exact.md (causes).
"""
import sys

# (attempt, 1-row verdict vs compiled, named cause); verdicts from README:9:
# candidates 104.3/103.6/109.5/94.0/92.1/--/93.8 vs compiled
# 77.6/73.1/86.9/73.5/75.9/74.8 -- slower at 1 row every timed attempt.
EXPERTS = [
    (1, "slower@1", "1-row occupancy: 4 threadgroups"),
    (2, "slower@1", "1-row occupancy: 4 threadgroups"),
    (3, "slower@1", "1-row occupancy: 4 threadgroups"),  # :254-258 refutes count as lever, same point
    (4, "slower@1", "1-row occupancy: fused packing"),
    (5, "slower@1", "1-row occupancy: fused packing"),
    (6, None, "G1 fail: threadgroup 512 > 448 max"),      # unlaunched, no verdict
    (7, "slower@1", "1-row occupancy: fused packing"),
]
# routing (README:10): attempt-4 wins everywhere at decode; mixed verdicts.
ROUTING = [
    (1, "mixed", None), (2, "G2-fail prefill", "prefill rounding"),
    (3, "slower@8,32", "latency-bound unstaged"), (4, "faster", None),
]

def replay(attempts, n=3):
    """Returns (trigger_after_attempt or None). G1/None verdicts pause, not reset."""
    run, point = 0, None
    for num, verdict, cause in attempts:
        if verdict in ("faster",) or verdict is None and cause and cause.startswith("G1"):
            if verdict == "faster":
                run, point = 0, None
            continue  # unlaunched: pause the counter, keep the point
        fp = (verdict, cause.split(":")[0] if cause else None)
        run = run + 1 if fp == point else 1
        point = fp
        if run >= n:
            return num, fp
    return None, None

results = []
def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    results.append(("PASS" if cond else "FAIL") + f" {name} {detail}")
    assert cond, name

num, fp = replay(EXPERTS)
check("experts triggers after attempt 3", num == 3, f"trigger={num} {fp}")
check("attempts saved", f"{7 - 3} of 7 fused attempts post-trigger (4-5,7 keep family)")
num, _ = replay(ROUTING)
check("routing never triggers", num is None, f"trigger={num}")
num, _ = replay(EXPERTS[:2])
check("no early trigger at 2", num is None)
# cause change resets even at same sizes: new diagnosis, new run
num, _ = replay([(1, "slower@1", "cause A"), (2, "slower@1", "cause A"), (3, "slower@1", "cause B")])
check("new cause restarts count", num is None)

print("\n".join(results))
print(f"\n{sum(r.startswith('PASS') for r in results)}/{len(results)} passed")
print("Design note: N=3 is evidence-grounded -- attempts 1-3 already spanned")
print("per-pair, block-split and 4-block packings (hyp-1 :178-241) at the same point.")
","path":"design-lab/designer-a/tests/test_failure_counter.py"}

{"content":""""The claim rules, replayed on round-2's Ready to test (no GPU).

Proposed rules (tracking.md number rule, extended):
 R1 every speed claim cites a measurement of exactly what is claimed at the
    level claimed (piece -> grader verdict file; end-to-end -> submission
    verdict file), or is labelled PREDICTION next to its measured value.
 R2 a prediction counts only the candidate's own measured effect; a
    combination's effect is measured as a combination (muse-all), never summed.
 R3 anything unmeasured is listed UNVERIFIED, never assumed free or neutral.

Claims below are quoted from muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:29-36.
"""
import sys

def judge(claim):
    """claim: dict(level, cites, own_effect_only, combination_measured,
    labelled_prediction, has_measured_beside, assumes_unmeasured).
    Returns [flags]."""
    flags = []
    if claim["level"] == "end-to-end" and claim["cites"] != "submission-verdict":
        if not (claim["labelled_prediction"] and claim["has_measured_beside"]):
            flags.append("R1: end-to-end claim without submission-verdict cite, "
                         "unlabelled or without measured value beside it")
    if not claim["own_effect_only"]:
        flags.append("R2: counts effect other than the candidate's own measured effect")
    if claim["is_combination"] and not claim["combination_measured"]:
        flags.append("R2: combination claimed from summed parts, not measured as one")
    if claim["assumes_unmeasured"]:
        flags.append("R3: unmeasured cost assumed free/neutral, not listed unverified")
    return flags

CASES = [
    ("routing -0.48/-0.50/-0.49 vs unchanged (README:33)",
     {"level": "end-to-end", "cites": "grader+old-G3", "own_effect_only": False,
      "is_combination": False, "combination_measured": False,
      "labelled_prediction": False, "has_measured_beside": False,
      "assumes_unmeasured": False},
     ["R1", "R2"]),  # borrows compiled refs' G3 offsets (-0.22/-0.18/-0.16)
    ("Together (sum) -0.84/-0.85/-0.84 (README:36)",
     {"level": "end-to-end", "cites": "arithmetic", "own_effect_only": True,
      "is_combination": True, "combination_measured": False,
      "labelled_prediction": False, "has_measured_beside": False,
      "assumes_unmeasured": True},  # interaction "unmeasured for the new pair" (:38)
     ["R1", "R2", "R3"]),
    ("piece basis -0.26/-0.32/-0.33 vs compiled, own run, labelled (allowed form)",
     {"level": "piece", "cites": "grader", "own_effect_only": True,
      "is_combination": False, "combination_measured": False,
      "labelled_prediction": True, "has_measured_beside": True,
      "assumes_unmeasured": False},
     []),
    ("prefill branch 'free apart from time to first token' (hyp-1:150-151)",
     {"level": "piece", "cites": "ADR-quote", "own_effect_only": True,
      "is_combination": False, "combination_measured": False,
      "labelled_prediction": False, "has_measured_beside": False,
      "assumes_unmeasured": True},
     ["R3"]),
]

results = []
def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    results.append(("PASS" if cond else "FAIL") + f" {name} {detail}")
    assert cond, name

for title, claim, want in CASES:
    flags = judge(claim)
    got = sorted(f.split(":")[0] for f in flags)
    check(title[:60], got == sorted(want), f"flags={got}")
    for f in flags:
        results.append(f"      flag: {f}")

print("\n".join(results))
n = sum(r.startswith("PASS") for r in results)
print(f"\n{n}/{len(CASES)} cases judged as designed")
print("Design note: every round-2 violation above is checkable by the verifier")
print("from cited files alone -- no GPU, no judgement call about physics.")
","path":"design-lab/designer-a/tests/test_claim_rules.py"}

{"content":"# Skill/brief text prototype: exact replacement blocks for the "one gate" design

Each block names its location (file + anchor lines at worktree commit 1113c2d),
quotes the current text briefly, and gives the replacement. Implementation is
review + paste + version bump; nothing here edits the originals.

Conventions reused: positive phrasing, explicit checkable rules (behaviour-4
lesson, CHANGELOG.md:12), one writer per document, versioned skill (v8).

---

## 1. SKILL.md:20 — the goal (proxy named as proxy, gate named as verdict)

Now: "The goal: kernels that pass G1 and G2 and have `beats_compiled` true, ..."

New:

> The goal: kernels that pass G1, G2 and the **submission check**: faster in
> one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither, against the unchanged
> model and the compiled reference, measured end to end
> ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); where the slot
> has a baseline, the attempt also beats it in the same grader run. The
> grader's `beats_compiled` is the filter builders use: cheap, per-slot, and
> explicitly a proxy. The submission check is the verdict. A faster decode
> step bought with a slower prefill is no improvement, in either.

## 2. SKILL.md:135-141 — harden (failure counter) and close (`candidate`)

Now: pick best (:136), "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can
name and remove" (:138), close `ready`/`dropped` (:140-141).

New step 5 (Harden):

> 5. **Harden.**
>    - Pick the best attempt: it passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, has
>      `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline,
>      `beats_baseline`, and it is the fastest across the six sizes.
>    - Set the status to `hardening`, and start a builder for that attempt's
>      next single change.
>    - Record each graded attempt's **failure point** in the hypothesis entry:
>      the sizes where it is `slower` than the compiled reference (or the
>      sizes where G2 fails), plus the cause you name for it.
>    - Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove,
>      except: **after 3 consecutive graded attempts fail at the same failure
>      point, the next builder takes a different approach** — a different
>      design family, named in the log (for example unfused kernels instead
>      of another fused packing) — **or you log why not.** An unlaunched
>      attempt (G1 fail) pauses the count without resetting it. A new cause
>      restarts the count only when it cites the measurement that refuted the
>      old one.

New step 6 (Close):

> 6. **Close.**
>    - **`candidate`:** the best attempt passes G1, G2 and its boundary
>      check, has `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline,
>      `beats_baseline` true, and you can name no further change worth
>      making. Write the **Decision**: the attempt, why it is best, its
>      failure-point history, and its piece-basis **prediction** for the
>      submission check, labelled as one, counting only the candidate's own
>      measured effect.
>    - **`dropped`:** say why. A slot whose hypotheses are all dropped keeps
>      its baseline, or the reference where it has none.
>    - Nothing is `ready` yet: that waits for the submission check at Finish.

## 3. SKILL.md:145-147 — Finish (check runs before Ready to test)

New step 5 opening + item 1:

> ### 5. Finish
>
> 1. **The submission check.** If any hypothesis closed `candidate`, run the
>    round's one submission check yourself (tracking.md *Rules for every
>    agent*): every candidate slot positionally in a single call, so the
>    combination is measured too. It takes about 15 minutes per slot once it
>    starts; it prints while it runs; stop it only after 90 minutes, and
>    record that as a fail. On `FAIL`, each failed hypothesis goes back to
>    `hardening` or `dropped` with the verdict as the reason; you may fix and
>    run **one** second check, then Finish with whatever passed. At most two
>    checks per round; log both, cite the last. Then set each checked
>    hypothesis `ready` (its variant `PASS`) or `dropped` (it did not pass),
>    in a checkpoint.
> 2. **The implementation README:** the final tracker, one paragraph per
>    hypothesis, and a **Ready to test** section. It names the attempt per
>    slot that goes to G3 — this round's `ready` attempt, the baseline kept,
>    or the reference — and reports, per slot and for the combination: the
>    submission verdict file, each judged variant's phases against both bars,
>    its token-exactness, the piece-basis prediction **labelled as one next
>    to the measured value**, and what stays **unverified**. When the
>    combination was not measured (single slot) or did not pass, say so; never
>    sum per-slot figures into a together-number.

(Renumber old items 2-4 to 3-5. Summary item "the expected G3 change" becomes
"the measured in-round change per slot and combination, with the prediction
it is compared against".)

## 4. SKILL.md:164 — G3 line (decided direction replaces the ban)

Now: "**G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team,** who run them after merging
your branch."

New:

> **The submission check is yours; G3 stays Claude's.** You measure your own
> submission end to end at Finish, through the GPU queue. After merging,
> surucuonur's team re-runs G1 and G2 and runs G3 independently; where their
> G3 disagrees with your submission check beyond the repeats' noise, theirs
> decides, and the next round's starting point records why.

## 5. tracking.md:108 — hypothesis statuses

Now: "`boundary`, `building`, `hardening`, `ready` and `dropped`."

New: "`boundary`, `building`, `hardening`, `candidate`, `ready` and `dropped`;
`candidate` passed the grader and awaits the submission check, `ready`
passed the submission check."

## 7. tracking.md:113 — Decision

should show."

## 8. tracking.md:152 — GPU jobs (two named jobs, one queue)

other GPU work ..."

New:

## 10. tracking.md:103 + SKILL.md:112-114 — predicted saving labelled

## 12. verifier.md — second task: check the round's speed claims

> 1. **Level and cite.** Each claim cites the measurement of exactly what it

{"content":"# Designer-A design: the round measures its own submission

Status, approach and evidence for the brief
`design-lab/brief.md`: make the Muse agent swarm pursue real efficiency.

Prototypes and tests alongside: `prototypes/check_submission.py`,
`prototypes/skill-text.md`, `tests/test_*.py`, `results/*.txt`.
All result files below are under `design-lab/designer-a/results/`; all
repository paths are relative to the worktree at commit `1113c2d`.

---

## 1. Status: READY

The design is complete and self-contained. It needs no protected-contract
change, no new Muse Code capability, no model or engine change, and no
`start.sh` change. Its one new tool delegates to the existing G3 code; its
skill edits are replacement wordings, prototyped verbatim in
`prototypes/skill-text.md`; its three mechanisms were replayed against
round-2 records and real result logs with 25/25 prototype checks passing
(`results/test_*.txt`).

---

## 2. Context and diagnosis

### 2.1 Verified facts (all read at 1113c2d; explorer reports cross-checked)

- The goal is phrased as passing gates: `.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:20`
  ("kernels that pass G1 and G2 and have `beats_compiled` true ... faster
  because they remove a cause you can name").
- In-round model runs are forbidden twice: `tracking.md:152` ("Load no model
  and start no other GPU work") and `SKILL.md:164` ("G3 and vLLM belong to
  surucuonur's team"). The brief's decided direction (§UNRESOLVED) explicitly
  replaces these two lines; this design does that replacement and nothing more.
- Ready to test *requires* an end-to-end number (`SKILL.md:147`: "the change
  you expect in G3's four workloads ... with how you worked it out") while the
  ban above forbids measuring it — so the number can only be piece arithmetic.
- The verifier checks exploration only (`verifier.md:5-25`; only
  `ineff-*.md`, only `confirmed`/`refuted` on cost/saving inputs). Nothing
  checks hypothesis Decisions, Ready-to-test arithmetic, or the summary. The
  lead writes all three unchecked (`SKILL.md:160-161`).
- The number rule blesses arithmetic: `tracking.md:153` accepts "arithmetic
  shown in full" as a source with no level or method constraint.
- The harden loop has a continue rule and no switch rule (`SKILL.md:135-138`:
  "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove").
- The builder self-checks predictions with no enforcement (`builder.md:24`
  prediction with arithmetic, `builder.md:30` 20%-miss analysis, no checker).
- One-run-one-attempt is explicit and held: `builder.md:13`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`
  (v4); round 2 ran 13 grader runs for 13 attempts (explorer-rounds B4-g).
  This is the demonstrated proof that explicit, checkable rules hold on this
  swarm — the design's central precedent.
- The tools already contain the needed measurement: `time_candidates.py`
  builds base/compiled-*/muse-*/compiled-all/muse-all variants
  (`time_candidates.py:111-132`), judges each muse-* vs base and its
  compiled-* bar with the ADR 0011 rule (`:163-197`), defaults to 5 repeats
  and the 4 G3 workloads (`:51-53`), and takes the GPU lock (`:224`).
- Three tool gaps verified by reading: (a) token `exact` is logged but never
  gated — `g3()` reads only `kind=="run"` records (`:168-171`); (b) the
  free flags (`--repeats/--settings/--tokens/--variant`) can shrink or skew
  the check, and `--variant muse-x` without a `compiled-x` bar crashes G3
  (`:177-183`, `min()` on empty); (c) the plain engine always reports
  `prompt_ms = 0.0` (`breakdown.py:468-484` records steps only for the decode
  loop; `repeat_fixes.py:277-282`) and never writes a G3 verdict
  (`time_candidates.py:260-261`).
- Round-2 records confirm every behaviour instance (explorer-rounds B1-B5):
  prefill priced at zero (`hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`), the
  −0.84/−0.85/−0.84 together-sum (`implementation/README.md:36`) 23 lines
  below "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose" (`:13`), borrowed compile
  offsets (`:29`), six timed fused experts attempts losing at 1 row
  (`README.md:9`), the unfused alternative named only in the summary
  (`round-2/summary.md:9`).
- Cost and duration anchors: round 2 took 63.4 min on Muse Wonder (~$58);
  a single-slot 5-repeat vLLM G3 call is ~13–14 min run wall extrapolated
  from `results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/muse-vllm.jsonl`
  (explorer-tools §1.2; mean 13.6 s/run over 60 runs for 3 variants).

### 2.2 Cause and certainty

The brief's root-cause hypothesis is confirmed with high certainty: inside a
round the swarm's only speed feedback is the grader's per-slot piece timing,
the real objective (G3 over whole requests) arrives only post-round, and the
swarm's end-to-end claims pass through three unchecked documents (Decision →
Ready to test → summary). Three structural facts jointly force behaviours
1–3, not merely allow them: the goal is defined in grader verdicts (so the
unmeasured is definitionally irrelevant), the Ready-to-test number is
demanded but unmeasurable in-round (so it must be arithmetic), and no checker
exists downstream (so arithmetic errors and borrowed gains survive).
Behaviour 5 is forced the same way by a loop whose only exit is "no further
change worth making", judged by the agent running the loop. Behaviour 4 is
already fixed and is the design's positive control: the fix worked by making
the rule explicit and countable.

---

## 3. Recommended design: one gate, one checker pass, one counter

The design adds exactly three mechanisms, each reusing an established
pattern. Together they close the feedback loop: the swarm sees the real
objective before it claims anything, an independent checker replays every
claim from cited files, and a counter forces design diversity.

### 3.1 The submission check (the gate; fixes behaviours 1–3 at the root)

**New tool `bench/grader/check_submission.py`** (prototype:
`prototypes/check_submission.py`), a ~150-line wrapper that:

- takes `<out> SLOT=FOLDER...` — every candidate slot positionally in ONE
  call, so per-slot variants AND `muse-all`/`compiled-all` are measured as a
  combination (`time_candidates.py:125-127`);
- delegates to `time_candidates.main()` with pinned arguments: engine `vllm`,
  the 4 G3 workloads, 5 repeats, 256 tokens (asserting equality with
  `G3_SETTINGS`/`G3_REPEATS` first, so upstream drift fails loudly);
- then audits `<out>/muse-vllm.jsonl` + `g3-vllm.json`: exact expected
  variant set, engine vllm, reps 0–4 present per (variant, rows, prompt), and
  `exact is True` for every judged variant at rows 1 and 32 (the brief's G2
  end-to-end check, currently ungated);
- writes `<out>/submission-verdict.json` (params echoed, per-variant pass,
  bars, phases, exact flags, problems list) and exits 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL,
  2 when the log is uncitable. "Passes" = exit 0 — a countable rule in the
  behaviour-4 mould.

The free flags do not exist on the wrapper, which removes the whole
`--repeats 1 / --settings subset / --tokens 9 / --variant` gaming catalogue
(explorer-tools §3) by construction rather than by prose. The G3 crash case
(`muse-x` without a bar) is unreachable: no `--variant` is accepted.

**Skill integration** (wordings in `prototypes/skill-text.md` §§1–4, 8):

- Goal (`SKILL.md:20`) rewritten: `beats_compiled` is named as the builders'
  cheap proxy filter; the submission check is the verdict.
- Hypotheses close to a new status **`candidate`** on grader+boundary
  (`tracking.md:108` statuses extended); nothing reaches **`ready`** until
  the submission check passes it. This satisfies acceptance criterion 2
  literally while costing ONE GPU run however many hypotheses closed.
- At Finish, the lead runs the check itself (the single exception to "you
  don't grade", which exists to avoid a grading bottleneck per ADR 0007 —
  inapplicable to one finish-time run when no builder is grading), then sets
  `ready`/`dropped` per variant verdict in a checkpoint. At most two checks
  per round (one scheduled + one re-check after a fix); both logged, the
  last cited. Zero candidates → no check; Ready to test names
  baselines/references and makes no end-to-end claim.
- Ready to test (`SKILL.md:147`) becomes a measured section: verdict file,
  per-variant phases vs both bars, exact flags, the piece-basis prediction
  labelled PREDICTION next to the measured value, and the UNVERIFIED list.
  If `muse-all` fails or a single slot has no combination, no together-number
  is written — ever.
- `SKILL.md:164` and `tracking.md:152` are replaced per the decided
  direction: two named GPU jobs (grader for builders, submission check for
  the lead), both through the lock (`gpu_lock.py:18-32`), nothing else; the
  plain engine's 0.0 prompt time is explicitly unusable for claims.

**Data flow:** candidate attempt folders (committed at collect) →
`check_submission.py` → `time_candidates vllm` (GPU, queued) →
`muse-vllm.jsonl` + `g3-vllm.json` → audit → `submission-verdict.json` →
cited by Ready to test / summary / Decisions → replayed by the verifier →
compared against Claude's post-round G3.

### 3.2 The claims pass (the checker; makes self-reports checked)

**`verifier.md` gains a second task** (wording in `skill-text.md` §12): at
Finish, after the submission check, the lead starts the verifier again to
check every speed claim in Decisions, Ready to test, and the summary:

1. level-and-cite (grader file for piece claims, `submission-verdict.json`
   with empty `problems` and pinned params for end-to-end, else labelled
   PREDICTION with measured beside);
2. own-effect-only (no borrowed compile offsets, no cross-slot borrowing);
3. combinations measured (`muse-all` cited, or explicitly not measured/not
   passed — never summed);
4. unverified listed (no free/neutral/invisible/zero assumption);
5. counters replayed from cited grader verdicts (§3.3);
6. inputs match (`git diff --exit-code` on the checked folders is empty).

Verdicts go under `## From other agents` as today; Finish commits only after
the pass returns. No GPU: every check replays cited files.

**The number rule (`tracking.md:153`) is extended** (`skill-text.md` §9) with
exactly these four lines (R1 cite-at-level-or-PREDICTION-beside-measured,
R2 own-effect + measured-combinations, R3 UNVERIFIED-never-free), so the
rule every agent reads already contains the discipline and the verifier
enforces it. Small conforming edits: `tracking.md:103` (predicted saving
labelled a prediction), `SKILL.md:112-114` (ranking by prediction),
`builder.md:24` (prediction labelled, own effect), `boundary.md` item 4
(can't-see list becomes the UNVERIFIED list with what would verify each),
brief `:213`/`:215` (submission check + G3 decide; finalists go to both).

### 3.3 The failure-point counter (fixes behaviour 5)

**Harden gains a counter** (`skill-text.md` §2, `tracking.md:111`):

- Each graded attempt records its **failure point**: sizes `slower` than
  compiled (or G2-fail sizes) + the named cause.
- After **3 consecutive** attempts fail at the same failure point, the next
  builder takes a **different approach** (a different design family, named
  in the log) **or the lead logs why not** (criterion 5's escape clause,
  kept deliberate).
- N=3 is evidence-grounded: round-2 experts attempts 1–3 already spanned
  per-pair, block-split and 4-block packings at the same 1-row point
  (`hyp-1-experts-exact.md:178-241`); the rule would have forced the
  "stop fusing" decision (`round-2/summary.md:9`) four attempts earlier.
- Anti-gaming: an unlaunched (G1-fail) attempt pauses without resetting; a
  new cause restarts the count only with a cited measurement refuting the
  old one (round-2 attempt-3's lever refutation, `:254-258`, is the model —
  genuine re-diagnosis still counts, renaming does not).

### 3.4 Integration points and interfaces

- **Tool contract:** `check_submission.py OUT SLOT=FOLDER... [--dry-run]`;
  reads attempt folders (spec.json + block-*.metal, unchanged format);
  writes `<out>/` under the round folder (`<round>/submission/`,
 子のnew untracked-until-committed dir — inside the round folder so hooks
  accept it); exit codes 0/1/2. Protected grader JSON keys untouched.
- **Skill contract:** new status `candidate`; `ready` redefined; lead runs
  one command; verifier runs twice. No new role card, no capacity change
  (12 agents suffice; the check needs none), no `start.sh` change.
- **Docs:** skill v8 (`CHANGELOG.md` entry in `skill-text.md` §15),
  glossary terms (Submission check, Failure point), `muse-swarm.md`
  honesty bullets, and a new ADR 0013 (see §8). ADRs 0010/0011 stay
  verbatim; 0013 sets the future convention that "Not covered" sections
  say "unverified: assume nothing".

---

## 4. Why it solves the underlying problem; acceptance criteria

The underlying problem is the gap between the proxy the swarm sees and the
objective it is judged on, plus unchecked self-reporting. The design moves
the objective into the round (the gate measures exactly what G3 measures,
with the same code and rule, plus the token gate) and puts a checker between
every claim and the reader. It does not patch five symptoms; behaviours 1–3
all become impossible-to-claim-without-measuring, behaviour 4's fix is
extended to the new GPU job by the same explicit-countable technique, and
behaviour 5 gets the missing loop exit.

| Criterion | How met |
|---|---|
| 1. Every speed claim cited at its level, or PREDICTION beside measured | R1 in `tracking.md:153` + verifier claims pass step 1; Ready-to-test/summary templates rewritten to the measured form. Prototype replay flags all round-2 violations (`results/test_claim_rules.txt`, 4/4). |
| 2. Nothing `ready`/Ready-to-test without an in-round ADR 0011 check vs unchanged + compiled | `candidate`→`ready` only on wrapper exit 0, which requires every judged variant's g3 pass vs both bars; Ready-to-test cites `submission-verdict.json`. |
| 3. Own effect only; combinations measured | R2 + single positional call producing measured `muse-all`; verifier steps 2–3. |
| 4. Unmeasured listed, never free | R3 + boundary UNVERIFIED list; verifier step 4. Replay flags hyp-1:150-151 (`results/test_claim_rules.txt`). |
| 5. 3 failures at one point → new approach or logged reason | Harden counter with the escape clause; verifier step 5 replays it. Replay triggers after experts attempt 3, never for routing (`results/test_failure_counter.txt`, 5/5). |
| 6. Post-round G3 agrees within noise | The in-round check IS G3's code, workloads, repeats and rule (plus token gate), so agreement is structural; residual noise sources are the documented ones (1-request whole-request spread, ADR 0011:52). Round-3 outcome shows success directly. |

Goodhart statement (required by the brief): the submission check becomes the
next proxy. Its game surface is enumerated in §6 with a mitigation per game;
the backstop is unchanged — Claude's independent post-round G3 (criterion 6)
and the starting-point record of prediction-vs-measured, which now carries
two comparable numbers instead of one man's arithmetic vs another's
measurement.

---

## 5. What remains unchanged; migration and compatibility

- **Unchanged:** model/engine; `check_candidate.py`, `time_candidates.py`,
  `gpu_lock.py`, `slots.py` (no tracked tool edited — the wrapper only
  calls); attempt format; grader JSON keys; ADR 0010/0011 rules; G2 token
  check; authorship separation, hooks, provenance check; frozen rounds and
  tags; swarm roles (no new card); no-attempt-limit; one-run-one-attempt;
  `start.sh`, launch flags, model choice; Claude's post-round process and
  authority.
- **Old data:** rounds 1–2 documents stay frozen and stay comparable:
  `submission-verdict.json` did not exist, so their claims keep their old
  form; the round-3 starting point (step 1) already compares "G3 effect vs
  prediction" and now additionally compares vs the new in-round measurement
  where present. No backfill needed or wanted.
- **Migration:** none — a skill version bump (v8) committed before round 3
  per the CHANGELOG convention, plus the new tool file. Partial rounds:
  `candidate` with no check yet resumes cleanly (step 0 carries on; Finish
  runs the check). A round with zero candidates skips the check entirely.

---

## 6. Failure handling, data integrity, security, operations

- **Per-game mitigations for the new check:** (a) weak `--baseline` choice —
  the submission judges vs base + compiled reference only; `beats_compiled`
  stays required at harden so a weak baseline can't promote; (b)
  `max_rows=32` prefill-"same" — the submission times the real prefill, and
  a hand-off genuinely runs the compiled code there (ADR 0011:33-35), so
  "same" is true, not a dodge; (c) post-check attempt edits — verifier step
  6 (`git diff --exit-code` on checked paths); attempts are also committed
  at collect and only builders write them; (d) selective median quoting —
  R1 allows only the verdict file; (e) direct `time_candidates` with gamed
  flags — only `submission-verdict.json` counts, and its `params` block
  (vllm/5/4×256) plus empty `problems` are verifier-checked; (f) lock
  bypass via `breakdown.py`/`repeat_fixes.py` direct use (they never call
  `hold()`) — forbidden by the rewritten GPU rule; detection stays absent
  (accepted: simple-over-airtight, and Claude's G3 is independent);
  re-check-until-noise-passes — capped at 2 checks/round, 5-repeat ranges
  (1/252 per check, ADR 0011:40), post-round G3 backstop; (h) counter
  reset by cause-renaming — restart requires a cited refuting measurement.
- **Noise:** the documented 1-request whole-request spread (6–41%,
  ADR 0011:52) mostly yields `same`, which passes "never slower" without
  showing gain — unchanged semantics, now visible in-round instead of
  surprising post-round.
- **GPU queue and duration:** one call per round (two at most), at Finish
  when builders are idle — zero contention with grader runs by scheduling.
  Cost at 13.6 s/run mean: 1 slot ≈ 60 runs ≈ 14 min; 2 slots ≈ 140 runs ≈
  32 min; 3 slots ≈ 180 runs ≈ 41 min (prediction from the engine-comparison
  log, same basis as explorer-tools §1.2). Round 3 ≈ 1.5–2.5 h total.
- **Memory:** a vLLM run at Finish contends with less (no concurrent
  builders) than a mid-round one; `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` default
  and Docker-quit guidance (`breakdown.py:54`) unchanged. 90-minute stop
  rule bounds a pathological run; a stop counts as FAIL and is recorded.
- **Integrity of the verdict:** the wrapper asserts constant-equality with
  `time_candidates` before delegating (drift fails loudly); the audit
  replays coverage from the log rather than trusting stdout; `problems`
  are written into the citable file, not just printed (prototype line
  `verdict["problems"]`, tested in `results/test_check_submission.txt`).
- **Security:** no credentials read (skill rule kept), no network, no new
  permissions; the wrapper runs the same local commands the swarm already
  runs.
- **Failure modes:** GPU lock held by a stale process — same as today
  (OS releases on process end, `gpu_lock.py:7`); wrapper crash mid-run —
  partial log fails the audit (missing reps → exit 2, uncitable, re-run);
  `attempts` overlapping parts — `time_candidates` already errors
  (`:221-223`); single-slot call — no `muse-all`, combination section
  says so.

## 7. Alternatives considered

1. **Skill-only fix: mandate the exact `time_candidates` command line, no
   wrapper.** Smallest diff (zero code). Rejected: every free flag stays a
   live game surface for an unattended contributor-model run; the token gate
   stays unenforced; the G3 crash case stays reachable. The wrapper's ~150
   lines convert five prose prohibitions into one inexistent-flagset plus an
   audit — cheaper to verify than to hope. (Prediction: prose-only pinning
   would be the next behaviour-4-style violation report.)
2. **Per-hypothesis end-to-end gates at close (one vLLM run per ready).**
   Matches criterion 2 without a new status. Rejected: 2–3× the GPU cost
   (base + compiled re-timed per call), mid-round queue contention with
   builders' grader runs, and — decisively — no measured combination
   without an extra run. The single submission call judges every slot AND
   the combination at once; the `candidate` status is a smaller price.
3. **Cheaper in-round proxy instead of full G3: fewer repeats/tokens or the
   plain engine.** Rejected on evidence: 3 repeats false-flagged an
   unchanged phase (ADR 0011:40); `--tokens` below 9 crashes and lower
   values reweight decode-vs-prompt silently; plain `prompt_ms` is always
   0.0, i.e. precisely behaviour 1 in tool form. A cheaper gate re-opens
   the proxy gap the brief pays to close.
4. **New checker role instead of extending the verifier.** Rejected:
   existing-system-first — the verifier pattern (independent agent, cited
   files, verdict sections, `## From other agents`) already exists and is
   trusted by judges; a second card duplicates it. The verifier's singleton
   naming is no obstacle (the lead restarts it with a new task prompt).
5. **Automatic counter enforcement in tooling (attempt registry, run
   counting).** Rejected: the tool cannot see design families or causes;
   behaviour 4's lesson is that the skill layer plus committed history is
   the enforcement point. The counter lives in the hypothesis entry where
   the causes live, replayed by the verifier.
6. **Forbidding piece-basis predictions entirely.** Rejected: predictions
   are the swarm's legitimate working language (builders must predict to
   choose directions; `builder.md:24` stays). The fix is labelling +
   beside-measured + own-effect, not silence.

---

## 8. Implementation handoff

Dependency order (all by Claude on main before round 3; ~2–3 h total):

1. **Tool** (30–45 min): copy `prototypes/check_submission.py` to
   `bench/grader/check_submission.py`; review the delegate + audit paths;
   run `tests/test_check_submission.py` (16 checks, no GPU) from the repo
   root; run `--dry-run`.
2. **Skill v8** (45–60 min): paste `prototypes/skill-text.md` §§1–13 into
   SKILL.md/tracking.md/builder.md/verifier.md/boundary.md; fix the two
   stale version stamps the explorers found (`SKILL.md:80` says skill
   version 6 while `:10` says 7; `tracking.md` version-line example);
   add the CHANGELOG v8 entry (§15).
3. **Brief + docs** (20–30 min): brief `:213`/`:215` (§14); glossary terms;
   `muse-swarm.md` honesty bullets; new **ADR 0013** (the fix; also records
   the one-run-one-attempt rule, currently missing from every ADR per
   explorer-findings §4, and the "unverified, never free" phrasing
   convention for future "Not covered" sections).
4. **Pre-round validation, no paid run** (15–20 min + one optional GPU run):
   - replay tests `test_failure_counter.py` (5/5) and `test_claim_rules.py`
     (4/4) — done, in `results/`;
   - hand-check: apply the verifier's 6 steps to round-2's Ready to test by
     reading (expect: claims 1–2 wrong per R1/R2, together-number wrong per
     R2/R3 — the test encodes the same);
   - RECOMMENDED one GPU run through the queue: the implemented wrapper on
     round-2's finalists (`routing/attempt-4`, `combine/attempt-1`) as a
     single call. Falsifiable expectations: the audit passes (exit 0/1, not
     2); `muse-routing` FAILs (prompt 7–10% slower is documented,
     `muse-round-2.md:134-141`); the run completes in ~30–35 min. If it
     does not FAIL routing, investigate before round 3 (the gate must catch
     a known-bad submission).
5. **Round-3 success read-out:** every `ready` cites `submission-verdict.json`
   with empty problems; Ready to test shows predictions beside measurements;
   UNVERIFIED lists exist; any 3-in-a-row shows a new family or a reason;
   Claude's G3 agrees with the submission verdicts within repeat noise
   (criterion 6). Failure of 6 with 1–5 held means the gate itself is miscalibrated —
   that becomes round 4's starting point, not a swarm failure.

Regression tests: the three prototype test files move with the implementation
(the wrapper test becomes the tool's test; the replay tests document the
rules' intent). Monitoring: none new — the round's own documents plus
Claude's findings carry the signal, as today. Rollback: skill v7 + ignore
the new tool (one commit revert); rounds run v7 semantics unchanged since no
tracked tool was modified.

---

## 9. Unverified assumptions, risks, decisions for the user

- **Assumed (brief §UNRESOLVED, kept):** explicit checkable rules hold on the
  contributor model (evidence: behaviour-4 fix held in round 2); the fix
  ships before 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC; Claude's G3 stays authoritative.
  Verified instead of assumed: every repository citation above was read at
  1113c2d; every performance figure traces to `results/` logs or the
  prototype results.
- **Prediction, not measurement:** submission-check durations (~14/32/41 min
  for 1/2/3 slots) extrapolate the engine-comparison mean; round-3's
  attempts could shift it (a very slow prefill lengthens runs, as the
  grader's 5-minute experts run foreshadows). The 90-minute stop bounds it.
- **Risk: one bad slot fails the combination.** If `muse-all` FAILs while
  slots pass (interference, seen in both rounds), the design reports it
  rather than fixing it — per-slot `ready`s still stand, the together-claim
  is withheld. That is deliberate (honesty over completeness), but judges
  should expect withheld together-claims.
- **Risk: the re-check budget burns on noise.** Two full checks ≈ 80 min
  worst case. Mitigated by the cap and by scheduling at Finish; if round 3
  shows noise-flips between the two checks, round 4 should widen repeats
  rather than re-checks.
- **Risk: contributor-model compliance with the 6-step verifier pass.**
  The pass is file-replay only (no judgement about physics), which is the
  easiest class of instruction to follow; the behaviour-4 precedent supports
  it, but it is untested until round 3.
- **Decision for surucuonur (before implementing):** confirm the lead runs
  the submission check itself (this design) vs a new helper role doing it.
  I chose the lead: one finish-time run, no bottleneck, no new card. If you
  prefer the lead to stay GPU-free, the fallback is a 10-line role card
  (`runner.md`: run the wrapper command, report exit code + verdict file)
  with no other change.
- **Decision (before implementing):** confirm the 2-check cap and the N=3
  counter threshold. Both are judgement calls anchored in round-2 evidence
  (14-min single-slot cost; 3 packings at one failure point); N=2 would
  churn, N=4+ repeats round 2.
- **Out of scope, noted for later:** `check_sizes.py` in-round use (row
  counts between the six G2 sizes stay boundary-reasoned, not measured);
  lock-bypass detection; the `PROVENANCE.md:42` vs ADRs sign-in
  contradiction (explorer-findings §5.6, load-bearing for isolation claims,
  untouched by this design).

Done. Full design in `design-lab/designer-a/design.md` (status READY), with prototypes, tests and results alongside. No tracked file touched, nothing committed.

**Approach in a paragraph:** the round measures its own submission. One new tool, `bench/grader/check_submission.py` (prototyped), runs every candidate slot in a single pinned `time_candidates.py vllm` call — G3's workloads, rule and repeats, with the end-to-end token check promoted to a gate — then audits the log and writes a citable `submission-verdict.json` (exit 0/1/2). Hypotheses close to a new `candidate` status on the grader and turn `ready` only on that check, so the swarm sees the real objective before claiming anything. The verifier gains a second, GPU-free pass at Finish replaying six claim rules (cite-at-level or PREDICTION-beside-measured, own-effect-only, measured combinations, UNVERIFIED-never-free, counter replay, inputs match), and the harden loop gains a failure-point counter: 3 consecutive failures at one point force a different design family or a logged reason. Three mechanisms, each reusing an established pattern (G3 code, verifier role, behaviour-4-style countable rules); no model, engine, hook, `start.sh`, or tracked-tool change.

**Key evidence:**
- Root cause confirmed at the cited lines: goal-as-gates (`SKILL.md:20`), measurement ban (`tracking.md:152`, `SKILL.md:164`), demanded-but-unmeasurable Ready-to-test number (`SKILL.md:147`), exploration-only verifier (`verifier.md`), arithmetic-as-source (`tracking.md:153`), switch-less harden loop (`SKILL.md:138`); tool gaps verified by reading (`time_candidates.py:168-197` token gate absent, `:260-261` plain never verdicts, `breakdown.py:468-484` plain prompt always 0.0).
- Prototype tests, all CPU-only, 25/25 pass (`results/test_*.txt`): wrapper pins flags and rejects all four gaming flags, passes a synthetic 5-repeat fixture, fails inexact-token and 1-repeat fixtures, and parses real logs — correctly ruling the round-2 log uncitable (3 repeats, no G3 file) and the handoff log uncitable on repeats while preserving its FAIL verdict.
- Rule replays on round-2 records: the claim rules flag the −0.48 routing figure (R1+R2), the −0.84 together-sum (R1+R2+R3) and the "free prefill" line (R3) while allowing labelled piece predictions; the N=3 counter triggers after experts attempt 3 (per-pair/block-split/4-block all at one 1-row point) and never for routing.
- Pre-round-3 validation proposed with a falsifiable GPU prediction: one wrapper run on round-2's finalists should audit cleanly and FAIL routing attempt-4 on prompt time (~30–35 min through the queue).

You write ONLY in design-lab/designer-b/: prototypes of your proposed changes (copies of skill files, role cards or tools, edited there), test scripts, measurement results. Your starting perspective is: contract-and-data-first. Begin with semantics, contracts, ownership, data shape and consistency, then choose responsibilities and integrations.

Now follow these instructions verbatim:
---
You are an independent senior software architect. Design the strongest coherent solution for the exact brief. You are responsible for the entire problem, not just your starting perspective; the perspective tells you where to begin and must not bias you into an inferior architecture.
Rules:
- Change no tracked file. Write only in design-lab/designer-b/: prototypes of your proposed changes, test scripts and results. Commit nothing, create no branches or worktrees, and call no paid or external services.
- Read the actual relevant source, callers, contracts, conventions and tests before making codebase-specific claims.
- Distinguish observed facts (with paths) from hypotheses and design decisions.
- Fix the root problem rather than a narrow symptom. Preserve unrelated, correct behavior.
- Choose one internally consistent approach; do not propose incompatible ideas as a single architecture.
- Explain effects on other modules, old data, deployment, edge cases, security, failure handling, maintenance, and future changes where they matter.
- Do not optimize for time-to-answer, diff size, code size or superficial novelty.
- Avoid unneeded abstractions and speculative scalability work.
- If an essential premise conflicts with code or is unknowable, return BLOCKED with exact evidence instead of assuming it away.
- No implementation in the repository: the design is your deliverable. Prototype and test it in design-lab/designer-b/ to see what it does, and report the commands, result files and what they showed.

Deliver:
1. Status: READY | CONDITIONAL | BLOCKED
2. Context and diagnosis: verified facts, example(s), cause and certainty.
3. Recommended design: responsibilities, important interfaces/contracts, data flow and integration points.
4. Why it solves the underlying problem and meets each acceptance criterion.
5. What remains unchanged; migration/compatibility effects if any.
6. Failure handling, data integrity, security and operational concerns if relevant.
7. Credible alternatives considered and their trade-offs.
8. Implementation handoff: dependency-ordered work, expected locations, acceptance/regression tests, monitoring and rollback if relevant.
9. Unverified assumptions, risks and decisions requiring the user.
---

DELIVERABLE: Write your full design (sections 1-9 above) to design-lab/designer-b/design.md, with prototypes/tests/results alongside in design-lab/designer-b/, then return your design's summary (status, approach in a paragraph, key evidence) as your final result.

1|# Solution design brief: make the Muse agent swarm pursue real efficiency, not its proxies (v1)
2|
3|## APPROVAL
4|- User approved this brief on 2026-11-04 (surucuonur). Decisions: the swarm may run end-to-end checks in-round through the GPU queue; Meta's Muse does the design work; from round 3 the launcher runs muse-spark-1.3-contributor with tool approvals off (ADR 0012, commit 1113c2d).
5|- Approved activity: one Muse Code session (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) whose lead starts its own helper agents, up to 12 at once, with no cost or time limit. Agents may prototype and test in design-lab/ (untracked, never committed) and run the measurement tools through the GPU queue. The repository's tracked files stay unchanged.
6|
7|## PROBLEM AND OUTCOME
8|- **Current problem:** two rounds of the Muse agent swarm (round 1: Muse Spark; round 2: Muse Wonder, 63 min, ~$58) produced no kernel that is a real efficiency improvement, while the swarm's own reports predicted gains. Five behaviours, each with evidence:
9|  1. **Treats unmeasured costs as free.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`: "Prefill speed is not timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart from time to first token", citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`. The result: experts attempt-7 is 16–28× slower than the compiled reference at prefill sizes, and routing attempt-4 2.6–8.7× slower (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`). Prompts took 6.6–14.5× and 7–10% longer, and throughput fell by up to 83% (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §5).
10|  2. **Claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Expected G3 = (compiled − candidate) µs × 20 layers (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md` *Ready to test*; `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`). Round 1 predicted −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.98/+0.16/−1.76. Round 2 predicted −0.84 at each and measured −0.73/−0.74/+0.53 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`, `muse-round-2.md`).
11|  3. **Reasons inconsistently.** The same README says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then reports "Together (sum) −0.84 ms". Combine's −0.35 ms prediction is −0.07 to −0.09 from its own timing plus −0.27 to −0.29 borrowed from what `mx.compile` gains end to end. Measured: +1.05 ms with 32 requests.
12|  4. **Used the grader as a search loop (round 1).** 29 grader runs on experts for 4 counted attempts, 18 on attempt-1 with edits between (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §5). Fixed since skill v4: one run is one attempt; round 2 ran 13 for 13.
13|  5. **Persists with a failing design family.** All 7 experts attempts in round 2 are fused kernels that lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs per layer). The cause, too few threadgroups at 1 row, was already known from round 1. The harden loop says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" (`.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:138`), and there is no rule for changing design.
14|- **Root cause** (likely; supported by the evidence above): inside a round, the swarm never sees the real objective. Its feedback is a per-slot proxy, the grader's piece timing. The real measurement, Claude's G3 over whole requests, arrives only after the round. The swarm's claims are self-reported and checked by no one before the summary.
15|  - *verified:* the rules forbid an in-round model run: `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:152` "Load no model and start no other GPU work" and `SKILL.md:164` "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team".
16|  - *verified:* the goal is phrased as passing gates (`SKILL.md:20`).
17|  - *verified:* the verifier checks only exploration's inefficiency entries (`verifier.md`). No one checks the implementation phase's predictions, combination claims or Ready-to-test arithmetic.
18|  - *partly fixed:* ADR 0011 (commit `2090949`) now times the prefill (grader at 6 sizes, G3 with prompt and whole-request time, 5 repeats), so behaviour 1's specific gap is closed. The general habit, treating anything outside the measurement as free, is not addressed.
19|- **Intended outcome:** in round 3 and later, the swarm's statements about speed match what Claude's independent G3 then measures. It marks something ready only when it is a real improvement under the ADR 0011 rule (faster in one phase, prefill or decode, slower in neither, no whole request slower). It stops repeating a design that keeps failing at the same point.
20|- **Why now:** surucuonur asked how to fix "these essential problems and behaviour of these agents". The hackathon deadline is 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, about 11.5 h from 14:30 UTC on 2026-11-04. Round 3 should run with the fix.
21|- **Maturity:** hackathon research tool; judges read the repo, the skill and the round documents.
22|- **User's suggested approach:** none given. Claude has suggested an in-round end-to-end check and prediction rules; treat these as hypotheses, not constraints.
23|
24|## SCOPE AND SUCCESS
25|- **In scope:**
26|  - the round skill (`.agents/skills/muse-round/`: SKILL.md, the role cards, tracking.md);
27|  - the brief (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md`);
28|  - the measurement tools the swarm may call (`bench/grader/`, `bench/micro/` entry points);
29|  - `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` if needed;
30|  - the docs that describe these (ADR, glossary, `claude/muse-swarm.md`, diagrams).
31|- **Out of scope:**
32|  - changing the model or the engine;
33|  - Claude's post-round measurement process, beyond what it needs to compare claims;
34|  - running round 3 itself;
35|  - Muse Code itself.
36|- **Observable acceptance criteria:**
37|  1. Every speed claim in a round's READMEs and summary is either backed by a measurement made in the round, with its run file cited, of exactly what is claimed (the slot or combination, at the end-to-end level claimed), or labelled as a prediction and shown next to the measured value.
38|  2. No hypothesis reaches `ready`, and no attempt goes to *Ready to test*, unless an in-round check shows it improves under ADR 0011's rule, against the unchanged model and the compiled reference.
39|  3. Predictions count only the candidate's own measured effect, and a combination's effect is measured as a combination.
40|  4. Anything the swarm did not measure is listed as unverified, never assumed free or neutral.
41|  5. After a stated number of failures of one design at the same size or phase for the same cause, the next attempt changes approach, or the log records why not.
42|  6. Claude's post-round G3 agrees with the swarm's in-round measured claims within the noise of the repeats. This is the ultimate test.
43|- **Quality guardrails:**
44|  - proportionate and simple: surucuonur rejected sandbox and guard-hook hardening before (memory `muse-isolation-simple`);
45|  - keep the documents readable by judges;
46|  - keep Muse-facing instructions in the repo.
47|
48|## VERIFIED SYSTEM CONTEXT
49|- **Launch:** `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` (`:71` first prompt "Run the muse-round skill…", `:136` `muse exec … -c agents.execution_capacity=12`). One Muse Code session per round, in worktree `../Hackathon-muse` on branch `muse-agent`, on the Meta Model API. Round 2 ran `muse-wonder-1.0` with approvals on; from step 0 the default is `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` with approvals off.
50|- **The swarm** (`SKILL.md:22-38`):
51|  - the lead coordinates and commits, but never explores, builds or grades;
52|  - explorers write `exploration/territory-*.md` and `ineff-*.md`;
53|  - the verifier confirms or refutes inefficiencies;
54|  - builders write and grade one attempt each (`builder.md`);
55|  - boundary agents write and check a hypothesis's boundary (`boundary.md`);
56|  - shared docs and logs per phase (`tracking.md`), checkpoints commit them.
57|- **Steps** (`SKILL.md`): 0 find where you are, 1 starting point, 2 exploration, 3 the analysis, 4 implementation (open hypothesis → boundary → compete → collect → harden → close `ready`/`dropped`), 5 finish (READMEs, *Ready to test*, summary).
58|- **Measurement tools:**
59|  - **`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`:** G1/G2 bit-exact at 6 sizes; paired piece timing with a sign test; `beats_compiled`/`beats_baseline` per ADR 0011; takes the GPU lock; loads the model on every run (ADR 0010).
60|  - **`bench/grader/time_candidates.py`:** end-to-end check and G3.
61|    - Engines: `plain` (MLX) or `vllm`.
62|    - Variants: base, compiled-<slot>, muse-<slot>, muse-all, `--variant`.
63|    - G2 compares greedy tokens; G3 records decode step, prompt time (vLLM only) and wall time; `--repeats` defaults to 5; writes `g3-vllm.json`.
64|    - Duration: about 8.5 s per run on average in vLLM, so roughly 10–12 min per candidate with base and compiled at 4 settings × 5 repeats.
65|    - The plain engine has no prompt time yet (`bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py:prompt_ms`, `breakdown.run_plain`).

67|- **Isolation and provenance:**
68|  - git hooks refuse Muse commits outside `muse-spark/`, changes to finished rounds' files, and merges;
69|  - `tools/provenance_check.py` audits authorship;

71|- **Round 3's starting point:** no baseline in any slot (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` *For round 3*).
72|- **Revision:** main at `2090949`, working tree clean apart from two uncommitted pilot files.

74|## PROTECTED CONTRACTS AND BEHAVIORS
75|- Authorship separation: the Muse agent writes only in `muse-spark/`, only the lead commits, with the Muse co-author line; Claude never commits on `muse-agent`; hooks and provenance check stay.
76|- Finished rounds stay frozen (tags `muse-round-1`, `muse-round-2`).
77|- Muse Code only, swarm design (ADR 0007), no attempt limit (ADR 0006: "limitless"), one grader run per attempt, the GPU queue.
78|- Grading rules of ADR 0010/0011 (bit-exact at 6 sizes, both phases, hand-off via `max_rows`); G2's token check.
79|- Claude's post-round independent measurement remains the authority for baselines.
80|- The attempt format (`spec.json` + `block-N.metal`) and the grader's JSON verdict keys (`g1`, `g2`, `beats_compiled`, `beats_baseline`, `timing_us_per_layer`, `phases_vs_compiled`).
81|
82|## CONSTRAINTS AND OPERATIONAL REALITY
83|- **Machine:** M1 Pro, 16 GB, heavy swapping (19–20 GB swap in use); one GPU job at a time. vLLM needs `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` (now the default in `breakdown.py`) and Docker quit. 1-request vLLM timings are noisy (6–41% spread).
84|- **Time:** about 11.5 h to the deadline, including implementing the fix, running round 3 (~1–2 h), and Claude's measurement and findings (~1 h). The fix should be implementable and checkable in roughly 2–3 h.
85|- **Cost:** round 2 on Muse Wonder cost about $58; on the contributor model a round costs about $1 (round 1: $0.70). Claude never runs `start.sh` or calls the Meta API without asking.
86|- **Hard constraints:** the protected items above, and the deadline.
87|- **Preferences:** simple over airtight (no sandboxing or guard hooks); rules phrased positively for agents (writing-for-agents guidance).
88|- **Decided:** round 3 runs on `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, round 1's model, which ADR 0008 judged less capable than Muse Wonder, with tool approvals off. No one approves tool calls during the round, so rules must hold without a human watching. Instructions must be explicit and checkable, since a less capable model follows general advice less reliably.
89|
90|## FAILURE MODES AND FUTURE CHANGES
91|- **Goodhart risk:** any new check becomes the next proxy. A design must say how the swarm could game it.
92|- **GPU queue contention:** a 10–12 min end-to-end check blocks builders' grader runs.
93|- **Memory:** a vLLM run inside the round competes with Muse Code's own processes and may page.
94|- **Noise:** at 1 request, end-to-end verdicts are mostly `same`.
95|- **Partial rounds:** a session can stop mid-round, and checks must leave the shared documents consistent.
96|- **The model can ignore instructions:** round 1 ignored "one attempt per grader run" before it became an explicit rule.
97|- **Future:** more slots or a different model; rounds 4+; possibly other engines.
98|- **Prior pitfalls:**
99|  - independent piece timing hid latency (fixed by ADR 0010);
100|  - tolerances let the tokens change (fixed by ADR 0010);
101|  - prefill was untimed (fixed by ADR 0011);
102|  - G3 with 3 repeats falsely flagged unchanged phases (fixed with 5 repeats).
103|

106|- Address whole-system effects: the GPU queue and round duration, memory, Claude's post-round role, the docs and judges.
107|- Cite repository evidence; distinguish verified facts from proposals.
108|- Specify the changes to the skill, cards, brief and tools, plus any new measurement entry point, at the level of what each says or does.
109|- Define how a future implementation is validated before round 3, without a paid Muse run if possible, and how round 3's own outcome would show success.
110|- Do not edit the repository's tracked code, data or configuration; prototypes and tests live in design-lab/.

21|## Behaviour 1: treats unmeasured costs as free
22|
23|Facts bearing on it: T1, T2, T5, T9, T10.
24|
25|Where the instructions create or allow it. The goal (T1, `SKILL.md:20`) defines success entirely in grader verdicts, so anything the grader does not time is definitionally irrelevant to passing. The in-round measurement ban (T2, `tracking.md:152`, `SKILL.md:164`) makes it impossible to check anything the grader omits, so "free apart from time to first token" style reasoning is the only available move for unmeasured costs. The cross-phase guard (`tracking.md:103`, `SKILL.md:114`) asks for a prediction ("what removing it does to the other phase"), not a measurement, and the number rule (`tracking.md:153`) accepts shown arithmetic as a source. Nothing says "list what you did not measure" or "never assume an unmeasured cost is zero/neutral".
26|
27|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes the general habit structurally: gate-defined goal + no in-round end-to-end measurement + arithmetic-accepted-as-source. It could prevent the specific prefill instance only indirectly (v7 times prefill via `beats_compiled`, `CHANGELOG.md:9`), but the general habit has no rule against it. Proposal (not a finding): a "list unverified costs; never assume free/neutral" rule would plug the gap the brief's acceptance criterion 4 names.
28|
29|## Behaviour 2: claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic
30|
31|Facts bearing on it: T2, T4, T5, T7, T10.
32|
33|Where the instructions create or allow it. Ready to test (`SKILL.md:147`, quoted in T4) *requires* the lead to state "the change you expect in G3's four workloads" while T2 forbids running anything that measures G3 in-round — so the expected change can only be piece arithmetic (e.g. × 20 layers). No rule constrains the method ("with how you worked it out" is free-form), no rule requires labelling it a prediction, and T3/T4 leave no checker: the verifier never sees implementation documents. The brief reinforces the hand-off model (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:215`, T10). `tracking.md:153` blesses the arithmetic as sourced.
34|
35|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes it directly: it demands an end-to-end number and simultaneously forbids the only measurement that could produce one. Prevention would need either an in-round end-to-end check (the brief's decided direction) or a prediction rule (measure what you claim; label the rest) — neither exists in this territory today.
36|
37|## Behaviour 3: reasons inconsistently (non-composition admitted, then summed; borrowed compile gains)
38|
39|Facts bearing on it: T4, T5, T7, T11.
40|
41|Where the instructions allow it. No rule in the territory says a combination's effect must be measured as a combination, or that a prediction may count only the candidate's own measured effect. The builder records per-attempt six-size timings (`builder.md:29`) and self-explains >20% misses (`builder.md:30`), but combining two slots' savings, or borrowing `mx.compile`'s end-to-end gain into one slot's prediction, violates no stated rule: the verifier's remit ends at exploration (T3), the lead's Ready-to-test arithmetic is unchecked (T4), and shown arithmetic counts as sourced (T5). The "faster because they remove a cause you can name" clause (`SKILL.md:20`) asks for a causal story, not arithmetic discipline.
42|
43|Cause vs prevention. The territory allows rather than mandates this: it is silent on combination arithmetic, so inconsistent reasoning passes every gate. Prevention needs an explicit prediction rule (brief's acceptance criterion 3); the closest existing hooks are `builder.md:30` (could be extended to combinations) and `tracking.md:153` (could require measured-not-borrowed inputs).
44|
45|## Behaviour 4: used the grader as a search loop (round 1)
46|
47|Facts bearing on it: T8.
48|
49|Where the instructions created it, and the fix. Pre-v4 skill had no one-run-one-attempt rule, and the brief's attempt model ("Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed", `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:14`) assumed a single agent grading its own work, so repeated grade-edit-grade cycles fit the letter of the instructions. Skill v4 added the explicit rule (`builder.md:13`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`), and the brief's stop rule was simultaneously voided (`SKILL.md:15`, `builder.md:13`: "the brief's *When a slot stops* rule no longer applies"). The fix works by making each run a countable, committed attempt ("Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try", `SKILL.md:15`).
50|
51|Cause vs prevention. This is the territory's one demonstrated self-correction: an explicit, checkable rule ("any change, even a one-line fix, is a new attempt") replaced a violated norm. It supports the brief's assumption that explicit checkable rules work on this swarm. Residual gap (proposal, not finding): nothing stops a builder from running the grader, then abandoning the attempt folder uncommitted — the lead commits "the attempt folder" at collect (`SKILL.md:133`), so an unreturned attempt could still hide a run; the history shows every *returned* try.
52|
53|## Behaviour 5: persists with a failing design family
54|
55|Facts bearing on it: T1, T6, T9.
56|
57|Where the instructions create or allow it. The harden loop (`SKILL.md:135-138`) only ever says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" — a skilled agent can always name one more cause, so the loop has no failure counter and no exit to a different design. `ready` (`SKILL.md:140`) requires only gate passage plus "no further change worth making", judged by the same lead running the loop. "Faster because they remove a cause you can name" (`SKILL.md:20`) rewards cause-naming, which is exactly what kept the fused-kernel family alive. The compete step (`SKILL.md:131`) diversifies directions once ("Give each a different direction"), but harden then single-threads on "the best attempt" (`SKILL.md:136`), so early convergence to one family is structural. No rule says "after N failures at the same size/phase for the same cause, change approach or log why not".
58|
59|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes it: single-threaded hill-climbing on a nameable-cause loop with no design-switch rule. The starting-point machinery (`SKILL.md:64-76`, step 1: "what keeps a starting point from passing G2, and where the attempt still spends its time") surfaces the repeated failure in prose but attaches no consequence. Prevention needs the brief's acceptance criterion 5 as an explicit rule, e.g. in the harden step.

40|  with exit code 0 (`check_candidate.py:378-383`): a wrapper must read the JSON,
41|  not the exit code.

43|  final attempt" (`check_candidate.py:74-88`). It must merely cover the slot's
44|  parts.
45|- `max_rows` hand-off (`slots.py:327-337`): above `max_rows` rows the compiled
46|  reference runs instead of the kernels. With `max_rows=32`, all prefill sizes
47|  compare compiled-vs-compiled ("same"), so `beats_compiled` needs only decode
48|  wins. Sanctioned by ADR 0011, but it makes prefill a non-event by delegation.

54|### 1.2 time_candidates.py — end-to-end check and G3
55|
56|- Engines `plain` (MLX in-process) or `vllm` (`time_candidates.py:202`).
57|- Variants are built positionally: `base`, per-slot `compiled-<slot>` and
58|  `muse-<slot>`, plus `compiled-all`/`muse-all` only when >1 attempt is passed
59|  (`time_candidates.py:111-132`). `--variant NAME:...` adds extras outside
60|  `muse-all`; `compiled` as a folder means that slot's compiled reference
61|  (`time_candidates.py:100-109`).
62|- Swapping is a runtime class-attribute patch of `MoE.__call__` in every layer
63|  (`time_candidates.py:134-135`, `slots.make_moe_call`, `slots.py:97-119`).
64|  Positional attempts must not share parts (`time_candidates.py:221-223`);
65|  `--variant` extras are not checked for overlap.
66|- G2 end-to-end: greedy tokens over 24 generated tokens at 1 and 32 requests
67|  must equal base's — `TOKENS=24` (`time_candidates.py:51,138-160`) for plain,
68|  `max_tokens=24` (`repeat_fixes.py:187`) for vLLM. Kernel counts are also
69|  recorded (`repeat_fixes.py:137-144`). **There is no pass/fail gate on token
70|  exactness**: `exact` is logged per check and G3 ignores it
71|  (`time_candidates.py:168-197` reads only `kind=="run"` records).
72|- Timing loop `repeat_fixes.time_variants` (`repeat_fixes.py:285-359`):
73|  `--repeats` (default 5), `--settings` (default `1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024`),
74|  `--tokens` (default 256 output tokens). Plan shuffled with fixed seeds
75|  (`repeat_fixes.py:299-303`). Each run records decode-step period

81|  slower; faster/slower = non-overlapping min–max ranges over repeats.

83|  (`time_candidates.py:177`) and looks up a bar named `compiled-<suffix>`. A

89|  verified, `plain-probe.stderr`. So the gaming floor for `--tokens` is 9, at

159|## 2. Behaviours 1–5: how the territory causes or could prevent each
160|
161|1. **Unmeasured costs as free.** Cause: the grader's piece timing never sees
162|   request-level effects by construction; worse, the plain engine reports
163|   `prompt_ms = 0.0` always (§1.3) — an in-round plain check literally prices
164|   the prefill at zero. `max_rows` lets prefill be "same by delegation" (§1.1).
165|   Prevent: G3's rule (faster in one phase, slower in none, no request slower,
166|   `time_candidates.py:187-194`) already encodes "nothing is free" across
167|   decode/prompt/request — if the swarm must run it and cite `g3-vllm.json`.
168|2. **Piece arithmetic.** Cause: both tools hand out medians that invite
169|   subtraction — `timing_us_per_layer` per-size medians
170|   (`check_candidate.py:367-374`) and the printed
171|   `(med-base ms, %)` summary (`repeat_fixes.py:335-359`, seen live in the
172|   probe). Neither tool computes a piece's end-to-end effect. Prevent: an
173|   in-round `time_candidates.py vllm` run measures the whole request directly,
174|   making the arithmetic unnecessary; the design must require citing it.
175|3. **Inconsistent reasoning.** Cause: two different "compiled" baselines exist —
176|   per-part `mx.compile(ref)` in piece timing (`check_candidate.py:360`) vs
177|   whole-MoE `compiled-<slot>` end to end (`time_candidates.py:119-122`) — so
178|   "what mx.compile gains" is ambiguous, inviting borrowed gains. Also
179|   `muse-all`/`compiled-all` exist only with >1 positional attempt
180|   (`time_candidates.py:125-127`); a single-slot invocation never measures a
181|   combination, leaving "Together (sum)" as the only available number.
182|   Prevent: require passing all submitted slots positionally in one call so
183|   `muse-all` is measured as a combination.
184|4. **Grader as search loop.** Cause/enabler: the tool allows unlimited runs and
185|   prints a rich per-size gradient every run; one-run-one-attempt is a skill
186|   rule the tool cannot see (no attempt registry, no run counting, `--out`
187|   arbitrary, exit 0 even on G1 failure). The tool cannot prevent this; only
188|   the skill plus post-hoc log audit can. Note the queue makes each extra run
189|   cost everyone time (§1.4).
190|5. **Failing design family.** The tool provides the per-size signal
191|   (`timing[size].vs_compiled`, e.g. slower at rows 1 in both my grade files)
192|   but no cross-attempt memory: each run is stateless JSON. Cause data (e.g.
193|   too few threadgroups) is not measurable by any tool here. Prevention is
194|   skill-level (aggregate verdicts across attempts); proposal: none in-tool
195|   beyond citing the existing per-size verdicts.
196|
197|## 3. In-round end-to-end check: reuse, needs, duration, gaming
198|
199|- **Reuse as-is:** `time_candidates.py vllm <out> SLOT=FOLDER...` with defaults
200|  (4 G3 settings, 5 repeats, 256 tokens) plus the `g3()` verdict in
201|  `g3-vllm.json` — the rule already matches ADR 0011. `engine_table.py` renders
202|  it for judges. `gpu_lock.hold()` is already inside.
203|- **Needs (gaps in the tool):** (a) pin the invocation — `--repeats`,
204|  `--settings`, `--tokens` are free flags; (b) require all submitted slots
205|  positionally so `muse-all` exists; (c) forbid/ignore `--variant` names
206|  starting with `muse-` (crashes G3) and note non-`muse-` names escape judgment;
207|  (d) token exactness is recorded but never gated — a wrong-tokens variant can
208|  still pass G3; the check must require `exact` in the log; (e) plain engine
209|  must not count as the check (zero prompt, no verdict).
210|- **Duration:** single-slot vLLM G3 ≈ 13–14 min run wall at 5 repeats
211|  (extrapolated, `vllm-duration-estimate.txt`); 3-slot ≈ 3×. Grader: ~13 s
212|  (routing) to ~5 min (experts) per run (§1.1). Plain probe: 10.5 s for the
213|  minimal shape (§1.3). All GPU work serialises on the lock.
214|- **Gaming catalogue:**
215|  - `--repeats 1`: min–max ranges collapse to points; non-overlap (spurious
216|    faster AND slower) becomes near-certain. Undetectable from the verdict
217|    alone — repeats are logged per record (`rep` field) so audit the log.
218|  - `--settings` subset (e.g. only `32x128`): shrinks the "every setting"
219|    burden; non-G3 settings also change KV bytes (§1.2), breaking
220|    comparability with Claude's G3.
221|  - `--tokens` down to 9: wall ≈ prompt + 8 steps; below 9 the tool crashes
222|    (§1.2). Changes the decode/prompt weight silently.
223|  - `--variant myname:...`: timed but never judged (§1.2) — free numbers to
224|    quote. `--variant muse-x:...`: crashes G3 (§1.2).
225|  - Single-slot calls: no `muse-all`; combination claims stay arithmetic (§2.3).
226|  - Plain engine: zero prompt time, no verdict file; quotable medians that look
227|    like end-to-end numbers (§1.3).
228|  - Quoting medians/ranges selectively from the jsonl instead of the verdict.
229|  - check_candidate: `--baseline` points at any folder (pick a slow one);
230|    `max_rows=32` makes prefill "same" without doing prefill work (§1.1);
231|    in-between row counts are untested by the grader (`check_sizes.py` is
232|    separate, §1.5); unlimited re-runs (§2.4).
233|  - Lock: bypass by not calling `hold()` (all of `breakdown.py` /
234|    `repeat_fixes.py` direct use does this); DoS by holding; `rm` the lock
235|    file (§1.4).

229|### Behaviour 1 — treats unmeasured costs as free
230|- **Caused by territory, directly.** ADR 0010's "Not covered: prefill speed…
231|  would go unnoticed, apart from the time to first token" (0010 `:44`, `:42`
232|  at round-2 time — verified via `git show 4033cae:`) was cited by
233|  `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151` to
234|  declare a slow-but-exact prefill branch "free apart from time to first
235|  token". The swarm's wording echoes the ADR's. The measurement design made
236|  the claim true at the time: G2 checked prefill-size *outputs* while G3
237|  timed decode steps only (0010 `:44`; `muse-round-2.md:146`).
238|- **Measured cost** (§1 tables): experts-7 prompts 6.6–14.5× slower,
239|  throughput −10% to −83%; routing-4 prompts 7–10% slower, −3.5% at
240|  32×1024 (`muse-round-2.md:134-146`).
241|- **Prevented in the specific case** by 0011 (both-phase rule, G3 prompt +
242|  whole-request times, hand-off). **Not prevented in general:** 0011 has its
243|  own "Not covered" (`:51`, other chunk/row counts) in the same citeable
244|  form, and the territory contains no rule that unmeasured = unverified.
245|  (Proposal: rephrase every "Not covered" as "unverified: assume nothing";
246|  this matches brief acceptance criterion 4.)

249|- **Caused structurally by territory.** The design gives the swarm only
250|  per-slot piece timing in-round; the real objective (G3 over whole
251|  requests) arrives post-round via Claude (0006 `:42`, `:49`;
252|  `muse-swarm.md:133`). Nothing in the ADRs defines a valid in-round

260|- **Partially addressed:** 0009's sign test (`:35-36`) and 0011's extension
