Read text file `.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md`.
1|---
2|name: muse-round
3|description: Run one round of the Muse agent on the MobileMoE-S kernels as a swarm. Explorers map the code and measurements into a shared analysis; then competing builders write and grade fused Metal kernels for the top inefficiencies. From round 2 on, the round starts from the previous rounds' results and must beat their best attempts. Both phases are tracked in shared documents.
4|---
5|
6|# One round of the Muse agent: a swarm explores, then builds
7|
8|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed on main and tagged `muse-code-era` before the first Muse Code session; each later version is committed before the round that uses it. [Who made what](../../../PROVENANCE.md).*
9|
10|**Skill version 7.** This file, the role cards and tracking.md are versioned together; [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) lists every version. Each round records the version it ran (see *Versions* in tracking.md).
11|
12|You are the **lead** of a Muse Code session in your own worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. The first prompt names the Meta model you run as, the name your commit subjects start with, and the co-author line every commit ends with. `claude/muse-agent-brief.md` fixes the task, the slots, the tools and limits, the grader command and the pass criteria (G1, G2). Four ADRs change it in five ways:
13|
14|1. **Harness** ([ADR 0006](../../../claude/adr/0006-muse-spark-in-muse-code.md)). You are a Muse Code session, not a Claude Code one. Muse Code adds no trailer, so you write the first prompt's co-author line on every commit yourself (see *Commits*).
15|2. **No attempt limit and no stop rule** (ADR 0006). The brief's *When a slot stops* no longer applies: you decide when a slot is done. Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try.
16|3. **A swarm** ([ADR 0007](../../../claude/adr/0007-muse-spark-swarm.md)). Helpers explore and build; you coordinate and commit.
17|4. **Files** (ADR 0007, [ADR 0009](../../../claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md)). Each round writes in its own **round folder**: round 1 at the top of `muse-spark/`, round N from 2 on in `muse-spark/round-<N>/`. It holds `exploration/` and `implementation/`, the round's shared documents, which replace `strategy.md`; `kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<M>/`; and `summary.md`. tracking.md writes it `<round>/`.
18|5. **Rounds build on each other** (ADR 0009). A finished round's files are frozen: read them and cite them, and the hooks refuse any change to them. From round 2 on, a slot may have a **baseline**: the best attempt so far that passes the current G2 and that Claude's G3 accepted: against the unchanged model and the compiled reference, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A new attempt must beat it in the same grader run. A slot without one has a **starting point** instead: an earlier attempt to build from, which Claude's measurement names, with what kept it from being a baseline.
19|
20|The rest of the brief stands. The goal: kernels that pass G1 and G2 and have `beats_compiled` true, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither (ADR 0011); where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline` true too; faster because they remove a cause you can name. A faster decode step bought with a slower prefill is no improvement. An attempt built for decode sizes may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference with `max_rows` (the brief's launch spec). The Muse agent was Muse Spark in round 1 and Muse Wonder in round 2 ([ADR 0008](../../../claude/adr/0008-muse-wonder.md)), and is Muse Spark's contributor model again from round 3 ([ADR 0012](../../../claude/adr/0012-muse-spark-contributor-unattended.md)); the first prompt names the model you run as, and documents from earlier rounds say the model of their round. No one approves your tool calls during the round, so the rules here are yours to keep.
21|
22|## The swarm
23|
24|| Role | Name | Task | Card |
25||---|---|---|---|
26|| **Lead** (you) | | Start the helpers, keep the two READMEs, settle clashes, commit | this file |
27|| **Explorer** | `explorer-<territory>` | Map one territory into entries, and find where it loses time | [explorer.md](explorer.md) |
28|| **Verifier** | `verifier` | Check every inefficiency against its sources | [verifier.md](verifier.md) |
29|| **Builder** | `builder-<n>-<letter>` | Write and grade one solution for one hypothesis: one attempt | [builder.md](builder.md) |
30|| **Boundary agent** | `boundary-<n>` | Write what a hypothesis's solution must keep identical, and check passing attempts against it | [boundary.md](boundary.md) |
31|
32|You don't explore, build or grade yourself. Start each helper with a prompt of this shape:
33|
34|> You are `<name>`, a `<role>` in round `<N>`'s swarm; this round writes in `<round folder>`. Read `.agents/skills/muse-round/<card>` and `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md`, then: `<task>`.
35|
36|[tracking.md](tracking.md) describes the shared documents (the two phase folders, their READMEs, entries and logs) and the rules every agent keeps. Read it before starting anyone. Up to 12 agents run at once, you included.
37|
38|**A checkpoint** is what you do each time a helper returns, and whenever the log shows something to settle:
39|1. **Read the log.** Read the phase log since your last checkpoint.
40|2. **Settle clashes.** When two entries describe one cause, keep the fuller one and set the other's status to `superseded by <entry>`. When two helpers work on one item, redirect one of them (`subagent_send_message`). Log what you decided.
41|3. **Refresh the tracker.** Update the phase README's tracker table, and raise the version of each hypothesis entry that changed.
42|4. **Raise the version.** Raise the phase README to its next version, and add its line to `## Versions`, naming the entries that changed and their versions (see *Versions* in tracking.md).
43|5. **Commit** the phase folder, plus any attempt that came back, as that version (see *Commits*).
44|
45|## The round
46|
47|### 0. Find where you are
48|
49|- Run `git log --oneline main -1`, then `git tag --list -n1 'muse-round-*'`, which lists the finished rounds. **This round** is one more than the highest; with none, it is round 1. Its folder is `muse-spark/round-<N>/` (round 1: `muse-spark/`).
50|- `git log --oneline --grep '^Muse ' muse-code-era..HEAD` lists the Muse agent's commits of every round.
51|- **From round 2 on,** read Claude's measurement of the previous round, `claude/findings/muse-round-<N-1>.md`. It has the G3 results and names each slot's baseline or starting point. If it is missing, stop and reply "Claude's measurement of round <N-1> is missing": this round builds on it.
52|- If this round's folder already exists, a session stopped partway: carry on from its READMEs' last versions.
53|- Read the brief.
54|
55|**Done** when you can name the round number and its folder, and from round 2 on each slot's baseline or starting point and the latest G3 results.
56|
57|### 1. The starting point (from round 2 on)
58|
59|This is the round's plan, built on what the earlier rounds learned. Read:
60|- the previous rounds' final exploration and implementation READMEs and `summary.md`;
61|- the `notes.md` of each baseline or starting-point attempt;
62|- Claude's measurement.
63|
64|Then write the opening of this round's `exploration/README.md` (set up as in step 2.1), a section **Starting point**:
65|- **Per slot:**
66|  - the baseline, or the starting point where there is none, and its piece timing;
67|  - its G3 effect, and how that compares with what was predicted, with the reason where Claude's measurement gives one;
68|  - what keeps a starting point from passing G2, and where the attempt still spends its time.
69|- **What is left:**
70|  - the confirmed inefficiencies not yet built or not fully removed, ranked by predicted saving against the baselines, or the reference where a slot has none;
71|  - the slots not yet tried, for example `routing+combine`;
72|  - the recommendations outside the slots.
73|- **Refuted claims,** which no one chases again.
74|- **Territories** this round opens (step 2.2), each with the line of this section that reopens it.
75|
76|Commit it as exploration v1. **Done** when every slot has its baseline or starting point and every territory has its reason.
77|
78|### 2. Exploration
79|
80|1. **Set up the folder.** Write `<round>/exploration/README.md` with a heading, its version line (v1, with skill version 6), the tracker (one row per territory) and `## Versions`, and an empty `log.md`.
81|2. **Start the explorers and the verifier,** all at once.
82|   - **Round 1** starts with these territories:
83|
84|     | Territory | Covers |
85|     |---|---|
86|     | `model` | `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py`: the decoder layer, `MoE.__call__` and everything around the slots |
87|     | `switch-layers` | `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py`: the routed experts' path, `gather_qmm`, the sort from 16 rows |
88|     | `quantized-kernels` | `quantized.h` and `quantized_utils.h` in `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mlx/include/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/`: the `affine_gather_*` kernels behind `gather_qmm` |
89|     | `other-kernels` | the other Metal kernels in the same folder that the routing and combine slots launch: sort, softmax, reductions, elementwise, copies |
90|     | `vllm-metal` | `third_party/vllm-metal/vllm_metal/`: how the engine runs a decode step and a prefill chunk around the model |
91|     | `grader` | `bench/grader/`: the slot interface, what G1, G2 and the piece timing measure, and so the boundary every solution keeps |
92|     | `findings` | `claude/findings/` and `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/` |
93|     | `runs` | `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/`, `2026-10-29-baseline/` and `2026-10-30-micro/` |
94|
95|   - **From round 2 on,** the starting point lists the territories:
96|     - `baseline-<slot>` for each slot: its baseline's kernels and `spec.json`, which are now the code in the slot, or its starting point's. Map them with the checklist, and find where they still lose time and, for a starting point, why it fails G2;
97|     - `g3`: Claude's measurement of the previous round, where the end-to-end change differs from the piece timing, and why;
98|     - of round 1's territories, only those the starting point reopens. An explorer starts from that territory's earlier entries and writes only what is new.
99|3. **Refocus as costs show up.** When an entry shows that one file holds most of a territory's cost, split it off as a territory of its own, with its own explorer. Merge or close a territory that turns out to hold nothing, and add one when an inefficiency points somewhere no one covers. Log each change and update the tracker.
100|4. **Checkpoint** each time a helper returns.
101|
102|**Done** when every territory entry is `done`, the verifier has returned, and every inefficiency is `confirmed`, `refuted` or `superseded`.
103|
104|### 3. The analysis
105|
106|Write the final `<round>/exploration/README.md`. It is the round's report on the code, for this round's builders and for future improvements:
107|
108|- **Tracker:** the final table.
109|- **Starting point** (from round 2 on), as written in step 1, with any correction exploration made.
110|- **Context:** the decode step and the prefill, the MoE block and its slots, and what the measurements say about where the time goes in each.
111|- **Territory map:** how the territories feed each other. For each territory: what it receives, what it passes on, and its measured cost.
112|- **Inefficiencies, ranked:**
113|  - the confirmed ones inside the slots, ranked by predicted saving as a share of the decode step, averaged over 1, 8 and 32 rows, or of the prefill chunk, averaged over 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows; from round 2 on, the saving is against the baseline where the slot has one;
114|  - each with what removing it does to the other phase, and whether a hand-off (`max_rows`) keeps that phase unchanged;
115|  - each with its cost, kind and entry;
116|  - Claude's findings marked as Claude's, earlier rounds' entries linked as theirs, and this round's own reading marked as yours.
117|- **Recommendations:** the confirmed inefficiencies outside the slots, with their evidence. They're for surucuonur's team.
118|- **Refuted claims,** in one line each, so no one chases them again.
119|- **Files read:** links to each territory entry's list.
120|
121|Commit it. **Done** when every ranked item links a confirmed entry and every number in the README has its source.
122|
123|### 4. Implementation
124|
125|Take the ranked inefficiencies in order, at most two at a time, in different slots so their attempts never touch. Write `<round>/implementation/README.md` with a heading, its version line, the tracker and `## Versions`, and an empty `log.md`. For each hypothesis:
126|
127|1. **Open the hypothesis.** Write `<round>/implementation/hyp-<n>-<slug>.md`, with status `boundary`, the inefficiency, the slot and, from round 2 on, the slot's baseline folder or `none`. Add its tracker row and log it.
128|2. **Draw its boundary.** Start `boundary-<n>` to write the boundary, and wait for it.
129|3. **Compete.**
130|   - Set the status to `building`.
131|   - Start 2 or 3 builders, `builder-<n>-a`, `-b` and `-c`. Give each a different direction drawn from the analysis: for example, fusing kernels, reading each weight byte once, or a different threadgroup shape. From round 2 on, a direction may start from the baseline's or starting point's kernels, or from scratch.
132|4. **Collect.** Each time a builder returns:
133|   - checkpoint, committing its attempt folder with the hypothesis entry, the README and the log;
134|   - if the attempt passed G2, start `boundary-<n>` to check it.
135|5. **Harden.**
136|   - Pick the best attempt: it passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, has `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline`, and it is the fastest across the six sizes.
137|   - Set the status to `hardening`, and start a builder for that attempt's next single change.
138|   - Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove.
139|6. **Close.**
140|   - **`ready`:** the best attempt passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, has `beats_compiled` true and, where the slot has a baseline, `beats_baseline` true, and you can name no further change worth making. Write the **Decision**: the attempt, why it is best, and what G3 should show.
141|   - **`dropped`:** say why. A slot whose hypotheses are all dropped keeps its baseline, or the reference where it has none.
142|
143|Then open the next-ranked inefficiency. **Done** when no confirmed inefficiency is left that you judge will pay. Write why in the implementation README.
144|
145|### 5. Finish
146|
147|1. **The implementation README:** the final tracker, one paragraph per hypothesis, and a **Ready to test** section. It names the attempt per slot that goes to G3, this round's, the baseline kept, or the reference, and the change you expect in G3's four workloads, in the decode step, the prompt time and the whole request, against the previous round's, with how you worked it out.
148|2. **The exploration README:** add *What building taught*, the analysis corrected by what the attempts showed.
149|3. **`<round>/summary.md`:** a `## Round N` section with:
150|   - the model, the skill version this round ran, and the final versions of both READMEs;
151|   - the final attempt per slot;
152|   - the number of graded attempts per slot, this round and over all rounds;
153|   - the expected G3 change;
154|   - what you'd try next;
155|   - your recommendations outside the slots.
156|4. **Commit,** then reply with this round's commits and the words "Round N finished".
157|
158|## Your own rules
159|
160|- **Writes:**
161|  - you write the two READMEs, the hypothesis entries' status blocks and decisions, and `summary.md`;
162|  - every helper writes only what its card names;
163|  - all of it stays in this round's folder.
164|- **G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team,** who run them after merging your branch.
165|- **The rules every agent keeps** are in tracking.md.
166|
167|## Commits
168|
169|You are the only agent that commits. Commit only on `muse-agent`.
170|- **What to add:** this round's phase folders that exist so far (only `exploration` until implementation starts) and the attempt folders that came back. An attempt another builder is still writing waits for its own commit. An entry that is mid-edit is committed as it stands, and finished in a later commit.
171|- **The message:**
172|  - every subject starts with the name the first prompt gives you, then a colon;
173|  - a checkpoint's subject is `<name>: <phase> v<N>: <what changed>`, the version it records;
174|  - every message ends with the first prompt's co-author line, exactly.
175|
176|For example, in round 2 as Muse Wonder:
177|
178|```bash
179|git add muse-spark/round-2/exploration muse-spark/round-2/implementation muse-spark/round-2/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<M>
180|git commit -m "Muse Wonder: implementation v4: experts attempt 3 graded, beats baseline" \
181|  -m "Co-Authored-By: Muse Wonder (Meta Model API) <muse-wonder@meta-model-api.invalid>"
182|```
183|
184|Use no other co-author. The hooks refuse a commit without a Muse agent's co-author, a commit outside `muse-spark/`, a change to a finished round's files, a new file outside this round's folder, and any merge. Push, merge, rebase, tags, git config and hook skipping stay with surucuonur.

1|# The swarm's shared documents, and the rules every agent keeps
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Part of the [muse-round skill](SKILL.md). [Who made what](../../../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|Every agent of the round reads this file. The documents below are how the swarm shares what it knows and how surucuonur follows the round while it runs, so keep them current as you work, not at the end.
6|
7|## The round folder and its two phase folders
8|
9|`<round>/` is this round's folder: `muse-spark/round-<N>/` from round 2 on (round 1's is `muse-spark/` itself). The lead's prompt names it.
10|
11|| Folder | Phase | Holds |
12||---|---|---|
13|| `<round>/exploration/` | Exploration | the analysis: `README.md`, territory and inefficiency entries, `log.md` |
14|| `<round>/implementation/` | Implementation | the report: `README.md`, hypothesis entries, `log.md` |
15|
16|Kernels go in `<round>/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/`, numbered from 1 in each round; the grader reads any attempt folder it is given.
17|
18|**Earlier rounds' folders are frozen.** Read them and cite them by path; write what you add in this round's entries. The hooks refuse a change to any file a finished round left.
19|
20|Each folder has three kinds of document:
21|
22|- **`README.md`.** The phase's document. Only the lead writes it, refreshing it and raising its version at every checkpoint. It opens with its version line and the tracker table below.
23|- **Entries.** One file per territory, inefficiency or hypothesis. The owner keeps it current, and other agents append notes.
24|- **`log.md`.** One line per event, from every agent, appended only.
25|
26|## Versions
27|
28|Every shared document carries a version number, so a reader knows which version they're looking at, and git holds every version.
29|
30|**Phase versions.** Each README opens with its version line:
31|
32|```markdown
33|**Version:** v5 · 2026-11-04T09:40Z · skill version 6
34|```
35|
36|- **Who raises it:** the lead, at every checkpoint, and each version is exactly one commit.
37|- **The commit:** its subject names the version, `<name>: exploration v5: <what changed>`, where `<name>` is the Muse agent's name from the lead's first prompt. `git log --grep 'exploration v5:'` finds it, and `git diff` between two such commits shows what changed.
38|- **The changelog:** the README ends with `## Versions`, one line per version, newest first, naming the entries that changed and their new versions:
39|
40|```markdown
41|- v5 · 2026-11-04T09:40Z · split quantized-kernels in two · changed: territory-quantized-kernels v4, ineff-quantized-kernels-2 v2
42|```
43|
44|**Entry versions.** Each entry's status block has a `Version` line, starting at 1:
45|- **Territory and inefficiency entries:** the owner raises it with every change to its own text. The verifier raises it when it writes the verdict.
46|- **Hypothesis entries:** the lead raises it at each checkpoint where the entry changed, builders' and the boundary agent's sections included.
47|- **Notes:** a note under `## From other agents` leaves the version alone. The owner raises it when folding the note in.
48|
49|**Times.** Every time you write, in a version line, a status block, a tracker row, a note or a log line, is the output of `date -u +%FT%TZ` run at that moment. Never estimate or round one.
50|
51|## The README trackers
52|
53|Exploration, `exploration/README.md`:
54|
55|| Territory | Agent | Status | Inefficiencies | Updated |
56||---|---|---|---|---|
57|| `quantized-kernels` | `explorer-quantized-kernels` | exploring | `ineff-quantized-kernels-1` (confirmed), `-2` (open) | 2026-11-04 09:40Z |
58|
59|Implementation, `implementation/README.md`:
60|
61|| Hypothesis | Slot | Builders | Attempts: G1, G2, µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows (compiled) | Status |
62||---|---|---|---|---|
63|| `hyp-1-fused-gather` | `experts` | `builder-1-a`, `builder-1-b` | 3: pass, pass, 41 / 55 / 180 (48 / 70 / 260) | hardening |
64|
65|From round 2 on, where the slot has a baseline, the attempts column also gives its time from the same run, and whether `beats_baseline` is true.
66|
67|## Entries
68|
69|Each entry opens with a status block that its owner keeps current:
70|
71|```markdown
72|- **Owner:** explorer-quantized-kernels
73|- **Status:** exploring
74|- **Version:** 3
75|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T09:40Z
76|- **Next:** read the 32-row dispatch of affine_gather_qmm
77|```
78|
79|Entries are named so that two agents never pick the same name:
80|- `<round>/exploration/territory-<territory>.md`
81|- `<round>/exploration/ineff-<territory>-<n>.md`, numbered by the explorer of that territory
82|- `<round>/implementation/hyp-<n>-<slug>.md`, numbered by the lead
83|
84|**Another agent's entry:** append under its `## From other agents` heading, starting with your name and the time. The owner's text stays as written, so two agents never overwrite each other. The owner reads these notes and folds in what holds.
85|
86|### Territory entry

88|1. Status block (statuses: `exploring`, `done`).

3|The independent grader for the Muse agent's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).

15|      [--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER ...]

191|def chained(fn, layers, names):
192|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
193|
194|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
195|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
196|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
197|    """
198|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
199|    outs = []
200|    for layer in layers:
201|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
202|        if outs:
203|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
204|        out = fn(**args)
205|        if isinstance(out, dict):
206|            out = list(out.values())
207|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
208|    return outs

211|def timed(fn, layers, names):
212|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
213|    for _ in range(3):
214|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
215|    times = []
216|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
217|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
218|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
219|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
220|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)

223|def paired_times(fns, layers, names):
224|    """Per-repeat µs per layer of each function, in rotating order within each repeat."""
225|    calls = [lambda f=f: mx.eval(chained(f, layers, names)) for f in fns]
226|    for _ in range(3):
227|        for call in calls:
228|            call()
229|    times = [[] for _ in fns]
230|    for i in range(REPEATS):
231|        for j in [(i + k) % len(fns) for k in range(len(fns))]:
232|            t0 = time.perf_counter()
233|            calls[j]()
234|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)
235|    return times

248|    """Each phase's verdict from its sizes' verdicts, and whether the candidate
249|    beats the bar: faster at every size of one phase, slower at no size of the other.
250|
251|    A phase is "faster" when every size is, "slower" when any size is, and
252|    "not slower" otherwise.

254|    phases = {}
255|    for phase, prefix in PHASES.items():
256|        sizes = [v for size, v in verdicts.items() if size.startswith(prefix)]

258|            "faster" if all(v == "faster" for v in sizes)
259|            else "slower" if "slower" in sizes

1|"""One GPU job at a time: the exclusive lock every grader entry point takes.
2|
3|Muse Spark's builder agents and Claude run these scripts on the same M1 Pro
4|GPU, and two runs at once distort each other's timings. A run that finds the
5|GPU busy says so and waits its turn, so runs queue and never overlap. The lock
6|file is in /tmp, so the main checkout and the Muse Spark worktree share it, and
7|the operating system releases it when the process ends, however it ends.
8|"""
9|
10|import fcntl
11|import os
12|import sys
13|
14|LOCK = "/tmp/mobilemoe-gpu.lock"
15|_held = []  # keeps the locked file open for the life of the process
16|
17|
18|def hold(job):
19|    """Take the GPU for this process, waiting while another run has it."""
20|    f = open(LOCK, "a+")
21|    try:
22|        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
23|    except BlockingIOError:
24|        f.seek(0)
25|        holder = f.read().strip() or "another run"
26|        print(f"{job}: waiting for the GPU ({holder})", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
27|        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
28|    f.seek(0)
29|    f.truncate()
30|    f.write(f"pid {os.getpid()}: {job}\n")
31|    f.flush()
32|    _held.append(f)

24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
29|
30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
50|
51|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
52|
53|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
54||---|---|---|---|
55|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
56|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
57|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
58|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
59|
60|Reference:
61|
62|```python
63|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
64|```
65|
66|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
67|
68|### `routing+combine`
69|
70|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
71|
72|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
73|
74|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
75||---|---|---|---|
76|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
77|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
78|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
79|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
80|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
81|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
82|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
83|
84|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
85|
86|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
87|
88|```python
89|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
90|```
91|
92|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
93|
94|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
95|
96|## Tools and limits
97|
98|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.
99|- **The grader runs no Python of yours.** It reads your launch spec as data and compiles only your Metal.
100|- **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes, longer for an attempt much slower than the reference at the prefill sizes; stop one that runs past 15.
101|- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.
102|
103|## Rules of this session
104|
105|These keep your work apart from everyone else's. Git hooks and an audit script enforce them, and a commit that breaks them is refused.
106|
107|- **Write only inside `muse-spark/`.** Never change `bench/`, `claude/`, `results/`, `tools/`, `third_party/`, or any other file. A copy of the grader you edit is never used.
108|- **Commit only on `muse-agent`,** with the co-author trailer your settings add: `Co-Authored-By: Muse Spark (Meta Model API) <muse-spark@meta-model-api.invalid>`. Start each subject with `Muse Spark:`. No other co-author.
109|- **Never push, merge, rebase, change git config, or skip hooks.**
110|- **Don't read `.env`** or any credentials file.
111|- One commit per attempt, after you've run the grader on it, so the history shows every attempt in order.
112|
113|## Your files
114|
115|```
116|muse-spark/
117|  strategy.md                                your choice and design, ending with the targets JSON
118|  kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/
119|    block-0.metal, block-1.metal, ...        Metal kernel bodies (and headers), numbered from 0
120|    spec.json                                the launch spec
121|    notes.md                                 optional: what you tried and why
122|  summary.md                                 your final attempt per slot
123|```
124|
125|`<slot-folder>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing-combine` or `experts`. Grade an attempt with:
126|
127|```bash
128|.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N> <slot>
129|```
130|
131|where `<slot>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing+combine` or `experts`.
132|
133|**The targets JSON** at the end of `strategy.md`:
134|
135|```json
136|{
137|  "targets": [
138|    {"slot": "routing+combine", "why": "...", "expected_saving_ms": {"rows_1": 0.0, "rows_32": 0.0}, "design": "..."}
139|  ]
140|}
141|```
142|
143|List one or two targets, in the order you work on them.
144|
145|**The launch spec** (`spec.json`):
146|
147|```json
148|{
149|  "kernels": [
150|    {
151|      "name": "fused_routing",
152|      "source_block": 0,
153|      "header_block": null,
154|      "inputs": ["x", "w_router", "bias"],
155|      "outputs": [
156|        {"name": "inds", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "uint32"},
157|        {"name": "weights", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "float32"}
158|      ],
159|      "grid": ["rows*32", 1, 1],
160|      "threadgroup": [32, 1, 1],
161|      "template": {"T": "bfloat16"},
162|      "init_value": null,
163|      "atomic_outputs": false
164|    }
165|  ],
166|  "slot_outputs": {"inds": "inds", "weights": "weights"}
167|}
168|```
169|
170|- **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
171|- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
172|- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
173|- **`max_rows`** (optional, an integer of at least 1): inputs with more rows than this skip your kernels and run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. Use it to keep prefill-sized inputs on MLX's own code when your kernels are built for decode sizes; MLX switches its own experts kernel at 60 rows. The hand-off is graded like the rest: bit-exact, and timed at the prefill sizes.
174|- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot, `max_rows` included: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
175|- **Shape and grid entries** are integers, or products of integers and the names `rows`, `D`, `E`, `K` and `H`, such as `"rows*32"`. Nothing else is evaluated.
176|- **dtypes** are `float32`, `bfloat16`, `float16`, `uint32` or `int32`.
177|- **Template values** are one of those dtypes, an integer or a boolean.
178|- **`grid`** counts threads, not threadgroups, as in `mx.fast.metal_kernel`.
179|
180|## How each attempt is judged
181|
182|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only. From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.
183|
184|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
185|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
186|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
187|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
188|
189|   At every size:
190|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
191|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
192|
193|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
194|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
195|3. **G3, faster, in vLLM.** Each workload runs 5 times in shuffled order: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts, 256 generated tokens each. Three times are measured per run:
196|   - the **decode step**, the median period between steady steps;
197|   - the **prompt time**, until every prompt was processed;
198|   - the **whole request**, from sending the requests to the last token.
199|
200|   Against both the original model and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code, the attempt passes when the decode step or the prompt time is faster in every workload, neither is slower in any, and no whole request is slower. Faster and slower mean that the ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
201|
202|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
203|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
204|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
205|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same` or `slower`); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.
206|
207|**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
208|- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
209|- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
210|- **Per phase:** decode (1, 8, 32 rows) and prefill (127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) are each `faster` when every size is, `slower` when any size is, and `not slower` otherwise.
211|- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
212|
213|It is a guide; G3 decides.
214|
215|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and has `beats_compiled` true, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

1|"""The parts of MobileMoE-S's MoE block that a Muse Spark kernel may replace.
2|
3|Each slot has a reference (the port's own code, split as in breakdown.py),
4|named inputs and outputs (claude/muse-agent-brief.md), and a way to install
5|an implementation into MoE.__call__ for every layer. build() turns a launch
6|spec (data, never code) into mx.fast.metal_kernel calls.
7|
8|Record the grader's inputs from a real decode step (plain MLX, no API):
9|
10|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/slots.py capture
11|"""
12|
13|import re
14|from pathlib import Path
15|
16|import mlx.core as mx
17|import numpy as np
18|
19|D, E, K, H = 768, 60, 4, 384
20|SCALE = 2.5  # routed_scaling_factor; norm_topk_prob is true
21|NAMES = {"D": D, "E": E, "K": K, "H": H}
22|DTYPES = {
23|    "float32": mx.float32,
24|    "bfloat16": mx.bfloat16,
25|    "float16": mx.float16,
26|    "uint32": mx.uint32,
27|    "int32": mx.int32,
28|}
29|SLOTS = {
30|    "routing": (["x", "w_router", "bias"], ["inds", "weights"]),
31|    "combine": (["y", "weights", "shared"], ["out"]),
32|}
33|EXPERT_WEIGHTS = [
34|    f"{p}_{t}" for p in ("gate", "up", "down") for t in ("w", "scales", "biases")
35|]
36|SLOTS["experts"] = (["x", "inds"] + EXPERT_WEIGHTS, ["y"])
37|SLOTS["routing+combine"] = (
38|    SLOTS["routing"][0] + ["y", "shared"],
39|    ["inds", "weights", "out"],
40|)
41|INPUTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "models" / "muse-inputs"

43|
44|def ref_routing(x, w_router, bias):
45|    scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)
46|    inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=K - 1, axis=-1)[:, :K]
47|    w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
48|    return inds, w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * SCALE
49|
50|
51|def ref_combine(y, weights, shared):
52|    return (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
53|
54|
55|def ref_experts(x, inds, *weights):
56|    """The port's SwitchGLU on flat rows: [rows, D] and [rows, K] -> [rows, K, D]."""
57|    from mlx_lm.models.activations import swiglu
58|    from mlx_lm.models.switch_layers import _gather_sort, _scatter_unsort
59|
60|    gate, up, down = weights[0:3], weights[3:6], weights[6:9]
61|    xx = mx.expand_dims(x, (-2, -3))
62|    do_sort = inds.size >= 64
63|    idx, inv = inds, None
64|    if do_sort:
65|        xx, idx, inv = _gather_sort(xx, inds)
66|
67|    def qmm(a, w):
68|        return mx.gather_qmm(
69|            a,
70|            *w,
71|            rhs_indices=idx,
72|            transpose=False,
73|            group_size=32,
74|            bits=4,
75|            mode="affine",
76|            sorted_indices=do_sort,
77|        )
78|
79|    y = qmm(swiglu(qmm(xx, gate), qmm(xx, up)), down)
80|    if do_sort:
81|        y = _scatter_unsort(y, inv, inds.shape)
82|    return y.squeeze(-2)
83|
84|
85|REFERENCE = {"routing": ref_routing, "combine": ref_combine, "experts": ref_experts}

88|def expert_weights(experts):
89|    """A layer's SwitchGLU weights, named as in the experts slot."""
90|    return {
91|        f"{p}_{t}": getattr(experts, f"{p}_proj")[k]
92|        for p in ("gate", "up", "down")
93|        for t, k in (("w", "weight"), ("scales", "scales"), ("biases", "biases"))
94|    }

97|def make_moe_call(routing=ref_routing, combine=ref_combine, experts=None):
98|    """MoE.__call__ with its slots swapped for *routing*, *combine*, *experts*.
99|
100|    With the references it gives the port's outputs bit for bit (checked by
101|    check_identity), so any difference comes from the swapped slot. With
102|    experts=None the port's own SwitchGLU runs.
103|    """
104|
105|    def moe_call(self, x):
106|        lead = x.shape[:-1]
107|        flat = x.reshape(-1, D)
108|        bias = self.expert_bias.astype(mx.float32)
109|        inds, weights = routing(flat, self.router.weight, bias)
110|        if experts is None:
111|            y = self.experts(x, inds.reshape(*lead, K))
112|        else:
113|            w = expert_weights(self.experts)
114|            y = experts(flat, inds, *[w[n] for n in EXPERT_WEIGHTS])
115|        shared = self.shared_expert(x)
116|        out = combine(y.reshape(-1, K, D), weights, shared.reshape(-1, D))
117|        return out.reshape(*lead, D)
118|
119|    return moe_call

304|def build(spec, sources, slot):
305|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks.
306|
307|    With "max_rows" in the spec, inputs with more rows than that run the slot's
308|    reference under mx.compile instead of the kernels, so an attempt can keep
309|    prompt-sized inputs on MLX's own code (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md).
310|    """
311|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
312|    kernels = []
313|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
314|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
315|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
316|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
317|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
318|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
319|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
320|            header=header,
321|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
322|        )
323|        kernels.append((k, fn))
324|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
325|    if missing:
326|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
327|    max_rows = spec.get("max_rows")
328|    if max_rows is not None:
329|        if isinstance(max_rows, bool) or not isinstance(max_rows, int) or max_rows < 1:
330|            raise ValueError(f"bad max_rows {max_rows!r}")
331|        compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])
332|
333|    def run(**inputs):
334|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
335|        if max_rows is not None and rows > max_rows:  # the compiled reference takes over
336|            out = compiled(*[inputs[n] for n in slot_in])
337|            return dict(zip(slot_out, out if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out]))
338|        env = dict(inputs)
339|        for k, fn in kernels:
340|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
341|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
342|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
343|            outs = fn(
344|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
345|                template=[
346|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
347|                ],
348|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
349|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
350|                output_shapes=[
351|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
352|                ],
353|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
354|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
355|            )
356|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
357|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
358|
359|    return run

5|# From round 3, an improvement must hold in both phases, decode and prefill, and an attempt may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference
6|
7|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
8|
9|**The change.** Claude's comparison of every engine version over whole requests ([findings](../findings/muse-round-2.md), section 5) found that the grader and G3 timed only the decode step. They never timed the prefill, the phase in which a request's whole prompt runs through the model:
10|- **Experts attempt-7** looked like round 2's largest gain, a 19% shorter decode step at 32 requests. It processed prompts 6.6 to 14.5 times slower and cut throughput by 10% to 83%.
11|- **Routing attempt-4,** round 2's only baseline, processed prompts 7% to 10% slower. At 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts it cost 3.5% of throughput.
12|
13|The Muse agent never saw either effect: its piece timing ran decode sizes only, and G3 measured the decode step only.
14|
15|On 2026-11-04 surucuonur set the rule: "The improvement should be in the two phases of it: decode and prefill. Then, we can consider it as an improvement." surucuonur chose:
16|- **faster in one phase, slower in neither;**
17|- **the hand-off:** an attempt may leave prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference. This replaces the part of [ADR 0010](0010-exact-at-every-size.md) that required the kernels to run in every call.
18|
19|## How it works
20|
21|- **The piece timing runs at the six G2 sizes** (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`): decode at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. The layers are still chained.
22|- **The verdict at each size comes from paired repeats.** The candidate and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times, and so does the baseline when one is given.
23|  - The candidate is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, a one-sided sign test at p < 0.01.
24|  - It is `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise.
25|
26|  This replaces the comparison of medians for the decode sizes too, since the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
27|- **The verdict per phase:**
28|  - a phase is `faster` when every one of its sizes is;
29|  - it is `slower` when any size is;
30|  - otherwise it is `not slower`.
31|
32|  `beats_compiled`, and `beats_baseline` against a baseline, are true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
33|- **The hand-off** (`max_rows` in `spec.json`, `bench/grader/slots.py`). Inputs with more rows than `max_rows` run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. G2 still checks every size.
34|  - On 2026-11-04 the compiled reference of each slot was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes (`bench/micro/compiled_exact.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`).
35|  - Above `max_rows` a hand-off runs the compiled reference itself, so it times `same` as the bar there, never better.
36|- **G3** (`bench/grader/time_candidates.py`, which writes `g3-vllm.json`):
37|  - **Workloads:** 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts.
38|  - **Measurements per run:** the decode step period, the prompt time and the whole-request time, over 5 shuffled repeats, up from 3.
39|  - **Faster and slower:** the two ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
40|  - **Why 5 repeats:** with 3 each, two identical engines' ranges miss each other by chance 1 time in 20 per direction. "Never slower" checks a phase 8 times (4 workloads, 2 bars), so a phase that changed nothing would fail about a third of the time. The first run under these rules showed it. A copy of experts attempt-7 with a hand-off at 59 rows came out `slower` on prompt time at 32 × 1,024, by 0.5% with ranges 16 ms apart, although above 59 rows it runs the compiled reference, whose own range overlapped the unchanged engine's (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`). With 5 repeats the chance is 1 in 252 per check, about 3% over 8.
41|  - **The pass rule:** against both the original model and the compiled reference, the decode step or the prompt time must be faster in every workload, neither may be slower in any, and no whole request may be slower.
42|- **The unchanged engine is vLLM's own.** The original model in G3 runs with Claude's step hooks, and with vLLM's engine inside the script's process. On 2026-11-04, alternating runs found it within −0.2% to +1.9% of vLLM with neither, inside the spread between repeats in every workload (`bench/micro/clean_vllm.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-clean-vllm/`).
43|
44|## Consequences
45|
46|- **Round 3 starts with no baseline.** Routing attempt-4 is `slower` at all three prefill sizes, 2.6 to 8.7 times the compiled reference's time. It fails G3 on prompt time at 8 and 32 requests. It becomes a starting point, so round 3's bar in every slot is the compiled reference.
47|- **A decode kernel no longer has to win at prefill sizes,** only to hand them off or not lose there. The attempt chooses the row count, so the boundary agent checks that the hand-off sits on the right side of 60 rows for the experts slot.
48|- **At prefill sizes, a slot with a hand-off is MLX's code, not the Muse agent's.** The claim for such an attempt is "faster decode, unchanged prefill".
49|- **Grader runs and G3 take longer.** Every attempt is now timed at three more sizes. G3 runs 5 repeats instead of 3, and its 32 × 1,024 workload adds at least 16 s per variant per repeat.
50|- **The decode verdict is stricter.** An attempt whose median beat the compiled reference by noise is now `same`.
51|- **Not covered:** prefill chunks of other sizes, and decode steps with other row counts. The boundary agent reports them; G3's four workloads are the end-to-end check.
52|- **At 1 request the whole-request time is noisy.** On 2026-11-04 its repeats spread 6% to 41%, so G3 there mostly says `same`, which passes the "never slower" test without showing a gain.
53|
54|## Considered options
55|
56|- **Faster in both phases.** The higher bar. A decode kernel would also have to beat MLX's large matrix kernels at 2,048 rows, which is not where the decode step loses its time. Not chosen.
57|- **Whole-request throughput alone.** Simple, but it lets a slower phase be traded for a faster one. surucuonur ruled that out.
58|- **Hand off to the uncompiled reference.** The prefill could then come out `slower` than the compiled reference wherever compiling helps; at 127 rows, routing's compiled reference takes 87 µs per layer against 102 µs uncompiled.
59|- **Keep the kernels in every call** (ADR 0010). The kernels could still branch on the row count inside themselves, but they couldn't use MLX's large-size kernels. surucuonur chose the hand-off.

3|Three changes, each exact (the same numbers, fewer kernels), applied at runtime:
4|
5|  bias_f32     each layer's expert_bias held in float32 instead of bfloat16, so

19|compared with the unchanged model's, and one decode step's graph is exported

1|"""Investigation: break a MobileMoE-S decode step into pieces and time each one.
2|
3|Each process runs one engine on the int4 model and appends one JSON line per
4|run to runs-<engine>.jsonl in the output folder:
5|
6|  plain   the mlx_lm port with its own KV cache, pipelined like mlx_lm generate
7|  vllm    vLLM in process: vllm-metal's model runner, paged attention, sampler
8|
9|Wrappers installed at runtime give each piece of the step a named span (the
10|model's layers, attention and expert parts, and in vLLM the runner's own
11|steps). Every run uses one mode:
12|
13|  bare        only the step-boundary hooks: the step period as served
14|  off         all wrappers installed but idle: the baseline for knock-outs
15|  cpu         spans timed, nothing else changed: CPU time of each piece
16|  sync        each span evaluates its inputs on entry and its outputs on
17|              exit, so its kernels are encoded and run on their own: encoding
18|              (CPU) and GPU time per piece. One step also exports each piece's
19|              graph (mx.export_to_dot) to count its operations.
20|  ko:<piece>  as off, but the piece (or group of pieces) is not run: each call
21|              returns the output it gave the first time it ran with inputs
22|              of that shape, tied to its current inputs with mx.depends so
23|              they are still computed. What the step gains without it.
24|  kc:<piece>  the control for ko:<piece>: the same bookkeeping and ties, but
25|              the piece still runs. At 1 row the step is CPU-bound, so the
26|              gain from removing a piece is the kc time minus the ko time.
27|
28|The model and engine code are not changed; outputs of knock-out runs are
29|meaningless, only their timing counts.
30|
31|Run from the repo root with .venv/bin/python, one engine at a time:
32|  .venv/bin/python bench/micro/breakdown.py plain results/runs/<date>-breakdown
33|  .venv/bin/python bench/micro/breakdown.py vllm results/runs/<date>-breakdown

182|    def replay(self, name, fn, args, kwargs):
183|        """Knock-out: the first output for inputs of this shape, without running.
184|
185|        Keyed by the first array argument's shape, not every input's: the
186|        plain engine's attention reads a key/value cache that grows each step.
187|        """

192|            out = fn(*args, **kwargs)

453|def prefill(model, ids, cache):
454|    """Run the prompts *ids* into *cache* and return the first new tokens.
455|
456|    The prompts run in chunks of at most PREFILL_TOKENS tokens, like vLLM's
457|    token budget, and only the last position is scored, as in mlx_lm generate:
458|    scoring all 32 x 1,024 positions at once needs 8.4 GB of logits.
459|    """
460|    chunk = max(1, PREFILL_TOKENS // ids.shape[0])
461|    end = ids.shape[1] - 1
462|    for i in range(0, end, chunk):
463|        model(ids[:, i : min(i + chunk, end)], cache=cache)
464|        mx.eval([c.state for c in cache])
465|    return greedy(model(ids[:, -1:], cache=cache))

481|        REC.call("wait_gpu", to_list, (y,), {})
482|        y = ny

# MobileMoE Bandwidth Study

*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*

How efficiently an inference engine turns an Apple Silicon GPU's memory bandwidth and compute into generated tokens when serving a small mixture-of-experts model.

## Hardware limits

**Peak bandwidth**:
The most bytes per second the GPU can read from unified memory, as rated by the manufacturer (about 200 GB/s on this project's M1 Pro).
_Avoid_: max bandwidth, memory speed

**Peak compute**:
The most floating-point operations per second the GPU can perform (about 5.2 TFLOPS on the 16-core M1 Pro GPU).
_Avoid_: max compute, TFLOPS (as the name of the limit)

**Achieved bandwidth**:
The bytes a decode step must read from memory (the weights it touches plus its share of cached attention state), divided by that step's duration.
_Avoid_: bandwidth usage, utilization (unqualified)

**Arithmetic intensity**:
Floating-point operations performed per byte read from memory during a decode step.
_Avoid_: compute density, FLOPs/byte ratio

**Ridge point**:
The arithmetic intensity at which peak bandwidth and peak compute meet (about 26 operations per byte here); below it a step is limited by bandwidth, above it by compute.

**Roofline**:
The chart of achievable throughput against arithmetic intensity, capped by peak bandwidth on the left and peak compute on the right, with measured decode steps plotted beneath it.

## Bottlenecks and fixes

**Bandwidth-bound**:
A decode step whose achieved bandwidth is close to peak bandwidth.

**Compute-bound**:
A decode step whose operation rate is close to peak compute.

**Overhead-bound**:
A decode step far below both limits, because its time goes to work other than reading weights or doing arithmetic, such as launching GPU jobs, routing tokens to experts or scheduling.
_Avoid_: latency-bound, CPU-bound (unless the CPU specifically is the cause)

**Bottleneck**:
The single cause, identified from measurements, that most limits throughput for a given workload.
_Avoid_: issue, slowness

**Kernel**:
One program the GPU runs as a unit, such as one matrix product or one element-wise add; a decode step is a chain of hundreds of them, each with a fixed start-up cost.
_Avoid_: GPU job, op (for a kernel launch)

**Occupancy**:
The share of the GPU's thread slots in use while it runs; low occupancy means most of the chip is idle even when the GPU counts as busy.
_Avoid_: GPU utilization (which only says the GPU had work)

**Knock-out**:
A measurement in which one piece of the decode step is replaced by a stand-in that returns the right shape without GPU work; the time and bytes the step saves are that piece's cost.
_Avoid_: ablation

**Baseline**:
The unmodified engine serving MobileMoE-S-QAT (int4), against which every fix is measured.

**Fix**:
One change to the engine, the model code or the configuration, measured against the baseline under the same workload.
_Avoid_: optimization (for a change that hasn't been measured), tweak

## Inference

**Prefill**:
Processing a request's whole prompt through the model before its first token is generated, in chunks of up to the engine's token budget per pass (2,048 tokens here).
_Avoid_: prompt phase (say prefill, or prompt processing)

**Decode step**:
One engine iteration that produces one new token for each request it includes.

**Decode rows**:
The number of requests the engine actually advanced in one decode step; the batch size that matters for the roofline.
_Avoid_: batch size (unqualified), concurrency

**Client concurrency**:
The number of requests the benchmark client keeps in flight; it caps decode rows but does not equal them.
_Avoid_: batch size

## Mixture of experts

**Expert**:
One of the interchangeable feed-forward blocks in a layer; MobileMoE-S has 60 routed experts per layer.

**Active experts**:
The experts the router picks for one token in one layer (4 for MobileMoE-S).
_Avoid_: selected experts, top-k experts

**Distinct experts**:
The number of different experts used by all decode rows together in one layer during one decode step; it decides how much expert weight data the step must read.
_Avoid_: unique experts, expert coverage

## Models

**MobileMoE-S**:
Meta's smallest on-device mixture-of-experts model (about 1.3B parameters in total, about 272M used per token), studied here in its SFT (full-precision) and QAT (int4) variants.

**Muse Spark**:
Meta's hosted model, and the Muse agent in round 1.

**Muse Wonder**:
Meta's most capable model family, in preview; its standard variant runs on Meta's Model API. The Muse agent in round 2.

**Muse Wonder Full**:
The higher-capability variant of Muse Wonder, available only in Muse Code with a subscription; not used in this project.

**Muse agent**:
The Meta model that chooses which pieces of the decode step to replace and writes their kernels, on the branch `muse-agent`: Muse Spark in round 1 and from round 3, Muse Wonder in round 2. It is never the model under study.
_Avoid_: Muse (alone), Meta agent

**Muse Code**:
Meta's own coding agent for the terminal; the only program in which the Muse agent does its work in this project.
_Avoid_: Muse CLI, Meta Code

**Muse agent session**:
A Muse Code session in which the Muse agent writes every turn, the lead's and every helper's, kept apart from Claude's work by its own branch, folder and commit trailer.
_Avoid_: Muse Spark session (round 2's model was Muse Wonder), guardrail (for the session itself), Meta mode

## The Muse agent's work

**Slot**:
One replaceable piece of the mixture-of-experts block (routing, combine, or the routed experts), with fixed inputs and outputs, that the Muse agent may replace with its own kernels.
_Avoid_: target (that is a slot the Muse agent has chosen), module

**Round**:
One Muse agent session in which a swarm explores and then builds, writing in its own round folder, followed by Claude's independent measurement of what it produced. Once a round is finished, its files are frozen.
_Avoid_: iteration, cycle

**Round folder**:
Where one round writes all its files: round 1 at the top of `muse-spark/`, each later round in `muse-spark/round-<N>/`.

**Starting point**:
The plan each round from round 2 on begins with, drawn from the earlier rounds and Claude's measurement: each slot's baseline, or the attempt to start from where it has none, with its end-to-end effect; what is left to build; the refuted claims; and the territories to explore again.
_Avoid_: recap, retrospective

**Improvement**:
An attempt that is faster than its bar in one phase, prefill or decode, and slower in neither; a faster decode step bought with a slower prefill is not one.
_Avoid_: speedup (for a change measured in one phase only)

**Hand-off**:
An attempt's choice to run the compiled reference instead of its own kernels above a row count it names, so prefill-sized inputs stay on MLX's code.
_Avoid_: fallback

**Baseline** (of a slot):
A slot's best attempt so far that passes the current G2 and that Claude's G3 accepted, named in Claude's measurement of the previous round; every new attempt for that slot must beat it in the same grader run. A slot may have none.
_Avoid_: reference (that is the original MLX code and its compiled version)

**Swarm**:
All the agents of one round, the lead and its helpers, working toward one goal through shared documents that each of them reads and adds to.
_Avoid_: team, crew

**Lead agent**:
The one agent of a swarm that starts the helpers, keeps the shared documents current, settles clashes and commits; it neither explores nor grades.
_Avoid_: orchestrator, main agent

**Helper agent**:
An agent the lead starts: an explorer, the verifier, a builder or a boundary agent. It reports back and never commits.
_Avoid_: worker, subagent (when the role matters, not the mechanism)

**Reminder agent**:
One of Muse Code's own background agents, which watch the lead's progress and may nudge it, for example to check a claim before it says it is done; the Muse agent's model writes their turns too, but they take no part in the work.
_Avoid_: helper (that is one the lead starts)

**Exploration phase**:
The first part of a round, in which explorers map the code and the measurements and find where the decode step loses time.

**Implementation phase**:
The second part of a round, in which builders write and grade solutions to the confirmed inefficiencies.
_Avoid_: hypothesis phase

**Territory**:
The part of the code or the measurements that one explorer covers: a module, a single important file, or a measurement document.
_Avoid_: area, lens

**Analysis**:
The swarm's shared account of the code, written during exploration: the context, how the territories feed each other, and the ranked inefficiencies, each with its cost and sources.
_Avoid_: diagnosis, findings (those are Claude's)

**Inefficiency**:
One cause of lost time in the decode step: where it is in the code, what it costs, and what removing it should save. It is confirmed or refuted against its sources before anyone builds on it.
_Avoid_: issue, bottleneck (that is the single largest cause)

**Hypothesis**:
A proposed solution to one inefficiency: the slot it replaces, the boundary it keeps and the saving it predicts, tested by competing attempts.
_Avoid_: strategy, plan

**Boundary**:
What a solution must keep identical so that the steps before and after its slot work exactly as before: the slot's inputs and outputs, their dtypes, and the rounding points.
_Avoid_: interface (unqualified), contract

**Attempt**:
One grader run of a solution a builder wrote, committed by the lead; attempts for a slot are numbered in order within each round and have no limit.
_Avoid_: try, submission, draft

4. **Builders compete.** Two or three builders each take a different direction from the analysis, for example fusing kernels, reading each weight byte once, or a different threadgroup shape. Each builder:
   1. claims the next attempt number with `mkdir`, which fails if another builder took it first;
   2. writes the kernels and a `notes.md` with the cause it removes and its predicted time per layer;
   3. grades the attempt with the grader. The GPU lock queues runs, so two gradings never overlap and the timings stay clean;
   4. records G1, G2 and its timings at the six sizes against the original and the compiled reference;
   5. if the attempt failed or missed its prediction by more than 20%, finds out why and adds the answer to the analysis.
5. **Commit and check.** When a builder returns, the lead commits its attempt as the next implementation version. The boundary agent then checks every attempt that passed G2 for what the grader can't see: other row counts, threadgroup memory read before it is written, and results that depend on thread timing.
6. **Harden or close.**
   - **Harden:** if the best attempt still has a cause that can be named and removed, a builder makes its next single change.
   - **Ready:** once it passes G1, G2 and its boundary check, and beats the compiled reference and any baseline in both phases (faster in decode or prefill, slower in neither; [ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)), the hypothesis is `ready`. Its Decision states what G3 should show.
   - **Dropped:** a hypothesis that doesn't pay off is `dropped`, with the reason.
7. **Next, and finish.**
   - Then comes the next-ranked inefficiency. There is no attempt limit; the lead ends the phase when it judges no remaining inefficiency will pay, and says why.
===
**Improvement**:
An attempt that is faster than its bar in one phase, prefill or decode, and slower in neither; a faster decode step bought with a slower prefill is not one.
_Avoid_: speedup (for a change measured in one phase only)

**Hand-off**:
An attempt's choice to run the compiled reference instead of its own kernels above a row count it names, so prefill-sized inputs stay on MLX's code.
_Avoid_: fallback

**Baseline** (of a slot):
A slot's best attempt so far that passes the current G2 and that Claude's G3 accepted, named in Claude's measurement of the previous round; every new attempt for that slot must beat it in the same grader run. A slot may have none.
_Avoid_: reference (that is the original MLX code and its compiled version)

===
**Attempt**:
One grader run of a solution a builder wrote, committed by the lead; attempts for a slot are numbered in order within each round and have no limit.
_Avoid_: try, submission, draft
===

# attempt-1 (round 2): branched fused experts, 512 threads/pair (builder-1-b)

Direction (b) on starting point `muse-spark/kernels/experts/attempt-4`
(baseline `none` — no earlier attempt passes the current G2). One fused
kernel, one threadgroup per (row, expert-slot) pair, branched in-Metal
on `rows >= 60` (`x_shape[0]`, the `gather_qmm_rhs` dispatch threshold,
not the grader's bracketing sizes):

- **Decode (`rows < 60`):** attempt-4's qvm arithmetic unchanged —
  `qvm_block` copied verbatim (strided lanes `k ≡ lane (mod 32)`,
  float32 dequant `x·(scale·q+bias)`, `simd_sum`), so every block's
  accumulation order is identical. The one change is width: 512
  threads/pair (16 simdgroups) instead of 256, so gate/up run their 12
  blocks in 1 wave (was 2) and down its 24 blocks in 2 waves (was 3):
  4 simd waves instead of 7, more blocks in flight per call. This is
  the ineff-baseline-experts-2 fix (1-row chained latency): at 1 row
  the call still has only 4 threadgroups, but each now keeps up to 16
  blocks in flight instead of 8.
- **Prefill (`rows >= 60`):** per-pair path with `gather_qmm_rhs`
  arithmetic — each weight dequantized to bfloat16 first
  (`bfloat(scale·q+bias)`, `qmm_accum` in block-1) and K accumulated
  contiguously in BK=32 tile order by a single thread per output (one
  output per lane, no `simd_sum`), mimicking BlockMMA's sequential
  tile order. Same silu (full-bfloat16, attempt-4's) and the same four
  bfloat16 rounding points (gate, up, hidden, down).

Removes: ineff-baseline-experts-1 (the G2 gate — the branch supplies
the prefill arithmetic attempt-4 lacks) and attacks
ineff-baseline-experts-2 (1-row latency) without touching any block's
`simd_sum` order. ineff-baseline-experts-3 (per-pair re-reads) is
deliberately kept — round-1 evidence says grouped reads lose at this
duty cycle; per-pair reads at/above 60 rows are correctness-only cost
(prefill is untimed).

Limits: 512 threads/group ≤ 1,024; threadgroup memory unchanged at
3,840 B (tg_x 768 + tg_gate/up/h 384×3 bfloat16) ≤ 32 KB. Valid at
every `rows` (grid `rows*2048` threads = `rows*4` groups of 512; the
branch is on the same `rows` the grid is built from).
