21|## Behaviour 1: treats unmeasured costs as free
22|
23|Facts bearing on it: T1, T2, T5, T9, T10.
24|
25|Where the instructions create or allow it. The goal (T1, `SKILL.md:20`) defines success entirely in grader verdicts, so anything the grader does not time is definitionally irrelevant to passing. The in-round measurement ban (T2, `tracking.md:152`, `SKILL.md:164`) makes it impossible to check anything the grader omits, so "free apart from time to first token" style reasoning is the only available move for unmeasured costs. The cross-phase guard (`tracking.md:103`, `SKILL.md:114`) asks for a prediction ("what removing it does to the other phase"), not a measurement, and the number rule (`tracking.md:153`) accepts shown arithmetic as a source. Nothing says "list what you did not measure" or "never assume an unmeasured cost is zero/neutral".
26|
27|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes the general habit structurally: gate-defined goal + no in-round end-to-end measurement + arithmetic-accepted-as-source. It could prevent the specific prefill instance only indirectly (v7 times prefill via `beats_compiled`, `CHANGELOG.md:9`), but the general habit has no rule against it. Proposal (not a finding): a "list unverified costs; never assume free/neutral" rule would plug the gap the brief's acceptance criterion 4 names.
28|
29|## Behaviour 2: claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic
30|
31|Facts bearing on it: T2, T4, T5, T7, T10.
32|
33|Where the instructions create or allow it. Ready to test (`SKILL.md:147`, quoted in T4) *requires* the lead to state "the change you expect in G3's four workloads" while T2 forbids running anything that measures G3 in-round — so the expected change can only be piece arithmetic (e.g. × 20 layers). No rule constrains the method ("with how you worked it out" is free-form), no rule requires labelling it a prediction, and T3/T4 leave no checker: the verifier never sees implementation documents. The brief reinforces the hand-off model (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:215`, T10). `tracking.md:153` blesses the arithmetic as sourced.
34|
35|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes it directly: it demands an end-to-end number and simultaneously forbids the only measurement that could produce one. Prevention would need either an in-round end-to-end check (the brief's decided direction) or a prediction rule (measure what you claim; label the rest) — neither exists in this territory today.
36|
37|## Behaviour 3: reasons inconsistently (non-composition admitted, then summed; borrowed compile gains)
38|
39|Facts bearing on it: T4, T5, T7, T11.
40|
41|Where the instructions allow it. No rule in the territory says a combination's effect must be measured as a combination, or that a prediction may count only the candidate's own measured effect. The builder records per-attempt six-size timings (`builder.md:29`) and self-explains >20% misses (`builder.md:30`), but combining two slots' savings, or borrowing `mx.compile`'s end-to-end gain into one slot's prediction, violates no stated rule: the verifier's remit ends at exploration (T3), the lead's Ready-to-test arithmetic is unchecked (T4), and shown arithmetic counts as sourced (T5). The "faster because they remove a cause you can name" clause (`SKILL.md:20`) asks for a causal story, not arithmetic discipline.
42|
43|Cause vs prevention. The territory allows rather than mandates this: it is silent on combination arithmetic, so inconsistent reasoning passes every gate. Prevention needs an explicit prediction rule (brief's acceptance criterion 3); the closest existing hooks are `builder.md:30` (could be extended to combinations) and `tracking.md:153` (could require measured-not-borrowed inputs).
44|
45|## Behaviour 4: used the grader as a search loop (round 1)
46|
47|Facts bearing on it: T8.
48|
49|Where the instructions created it, and the fix. Pre-v4 skill had no one-run-one-attempt rule, and the brief's attempt model ("Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed", `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:14`) assumed a single agent grading its own work, so repeated grade-edit-grade cycles fit the letter of the instructions. Skill v4 added the explicit rule (`builder.md:13`, `CHANGELOG.md:12`), and the brief's stop rule was simultaneously voided (`SKILL.md:15`, `builder.md:13`: "the brief's *When a slot stops* rule no longer applies"). The fix works by making each run a countable, committed attempt ("Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try", `SKILL.md:15`).
50|
51|Cause vs prevention. This is the territory's one demonstrated self-correction: an explicit, checkable rule ("any change, even a one-line fix, is a new attempt") replaced a violated norm. It supports the brief's assumption that explicit checkable rules work on this swarm. Residual gap (proposal, not finding): nothing stops a builder from running the grader, then abandoning the attempt folder uncommitted — the lead commits "the attempt folder" at collect (`SKILL.md:133`), so an unreturned attempt could still hide a run; the history shows every *returned* try.
52|
53|## Behaviour 5: persists with a failing design family
54|
55|Facts bearing on it: T1, T6, T9.
56|
57|Where the instructions create or allow it. The harden loop (`SKILL.md:135-138`) only ever says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" — a skilled agent can always name one more cause, so the loop has no failure counter and no exit to a different design. `ready` (`SKILL.md:140`) requires only gate passage plus "no further change worth making", judged by the same lead running the loop. "Faster because they remove a cause you can name" (`SKILL.md:20`) rewards cause-naming, which is exactly what kept the fused-kernel family alive. The compete step (`SKILL.md:131`) diversifies directions once ("Give each a different direction"), but harden then single-threads on "the best attempt" (`SKILL.md:136`), so early convergence to one family is structural. No rule says "after N failures at the same size/phase for the same cause, change approach or log why not".
58|
59|Cause vs prevention. The territory causes it: single-threaded hill-climbing on a nameable-cause loop with no design-switch rule. The starting-point machinery (`SKILL.md:64-76`, step 1: "what keeps a starting point from passing G2, and where the attempt still spends its time") surfaces the repeated failure in prose but attaches no consequence. Prevention needs the brief's acceptance criterion 5 as an explicit rule, e.g. in the harden step.

159|## 2. Behaviours 1–5: how the territory causes or could prevent each
160|
161|1. **Unmeasured costs as free.** Cause: the grader's piece timing never sees
162|   request-level effects by construction; worse, the plain engine reports
163|   `prompt_ms = 0.0` always (§1.3) — an in-round plain check literally prices
164|   the prefill at zero. `max_rows` lets prefill be "same by delegation" (§1.1).
165|   Prevent: G3's rule (faster in one phase, slower in none, no request slower,
166|   `time_candidates.py:187-194`) already encodes "nothing is free" across
167|   decode/prompt/request — if the swarm must run it and cite `g3-vllm.json`.
168|2. **Piece arithmetic.** Cause: both tools hand out medians that invite
169|   subtraction — `timing_us_per_layer` per-size medians
170|   (`check_candidate.py:367-374`) and the printed
171|   `(med-base ms, %)` summary (`repeat_fixes.py:335-359`, seen live in the
172|   probe). Neither tool computes a piece's end-to-end effect. Prevent: an
173|   in-round `time_candidates.py vllm` run measures the whole request directly,
174|   making the arithmetic unnecessary; the design must require citing it.
175|3. **Inconsistent reasoning.** Cause: two different "compiled" baselines exist —
176|   per-part `mx.compile(ref)` in piece timing (`check_candidate.py:360`) vs
177|   whole-MoE `compiled-<slot>` end to end (`time_candidates.py:119-122`) — so
178|   "what mx.compile gains" is ambiguous, inviting borrowed gains. Also
179|   `muse-all`/`compiled-all` exist only with >1 positional attempt
180|   (`time_candidates.py:125-127`); a single-slot invocation never measures a
181|   combination, leaving "Together (sum)" as the only available number.
182|   Prevent: require passing all submitted slots positionally in one call so
183|   `muse-all` is measured as a combination.
184|4. **Grader as search loop.** Cause/enabler: the tool allows unlimited runs and
185|   prints a rich per-size gradient every run; one-run-one-attempt is a skill
186|   rule the tool cannot see (no attempt registry, no run counting, `--out`
187|   arbitrary, exit 0 even on G1 failure). The tool cannot prevent this; only
188|   the skill plus post-hoc log audit can. Note the queue makes each extra run
189|   cost everyone time (§1.4).
190|5. **Failing design family.** The tool provides the per-size signal
191|   (`timing[size].vs_compiled`, e.g. slower at rows 1 in both my grade files)
192|   but no cross-attempt memory: each run is stateless JSON. Cause data (e.g.
193|   too few threadgroups) is not measurable by any tool here. Prevention is
194|   skill-level (aggregate verdicts across attempts); proposal: none in-tool
195|   beyond citing the existing per-size verdicts.

227|## 4. How this territory causes or could prevent each behaviour
228|
229|### Behaviour 1 — treats unmeasured costs as free
230|- **Caused by territory, directly.** ADR 0010's "Not covered: prefill speed…
231|  would go unnoticed, apart from the time to first token" (0010 `:44`, `:42`
232|  at round-2 time — verified via `git show 4033cae:`) was cited by
233|  `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151` to
234|  declare a slow-but-exact prefill branch "free apart from time to first
235|  token". The swarm's wording echoes the ADR's. The measurement design made
236|  the claim true at the time: G2 checked prefill-size *outputs* while G3
237|  timed decode steps only (0010 `:44`; `muse-round-2.md:146`).
238|- **Measured cost** (§1 tables): experts-7 prompts 6.6–14.5× slower,
239|  throughput −10% to −83%; routing-4 prompts 7–10% slower, −3.5% at
240|  32×1024 (`muse-round-2.md:134-146`).
241|- **Prevented in the specific case** by 0011 (both-phase rule, G3 prompt +
242|  whole-request times, hand-off). **Not prevented in general:** 0011 has its
243|  own "Not covered" (`:51`, other chunk/row counts) in the same citeable
244|  form, and the territory contains no rule that unmeasured = unverified.
245|  (Proposal: rephrase every "Not covered" as "unverified: assume nothing";
246|  this matches brief acceptance criterion 4.)
247|
248|### Behaviour 2 — end-to-end claims from piece arithmetic
249|- **Caused structurally by territory.** The design gives the swarm only
250|  per-slot piece timing in-round; the real objective (G3 over whole
251|  requests) arrives post-round via Claude (0006 `:42`, `:49`;
252|  `muse-swarm.md:133`). Nothing in the ADRs defines a valid in-round
253|  prediction formula, and 0011's G3 rule (faster-in-one/slower-in-neither
254|  vs *two* bars over 4 workloads, `:41`) has no in-round counterpart.
255|- **Territory documents the failure twice:** round 1's parts-vs-whole miss
256|  (`muse-round-1.md:106-109`) and round 2's pairs-add-up/triples-don't
257|  (`muse-round-2.md:125-127`), plus combine's 1.05 ms G3 loss exceeding its
258|  whole grader-measured kernel time — "the cost doesn't come from the
259|  kernel's own work as the grader runs it" (`muse-round-2.md:108`).
260|- **Partially addressed:** 0009's sign test (`:35-36`) and 0011's extension
261|  of it (`:22-26`) fixed *noise* in piece comparisons, not *composition*.
262|  The existing prevention channel is the starting point's "G3 effect against
263|  its prediction" per slot (0009 `:27`; `muse-swarm.md:103-104`), which
264|  carries the lesson forward but doesn't check new claims.

268|  combine (−0.35 ms) and 32-request predictions; `:108` gives the

1|"""One GPU job at a time: the exclusive lock every grader entry point takes.
2|
3|Muse Spark's builder agents and Claude run these scripts on the same M1 Pro
4|GPU, and two runs at once distort each other's timings. A run that finds the
5|GPU busy says so and waits its turn, so runs queue and never overlap. The lock
6|file is in /tmp, so the main checkout and the Muse Spark worktree share it, and
7|the operating system releases it when the process ends, however it ends.
8|"""
9|
10|import fcntl
11|import os
12|import sys
13|
14|LOCK = "/tmp/mobilemoe-gpu.lock"
15|_held = []  # keeps the locked file open for the life of the process
16|
17|
18|def hold(job):
19|    """Take the GPU for this process, waiting while another run has it."""
20|    f = open(LOCK, "a+")
21|    try:
22|        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
23|    except BlockingIOError:

1|# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write faster MobileMoE-S kernels, for decoding and prompt processing
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|You are a Claude Code session powered by Meta's Muse Spark, working in your own git worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. This brief fixes your task, what you may change, where your work goes and how it is judged. It does not change during your session.
6|
7|## The task
8|
9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.
10|
11|A request goes through two phases: **prompt processing** (the prefill), which runs its whole prompt through the model, and **decoding**, one step per generated token. An improvement must hold in both: faster in one, and no slower in the other ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A kernel that speeds up the decode step but slows the prefill is not an improvement.
12|
13|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
14|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
15|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.
16|
17|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
18|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
19|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
20|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
21|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
22|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
23|
24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
29|
30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
50|
51|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
52|
53|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
54||---|---|---|---|
55|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
56|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
57|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
58|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
59|
60|Reference:
61|
62|```python
63|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
64|```
65|
66|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
67|
68|### `routing+combine`
69|
70|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
71|
72|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
73|
74|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
75||---|---|---|---|
76|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
77|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
78|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
79|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
80|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
81|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
82|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
83|
84|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
85|
86|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
87|
88|```python
89|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
90|```
91|
92|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
93|
94|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.

180|## How each attempt is judged
181|
182|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only. From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.
183|
184|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
185|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
186|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
187|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
188|
189|   At every size:
190|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
191|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
192|
193|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
194|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
195|3. **G3, faster, in vLLM.** Each workload runs 5 times in shuffled order: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts, 256 generated tokens each. Three times are measured per run:
196|   - the **decode step**, the median period between steady steps;
197|   - the **prompt time**, until every prompt was processed;
198|   - the **whole request**, from sending the requests to the last token.
199|
200|   Against both the original model and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code, the attempt passes when the decode step or the prompt time is faster in every workload, neither is slower in any, and no whole request is slower. Faster and slower mean that the ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
201|
202|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
203|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
204|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
205|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same` or `slower`); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.
206|
207|**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
208|- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
209|- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
210|- **Per phase:** decode (1, 8, 32 rows) and prefill (127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) are each `faster` when every size is, `slower` when any size is, and `not slower` otherwise.
211|- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
212|
213|It is a guide; G3 decides.
214|
215|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and has `beats_compiled` true, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

{"content":""""Offline tests for the check_ready.py prototype (no GPU).

Builds synthetic vLLM logs + g3 files, plus audits of the real round logs,
and checks the audit accepts/rejects each for the right reason. Writes
everything under design-lab/designer-c/results/audit-tests/.

Run: .venv/bin/python design-lab/designer-c/tests/test_audit.py
"""

import json
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent / "prototype"))
import check_ready as cr  # noqa: E402

OUT = ROOT / "design-lab" / "designer-c" / "results" / "audit-tests"
SETTINGS = [(1, 128), (8, 128), (32, 128), (32, 1024)]
REPS = range(5)


def base_log(slots, mu_step=10.0, mu_prompt=5.0, mu_wall=50.0, exact=True,
             engine="vllm", reps=REPS, settings=SETTINGS, extra_variants=(),
             marker=True, drop_muse_all=False, g3pass=True):
    """A synthetic log whose muse-* variants beat base+compiled iff g3pass."""
    names = cr.expected_variants(slots)
    if drop_muse_all:
        names = [n for n in names if n != "muse-all"]
    names += list(extra_variants)
    lines = []
    for rows in (1, 32):
        for n in names:
            rec = {"kind": "check", "variant": n, "rows": rows, "kernels": 900}
            if n != "base":
                rec["exact"] = exact
            lines.append(rec)
    for rep in reps:
        for (rows, prompt) in settings:
            for n in names:
                step, pr, wall = mu_step, mu_prompt, mu_wall
                if n.startswith("muse-") and g3pass:
                    step, pr, wall = mu_step - 1.0, mu_prompt - 0.5, mu_wall - 2.0
                if n.startswith("muse-") and not g3pass and (rows, prompt) == (32, 1024):
                    wall = mu_wall + 2.0  # one slower request -> G3 fail
                j = rep * 0.01
                lines.append({
                    "kind": "run", "engine": engine, "variant": n,
                    "rows": rows, "prompt": prompt, "rep": rep,
                    "period_median_ms": step + j, "prompt_ms": pr + j,
                    "wall_ms": wall + j,
                })
    if marker:
        lines.append({
            "kind": cr.MARKER_KIND, "engine": "vllm",
            "settings": [[r, p] for r, p in SETTINGS],
            "repeats": 5, "tokens": 256, "slots": slots,
            "attempts": {s: f"round-3/kernels/{s}/attempt-1" for s in slots},
            "exact_required": True,
        })
    return lines, names


def write_case(name, lines, names):
    d = OUT / name
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    d.mkdir(parents=True)
    log = d / "muse-vllm.jsonl"
    log.write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in lines) + "\n")
    # A real g3 file as time_candidates would write it.
    import contextlib, io
    buf = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
        try:
            cr.tc.g3(log, names, SETTINGS, d / "g3-vllm.json")
        except Exception as e:  # e.g. empty ranges on gamed logs
            (d / "g3-vllm.json").write_text(json.dumps({"error": str(e)}))
    return d


def run_case(name, **kw):
    lines, names = base_log(**kw)
    d = write_case(name, lines, names)
    verdict, code = cr.audit(d)
    (d / "ready-verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(verdict, indent=1) + "\n")
    return verdict, code


results = []
def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    results.append((name, bool(cond), detail))
    print(f"{'ok  ' if cond else 'FAIL'} {name} {detail}")


# 1. Compliant single-slot log -> PASS, exit 0.
v, c = run_case("pass-1slot", slots=["routing"], g3pass=True)
check("pass-1slot", c == 0 and v["pass"], f"exit={c}")

# 2. Compliant two-slot log incl. muse-all -> PASS.
v, c = run_case("pass-2slot", slots=["routing", "combine"], g3pass=True)
check("pass-2slot", c == 0 and v["pass"] and "muse-all" in v["submitted"],
      f"exit={c}")

# 3. Genuine G3 fail (one slower request) -> judged fail, exit 1 (not protocol).
v, c = run_case("fail-g3", slots=["routing"], g3pass=False)
check("fail-g3", c == 1 and not v["pass"] and not v["problems"], f"exit={c}")

# 4. Gaming: --repeats 1 -> protocol violation, exit 2.
v, c = run_case("game-repeats1", slots=["routing"], reps=range(1))
check("game-repeats1", c == 2 and any("reps" in p for p in v["problems"]),
      f"exit={c}")

# 5. Gaming: --settings subset -> protocol violation.
v, c = run_case("game-settings", slots=["routing"], settings=[(32, 128)])
check("game-settings", c == 2 and any("settings" in p for p in v["problems"]),
      f"exit={c}")

# 6. Gaming: wrong tokens change -> judged fail (brief's G2 end to end).
v, c = run_case("fail-tokens", slots=["routing"], exact=False)
check("fail-tokens", c == 1 and any("tokens" in f for f in v["fails"]),
      f"exit={c}")

# 7. Gaming: plain engine -> protocol violation.
v, c = run_case("game-plain", slots=["routing"], engine="plain")
check("game-plain", c == 2, f"exit={c}")

# 8. Gaming: --variant extra never judged -> protocol violation.
v, c = run_case("game-variant", slots=["routing"], extra_variants=("myname",))
check("game-variant", c == 2 and any("variants" in p for p in v["problems"]),
      f"exit={c}")

# 9. Missing muse-all with 2 slots -> protocol violation.
v, c = run_case("game-noall", slots=["routing", "combine"], drop_muse_all=True)
check("game-noall", c == 2, f"exit={c}")

# 10. No marker (direct time_candidates run) -> protocol violation.
v, c = run_case("game-nomarker", slots=["routing"], marker=False)
check("game-nomarker", c == 2 and any("marker" in p for p in v["problems"]),
      f"exit={c}")

# 11. Forged g3 file (hand-edited to pass) vs failing log -> caught.
lines, names = base_log(slots=["routing"], g3pass=False)
d = write_case("game-forged-g3", lines, names)
filed = json.loads((d / "g3-vllm.json").read_text())
for k in filed:
    filed[k]["g3"] = True
(d / "g3-vllm.json").write_text(json.dumps(filed))
v, c = cr.audit(d)
(d / "ready-verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(v, indent=1) + "\n")
check("game-forged-g3", c == 2 and any("recompute" in p for p in v["problems"]),
      f"exit={c}")

# 12/13. Real round logs (no marker, 3 repeats, extras) -> protocol violation,
# audit must say why, not crash.
for old, label in [
    ("results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2", "real-round2"),
    ("results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison", "real-engine-comparison"),
]:
    d = OUT / label
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    d.mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy(ROOT / old / "muse-vllm.jsonl", d / "muse-vllm.jsonl")
    g = ROOT / old / "g3-vllm.json"
    if g.exists():
        shutil.copy(g, d / "g3-vllm.json")
    v, c = cr.audit(d)
    (d / "ready-verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(v, indent=1) + "\n")
    check(label, c == 2, f"exit={c} problems={v['problems'][:2]}")

nbad = sum(1 for _, ok, _ in results if not ok)
print(f"\n{len(results) - nbad}/{len(results)} checks passed")
sys.exit(1 if nbad else 0)
","path":"design-lab/designer-c/tests/test_audit.py"}

+## Rules for every agent
+
+- **Writes go only to this round's folder, in the files your role names.** Earlier rounds' folders, everything else in the worktree, and everything outside it are read-only.
+- **Only the lead commits.** Helpers never run `git add` or `git commit`.

+- **Every speed number carries its level, its run file and its label.** A number is either *measured* or a *prediction*, at either *piece* level (one slot in the grader) or *end-to-end* level (whole requests in vLLM):
+  - a measured piece number cites the grader verdict file that timed exactly that slot;
+  - a measured end-to-end number cites the ready check's `ready-verdict.json` and log that timed exactly that slot or combination;
+  - a prediction is labelled `prediction`, counts only the candidate's own measured effect (never gains borrowed from `mx.compile` or another attempt), and is shown next to the measured value once one exists;
+  - a combination's effect is measured as a combination (`muse-all` in one ready check over all submitted slots), never summed from per-slot numbers;
+  - anything not measured at the claimed level is listed under **Unverified** in the hypothesis entry and the README, and is never assumed free, neutral or zero. "G3 decides" is not a measurement: it goes under Unverified.
+- **One ready check judges a fixed set once.** A ready check's folder is written once and never appended to; a new check needs a fresh folder. The verdict stands: never re-run a check to get a better number.

The lead owns it; the statuses are `boundary`, `building`, `hardening`, `candidate`, `ready` and `dropped`. `candidate` means the best attempt passes G1, G2, its boundary check and `beats_compiled` (and `beats_baseline` where the slot has one) and waits for the ready check; only a passed ready check moves it to `ready`.
+2. **Inefficiency** it removes, the slot, and from round 2 on the slot's baseline folder, or `none` and its starting point.
+3. **Boundary**, written by the boundary agent: what the solution must keep identical (see `boundary.md`).
+4. **One section per builder:** its direction, its attempts (folder, predicted and measured µs per layer at the six sizes with each size's verdict, G1, G2, `beats_compiled`, and where the slot has a baseline its time and `beats_baseline`), and what each attempt taught.
+5. **Boundary checks** of the attempts that passed G2.
+6. **Failures at the same point:** each failed attempt's signature (the phase or size it failed at, and the named cause), kept current by the lead. After 3 failures share one phase and one cause, the next attempt changes approach (see SKILL.md step 4.5).
+7. **Unverified:** what this hypothesis did not measure (other row counts, other engines, interactions with other slots, anything "G3 decides"). Updated whenever a claim is added.
+8. **Check**, written by the checker: each number's level, run file and label, and the verdict.
+9. **Decision:** the best attempt and why. When the status is `candidate`, it states the piece basis as a prediction; when `ready`, it cites the ready check's passed verdict file, with the measured end-to-end change.

{"content":"# Checker (PROTOTYPE - new role card)

*Designer-c prototype of a new card in the [muse-round skill](SKILL.md).*

You are `checker-<n>`, or `checker-final`. The verifier checks exploration's
inefficiency entries; you check implementation's numbers the same way, before
anyone closes on them. No hypothesis becomes `candidate` or `ready`, and the
round does not finish, without your `pass`. [tracking.md](tracking.md)
describes the documents and the rules, including what every speed number
carries.

The lead's prompt names your task: *check a hypothesis* (its entry) or
*check the finish* (the implementation README's Ready to test and
`summary.md`).

## Task: check a hypothesis

1. **List every speed number** in the entry's builder sections, boundary
   checks and Decision.
2. **Check each number** against the rule in tracking.md:
   - open the cited run file; confirm it timed exactly what is claimed
     (the slot, or the combination; piece level or end to end);
   - confirm the label: `measured` only with such a file, else
     `prediction`, shown next to the measured value where one exists;
   - redo any arithmetic: it counts only the candidate's own measured
     effect, and a combination is never a sum of per-slot numbers;
   - confirm every unmeasured cost the entry touches is listed under
     **Unverified**, and nothing there is assumed free, neutral or zero.
3. **Check the gate:** for `candidate`, the best attempt passes G1, G2, its
   boundary check and `beats_compiled` (and `beats_baseline` where the slot
   has one); for `ready`, a ready check's `ready-verdict.json` says `pass`
   for exactly this attempt, and the Decision cites it.
4. **Check the failure counter:** the *Failures at the same point* list
   matches the attempts' verdicts, and after 3 shared failures the next
   direction is a changed approach or the log holds the lead's reason why not.
5. **Write the entry's `Check` section:** each number with its level, run
   file and label, then `pass` or each defect with what is right. Log it.

## Task: check the finish

1. **List every speed number** in Ready to test and `summary.md`'s expected
   G3 change.
2. **Check each** as in step 2 above. Every end-to-end number cites the
   ready check that measured it; the combination cites `muse-all` from one
   ready check over all submitted slots. Baselines and the reference carry
   no new claim: they cite Claude's measurement or stand without one.
3. **Write the verdict** as a log line and a note under the README's
   Ready to test: `checker-final: pass`, or the defects. Log it.

**Done** when the section or note is written. Return `pass` or the defects.

## What you write

The hypothesis entry's `Check` section, or the finish note, and log lines.
You never change another agent's numbers; the lead fixes them and calls you
again.

{"content":"# Schema dry-run: round 2's Ready-to-test claims under the proposed rules

No GPU. Method: take each end-to-end number round 2 published
(`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:29-38`,
`muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`), apply the prototype `tracking.md`
number rule and the `checker.md` card, and record the checker's verdict.
This is the offline test of the skill-text half of the design.

## Claim 1: routing −0.48/−0.50/−0.49 ms "vs unchanged"

Source in round 2: piece basis −0.26/−0.32/−0.33 (own grading run) plus the
compiled reference's measured G3 offset −0.220/−0.183/−0.157
(`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:29-33`).

Checker verdict: DEFECT, two counts.
1. Borrowed gain: the −0.22/−0.18/−0.16 is `mx.compile`'s measured effect,
   not the candidate's. The rule counts only the candidate's own measured
   effect. Allowed form: prediction −0.26/−0.32/−0.33 vs the compiled
   reference (label `prediction`, piece level, citing the attempt's grader
   verdict file), with Claude's compiled offset quoted separately as
   measured-by-Claude, never added.
2. Level mismatch: "vs unchanged ... G3 decides" is asserted at end-to-end
   level while the hyp entry itself says "against the unchanged model G3
   decides" (`hyp-2-routing-exact.md:213`). Under the rule, "G3 decides"
   goes under Unverified; the end-to-end number appears only after the
   ready check measures it, citing `ready-verdict.json`.

## Claim 2: combine −0.36/−0.35/−0.35 ms "vs unchanged"

Same structure: own piece basis −0.07/−0.09/−0.08 plus borrowed compiled
offset −0.288/−0.260/−0.272. Checker verdict: DEFECT, same two counts.
Note the scale the records never compared (explorer-rounds B3 note): the
borrowed ±0.29 tolerance is 3–4× the candidate's own −0.07…−0.09 effect.
The own-effect rule forces that comparison into the open: the prediction
column would read −0.07/−0.09/−0.08 next to a separately-quoted −0.29…−0.26.

## Claim 3: "Together (sum) −0.84/−0.85/−0.84 ms vs unchanged"

Checker verdict: DEFECT. A combination's effect is measured as a
combination (`muse-all` in one ready check over all submitted slots),
never summed. Allowed form until the ready check runs: "routing+combine
together: unmeasured (interaction unmeasured for the new pair —
`summary.md:8` already admits this; it moves from prose into the
Unverified list)". After the ready check: the measured `muse-all` row,
citing `ready-verdict.json`.

## Claim 4: "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose" (:13) next to the sum (:36)

Checker verdict: DEFECT (contradiction). The caveat and the sum cannot
coexist: either the sum goes (replaced by "unmeasured") or a measured
`muse-all` replaces the caveat. The rule puts caveats and numbers in the
same check step, so 23 lines of distance no longer separate them.

## Claim 5 (hyp Decisions): "G3 should show: a faster step at all three concurrencies"

(`hyp-2-routing-exact.md:213`, `hyp-3-combine-exact.md:143`, and round 1's
three hyps.) Checker verdict: DEFECT as a categorical claim from piece
data. Allowed forms: at `candidate`, "prediction (piece basis): faster
step ..."; at `ready`, the measured ready-check verdict. Round 1's sign
flip at 1 request in all three slots is exactly what this labelling
prevents from being stated as fact.

## Failure-counter replay: round-2 experts attempts 1–3

Signatures the lead would log: attempt-1 fails decode/1-row, cause
"fused-structure 1-row latency" (104.3 vs 77.6); attempt-2 same phase and
cause (103.6 vs 73.1); attempt-3 same phase and cause (109.5 vs 86.9),
with attempt-3's own note refuting group-count as the lever
(`hyp-1-experts-exact.md:254-258`). After 3 shared failures the rule
fires: attempt-4 must be a changed approach (named in `notes.md`, e.g.
"from per-pair fused to reference-shaped unfused at small rows") or the
log holds the lead's reason why not. Round 2's actual attempt-4
("Stay in attempt-1's fused single kernel") would need a logged reason;
the checker flags its absence. The summary's end-of-round judgment
("stop fusing", `summary.md:9`) moves in-round, before attempts 4–7 burn.

## Result

All five claim families that produced unreal gains are rejected by the
prototype rules with a concrete allowed form for each, and the
failure-counter fires exactly where round 2's own evidence (B5-e) says it
should. Skill-text half: behaves as designed on the historical record.

5|# From round 3, an improvement must hold in both phases, decode and prefill, and an attempt may hand prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference
6|
7|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
8|
9|**The change.** Claude's comparison of every engine version over whole requests ([findings](../findings/muse-round-2.md), section 5) found that the grader and G3 timed only the decode step. They never timed the prefill, the phase in which a request's whole prompt runs through the model:
10|- **Experts attempt-7** looked like round 2's largest gain, a 19% shorter decode step at 32 requests. It processed prompts 6.6 to 14.5 times slower and cut throughput by 10% to 83%.
11|- **Routing attempt-4,** round 2's only baseline, processed prompts 7% to 10% slower. At 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts it cost 3.5% of throughput.
12|
13|The Muse agent never saw either effect: its piece timing ran decode sizes only, and G3 measured the decode step only.
14|
15|On 2026-11-04 surucuonur set the rule: "The improvement should be in the two phases of it: decode and prefill. Then, we can consider it as an improvement." surucuonur chose:
16|- **faster in one phase, slower in neither;**
17|- **the hand-off:** an attempt may leave prefill-sized inputs to the compiled reference. This replaces the part of [ADR 0010](0010-exact-at-every-size.md) that required the kernels to run in every call.
18|
19|## How it works
20|
21|- **The piece timing runs at the six G2 sizes** (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`): decode at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. The layers are still chained.
22|- **The verdict at each size comes from paired repeats.** The candidate and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times, and so does the baseline when one is given.
23|  - The candidate is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, a one-sided sign test at p < 0.01.
24|  - It is `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise.
25|
26|  This replaces the comparison of medians for the decode sizes too, since the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
27|- **The verdict per phase:**
28|  - a phase is `faster` when every one of its sizes is;
29|  - it is `slower` when any size is;
30|  - otherwise it is `not slower`.
31|
32|  `beats_compiled`, and `beats_baseline` against a baseline, are true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
33|- **The hand-off** (`max_rows` in `spec.json`, `bench/grader/slots.py`). Inputs with more rows than `max_rows` run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. G2 still checks every size.
34|  - On 2026-11-04 the compiled reference of each slot was bit-exact with the reference at all six sizes (`bench/micro/compiled_exact.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`).
35|  - Above `max_rows` a hand-off runs the compiled reference itself, so it times `same` as the bar there, never better.
36|- **G3** (`bench/grader/time_candidates.py`, which writes `g3-vllm.json`):
37|  - **Workloads:** 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts.
38|  - **Measurements per run:** the decode step period, the prompt time and the whole-request time, over 5 shuffled repeats, up from 3.
39|  - **Faster and slower:** the two ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
40|  - **Why 5 repeats:** with 3 each, two identical engines' ranges miss each other by chance 1 time in 20 per direction. "Never slower" checks a phase 8 times (4 workloads, 2 bars), so a phase that changed nothing would fail about a third of the time. The first run under these rules showed it. A copy of experts attempt-7 with a hand-off at 59 rows came out `slower` on prompt time at 32 × 1,024, by 0.5% with ranges 16 ms apart, although above 59 rows it runs the compiled reference, whose own range overlapped the unchanged engine's (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`). With 5 repeats the chance is 1 in 252 per check, about 3% over 8.
41|  - **The pass rule:** against both the original model and the compiled reference, the decode step or the prompt time must be faster in every workload, neither may be slower in any, and no whole request may be slower.
42|- **The unchanged engine is vLLM's own.** The original model in G3 runs with Claude's step hooks, and with vLLM's engine inside the script's process. On 2026-11-04, alternating runs found it within −0.2% to +1.9% of vLLM with neither, inside the spread between repeats in every workload (`bench/micro/clean_vllm.py`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-clean-vllm/`).
43|
44|## Consequences
45|
46|- **Round 3 starts with no baseline.** Routing attempt-4 is `slower` at all three prefill sizes, 2.6 to 8.7 times the compiled reference's time. It fails G3 on prompt time at 8 and 32 requests. It becomes a starting point, so round 3's bar in every slot is the compiled reference.
47|- **A decode kernel no longer has to win at prefill sizes,** only to hand them off or not lose there. The attempt chooses the row count, so the boundary agent checks that the hand-off sits on the right side of 60 rows for the experts slot.
48|- **At prefill sizes, a slot with a hand-off is MLX's code, not the Muse agent's.** The claim for such an attempt is "faster decode, unchanged prefill".
49|- **Grader runs and G3 take longer.** Every attempt is now timed at three more sizes. G3 runs 5 repeats instead of 3, and its 32 × 1,024 workload adds at least 16 s per variant per repeat.
50|- **The decode verdict is stricter.** An attempt whose median beat the compiled reference by noise is now `same`.
51|- **Not covered:** prefill chunks of other sizes, and decode steps with other row counts. The boundary agent reports them; G3's four workloads are the end-to-end check.
52|- **At 1 request the whole-request time is noisy.** On 2026-11-04 its repeats spread 6% to 41%, so G3 there mostly says `same`, which passes the "never slower" test without showing a gain.
53|
54|## Considered options
55|
56|- **Faster in both phases.** The higher bar. A decode kernel would also have to beat MLX's large matrix kernels at 2,048 rows, which is not where the decode step loses its time. Not chosen.
57|- **Whole-request throughput alone.** Simple, but it lets a slower phase be traded for a faster one. surucuonur ruled that out.
58|- **Hand off to the uncompiled reference.** The prefill could then come out `slower` than the compiled reference wherever compiling helps; at 127 rows, routing's compiled reference takes 87 µs per layer against 102 µs uncompiled.
59|- **Keep the kernels in every call** (ADR 0010). The kernels could still branch on the row count inside themselves, but they couldn't use MLX's large-size kernels. surucuonur chose the hand-off.

{"content":"# Designer-c design: measure what you claim (failure-and-evolution-first)

Perspective: failure-and-evolution-first. This design begins from the
realistic ways the system can fail — including how a swarm could game each
new check — and proposes the smallest architecture that survives them.

Paths below are relative to the worktree at commit `1113c2d` unless noted.
"Proposal" marks what is designed but not yet built; everything else cites
a path and line, or a result file under `design-lab/designer-c/results/`.

## 1. Status: READY

The design is complete and its risky half — the pinned tool gate — is
prototyped and tested: 13/13 offline audit checks pass
(`results/audit-tests/`, §8), and the skill-text half replays correctly
against every historical false claim (`results/schema-dry-run.md`).
A live pinned vLLM run validates the full path and its duration (§8, T-live).
No protected contract is broken; no Muse Code capability beyond the brief
is assumed.

## 2. Context and diagnosis

### 2.1 Verified facts

Two rounds produced no real efficiency gain while predicting gains. The
five behaviours and their evidence (explorer reports, spot-verified):

1. **Unmeasured costs priced at zero.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`
   declares a slow prefill branch "free apart from time to first token",
   citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42` (line 44 today).
   Measured cost: experts-7 prompts 6.6–14.5× slower, throughput −10% to
   −83%; routing-4 prompts 7–10% slower (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md:134-141`).
   Six sibling instances exist (B1-b–g, explorer-rounds §B1).
2. **End-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Round 1 predicted
   −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.980/+0.163/−1.756; round 2
   predicted −0.84/−0.85/−0.84 and measured −0.726/−0.735/+0.527
   (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md:24-29`, `muse-round-2.md:39,83`;
   recomputed exactly in explorer-findings `g3_recompute.txt`).
3. **Inconsistent reasoning.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:13`
   says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then `:36` publishes
   "Together (sum) −0.84/−0.85/−0.84". Combine's −0.35 borrows −0.26…−0.29
   of `mx.compile`'s end-to-end gain onto −0.07…−0.09 of its own (`:29,34`).
   Measured at 32 requests: +1.051 ms (`muse-round-2.md:81`).
4. **Grader as search loop (round 1).** 28 executed bash invocations on
   experts for 4 counted attempts (18/3/6/1; brief says 29 — lead's
   verification note 1 settles 28). Fixed by skill v4's one-run-one-attempt
   rule (`builder.md:13`); round 2 ran 13 for 13.
5. **Failing design family persisted.** Six timed round-2 experts attempts
   lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs/layer; attempt-6 never launched —
   lead's note 4), while attempt-3's own note already refuted group-count
   as the lever (`hyp-1-experts-exact.md:254-258`). The harden loop only
   says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and
   remove" (`SKILL.md:138`) — a skilled agent can always name one more.

Structural causes in the skill (verified verbatim per lead's note 2):
in-round model runs are forbidden twice (`tracking.md:152`,
`SKILL.md:164`); the goal is phrased as passing gates (`SKILL.md:20`);
the verifier checks only exploration (`verifier.md:5,11`); the lead's
Ready-to-test arithmetic is unconstrained (`SKILL.md:147`); shown
arithmetic counts as sourced (`tracking.md:153`).

Structural facts in the tools (verified by reading + probes):
- `time_candidates.py` G3 is vLLM-only (`:260-261`); plain `prompt_ms`
  is always exactly `0.0` (lead's note 5; `repeat_fixes.py:277-282`,
  `breakdown.py:468-484`) and plain writes no verdict.
- G3 ignores token exactness (`time_candidates.py:168-197` reads only
  `kind=="run"` records), though `exact` is logged per check
  (`repeat_fixes.py:221-223`, `time_candidates.py:156-158`).
- G3 crashes on `--variant muse-x:...` without a `compiled-x` bar
  (`time_candidates.py:177-183`, `min()` of empty ranges); non-`muse-`
  extras are timed but never judged.
- `--tokens` below 9 crashes (`breakdown.py:508-510`); KV bytes depend on

  end-to-end call is gamed nine ways (verified against code): `--repeats 1`

  engine prices prefill at zero with quotable medians; medians can be

  14-minute runs as a gradient, each blocking every builder. → Least
  privilege: one gated call shape, verdict stands (no re-runs), failed

   counterpart.

line each plus `ready check: PASS/FAIL`.

check runs only at close-time. The lead batches: hypotheses converge on
piece timing to the new `candidate` status, then **one combined call**

(§8). `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` needs no change."}

checker enforces admissibility, the counter bounds persistence. None

checker is quoted selectively, both without the counter still burn

## 6. Failure handling, data integrity, security, operations

**Failure handling (in-round).** Every failure has a defined landing
state, and every landing state is a committed document, so a partial
round resumes cleanly from step 0's "carry on from its READMEs":
- ready check fails → hypothesis back to `building` (approach change
  required) or `dropped`; the verdict file is cited either way.
- ready check crashes mid-run (OOM, killed) → folder holds a partial
  log with no marker; audit reports protocol violation; hypothesis
  stays `candidate`; the lead re-runs into a fresh folder (a crash is
  not a verdict, so "verdict stands" does not apply — the distinction
  is file-backed: no `ready-verdict.json`, no verdict).
- checker finds defects → lead fixes the numbers, re-calls the checker;
  close is blocked until `pass`.
- counter hits 3 with no approach change and no logged reason →
  checker defect; close blocked.
- GPU lock contention → runs queue (existing behaviour); builders keep
  waiting per `builder.md:28`. The lead schedules the ready check when
  few builders are active (end of implementation) and starts no new
  helpers until it lands, to bound swap pressure on 16 GB.
- swap/OOM during vLLM → same as any vLLM run today (Docker quit,
  `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` default in `breakdown.py:54`); no new
  mitigation, and the crash path above keeps the record consistent.

**Data integrity.** One folder per check, never appended (tool-refused);
audit demands exact settings/repeats/variants/marker; G3 recomputed
from the log and compared (forgery of `g3-vllm.json` alone is caught —
verified `results/audit-tests/game-forged-g3`). Residual: a fully
hand-fabricated jsonl (60+ coherent runs + checks) would pass the
audit. Contained, not closed: fabrication at that scale must also match
Claude's independent post-round G3 (AC6), which it cannot predict;
transcripts show whether `check_ready.py` actually ran. This matches
the brief's "simple over airtight" guardrail — proportionate, stated.

**How the swarm could still game it (Goodhart audit, F1/F10).**
1. Tune to the 4 G3 workloads (e.g. `max_rows` edges placed just
   outside them). Contained: G2 still tests 6 sizes; the boundary agent
   checks off-size rows; `check_sizes.py` exists for Claude's audit.
2. Pick attempt folders that flatter (e.g. a weak `--baseline`) — the
   ready check has no `--baseline` flag; bars are fixed (base + compiled).
3. Time-of-day gaming (run when the machine is quiet). Inherent to all
   timing here; paired repeats (piece) and shuffled repeats (G3) bound it.
4. Quote piece medians as end-to-end. Killed by the level+label rule +
   checker + marker requirement.
5. Skip the checker (lead closes without calling it). The signature is
   file-backed and Claude's post-round audit checks presence (§8, M3);
   transcripts record helper starts. A lead that forges a signature is
   visible in the same audit. Residual accepted (see §9).
6. Three failures, cosmetic "approach change" (rename, not redesign).
   The checker judges the notes' from-X-to-Y statement; weak but
   auditable. AC5's "or log why not" already concedes this boundary.

**Security.** No new surface: no network, no credentials (rule stands),
no sandbox change, no hook change. The wrapper runs the same local
binaries the swarm already runs. The marker is provenance, not trust —
Claude's independent measurement stays the authority.

**Operations.** Round duration grows by typically one vLLM run
(§3A: ~14 min/1 slot, ~25–40/2–3; measured live in §8 T-live) plus
checker agents (minutes, no GPU). Cost stays ~$1/round (contributor
model). Memory: schedule the check late; the lead pauses new helper
starts while it runs. Monitoring: §8 M1–M4.

## 7. Credible alternatives considered and their trade-offs

1. **Skill rules only (no tool change).** "Run `time_candidates.py vllm`
   with these exact flags." Rejected: nine gaming vectors (§2.1), and
   the contributor model follows explicit rules but cannot self-police
   flag discipline against its own incentive to show gains. Behaviour 4
   cuts the other way — but that rule was countable post-hoc (runs ==
   attempts), while flag values evaporate unless audited. The wrapper
   makes the protocol countable.
2. **Pin by editing `time_candidates.py` (remove flags / add a `--g3`
   mode).** Rejected: it changes Claude's own measurement path (risk to
   the authority), and any flag the script accepts stays available to
   the swarm. The additive wrapper leaves the authority untouched (§5).
3. **Plain-engine in-round check (fast: seconds, not minutes).**
   Rejected: plain `prompt_ms` is always 0.0 and writes no verdict
   (§2.1) — it would re-legalise behaviour 1 (prefill priced at zero)
   as the official gate. Speed is the attraction; wrongness is
   disqualifying. (If plain ever gains real prompt timing + verdict,
   the wrapper can pin it as a pre-gate — evolution path, F10.)
4. **Extend the verifier instead of adding a checker.** Rejected
   narrowly: the verifier is exploration-scoped and returns before
   implementation (`verifier.md:25`); re-tasking it mid-round muddies
   its proven remit and its Done condition. A sibling card with the
   same method reuses what works without touching it. If agent count
   ever binds, merging the cards is a safe refactor (same method).
5. **Hard attempt/family cap (e.g. "drop after 3 failures", no escape).**
   Rejected: AC5 explicitly allows "or the log records why not", and a
   hard cap risks killing a slow-converging real improvement (round-2
   routing improved across 4 attempts). The approach-change rule bounds
   cost while preserving the escape hatch, file-backed.
6. **Re-run-on-noise tiebreak (allow one repeat on marginal `slower`).**
   Rejected (F4): any re-roll rule is a license to re-roll, and "marginal"
   needs a threshold that becomes the next proxy. Precision beats recall
   here; a noise-killed candidate is merely unsubmitted, while a
   noise-crowned one corrupts the baseline chain.
7. **Full provenance (signed logs, trusted timestamps, sandboxing).**
   Rejected per the brief's guardrails (surucuonur rejected sandbox/hook
   hardening; "simple over airtight"). The recompute-and-compare +
   independent-G3 pairing gives two independent observations of the same
   protocol, which is the proportionate integrity story."}

137|- **F9. Docs drift and "Not covered" repeats.** ADR 0010's "Not covered:
138|  prefill speed" was cited to justify behaviour 1; ADR 0011 has its own

140|  fix never reached any ADR; `SKILL.md:80` stamps "skill version 6" while
141|  `:10` declares v7. → Rephrase every coverage gap as "unverified: assume
142|  nothing"; record the fix in an ADR; repair the version stamp.
143|- **F10. Evolution.** More slots, other engines, rounds 4+, other models.
144|  A fix wired to "vLLM, 3 slots, 4 workloads" rots. → The pinned protocol
145|  lives in one audited place (the wrapper + marker); the skill cites the
146|  wrapper, not flag values; the glossary holds the shared definitions.
147|
148|### 2.3 Root cause and certainty
149|
150|**Cause (high certainty — five independent behaviour chains converge):**
151|inside a round the swarm never observes the real objective. Its only
152|feedback is per-slot piece timing, while the real measurement (G3 over
153|whole requests) arrives post-round; and its end-to-end claims pass from
154|hypothesis to README to summary with no recorded check step (verifier
155|verdicts appear in every exploration entry and nowhere in
156|`implementation/`). Behaviour 2 is directly *mandated* by this structure:
157|`SKILL.md:147` requires an end-to-end number while `tracking.md:152` and
158|`SKILL.md:164` forbid the only measurement that could produce one.
159|
160|**Why behaviour 1's specific fix (ADR 0011) is not enough (high
161|certainty):** it closes the prefill gap but leaves the general habit —
162|"anything outside the measurement is free" — unaddressed, and adds a new
163|citeable "Not covered" (`0011:51`).
164|
165|**Why rules alone are not enough (medium-high certainty):** behaviour 4
166|shows rules work when explicit and checkable — but an end-to-end call with
167|free flags has nine gaming vectors (§2.1), several undetectable from the
168|verdict alone. The flags must be mechanically pinned, not merely
169|listed. Conversely, tools alone are not enough either: no tool sees
170|unwritten assumptions, borrowed arithmetic, or design-family persistence —
171|those need the checker and the counter.
172|
173|## 3. Recommended design: measure what you claim
174|
175|One principle, three pillars. **Every speed claim in a round is either a
176|measurement of exactly what is claimed, at the level claimed, citing its
177|run file — or a labelled prediction shown next to the measured value.**
178|Proposal in full; prototypes live in `prototype/`.
179|
180|### Pillar A — a pinned in-round end-to-end gate (tool)
181|
182|**New entry point `bench/grader/check_ready.py`** (proposal; prototype:
183|`prototype/check_ready.py`, 13/13 audit tests pass). It is the only
184|end-to-end evidence the swarm may cite. It does exactly two things:
185|
186|1. **Runs one pinned invocation** — `time_candidates.py vllm` with the G3
187|   protocol fixed in code: 4 G3 settings (`1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024`),
188|   5 repeats, 256 tokens, positional `SLOT=FOLDER` only. There are no
189|   `--repeats`, `--settings`, `--tokens`, `--variant` or engine flags to
190|   game (F1: seven vectors removed by construction). It takes the GPU lock
191|   through `time_candidates.main()`'s existing `hold()` (no second hold:
192|   a same-process re-hold would self-deadlock on `flock`, F8 note), loads
193|   the model inside the run, and appends a `ready-protocol` marker record
194|   to the jsonl pinning what ran.
195|2. **Audits the log instead of trusting it** — exactly one marker with
196|   pinned values; every run vLLM at the 4 settings × 5 repeats; the exact
197|   variant set (`base`, `compiled-<slot>`, `muse-<slot>` per slot, plus
198|   `compiled-all`/`muse-all` when >1 slot, so a combination is always
199|   measured as a combination); every non-base variant keeps base's greedy
200|   tokens at rows 1 and 32 (the brief's end-to-end G2, which G3 itself
201|   ignores — §2.1); the G3 verdict **recomputed from the log** and
202|   compared with `g3-vllm.json` (kills lazy forgery, F8); every submitted
203|   `muse-<slot>` and `muse-all` passing G3 against base and its compiled
204|   counterpart.
205|
206|**Contract.** CLI: `check_ready.py <out-dir> SLOT=FOLDER [...]`, plus
207|`--audit <out-dir>` (no GPU; re-audits any folder — also useful to
208|Claude post-round). Refuses a non-empty out-dir (F6: no appends, one
209|folder per check). Writes `muse-vllm.jsonl`, `g3-vllm.json`,
210|`ready-verdict.json` (schema: `pass`, per-variant `g3`/`vs`/`phases`,
211|`exact` table, `protocol`, file paths). Exit 0 pass / 1 judged fail /
212|2 protocol violation; every path writes `ready-verdict.json` so the
213|checker can cite even failures. Prints one `ready <variant>: pass/fail`
214|line each plus `ready check: PASS/FAIL`.
215|
216|**Scheduling (F3).** Piece timing stays the search signal; the ready
217|check runs only at close-time. The lead batches: hypotheses converge on
218|piece timing to the new `candidate` status, then **one combined call**
219|over all submitted slots judges every `muse-<slot>` and `muse-all`
220|together. Typical cost: one vLLM run per round (~14 min for 1 slot,
221|~25–40 for 2–3). A failed check returns the hypothesis to building only
222|with a changed approach, else drops it (F2: bounded by genuine
223|redesigns, never a loop). The verdict stands — no re-runs (F4).
224|
225|### Pillar B — claim discipline with an independent checker (skill)
226|
227|**Number rule rewrite** (`tracking.md:153`; prototype:
228|`prototype/skill/tracking.md`). The old rule accepts shown arithmetic as
229|a source — the letter that blessed behaviours 2–3. The new rule: every
230|speed number carries level (piece/end-to-end), run file, and label
231|(measured/prediction). Measured piece numbers cite the grader verdict
232|that timed exactly that slot; measured end-to-end numbers cite the ready
233|check that timed exactly that slot or combination; predictions count
234|only the candidate's own measured effect and sit next to the measured
235|value; combinations are measured as combinations, never summed;
236|everything unmeasured goes under **Unverified** and is never assumed
237|free, neutral or zero — "G3 decides" is an Unverified entry, not a
238|measurement. GPU rule (`tracking.md:152`) becomes "the grader and the
239|ready check are the only GPU jobs", run only as builder / only as lead
240|respectively, with direct `time_candidates.py`/`breakdown.py`/
241|`repeat_fixes.py` runs explicitly not evidence (F8).
242|
243|**New `candidate` status + `ready` gate** (prototype:
244|`prototype/skill/tracking.md` hypothesis schema). `candidate` = passes
245|G1, G2, boundary check, `beats_compiled` (+ `beats_baseline`) on piece
246|timing, checker-signed, awaiting the ready check. `ready` = the ready
247|check's `ready-verdict.json` says `pass` for exactly this attempt. The
248|Decision at `candidate` states the piece basis as a prediction; at
249|`ready` it cites the verdict file with the measured change. Ready to
250|test names only `ready` attempts (or kept baselines / the reference,
251|which carry no new claim). This is AC2 made mechanical (F5: file-backed).
252|
253|**New role: checker** (proposal; prototype card:
254|`prototype/skill/checker.md`). The verifier's implementation-phase
255|counterpart — same method (open the cited file, redo the arithmetic),
256|because that method is proven. `checker-<n>` signs each hypothesis
257|before `candidate`/`ready`; `checker-final` signs Ready to test and the
258|summary. It checks levels, run files, labels, own-effect-only arithmetic,
259|Unverified completeness, the failure counter (§3C), and the ready-gate.
260|The lead cannot close without its `pass` in the `Check` section / log.
261|Like the verifier it never edits others' numbers; the lead fixes and
262|re-calls. One agent per check keeps it cheap; post-round, Claude audits
263|that the signatures exist (F7, §8).
264|
265|### Pillar C — a design-family switch rule (skill)
266|
267|**Failure signatures + count of 3** (proposal; schema in
268|`prototype/skill/tracking.md`, rule text for `SKILL.md` step 4 in §8).
269|The lead logs each failed attempt's signature — the phase/size it failed
270|at plus the named cause. After **3 failures sharing one phase and one
271|cause**, the next attempt must be a **changed approach** (different
272|kernel structure, parallelisation or dataflow — not tuning), named in
273|`notes.md` as "approach change: from X to Y", or the log holds the
274|lead's reason why not. The checker verifies the counter. A failed ready
275|check logs an end-to-end-level signature under the same counter.
276|Why 3: round-2 experts' attempts 1–3 share decode/1-row + "fused-structure
277|1-row latency", and attempt-3's own note refuted the lever — the rule
278|fires exactly where the record says it should (`results/schema-dry-run.md`),
279|while allowing genuine iteration (F5: countable, not advisory).
280|
281|### Data flow and integration points
282|
283|```text
284|builder → grader (piece) → hyp entry → boundary check → checker-<n> pass
285|  → candidate ─┐
286|               ├→ lead: ONE check_ready.py over all candidates (+muse-all)
287|candidate ─────┘         → ready-verdict.json pass → ready (per slot)
288|                       → fail → redesign (approach change) or dropped
289|ready set → Ready to test + summary → checker-final pass → commit → Claude's G3
290|```
291|
292|Integration points: `check_ready.py` imports `time_candidates` (calls
293|`main()` with a pinned argv, reuses `g3()` for recompute) and needs no
294|change to it; skill changes touch `SKILL.md` (goal line, step 4–5,
295|role table, `:164` ownership line), `tracking.md` (rules + schema),
296|new `checker.md`, `builder.md` (notes gain an Unverified line),
297|`boundary.md` ("can't see" list becomes Unverified entries),
298|`claude/muse-agent-brief.md` (`:213-215` end-to-end ownership),
299|`CHANGELOG.md` (v8), glossary (`Ready check`, `Candidate`,

419|transcripts show whether `check_ready.py` actually ran. This matches
420|the brief's "simple over airtight" guardrail — proportionate, stated.

423|1. Tune to the 4 G3 workloads (e.g. `max_rows` edges placed just

text:
**Status: READY.** Full design (sections 1–9) in `design-lab/designer-c/design.md`; tracked tree untouched (`git status` shows only untracked `design-lab/`).

**Approach — "measure what you claim", one principle in three pillars.** (A) A new pinned tool gate, `bench/grader/check_ready.py`: the only end-to-end evidence the swarm may cite. It runs `time_candidates.py vllm` with the G3 protocol fixed in code (no flags to game), then audits the log instead of trusting it — marker, exact 4-settings×5-repeats variant set with `muse-all`, token exactness, and G3 recomputed from the log vs the filed verdict. Exit 0/1/2 (pass/judged-fail/protocol-violation). The lead batches all close-time candidates into one combined call (~9 min measured for 1 slot). (B) Skill claim discipline: every speed number carries level + run file + label (measured/prediction); predictions count only the candidate's own effect; combinations measured as combinations; everything unmeasured goes on a required Unverified list; a new independent `checker` role (the verifier's proven method, applied to implementation) must sign every close; new `candidate` status separates piece-done from end-to-end-proven, and `ready` is defined as a passing `ready-verdict.json`. (C) A design-family switch rule: after 3 failures sharing one phase and cause, the next attempt changes approach (named from-X-to-Y) or the log records why not — checker-verified.

**Key evidence.**
- Audit prototype: 13/13 offline checks pass (`tests/test_audit.py` → `results/audit-tests/`), covering every end-to-end gaming vector, forged-g3 detection, and old-log rejection; CLI exits 0/1/2 confirmed; crash-partial log and non-empty-dir refusal verified.
- Live pinned vLLM run on round-2 routing attempt-4 (`results/ready-routing-a4/`, 60 runs, 9m09s): judged FAIL with zero protocol problems — prompt slower at 8/32 requests — reproducing ADR 0011's demotion exactly, i.e. the in-round gate and post-round authority agree at verdict level (AC6 premise validated; decode medians drift ~0.1–0.2 ms across sessions, noted for tolerance).
- Schema dry-run (`results/schema-dry-run.md`): all five historical false-claim families rejected with allowed forms; the 3-failure counter fires exactly at round-2 experts attempt-3, where the record's own note refuted the lever.
- Failure-first grounding: 10 failure modes (F1–F10) each mapped to a design element; Goodhart audit of six residual gaming paths; same-process `flock` re-hold proven blocking (grounds the no-second-hold + idempotency call); seven alternatives rejected with reasons; no `time_candidates.py`/`check_candidate.py` edits, rollback by deletion.

Role: independent tester for design A
Objective: You are tester-a in a one-off design session. Do NOT run the muse-round skill. You test designer-a's design ONLY.

Reference for expected values: claude/findings/muse-round-2.md and results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json.

Session rules (binding):
- The repository's tracked files stay as they are: change, move or delete none of them, run no git command that changes anything, and commit nothing.
- You write ONLY in design-lab/tester-a/. To run the design's prototype, COPY it into design-lab/tester-a/ first and run the copy (never edit the designer's files). All outputs go under design-lab/tester-a/.
- The GPU runs one job at a time: the prototype takes the lock in bench/grader/gpu_lock.py and waits its turn (import gpu_lock; gpu_lock.hold("<what>") for any GPU work you run directly). Load a model only inside such a run. The machine has 16 GB and pages heavily; a vLLM run takes about 10-12 minutes with 5 repeats. Sibling testers hold the lock too — queue waits are normal; record them.
- Never read credentials: .env files, ~/.config/muse, or any key store. No network calls.
- Every claim about the repository cites a path and line, and every claim about performance cites the result file it comes from; mark proposals, predictions and assumptions as such.

TESTS (all by running, not by reading):
1. CATCH TEST (live GPU): run the copied check_submission.py on round-2's real submission in ONE call: routing=muse-spark/round-2/kernels/routing/attempt-4 combine=muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1. Record wall time, exit code, submission-verdict.json. Then judge: would this in-round check have caught behaviours 1-3? Expected from Claude's measurements (verify against claude/findings/muse-round-2.md, don't take my word): routing FAILs (prompt 7-10% slower), combine FAILs (decode +1.051ms at 32 requests), muse-all FAILs. State for each variant PASS/FAIL and whether it matches Claude's post-round verdict.
2. DESIGNER'S OWN TESTS: re-run the designer's CPU tests from your copies; confirm or refute the claimed 25/25 (results/test_*.txt).

For each: PASS/FAIL/exit code and whether the game is caught.
4. NOISE TEST (CPU + your live log): from your live run's jsonl plus results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/muse-vllm.jsonl, report repeat spreads per setting and identify any verdict that sits on a range-overlap boundary (faster/same/slower flips). Assess: would 5 repeats give a stable verdict here?
5. PROTECTED TESTS: verify and report with evidence: git status shows no tracked file changed; attempt format (spec.json + block-N.metal) untouched; grader JSON keys (g1, g2, beats_compiled, beats_baseline, timing_us_per_layer, phases_vs_compiled) untouched; the check goes through gpu_lock; one-grader-run-per-attempt is unaffected; Claude's post-round G3 path (time_candidates.py) is unmodified.

Read text file `design-lab/brief.md`.
1|# Solution design brief: make the Muse agent swarm pursue real efficiency, not its proxies (v1)
2|
3|## APPROVAL
4|- User approved this brief on 2026-11-04 (surucuonur). Decisions: the swarm may run end-to-end checks in-round through the GPU queue; Meta's Muse does the design work; from round 3 the launcher runs muse-spark-1.3-contributor with tool approvals off (ADR 0012, commit 1113c2d).
5|- Approved activity: one Muse Code session (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) whose lead starts its own helper agents, up to 12 at once, with no cost or time limit. Agents may prototype and test in design-lab/ (untracked, never committed) and run the measurement tools through the GPU queue. The repository's tracked files stay unchanged.
6|
7|## PROBLEM AND OUTCOME
8|- **Current problem:** two rounds of the Muse agent swarm (round 1: Muse Spark; round 2: Muse Wonder, 63 min, ~$58) produced no kernel that is a real efficiency improvement, while the swarm's own reports predicted gains. Five behaviours, each with evidence:
9|  1. **Treats unmeasured costs as free.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`: "Prefill speed is not timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart from time to first token", citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`. The result: experts attempt-7 is 16–28× slower than the compiled reference at prefill sizes, and routing attempt-4 2.6–8.7× slower (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`). Prompts took 6.6–14.5× and 7–10% longer, and throughput fell by up to 83% (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §5).
10|  2. **Claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Expected G3 = (compiled − candidate) µs × 20 layers (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md` *Ready to test*; `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`). Round 1 predicted −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.98/+0.16/−1.76. Round 2 predicted −0.84 at each and measured −0.73/−0.74/+0.53 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`, `muse-round-2.md`).
11|  3. **Reasons inconsistently.** The same README says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then reports "Together (sum) −0.84 ms". Combine's −0.35 ms prediction is −0.07 to −0.09 from its own timing plus −0.27 to −0.29 borrowed from what `mx.compile` gains end to end. Measured: +1.05 ms with 32 requests.
12|  4. **Used the grader as a search loop (round 1).** 29 grader runs on experts for 4 counted attempts, 18 on attempt-1 with edits between (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §5). Fixed since skill v4: one run is one attempt; round 2 ran 13 for 13.
13|  5. **Persists with a failing design family.** All 7 experts attempts in round 2 are fused kernels that lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs per layer). The cause, too few threadgroups at 1 row, was already known from round 1. The harden loop says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" (`.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:138`), and there is no rule for changing design.

96|## 3. Recommended design: one gate, one checker pass, one counter
97|
98|The design adds exactly three mechanisms, each reusing an established
99|pattern. Together they close the feedback loop: the swarm sees the real
100|objective before it claims anything, an independent checker replays every
101|claim from cited files, and a counter forces design diversity.
102|
103|### 3.1 The submission check (the gate; fixes behaviours 1–3 at the root)
104|
105|**New tool `bench/grader/check_submission.py`** (prototype:
106|`prototypes/check_submission.py`), a ~150-line wrapper that:
107|
108|- takes `<out> SLOT=FOLDER...` — every candidate slot positionally in ONE
109|  call, so per-slot variants AND `muse-all`/`compiled-all` are measured as a
110|  combination (`time_candidates.py:125-127`);
111|- delegates to `time_candidates.main()` with pinned arguments: engine `vllm`,
112|  the 4 G3 workloads, 5 repeats, 256 tokens (asserting equality with
113|  `G3_SETTINGS`/`G3_REPEATS` first, so upstream drift fails loudly);
114|- then audits `<out>/muse-vllm.jsonl` + `g3-vllm.json`: exact expected
115|  variant set, engine vllm, reps 0–4 present per (variant, rows, prompt), and

117|  end-to-end check, currently ungated);
118|- writes `<out>/submission-verdict.json` (params echoed, per-variant pass,
119|  bars, phases, exact flags, problems list) and exits 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL,
