225|## 4. Why it solves the underlying problem; acceptance criteria
226|
227|The underlying problem is the gap between the proxy the swarm sees and the
228|objective it is judged on, plus unchecked self-reporting. The design moves
229|the objective into the round (the gate measures exactly what G3 measures,
230|with the same code and rule, plus the token gate) and puts a checker between
231|every claim and the reader. It does not patch five symptoms; behaviours 1–3
232|all become impossible-to-claim-without-measuring, behaviour 4's fix is
233|extended to the new GPU job by the same explicit-countable technique, and
234|behaviour 5 gets the missing loop exit.
235|
236|| Criterion | How met |
237||---|---|
238|| 1. Every speed claim cited at its level, or PREDICTION beside measured | R1 in `tracking.md:153` + verifier claims pass step 1; Ready-to-test/summary templates rewritten to the measured form. Prototype replay flags all round-2 violations (`results/test_claim_rules.txt`, 4/4). |

123|| the three alone, added up | −0.564 | −1.867 | −4.389 |
124|
125|- **Every pair comes within 0.5 ms of its parts' sum.**
126|- **All three together, with 8 requests, are 2.8 ms slower than their parts.** It is the only case that misses by much.
127|- **Round 1 did the same.** Its three kernels, with 8 requests, came out at +0.88 ms in plain MLX against −1.95 ms for the parts ([round 1](muse-round-1.md#3-g3-the-decode-step)). Two different sets of kernels show it, so the cause is likely in how the step runs with all three slots replaced at that size, not in one kernel. It is not explained.
128|- **The fastest decode step with exact output** is routing attempt-4 with experts attempt-7: −20% with 32 requests, −10% with 8 and −6% with 1 in plain MLX, and −18.8% with 32 requests in vLLM (section 5). Over whole requests it is the slowest version measured, because of experts attempt-7's prompt processing.
129|
130|## 5. Whole requests: prompts and throughput
131|
132|A last vLLM run (`results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/`, tables built by `bench/grader/engine_table.py`) timed eight versions of the engine at four workloads: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts. Besides the decode step it recorded the time until every prompt was processed and each run's whole time, as generated tokens per second. Every version but round 1's kept the tokens identical. Throughput change against the unchanged engine (prompt time as a multiple of the unchanged engine's in brackets):
133|
134|| Version | 1 × 128 | 8 × 128 | 32 × 128 | 32 × 1,024 |
135||---|---|---|---|---|
136|| compiled references, all three slots | +11.9% (1.04×) | +3.1% (0.99×) | +0.6% (0.98×) | +0.9% (0.98×) |
137|| round 2: routing attempt-4 | +10.2% (1.07×) | +1.8% (1.09×) | +0.3% (1.10×) | −3.5% (1.10×) |
138|| round 2 submission: routing + combine | +15.9% (1.11×) | +2.1% (1.09×) | −2.7% (1.08×) | −4.1% (1.09×) |
139|| round 2: routing + experts attempt-7 | −10.0% (6.63×) | −37.5% (14.50×) | −48.0% (12.50×) | −82.5% (13.09×) |
140|| round 2: all three with experts attempt-7 | −10.7% (6.75×) | −43.0% (14.33×) | −53.7% (14.37×) | −83.3% (13.66×) |
141|| round 1: all three (changes the output) | −13.3% (1.60×) | −9.6% (2.30×) | −8.1% (2.30×) | −33.6% (2.32×) |
142|
143|- **Compiling MLX's own code for the three slots,** with no new kernel, gains 0.6% to 3.1% with 8 and 32 requests, where its repeats and the unchanged engine's don't overlap. With 1 request its median gain is 11.9%, but one of its three repeats falls inside the unchanged engine's range (1,374 to 1,559 ms against 1,486 to 1,580), so that gain is not certain. No Muse version gains in every workload.
144|- **The unchanged engine is vLLM's own.** It ran with Claude's step hooks and vLLM's engine in the script's process. Alternating runs on the same afternoon found it within −0.2% to +1.9% of vLLM with neither, inside the spread between repeats in every workload (`bench/micro/clean_vllm.py`, [results/runs/2026-11-04-clean-vllm/](../../results/runs/2026-11-04-clean-vllm/)).
145|- **Round 2's kernels are slower than MLX's when processing prompts,** in every slot measured: routing alone by 7–10%, routing with combine by 8–11%, and experts attempt-7 by 6.6 to 14.5 times. Every prompt chunk here has at least 128 rows, so it runs experts attempt-7's path for 60 rows and more, which copies `gather_qmm_rhs`'s rounding but not its speed.
146|- **The grader checks the kernels' output at prompt sizes, and G3 times only decode steps,** so neither saw this. Its decode-step figures in sections 1 to 4 stand; they describe one part of a request.
147|
148|## 6. How round 2 worked
149|
150|- **Time:** 63 minutes; the lead and 34 helpers; 983 model calls. 981 were `muse-wonder-1.0`, and 2 were Muse Code's reminder agents on `muse-spark-1.3` (`muse-spark/transcripts/01a1a48b-e027-7462-898f-0b01290c8c9a.summary.json`).
151|- **Tokens:** 125.6M input, of which 121.1M were cached, and 0.77M output. At Muse Wonder's prices that is about $58: $18 uncached input, $24 cached input and $15 output. It would be about $65 if the 0.36M reasoning tokens are billed on top of the output.
152|- **Attempts:** one grader run per attempt, 13 in total, as the skill asks. Every graded attempt is committed.
153|- **What it got right:** it read round 1's measurement, made exactness its first goal, and met it in every slot. Its explorers found that routing's reference changes its matrix-product strategy in row-count regimes, and its builder copied each regime exactly. Those regimes are what section 2 tests.
154|- **What it missed:** its prediction for combine (−0.35 ms) and for the submission at 32 requests. The chained piece timing still doesn't show combine's cost in the step.
155|
156|## For round 3: baselines and starting points
157|
158|**The rule,** from round 3 ([ADR 0011](../adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)): a slot's baseline is its best attempt so far that passes the current G2, has `beats_compiled` true in the grader, and passes G3. Both of those now judge two phases, decode and prefill: faster in one, slower in neither, and in G3 no whole request slower, against the unchanged model and the compiled reference. An attempt that passes G2 but not the rest is a starting point, not a bar: making it the bar would ask a fix to beat it where it already wins.
159|
160|The current grader re-graded round 2's three kernels on 2026-11-04 (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`). Times are multiples of the compiled reference's, per layer:
161|
162|| Slot | Baseline | Starting point | Decode, 1 / 8 / 32 rows | Prefill, 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows | Why it is no baseline |
163||---|---|---|---|---|---|
164|| `routing` | none | `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/routing/attempt-4` | 0.76 / 0.84 / 0.84, faster | 2.6 / 5.9 / 8.7, slower | Slower at every prefill size, so prompts take 7–10% longer and whole requests with 1,024-token prompts lose 3.5% (section 5). |
165|| `combine` | none | `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1` | 0.86 / 0.85 / 0.93, faster | 0.95 / 0.83 / 0.52, faster | Its decode step in G3 was 1.05 ms slower than the unchanged model's with 32 requests, for a reason the grader doesn't show (section 3). |
166|| `experts` | none | `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7` | 1.17 / 0.69 / 0.65, slower at 1 row | 15.8 / 27.7 / 20.1, slower | Slower at 1 row and at every prefill size, so prompts take 6.6 to 14.5 times as long (section 5). |
167|
168|Round 3 has no baseline in any slot, so its bar is the compiled reference everywhere.
169|
170|**What round 3 has to find out,** in Claude's reading of these results:
171|1. **experts with 1 row.** attempt-7 keeps its 8- and 32-row speed and loses at 1 row, as every fused design in round 2 did (92 to 110 µs per layer chained, against 73 to 87 for the compiled reference, in round 2's runs). Round 2's summary suggests copying the reference's unfused structure exactly for small row counts.
172|2. **Why combine attempt-1 costs 1 ms in the step with 32 requests** and not in the grader.
173|3. **Why all three slots replaced at once lose 2.8 ms with 8 requests,** when every pair adds up (section 4).
174|4. **Prefill speed.** From round 3 the grader times the prefill sizes and G3 times prompts and whole requests (ADR 0011). routing attempt-4 and experts attempt-7 are slower than the compiled reference at every prefill size; combine attempt-1 is faster. An attempt may keep inputs above a row count it names on the compiled reference (`max_rows`, in the brief). Claude checked that hand-off on a copy of experts attempt-7 with `max_rows` 59: bit-exact at all six sizes, and the `same` as the compiled reference at every prefill size (`results/runs/2026-11-04-handoff-check/`).

1|"""The round's submission check: one pinned end-to-end run, judged like G3.
2|
3|PROTOTYPE for design-lab/designer-a (design: "one gate"). Proposed real
4|location: bench/grader/check_submission.py. It changes no tracked file; it
5|delegates the GPU work to bench/grader/time_candidates.py with pinned
6|arguments, then audits the log and the G3 verdict.
7|
8|  python check_submission.py <out dir> <SLOT=FOLDER>... [--dry-run]
9|
10|What it pins (the G3 rule of claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md:36-41):
11|engine vllm, 4 workloads (1x128, 8x128, 32x128, 32x1024), 5 repeats,
12|256 tokens, every submitted slot passed positionally in one call so
13|muse-all is measured as a combination, no --variant extras.
14|
15|What it adds over calling time_candidates.py directly:
16|- the free flags (--repeats, --settings, --tokens, --variant) do not exist,
17|  so the run cannot be shrunk or widened by accident or design;
18|- the end-to-end token check (exact greedy tokens at 1 and 32 requests,
19|  the brief's G2) becomes a gate: time_candidates.py logs `exact` but
20|  never judges it (time_candidates.py:168-197 reads only kind=="run");
21|- the audit replays the log: every expected (variant, rows, prompt, rep)
22|  run present, engine vllm, then every judged muse-* variant's g3 pass.
23|
24|It writes <out>/submission-verdict.json (the file the swarm cites) and:
25|- exit 0 with PASS lines: every judged variant passes vs base and its
26|  compiled-* bar, with exact tokens;
27|- exit 1: a variant fails (verdict FAIL, still written);
28|- exit 2: usage error or the log is incomplete (never cite it).
29|
30|The GPU lock is taken by time_candidates.py (time_candidates.py:224);
31|--dry-run prints the pinned command and touches nothing.
32|"""
33|
34|import argparse
35|import json
36|import sys
37|from pathlib import Path
38|
39|# Pinned G3 shape. Must equal time_candidates.G3_SETTINGS / G3_REPEATS and
40|# the --tokens default; main() asserts that before delegating, so drift fails
41|# loudly instead of silently running a different check.
42|EXPECTED_SETTINGS = ((1, 128), (8, 128), (32, 128), (32, 1024))
43|EXPECTED_REPEATS = 5
44|EXPECTED_TOKENS = 256
45|
46|
47|def expected_variants(slots):
48|    """Variant names one pinned call builds (time_candidates.py:111-132)."""
49|    names = ["base"]
50|    for slot in slots:
51|        names += [f"compiled-{slot}", f"muse-{slot}"]
52|    if len(slots) > 1:
53|        names += ["compiled-all", "muse-all"]
54|    return names
55|
56|
57|def judged_variants(slots):
58|    """Variants the verdict must pass: each muse-<slot>, plus muse-all."""
59|    names = [f"muse-{s}" for s in slots]
60|    if len(slots) > 1:
61|        names.append("muse-all")
62|    return names
63|
64|
65|def audit(out, slots):
66|    """Replay <out>/muse-vllm.jsonl + g3-vllm.json. Returns (verdict, problems).
67|
68|    verdict: {"pass": bool, "variants": {name: {...}}, "params": {...}}.
69|    problems: lines explaining why the log cannot be cited (empty when citable).
70|    """
71|    problems = []
72|    log = out / "muse-vllm.jsonl"
73|    g3file = out / "g3-vllm.json"
74|    if not log.exists():
75|        return None, [f"missing {log}"]
76|    if not g3file.exists():
77|        return None, [f"missing {g3file} (no G3 verdict: not a vllm run?)"]
78|    records = [json.loads(line) for line in log.read_text().splitlines()]
79|    runs = [r for r in records if r.get("kind") == "run"]
80|    checks = [r for r in records if r.get("kind") == "check"]
81|
82|    want = expected_variants(slots)
83|    got = sorted({r["variant"] for r in runs})
84|    if got != sorted(want):
85|        problems.append(f"variants {got}, want {want}")
86|    for r in runs:
87|        if r.get("engine") != "vllm":
88|            problems.append(f"run {r.get('variant')} rep {r.get('rep')}: engine {r.get('engine')!r}, want 'vllm'")
89|            break
90|    for name in want:
91|        for rows, prompt in EXPECTED_SETTINGS:
92|            reps = sorted(
93|                r["rep"]
94|                for r in runs
95|                if (r["variant"], r["rows"], r["prompt"]) == (name, rows, prompt)
96|            )
97|            if reps != list(range(EXPECTED_REPEATS)):
98|                problems.append(
99|                    f"{name} {rows}x{prompt}: reps {reps}, want 0..{EXPECTED_REPEATS - 1}"
100|                )
101|
102|    exact = {}
103|    for name in judged_variants(slots):
104|        for rows in (1, 32):
105|            recs = [
106|                c for c in checks
107|                if (c["variant"], c["rows"]) == (name, rows)
108|            ]
109|            if len(recs) != 1:
110|                problems.append(f"check {name} rows {rows}: {len(recs)} records, want 1")
111|                exact[(name, rows)] = False
112|            else:
113|                exact[(name, rows)] = recs[0].get("exact") is True
114|                if not exact[(name, rows)]:
115|                    problems.append(
116|                        f"check {name} rows {rows}: exact is {recs[0].get('exact')!r}, "
117|                        f"want True ({recs[0].get('rows_differ')} sequences differ)"
118|                    )
119|
120|    g3 = json.loads(g3file.read_text())
121|    verdict = {"params": {
122|        "engine": "vllm", "repeats": EXPECTED_REPEATS, "tokens": EXPECTED_TOKENS,
123|        "settings": [f"{r}x{p}" for r, p in EXPECTED_SETTINGS],
124|        "slots": list(slots),
125|    }, "variants": {}}
126|    allpass = not problems
127|    for name in judged_variants(slots):
128|        v = g3.get(name, {})
129|        bars = {b: v.get(b, {}) for b in ("base", "compiled-" + name.removeprefix("muse-"))}
130|        ok = v.get("g3") is True and all(b.get("pass") is True for b in bars.values())
131|        verdict["variants"][name] = {
132|            "pass": ok and all(exact.get((name, r), False) for r in (1, 32)),
133|            "g3": v.get("g3"),
134|            "bars": {b: bars[b].get("pass") for b in bars},
135|            "phases": {b: bars[b].get("phases") for b in bars},
136|            "exact_1": exact.get((name, 1)), "exact_32": exact.get((name, 32)),
137|        }
138|        allpass = allpass and verdict["variants"][name]["pass"]
139|    verdict["pass"] = allpass
140|    verdict["problems"] = problems
141|    return verdict, problems
142|
143|
144|def main(argv=None):
145|    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
146|    ap.add_argument("out", type=Path)
147|    ap.add_argument("attempts", nargs="+", metavar="SLOT=FOLDER")
148|    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
149|    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
150|    slots = [a.partition("=")[0] for a in args.attempts]
151|    if any(not s or "=" not in a for s, a in zip(slots, args.attempts)):
152|        ap.error("give SLOT=FOLDER per submitted slot")
153|
154|    if args.dry_run:
155|        print("pinned run: time_candidates.py vllm"
156|              f" {args.out} {' '.join(args.attempts)}"
157|              f" --repeats {EXPECTED_REPEATS} --tokens {EXPECTED_TOKENS}"
158|              " --settings " + ",".join(f"{r}x{p}" for r, p in EXPECTED_SETTINGS))
159|        print("judged:", " ".join(judged_variants(slots)))
160|        return 0
161|
162|    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("bench/grader").resolve()))
163|    import time_candidates as tc
164|
165|    assert tc.G3_SETTINGS == ",".join(f"{r}x{p}" for r, p in EXPECTED_SETTINGS), \
166|        f"G3_SETTINGS drifted: {tc.G3_SETTINGS}"
167|    assert tc.G3_REPEATS == EXPECTED_REPEATS, f"G3_REPEATS drifted: {tc.G3_REPEATS}"
168|    sys.argv = ["time_candidates.py", "vllm", str(args.out), *args.attempts,
169|                "--repeats", str(EXPECTED_REPEATS), "--tokens", str(EXPECTED_TOKENS),
170|                "--settings", tc.G3_SETTINGS]
171|    tc.main()
172|    verdict, problems = audit(args.out, slots)
173|    (args.out / "submission-verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(verdict, indent=1) + "\n")
174|    for line in problems:
175|        print(f"UNCITABLE: {line}")
176|    for name, v in verdict["variants"].items():
177|        print(f"{'PASS' if v['pass'] else 'FAIL'} {name}"
178|              f" g3={v['g3']} bars={v['bars']} exact={v['exact_1']}/{v['exact_32']}")
179|    if problems:
180|        return 2
181|    return 0 if verdict["pass"] else 1
182|
183|
184|if __name__ == "__main__":
185|    sys.exit(main())

2|
3|Variants, applied at runtime to MoE.__call__ in every layer:
4|
5|  base                the port's MoE, unchanged
6|  compiled-<slot>     the slot's reference code under mx.compile (our baseline)
7|  muse-<slot>         the Muse agent's attempt for the slot
8|  compiled-all        with several slots: all their references compiled at once
9|  muse-all            with several slots: all the attempts at once
10|  <name>              each --variant NAME:SLOT=FOLDER[+SLOT=FOLDER...]: other
11|                      attempts, timed in the same run but outside muse-all,
12|                      such as an earlier round's or one not submitted; the
13|                      FOLDER `compiled` is that slot's compiled reference
14|
15|G2 end to end: each variant's greedy tokens over 24 generated tokens, at 1
16|and 32 requests, must equal base's. G3 (vllm): each run's steady decode step
17|period, its prompt time (until every prompt was processed) and its
18|whole-request time, as repeat_fixes.py measures them (G3_REPEATS repeats,
19|shuffled), at 1, 8 and 32 requests of 128-token prompts and 32 of 1,024. A muse-*
20|variant passes against base and against its compiled-* counterpart when
21|one phase, decode or prompt, is faster in every setting, neither is slower
22|in any, and no request is slower; faster and slower mean the two ranges over
23|the repeats don't overlap (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md). With 5
24|repeats each, two identical engines' ranges miss each other by chance 1 time
25|in 252 per direction; with 3 it was 1 in 20, and the "never slower" checks,
26|8 per phase, would fail an unchanged phase about a third of the time. The
27|verdict goes to g3-vllm.json.
28|
29|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/time_candidates.py plain results/runs/<date>-muse <slot>=<attempt dir> ...
30|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/time_candidates.py vllm  results/runs/<date>-muse <slot>=<attempt dir> ...

57|def as_routing(fn):

"""One GPU job at a time: the exclusive lock every grader entry point takes.

Muse Spark's builder agents and Claude run these scripts on the same M1 Pro
GPU, and two runs at once distort each other's timings. A run that finds the
GPU busy says so and waits its turn, so runs queue and never overlap. The lock
file is in /tmp, so the main checkout and the Muse Spark worktree share it, and
the operating system releases it when the process ends, however it ends.
"""

import fcntl
import os
import sys

LOCK = "/tmp/mobilemoe-gpu.lock"
_held = []  # keeps the locked file open for the life of the process


def hold(job):
    """Take the GPU for this process, waiting while another run has it."""
    f = open(LOCK, "a+")
    try:
        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
    except BlockingIOError:
        f.seek(0)
        holder = f.read().strip() or "another run"
        print(f"{job}: waiting for the GPU ({holder})", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
    f.seek(0)
    f.truncate()
    f.write(f"pid {os.getpid()}: {job}\n")
    f.flush()
    _held.append(f)

text:
Designing a gaming_audit driver that calls cs audit directly to generate fixtures and verdicts for five CPU test cases.

Defining five explicit fixture cases for the audit path and exit-code behavior.

Adding a forged g3 verdict test and a git-diff simulation for post-check edit detection.
Designer tests confirmed 25/25, byte-identical. Now building the gaming fixtures.

tool_calls.name: write_file
tool_calls.args:
{"content":""""Tester-a gaming tests: feed the audit path gamed inputs, record each verdict.

Runs ONLY the audit path (cs.audit + verdict/exit-code logic mirroring
check_submission.main lines 172-181) on synthetic fixtures. No GPU.
Writes fixtures + verdicts under design-lab/tester-a/gaming/<case>/.
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import check_submission as cs

GAMING = HERE / "gaming"
SETTINGS = list(cs.EXPECTED_SETTINGS)


def write_log(d, slots, reps, settings, engine="vllm", exact=True,
              prompt_ms=10.0, period=None):
    """Synthetic run log + check records. period: dict variant->ms or None."""
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with (d / "muse-vllm.jsonl").open("w") as f:
        for name in cs.expected_variants(slots):
            for rows in (1, 32):
                rec = {"kind": "check", "variant": name, "rows": rows,
                       "kernels": 900}
                if name != "base":
                    rec |= {"exact": exact, "rows_differ": 0 if exact else 3,
                            "first_differ_step": None if exact else 0}
                f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
        for name in cs.expected_variants(slots):
            for rows, prompt in settings:
                for rep in reps:
                    ms = period.get(name, 5.0) if period else 5.0
                    f.write(json.dumps({
                        "kind": "run", "engine": engine, "variant": name,
                        "rows": rows, "prompt": prompt, "rep": rep,
                        "period_median_ms": ms, "prompt_ms": prompt_ms,
                        "wall_ms": 100.0,
                    }) + "\n")


def write_g3(d, slots, g3pass=True):
    g3 = {}
    for name in cs.judged_variants(slots):
        bar = "compiled-" + name.removeprefix("muse-")
        ph = {"decode": "faster", "prompt": "not slower",
              "request": "not slower"}
        g3[name] = {"base": {"pass": g3pass, "phases": ph},
                    bar: {"pass": g3pass, "phases": ph}, "g3": g3pass}
    (d / "g3-vllm.json").write_text(json.dumps(g3))
    return g3


def run_case(case, slots):
    """Mirror main(): audit, write verdict file, map to exit code."""
    d = GAMING / case
    verdict, problems = cs.audit(d, slots)
    if verdict is not None:
        (d / "submission-verdict.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(verdict, indent=1) + "\n")
        code = 2 if problems else (0 if verdict["pass"] else 1)
    else:
        code = 2
    print(f"--- {case} ---")
    print(f"exit={code} problems={problems[:2]}")
    if verdict is not None:
        for name, v in verdict["variants"].items():
            print(f"  {name}: pass={v['pass']} g3={v['g3']} "
                  f"exact={v['exact_1']}/{v['exact_32']}")
    return code


results = []

# G1: 3-repeat log passed off as 5-repeat (g3 file claims pass)
write_log(GAMING / "g1_3repeat", ["routing", "combine"], reps=range(3),
          settings=SETTINGS)
write_g3(GAMING / "g1_3repeat", ["routing", "combine"], g3pass=True)
c = run_case("g1_3repeat", ["routing", "combine"])
results.append(("G1 3-repeat-as-5 -> exit 2 (caught)", c == 2))

# G2: settings-subset log (32x1024 dropped: hides prompt-phase loss)
write_log(GAMING / "g2_subset", ["routing", "combine"], reps=range(5),
          settings=[s for s in SETTINGS if s != (32, 1024)])
write_g3(GAMING / "g2_subset", ["routing", "combine"], g3pass=True)
c = run_case("g2_subset", ["routing", "combine"])
results.append(("G2 settings-subset -> exit 2 (caught)", c == 2))

# G3: plain-engine log (prompt_ms 0.0) relabelled as the vllm check
write_log(GAMING / "g3_plain", ["routing", "combine"], reps=range(5),
          settings=SETTINGS, engine="plain", prompt_ms=0.0)
write_g3(GAMING / "g3_plain", ["routing", "combine"], g3pass=True)
c = run_case("g3_plain", ["routing", "combine"])
results.append(("G3 plain-engine log -> exit 2 (caught)", c == 2))

# G4: forged g3-vllm.json (claims pass) over a jsonl where muse-* is 10x slower
slow = {"muse-routing": 50.0, "muse-combine": 50.0, "muse-all": 50.0}
write_log(GAMING / "g4_forged", ["routing", "combine"], reps=range(5),
          settings=SETTINGS, period=slow)
write_g3(GAMING / "g4_forged", ["routing", "combine"], g3pass=True)
# independent oracle: recompute decode ranges from the jsonl
runs = [json.loads(li) for li in
        (GAMING / "g4_forged" / "muse-vllm.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()
        if json.loads(li)["kind"] == "run"]
for name in ("base", "muse-routing"):
    vals = [r["period_median_ms"] for r in runs
            if r["variant"] == name and (r["rows"], r["prompt"]) == (1, 128)]
    print(f"  oracle jsonl {name} 1x128 decode range: "
          f"{min(vals):.1f}..{max(vals):.1f} ms")
c = run_case("g4_forged", ["routing", "combine"])
results.append(("G4 forged-g3-over-slow-jsonl -> exit 0 (NOT caught)", c == 0))

# G4-control: same slow jsonl, honest g3 (fail) -> exit 1, still citable
write_log(GAMING / "g4_control", ["routing", "combine"], reps=range(5),
          settings=SETTINGS, period=slow)
write_g3(GAMING / "g4_control", ["routing", "combine"], g3pass=False)
c = run_case("g4_control", ["routing", "combine"])
results.append(("G4-control honest-g3-fail -> exit 1 (citable FAIL)", c == 1))

# G6 (extra): split single-slot calls dodge muse-all; audit each alone
for slot in ("routing", "combine"):
    case = f"g6_split_{slot}"
    write_log(GAMING / case, [slot], reps=range(5), settings=SETTINGS)
    write_g3(GAMING / case, [slot], g3pass=True)
    c = run_case(case, [slot])
    results.append((f"G6 split single-slot {slot} -> exit 0 (audit alone "
                    f"cannot see the missing combination)", c == 0))

print()
for title, ok in results:
    print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'} {title}")
print(f"\n{sum(ok for _, ok in results)}/{len(results)} gaming expectations met")
","path":"design-lab/tester-a/gaming_audit.py"}

text: Analyzing benchmark results across variants and settings, computing spreads and verdict stability from repeated runs.

tool_calls.name: write_file
tool_calls.args:
{"content":""""Tester-a noise test part 1 (CPU): repeat spreads + range-overlap boundaries.

Source: results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/muse-vllm.jsonl (3 repeats).
Logic mirrors bench/grader/time_candidates.py:163-197 (against + phases).
Output: design-lab/tester-a/noise-spreads.txt
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
LOG = ROOT / "results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/muse-vllm.jsonl"
MEASURES = {"decode": "period_median_ms", "prompt": "prompt_ms",
            "request": "wall_ms"}


def against(c, b):
    return "faster" if c[1] < b[0] else "slower" if c[0] > b[1] else "same"


def margin(c, b):
    """Gap between ranges; >0 separated, <0 overlap depth (ms)."""
    if c[1] < b[0]:
        return b[0] - c[1]
    if c[0] > b[1]:
        return -(c[0] - b[1])
    return -min(c[1], b[1]) + max(c[0], b[0])  # negative overlap depth


runs = [json.loads(li) for li in LOG.read_text().splitlines()
        if json.loads(li)["kind"] == "run"]
settings = sorted({(r["rows"], r["prompt"]) for r in runs})


def rng(name, rows, prompt, key):
    vals = [r[key] for r in runs
            if (r["variant"], r["rows"], r["prompt"]) == (name, rows, prompt)]
    return min(vals), max(vals), sum(vals) / len(vals), len(vals)


out = [f"log: {LOG}", f"n runs: {len(runs)}",
       "spread% = (max-min)/mean over repeats",
       "margin = gap between ranges in ms (>0 separated, <0 overlap)",
       ""]
out.append("== repeat spreads per setting (decode period_median_ms) ==")
for name in ("base", "compiled-routing", "muse-routing", "round2-submitted"):
    for rows, prompt in settings:
        lo, hi, mean, n = rng(name, rows, prompt, "period_median_ms")
        out.append(f"{name:16s} {rows:2d}x{prompt:4d}: n={n} "
                   f"{lo:7.3f}..{hi:7.3f} spread={(hi-lo)/mean*100:5.1f}%")
out.append("")
out.append("== prompt_ms spreads (routing prompt-slowdown region) ==")
for name in ("base", "muse-routing", "round2-submitted"):
    for rows, prompt in settings:
        lo, hi, mean, n = rng(name, rows, prompt, "prompt_ms")
        out.append(f"{name:16s} {rows:2d}x{prompt:4d}: n={n} "
                   f"{lo:9.1f}..{hi:9.1f} spread={(hi-lo)/mean*100:5.1f}%")

out.append("")
out.append("== range comparisons (candidate vs bar), all 3 measures ==")
pairs = [("muse-routing", "base"), ("muse-routing", "compiled-routing"),
         ("round2-submitted", "base"), ("round2-submitted", "compiled-3")]
boundary = []
for cand, bar in pairs:
    for rows, prompt in settings:
        row = []
        for m, key in MEASURES.items():
            clo, chi, _, _ = rng(cand, rows, prompt, key)
            blo, bhi, _, _ = rng(bar, rows, prompt, key)
            v = against((clo, chi), (blo, bhi))
            mg = margin((clo, chi), (blo, bhi))
            spread = max(chi - clo, bhi - blo)
            flag = ""
            if v == "same" or abs(mg) < spread:
                flag = "  <-- BOUNDARY" if v == "same" else "  <-- thin"
                boundary.append((cand, bar, rows, prompt, m, v, mg))
            row.append(f"{m}={v}(m={mg:+.3f}){flag}")
        out.append(f"{cand} vs {bar} {rows}x{prompt}: " + " ".join(row))

out.append("")
out.append(f"== {len(boundary)} boundary/thin cells (of "
           f"{len(pairs)*len(settings)*len(MEASURES)}) ==")
text = "\n".join(out)
(HERE_OUT := Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "noise-spreads.txt")\
    .write_text(text + "\n")
print(text)
","path":"design-lab/tester-a/noise_spreads.py"}

prompt:
Role: independent tester for design B
Objective: You are tester-b in a one-off design session. Do NOT run the muse-round skill. You test designer-b's design ONLY.

First read: design-lab/brief.md (the brief), design-lab/designer-b/design.md (the design under test), and skim design-lab/designer-b/prototypes/ (check_submit.py, check_claims.py, ledger_replay.py, checker.md, claim-schema.md, skill-patch.md) and design-lab/designer-b/test-results/ (what the designer claims). Reference for expected values: claude/findings/muse-round-2.md and results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json.

Session rules (binding):
- The repository's tracked files stay as they are: change, move or delete none of them, run no git command that changes anything, and commit nothing.
- You write ONLY in design-lab/tester-b/. To run the design's prototypes, COPY them into design-lab/tester-b/ first and run the copies (never edit the designer's files). All outputs go under design-lab/tester-b/.
- The GPU runs one job at a time: the prototype takes the lock in bench/grader/gpu_lock.py and waits its turn (import gpu_lock; gpu_lock.hold("<what>") for any GPU work you run directly). Load a model only inside such a run. The machine has 16 GB and pages heavily; a vLLM run takes about 10-12 minutes with 5 repeats. Sibling testers hold the lock too — queue waits are normal; record them.
- Never read credentials: .env files, ~/.config/muse, or any key store. No network calls.
- Every claim about the repository cites a path and line, and every claim about performance cites the result file it comes from; mark proposals, predictions and assumptions as such.

TESTS (all by running, not by reading):
1. CATCH TEST (live GPU): run the copied check_submit.py on round-2's dropped experts attempt (the extreme-prefill case): experts=muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7. WARNING: this kernel is 16-28x slower than compiled at prefill sizes, so the run may take much longer than 10-12 min — allow up to 60 min wall, record actual wall time, exit code, submit.json. Then judge: would this in-round check have caught behaviours 1-3? Expected from Claude's measurements (verify against claude/findings/muse-round-2.md, don't take my word): experts FAILs hard (prompt 6.6-14.5x slower, throughput down up to 83%). State PASS/FAIL and whether it matches Claude's post-round verdict. If the run is impractically slow (>60 min), stop it, report the partial evidence, and run check_submit.py on combine=muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1 instead (expect FAIL: decode +1.051ms at 32 requests).
2. DESIGNER'S OWN TESTS: re-run the designer's CPU tests from your copies (test_check_submit.py 5 tests, check_claims recast/conforming pair, ledger_replay.py); confirm or refute each claimed result in test-results/.
3. GAMING TESTS (CPU): feed the submit.json audit at least these gamed inputs and record each verdict: a 3-repeat log passed off as 5-repeat; a settings-subset log; a plain-engine log (prompt_ms 0.0); a forged g3 section that disagrees with the jsonl; a two-slot log missing muse-all; a wrong-tokens variant (exact false). For each: pass true/false and whether the game is caught. Also check the designer's admitted gap: is --tokens really unaudited (§9 risk b)?
4. NOISE TEST (CPU + your live log): from your live run's jsonl plus results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/muse-vllm.jsonl, report repeat spreads per setting and identify any verdict on a range-overlap boundary. Assess: would 5 repeats give a stable verdict here?
5. PROTECTED TESTS: verify and report with evidence: git status shows no tracked file changed; attempt format (spec.json + block-N.metal) untouched; grader JSON keys (g1, g2, beats_compiled, beats_baseline, timing_us_per_layer, phases_vs_compiled) untouched; the check goes through gpu_lock; one-grader-run-per-attempt is unaffected; Claude's post-round G3 path (time_candidates.py) is unmodified.

DELIVERABLE: Write design-lab/tester-b/report.md with: every command you ran, every result file, and what each showed (PASS/FAIL vs the design's claims). Then return a concise summary (catch verdicts, duration, gaming results, noise verdict, protected verdict) as your final result.

Read text file `design-lab/brief.md`.
1|# Solution design brief: make the Muse agent swarm pursue real efficiency, not its proxies (v1)
2|
3|## APPROVAL
4|- User approved this brief on 2026-11-04 (surucuonur). Decisions: the swarm may run end-to-end checks in-round through the GPU queue; Meta's Muse does the design work; from round 3 the launcher runs muse-spark-1.3-contributor with tool approvals off (ADR 0012, commit 1113c2d).
5|- Approved activity: one Muse Code session (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) whose lead starts its own helper agents, up to 12 at once, with no cost or time limit. Agents may prototype and test in design-lab/ (untracked, never committed) and run the measurement tools through the GPU queue. The repository's tracked files stay unchanged.
6|
7|## PROBLEM AND OUTCOME
8|- **Current problem:** two rounds of the Muse agent swarm (round 1: Muse Spark; round 2: Muse Wonder, 63 min, ~$58) produced no kernel that is a real efficiency improvement, while the swarm's own reports predicted gains. Five behaviours, each with evidence:
9|  1. **Treats unmeasured costs as free.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`: "Prefill speed is not timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart from time to first token", citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42`. The result: experts attempt-7 is 16–28× slower than the compiled reference at prefill sizes, and routing attempt-4 2.6–8.7× slower (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-*.json`). Prompts took 6.6–14.5× and 7–10% longer, and throughput fell by up to 83% (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §5).
10|  2. **Claims end-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Expected G3 = (compiled − candidate) µs × 20 layers (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md` *Ready to test*; `muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`). Round 1 predicted −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.98/+0.16/−1.76. Round 2 predicted −0.84 at each and measured −0.73/−0.74/+0.53 (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md`, `muse-round-2.md`).
11|  3. **Reasons inconsistently.** The same README says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then reports "Together (sum) −0.84 ms". Combine's −0.35 ms prediction is −0.07 to −0.09 from its own timing plus −0.27 to −0.29 borrowed from what `mx.compile` gains end to end. Measured: +1.05 ms with 32 requests.
12|  4. **Used the grader as a search loop (round 1).** 29 grader runs on experts for 4 counted attempts, 18 on attempt-1 with edits between (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md` §5). Fixed since skill v4: one run is one attempt; round 2 ran 13 for 13.
13|  5. **Persists with a failing design family.** All 7 experts attempts in round 2 are fused kernels that lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs per layer). The cause, too few threadgroups at 1 row, was already known from round 1. The harden loop says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and remove" (`.agents/skills/muse-round/SKILL.md:138`), and there is no rule for changing design.
14|- **Root cause** (likely; supported by the evidence above): inside a round, the swarm never sees the real objective. Its feedback is a per-slot proxy, the grader's piece timing. The real measurement, Claude's G3 over whole requests, arrives only after the round. The swarm's claims are self-reported and checked by no one before the summary.
15|  - *verified:* the rules forbid an in-round model run: `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md:152` "Load no model and start no other GPU work" and `SKILL.md:164` "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team".
16|  - *verified:* the goal is phrased as passing gates (`SKILL.md:20`).
17|  - *verified:* the verifier checks only exploration's inefficiency entries (`verifier.md`). No one checks the implementation phase's predictions, combination claims or Ready-to-test arithmetic.
18|  - *partly fixed:* ADR 0011 (commit `2090949`) now times the prefill (grader at 6 sizes, G3 with prompt and whole-request time, 5 repeats), so behaviour 1's specific gap is closed. The general habit, treating anything outside the measurement as free, is not addressed.
19|- **Intended outcome:** in round 3 and later, the swarm's statements about speed match what Claude's independent G3 then measures. It marks something ready only when it is a real improvement under the ADR 0011 rule (faster in one phase, prefill or decode, slower in neither, no whole request slower). It stops repeating a design that keeps failing at the same point.
20|- **Why now:** surucuonur asked how to fix "these essential problems and behaviour of these agents". The hackathon deadline is 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, about 11.5 h from 14:30 UTC on 2026-11-04. Round 3 should run with the fix.
21|- **Maturity:** hackathon research tool; judges read the repo, the skill and the round documents.
22|- **User's suggested approach:** none given. Claude has suggested an in-round end-to-end check and prediction rules; treat these as hypotheses, not constraints.
23|
24|## SCOPE AND SUCCESS
25|- **In scope:**
26|  - the round skill (`.agents/skills/muse-round/`: SKILL.md, the role cards, tracking.md);
27|  - the brief (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md`);
28|  - the measurement tools the swarm may call (`bench/grader/`, `bench/micro/` entry points);
29|  - `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` if needed;
30|  - the docs that describe these (ADR, glossary, `claude/muse-swarm.md`, diagrams).
31|- **Out of scope:**
32|  - changing the model or the engine;
33|  - Claude's post-round measurement process, beyond what it needs to compare claims;
34|  - running round 3 itself;
35|  - Muse Code itself.
36|- **Observable acceptance criteria:**
37|  1. Every speed claim in a round's READMEs and summary is either backed by a measurement made in the round, with its run file cited, of exactly what is claimed (the slot or combination, at the end-to-end level claimed), or labelled as a prediction and shown next to the measured value.
38|  2. No hypothesis reaches `ready`, and no attempt goes to *Ready to test*, unless an in-round check shows it improves under ADR 0011's rule, against the unchanged model and the compiled reference.
39|  3. Predictions count only the candidate's own measured effect, and a combination's effect is measured as a combination.
40|  4. Anything the swarm did not measure is listed as unverified, never assumed free or neutral.
41|  5. After a stated number of failures of one design at the same size or phase for the same cause, the next attempt changes approach, or the log records why not.
42|  6. Claude's post-round G3 agrees with the swarm's in-round measured claims within the noise of the repeats. This is the ultimate test.
43|- **Quality guardrails:**
44|  - proportionate and simple: surucuonur rejected sandbox and guard-hook hardening before (memory `muse-isolation-simple`);
45|  - keep the documents readable by judges;
46|  - keep Muse-facing instructions in the repo.
47|
48|## VERIFIED SYSTEM CONTEXT
49|- **Launch:** `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` (`:71` first prompt "Run the muse-round skill…", `:136` `muse exec … -c agents.execution_capacity=12`). One Muse Code session per round, in worktree `../Hackathon-muse` on branch `muse-agent`, on the Meta Model API. Round 2 ran `muse-wonder-1.0` with approvals on; from step 0 the default is `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` with approvals off.
50|- **The swarm** (`SKILL.md:22-38`):
51|  - the lead coordinates and commits, but never explores, builds or grades;
52|  - explorers write `exploration/territory-*.md` and `ineff-*.md`;
53|  - the verifier confirms or refutes inefficiencies;
54|  - builders write and grade one attempt each (`builder.md`);
55|  - boundary agents write and check a hypothesis's boundary (`boundary.md`);
56|  - shared docs and logs per phase (`tracking.md`), checkpoints commit them.
57|- **Steps** (`SKILL.md`): 0 find where you are, 1 starting point, 2 exploration, 3 the analysis, 4 implementation (open hypothesis → boundary → compete → collect → harden → close `ready`/`dropped`), 5 finish (READMEs, *Ready to test*, summary).
58|- **Measurement tools:**
59|  - **`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`:** G1/G2 bit-exact at 6 sizes; paired piece timing with a sign test; `beats_compiled`/`beats_baseline` per ADR 0011; takes the GPU lock; loads the model on every run (ADR 0010).
60|  - **`bench/grader/time_candidates.py`:** end-to-end check and G3.
61|    - Engines: `plain` (MLX) or `vllm`.
62|    - Variants: base, compiled-<slot>, muse-<slot>, muse-all, `--variant`.
63|    - G2 compares greedy tokens; G3 records decode step, prompt time (vLLM only) and wall time; `--repeats` defaults to 5; writes `g3-vllm.json`.
64|    - Duration: about 8.5 s per run on average in vLLM, so roughly 10–12 min per candidate with base and compiled at 4 settings × 5 repeats.
65|    - The plain engine has no prompt time yet (`bench/micro/repeat_fixes.py:prompt_ms`, `breakdown.run_plain`).
66|  - **`bench/grader/gpu_lock.py`:** one GPU job at a time; later ones wait.
67|- **Isolation and provenance:**
68|  - git hooks refuse Muse commits outside `muse-spark/`, changes to finished rounds' files, and merges;
69|  - `tools/provenance_check.py` audits authorship;
70|  - Claude merges each round, measures it independently (G3) and writes `claude/findings/muse-round-<N>.md`, which the next round reads as its starting point.
71|- **Round 3's starting point:** no baseline in any slot (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` *For round 3*).
72|- **Revision:** main at `2090949`, working tree clean apart from two uncommitted pilot files.
73|
74|## PROTECTED CONTRACTS AND BEHAVIORS
75|- Authorship separation: the Muse agent writes only in `muse-spark/`, only the lead commits, with the Muse co-author line; Claude never commits on `muse-agent`; hooks and provenance check stay.
76|- Finished rounds stay frozen (tags `muse-round-1`, `muse-round-2`).
77|- Muse Code only, swarm design (ADR 0007), no attempt limit (ADR 0006: "limitless"), one grader run per attempt, the GPU queue.
78|- Grading rules of ADR 0010/0011 (bit-exact at 6 sizes, both phases, hand-off via `max_rows`); G2's token check.
79|- Claude's post-round independent measurement remains the authority for baselines.
80|- The attempt format (`spec.json` + `block-N.metal`) and the grader's JSON verdict keys (`g1`, `g2`, `beats_compiled`, `beats_baseline`, `timing_us_per_layer`, `phases_vs_compiled`).
81|
82|## CONSTRAINTS AND OPERATIONAL REALITY
83|- **Machine:** M1 Pro, 16 GB, heavy swapping (19–20 GB swap in use); one GPU job at a time. vLLM needs `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` (now the default in `breakdown.py`) and Docker quit. 1-request vLLM timings are noisy (6–41% spread).
84|- **Time:** about 11.5 h to the deadline, including implementing the fix, running round 3 (~1–2 h), and Claude's measurement and findings (~1 h). The fix should be implementable and checkable in roughly 2–3 h.
85|- **Cost:** round 2 on Muse Wonder cost about $58; on the contributor model a round costs about $1 (round 1: $0.70). Claude never runs `start.sh` or calls the Meta API without asking.
86|- **Hard constraints:** the protected items above, and the deadline.
87|- **Preferences:** simple over airtight (no sandboxing or guard hooks); rules phrased positively for agents (writing-for-agents guidance).
88|- **Decided:** round 3 runs on `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, round 1's model, which ADR 0008 judged less capable than Muse Wonder, with tool approvals off. No one approves tool calls during the round, so rules must hold without a human watching. Instructions must be explicit and checkable, since a less capable model follows general advice less reliably.
89|
90|## FAILURE MODES AND FUTURE CHANGES
91|- **Goodhart risk:** any new check becomes the next proxy. A design must say how the swarm could game it.
92|- **GPU queue contention:** a 10–12 min end-to-end check blocks builders' grader runs.
93|- **Memory:** a vLLM run inside the round competes with Muse Code's own processes and may page.
94|- **Noise:** at 1 request, end-to-end verdicts are mostly `same`.
95|- **Partial rounds:** a session can stop mid-round, and checks must leave the shared documents consistent.
96|- **The model can ignore instructions:** round 1 ignored "one attempt per grader run" before it became an explicit rule.
97|- **Future:** more slots or a different model; rounds 4+; possibly other engines.
98|- **Prior pitfalls:**
99|  - independent piece timing hid latency (fixed by ADR 0010);
100|  - tolerances let the tokens change (fixed by ADR 0010);
101|  - prefill was untimed (fixed by ADR 0011);
102|  - G3 with 3 repeats falsely flagged unchanged phases (fixed with 5 repeats).
103|
104|## DESIGN EXPECTATIONS
105|- Deliver one coherent approach that fixes the root cause (the gap between the proxy and the objective, and unchecked self-reports) and covers behaviours 1–5, not one patch per symptom.
106|- Address whole-system effects: the GPU queue and round duration, memory, Claude's post-round role, the docs and judges.
107|- Cite repository evidence; distinguish verified facts from proposals.
108|- Specify the changes to the skill, cards, brief and tools, plus any new measurement entry point, at the level of what each says or does.
109|- Define how a future implementation is validated before round 3, without a paid Muse run if possible, and how round 3's own outcome would show success.
110|- Do not edit the repository's tracked code, data or configuration; prototypes and tests live in design-lab/.
111|
112|## UNRESOLVED ASSUMPTIONS AND STOP CONDITIONS
113|- **Decided (surucuonur, 2026-11-04):** the swarm may run an end-to-end check itself during the round, through the GPU queue. This replaces "Load no model…" (`tracking.md:152`) and "G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team" (`SKILL.md:164`) as needed. Claude's post-round G3 remains the independent authority.
114|- **Assumed (unanswered):** the fix must be ready for round 3 before 2026-11-05 02:00 UTC, implementable and checkable in about 2–3 h.
115|- **Assumption:** the Muse agent follows explicit, checkable rules better than general advice (round 2 kept "one run per attempt" once it was a rule).
116|- **Return BLOCKED if:** the design requires breaking a protected contract, or depends on a Muse Code capability not documented here.
