results.text:
Read text file `design-lab/designer-b/design.md`.
1|# Designer-B design: typed claims, an owned request check, and a checker
2|
3|*Perspective: contract-and-data-first. Worktree commit 1113c2d. No tracked
4|file changed; prototypes, fixtures and results live in
5|`design-lab/designer-b/prototypes/` and `design-lab/designer-b/test-results/`.*
6|
7|## 1. Status: READY
8|
9|The design is complete and implementable as skill v8 plus one new pinned tool
10|(`bench/grader/check_submit.py`) before round 3. It breaks no protected
11|contract, needs no Muse Code capability beyond what the brief documents, and
12|was prototyped and tested CPU-only (5/5 wrapper tests, claim-contract
13|fail/pass pair, ledger replay all green; no GPU run was needed — see §8).
14|
15|## 2. Context and diagnosis: verified facts, examples, cause, certainty
16|
17|### 2.1 The four data contracts that exist today
18|
19|I read the skill, the brief, both measurement tools and the round records
20|first-hand. Four contracts govern what the swarm can say about speed:
21|
22|1. **The piece contract (tool-owned, sound).** `bench/grader/check_candidate.py`
23|   computes per-size paired verdicts (30 repeats, 22 wins, one-sided sign test
24|   p<0.01 — `:52-57`, `:238-244`), per-phase verdicts and `beats_compiled`
25|   under the ADR 0011 rule (faster in one phase, slower in neither — `:247-263`).
26|   The verdict JSON keys (`g1`, `g2`, `beats_compiled`, `timing_us_per_layer`,
27|   `phases_vs_compiled`) are protected and stay.
28|2. **The request contract (tool-owned, sound but unreachable in-round).**
29|   `bench/grader/time_candidates.py` `g3()` judges each `muse-*` variant
30|   against `base` and its `compiled-*` bar over 4 workloads × 3 measures
31|   (`:168-197`, measures `:54`), with non-overlapping min–max ranges as the
32|   faster/slower test (`:163-166`). The swarm is forbidden to run it:
33|   `tracking.md:152` ("Load no model and start no other GPU work") and
34|   `SKILL.md:164` ("G3 and vLLM belong to surucuonur's team").
35|3. **The claim contract (untyped prose — the hole).** `tracking.md:153`
36|   ("Every number has a source ... or arithmetic shown in full") accepts shown
37|   arithmetic as a source. There is no distinction between a measured number,
38|   a prediction, and an assumption, and no rule tying a claim's level (piece
39|   vs whole request) to the file that may source it.
40|4. **The verification contract (half-built).** The verifier checks only
41|   exploration inefficiency entries (`verifier.md:5`, `:11`), by reopening
42|   cited files and redoing arithmetic (`:12-15`). Nothing checks
43|   implementation-phase numbers: the lead writes them unchecked (`SKILL.md:160-161`),
44|   and *Ready to test* (`SKILL.md:147`) requires an expected G3 change "with
45|   how you worked it out" — free-form, citable to arithmetic.
46|
47|### 2.2 The five behaviours as contract failures (all verified first-hand)
48|
49|- **B1, unmeasured costs priced at zero.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-152`:
50|  "Prefill speed is not timed — a slow-but-exact prefill branch is free apart
51|  from time to first token", citing ADR 0010's "Not covered" line. I found a
52|  second instance in the same family: `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-1/notes.md:30-31`
53|  ("per-pair reads at/above 60 rows are correctness-only cost (prefill is
54|  untimed)"). *Contract cause:* with no UNVERIFIED kind, the boundary's
55|  can't-see list (`boundary.md:13`) is a deferral list, and the only available
56|  move for an unmeasured cost is to narrate it as free. ADR 0011 closed the
57|  prefill instance (`:21-32`) but kept the shape: its own "Not covered" (`:51`,
58|  other chunk/row counts) is equally citable as permission.
59|- **B2, request gains from piece arithmetic.** Round-2 *Ready to test*
60|  (`muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:29-38`) computes
61|  "(compiled − candidate) µs/layer × 20 layers" plus borrowed offsets and
62|  publishes "Together (sum) −0.84/−0.85/−0.84 ms" (`:36`); the summary repeats
63|  it (`muse-spark/round-2/summary.md:8`). *Contract cause:* the skill demands
64|  a request-level number (`SKILL.md:147`) while forbidding the only
65|  measurement that produces one (`SKILL.md:164`) — arithmetic is the only
66|  compliant output, and `tracking.md:153` blesses it.
67|- **B3, inconsistent reasoning.** Same README `:13` ("per-slot wins are not
68|  assumed to compose") vs `:36` (the sum); combine's −0.35 ms is −0.07..−0.09
69|  own effect plus −0.26..−0.29 borrowed from `mx.compile`'s end-to-end gain
70|  (`:29`, `:34`). *Contract cause:* no rule says a combination must be
71|  measured as a combination, or that a prediction may count only the
72|  candidate's own effect. The tool side invites it too: per-part `mx.compile`
73|  in piece timing (`check_candidate.py:360`) vs whole-MoE `compiled-<slot>`
74|  end to end (`time_candidates.py:119-122`) are two different "compiled" bars
75|  with one name.
76|- **B4, grader as search loop (fixed, and the fix is the template).**
77|  Round-1 experts: 28 executed bash grader invocations for 4 counted attempts
78|  (18/3/6/1 — I accept the lead's settled count of 28 over the brief's 29).
79|  Skill v4's explicit rule (`builder.md:13`, "One grader run is one attempt")
80|  held in round 2 (13 for 13). *Lesson, verified:* explicit, checkable,
81|  countable rules hold on this swarm; norms don't. The design below copies
82|  that shape four times (pinned command, one file per claim, countable ledger,
83|  stamped check).
84|- **B5, one family pasted to the wall.** Round-2 experts attempts 1–5,7 all
85|  keep the per-pair fused structure ("Stay in attempt-1's fused single
86|  kernel", `round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-4/notes.md:16`) and all lose at
87|  1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs/layer, README `:9`); the unfused alternative is
88|  named only in the summary (`summary.md:9`, "so stop fusing") — after the
89|  attempts are spent. *Contract cause:* the harden loop (`SKILL.md:135-138`)
90|  has a continue rule ("Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can
91|  name and remove") and no data structure for repeated failure: builder
92|  sections end in "Next: one change", so the loop can terminate a change but
93|  never a family.
94|
95|### 2.3 Root cause and certainty
96|
97|**Root cause (high certainty — mechanism verified at both ends):** the swarm's
98|in-round feedback is untyped. Piece verdicts, request verdicts, predictions and
99|assumptions all travel as undifferentiated prose under one citation rule that
100|accepts arithmetic, while the only request-level measurement is forbidden
101|in-round and arrives post-round. Behaviours 1–3 are then not mistakes but the
102|only compliant outputs; behaviour 5 follows because repeated failure has no
103|record with a consequence attached. The miss-analysis ritual (builder.md:30)
104|proves the records *can* carry correction — every attempt carries predicted vs
105|measured — but no slot forces *Ready to test* to answer it.
106|
107|Two load-bearing tool facts sharpen the fix (both verified by reading, one by
108|my own test run): `g3()` ignores token exactness (`time_candidates.py:168-197`
109|reads only `kind=="run"` records), so a wrong-tokens variant can pass G3; and
110|the plain engine's `prompt_ms` is always exactly 0.0 with no verdict file
111|(`breakdown.py:468-484` records steps only for the decode loop;
112|`time_candidates.py:260-261`; lead's settled note 5). Any in-round check must
113|therefore be vLLM-only and must gate exactness itself.
114|
115|## 3. Recommended design
116|
117|One approach with four parts: **type every speed claim; pin the request
118|measurement into one owned command; check every claim before it closes; count
119|repeated failure per family.** Semantics first (what a number *is*), then
120|ownership (who computes, who cites, who verifies), then the tools that make
121|each step mechanical for an unattended contributor model
122|(ADR 0012:32: "explicit and checkable").
123|
124|### 3.1 The claim contract (the semantic core)
125|
126|Every speed number in a hypothesis entry, the implementation README, or the
127|summary is exactly one of (prototype text:
128|`prototypes/claim-schema.md`):
129|
130|- **measured / piece** — from a `grade.json` the builder wrote with the
131|  grader's `--out`: per-size times, `vs_compiled`, phase verdicts,
132|  `beats_compiled`/`beats_baseline`. Cites file + key; value matches verbatim.
133|- **measured / request** — from a `submit.json` the submission check wrote: a
134|  `g3` verdict, or a median with its [min–max] over the 5 repeats. Cites
135|  `submit.json` + key and the jsonl cell (variant, setting).
136|- **predicted** — everything else numeric: shows its formula, every input is
137|  the candidate's own measured number, and it stands next to its measured
138|  value with the miss (or "unvalidated: first of its kind").
139|
140|Two structural rules do most of the work. **Level integrity:** a grader file
141|never sources a request-level claim — piece timing cannot, by type, evidence
142|a whole-request sentence. **Nothing unmeasured is free:** anything not
143|measured goes under **Unverified** (at least the boundary's can't-see items,
144|prefill chunks of other sizes, decode row counts other than 1/8/32, 1-request
145|whole-request noise); the words *free/neutral/invisible* about an unmeasured
146|cost are a defect. Predictions count only the candidate's own measured
147|effect: no borrowed `mx.compile` offsets, no cross-slot sums — a sum across
148|slots is a prediction until a `muse-all` row measures it, and then it is
149|measured, not predicted.
150|
151|### 3.2 The submission check (measurement ownership)
152|
153|New tool `bench/grader/check_submit.py` (prototype:
154|`prototypes/check_submit.py`): a pinned, vLLM-only wrapper with the smallest
155|possible surface — `check_submit.py <out> SLOT=FOLDER...` and no other flags.
156|It calls `time_candidates.main` with the G3 argv (repeats 5, the 4 workloads,
157|256 tokens — the constants stay in `time_candidates.py`, which is untouched),
158|then composes **one** verdict file, `submit.json`:
159|
160|```json
161|{"check": "submit", "attempts": {"routing": "..."},
162| "invocation": {"engine": "vllm", "settings": "1x128,...", "repeats": 5, "tokens": 256, ...},
163| "exact": {"muse-routing": {"1": true, "32": true}}, "exact_pass": true,
164| "g3": {"muse-routing": "...same verdict dict as g3-vllm.json..."},
165| "target": "muse-all | muse-<slot>", "target_pass": true,
166| "medians": {"muse-routing": {"1x128": {"decode": {"median": 0.0, "min": 0.0, "max": 0.0, "n": 5}}}},
167| "pass": true, "unverified": ["prefill chunks of other sizes", "..."]}
168|```
169|
170|The wrapper adds what `g3()` lacks: the **token-exact gate** (every judged
171|variant `exact` at rows 1 *and* 32 — base exact by definition), a **per-cell
172|repeat audit** (exactly 5 runs per variant × setting, so a non-G3 run cannot
173|source a claim), the **invocation record**, and the **static Unverified list**.
174|The gate target is `muse-all` when more than one slot is submitted, else the
175|single `muse-<slot>`; a two-slot run whose verdict lacks `muse-all` fails
176|cleanly ("the combination was not measured as a combination"). Overall
177|`pass` = `exact_pass` and target `g3` true — the ADR 0011 rule, against base
178|and compiled, over whole requests. It takes the GPU lock through the existing
179|path. Out dir is `<round>/evals/<name>/`, committed with the round.
180|
181|### 3.3 The checker (verification ownership)
182|
183|New role card `checker.md` (prototype: `prototypes/checker.md`), mirroring
184|`boundary.md`'s two-task shape, CPU-only (never runs GPU work):
185|
186|- **Check a hypothesis** (before it closes `ready`): every measured row
187|  resolves verbatim to its `grade.json`/`submit.json` key; every prediction
188|  shows formula + own inputs + miss; Unverified covers the boundary items and
189|  the mandatory four; the ledger recomputes from the cited verdicts. Stamps
190|  `check: pass/fail` with file+line defects into the entry's new **Checks**
191|  section. `ready` needs the pass.
192|- **Check the submission** (once, over *Ready to test* + summary): the
193|  expected G3 change is a measured/request table from the submission
194|  `submit.json`; any cross-slot measured number cites `muse-all`; Unverified
195|  travels. The round finishes only on this pass.
196|
197|Ownership summary: tools compute verdicts; builders cite piece verdicts;
198|the lead cites request verdicts and owns claim tables and the ledger; the
199|checker verifies all three and changes no number it checks; **only Claude's
200|post-round G3 names baselines** — the in-round check gates, never grants.
201|
202|### 3.4 The failure ledger (family-change data)
203|
204|Each hypothesis entry gains a lead-kept **failure ledger**: one row per graded
205|attempt (family, loss sizes/phases vs compiled from `grade.json`, named
206|cause). Families are the lead's compete directions (`SKILL.md:131`); the lead
207|assigns each row's family at collect — builders only propose — so the
208|granularity is auditable in one place and ungameable by renaming. Rule:
209|**after 3 graded, timed attempts of one family lose at the same size or
210|phase, the next attempt uses a different family, or the log records why not
211|with the evidence.** The K=3 value is stated in the skill (see §4.5 for the
212|calibration). Harden's "repeat while cause nameable" keeps running *unless*
213|the ledger asks for a family change.
214|
215|### 3.5 Data flow and integration points
216|
217|Per hypothesis: builder writes kernels + `notes.md` (family, prediction with
218|own inputs + last miss) → grades once with `--out attempt-N/grade.json` →
219|lead commits attempt + entry at collect, appends the ledger row → on a
220|`ready` candidate, a builder runs the submission check (explicitly *not* an
221|attempt, creates no attempt number) → `checker-<n>` stamps → `ready` or back
222|to hardening with request-level evidence. At finish: lead runs the submission
223|check over all submitted slots at once (so `muse-all` exists), drafts
224|*Ready to test* + summary as claim tables, `checker-submit` stamps, commit,
225|"Round N finished".
226|
227|Consequences with teeth: a hypothesis whose check fails goes back to
228|hardening or drops — nothing failing reaches *Ready to test* (criterion 2).
229|If `muse-all` fails while singles passed (the documented interaction loss),
230|the combination is not submitted; the lead re-checks a passing subset (each
231|run committed under a new eval folder; claims cite the latest) or submits
232|nothing. Re-running the check on unchanged kernels to hunt noise is forbidden.
233|
234|GPU/queue integration: checks = (#ready hypotheses) + 1 submission, each
235|~13–14 min single-slot (tool-explorer extrapolation from the current-format
236|log), serialised on the existing lock. Builders keep writing Metal (CPU work)
237|while a check holds the GPU; only GPU runs wait. No lock, hook, sandbox or
238|`start.sh` change: capacity 12 absorbs one checker, and the check reuses
239|`gpu_lock.hold`.
240|
241|The exact text changes are prototyped as P1–P15 in
242|`prototypes/skill-patch.md`: goal sentence (`SKILL.md:20`), swarm table
243|(`:24-30`), harden/ready (`:135-140`), *Ready to test* (`:147`), summary
244|(`:153`), the G3 line (`:164`), hypothesis entry sections
245|(`tracking.md:106-113`), GPU rule (`:152`), number rule (`:153`), builder
246|prediction/`--out`/family rules (`builder.md:13,24,28,30`), boundary
247|can't-see wording (`boundary.md:13`), brief hand-off model (`:213-215`), plus
248|new `checker.md` and `check_submit.py`. `verifier.md` is deliberately
249|untouched.
250|
251|## 4. Why it solves the underlying problem and meets each acceptance criterion
252|
253|The root cause is untyped feedback: the proxy and the objective travel in the
254|same prose with the same citation rule. The design fixes that structurally —
255|the type of each number dictates which file may source it, the objective's own
256|procedure runs in-round behind one pinned command, and a second pair of eyes
257|owns the mapping. No behaviour below is fixed by advice; each is fixed by a
258|type, a gate, or a count.
259|
260|- **Criterion 1 (every claim measured-and-cited or labelled-predicted with
261|  its miss).** The three claim kinds are exhaustive: a speed number with no
262|  kind is a checker defect by construction. Measured rows resolve verbatim to
263|  `grade.json`/`submit.json` keys; predictions stand next to their measured
264|  value with the miss. *Evidence it bites:* the validator prototype
265|  (`prototypes/check_claims.py`) run over round-2's *Ready to test* recast
266|  reports 8 defects — missing verdict file, level violation, combination
267|  without `muse-all`, borrowed input, 3 missing Unverified items — while the
268|  conforming fixture passes (`test-results/check_claims-tests.txt`).
269|- **Criterion 2 (ready / Ready-to-test only on an in-round ADR 0011
270|  improvement vs unchanged + compiled).** `ready` needs `submit.json` `pass`
271|  (exact + target `g3` vs both bars) *and* the checker stamp; the submission
272|  needs the same over all submitted slots at once. A failing hypothesis
273|  returns to hardening or drops; a failing combination is not submitted.
274|  This closes B1's general habit (the check prices prefill and whole requests
275|  directly) and B2 (no arithmetic path to *Ready to test* exists).
276|- **Criterion 3 (predictions count own effect; combinations measured as
277|  combinations).** Own-inputs rule + `muse-all` requirement, both checker
278|  enforced. Round-2's combine prediction (own −0.07 plus borrowed −0.28) and
279|  "Together (sum)" both fail the prototype validator today (R4/R5 in
280|  `test-results/check_claims-tests.txt`). The tool side cooperates: the
281|  wrapper has no `--variant` flag, so nothing escapes judgment or crashes the
282|  bar lookup, and multi-slot runs always build `muse-all`/`compiled-all`
283|  (`time_candidates.py:125-127`).
284|- **Criterion 4 (unmeasured listed, never free).** The Unverified list is
285|  mandatory content with a mandatory minimum (boundary items + other chunk
286|  sizes + other row counts + 1-request noise), travelling from hypothesis
287|  entry to README to summary; *free/neutral/invisible* is defect language.
288|  ADR 0011's "Not covered" (`:51`) becomes the wrapper's static Unverified
289|  list — the same gap, phrased as "assume nothing" instead of citable
290|  permission.
291|- **Criterion 5 (N failures → change approach or log why not).** The ledger
292|  with stated K=3, lead-assigned families, mechanical loss signal (same run's
293|  `vs_compiled`). Calibration: replayed on round-2's parsed tracker, the rule
294|  triggers for experts after attempt-3 (six 1-row losses of one family —
295|  exactly where "stop fusing" belonged) and correctly stays silent for
296|  routing (losses scattered across sizes/families):
297|  `test-results/ledger_replay.txt`. K=2 would fire on noise at the twitchy
298|  1-row size (the findings note even within-run 1-row comparison "is close to
299|  the noise"); K=4 would have spent one more fused attempt for nothing.
300|- **Criterion 6 (in-round claims agree with Claude's G3 within repeat noise).**
301|  The in-round check *is* Claude's procedure (same tool, same argv, same 4
302|  workloads → same 1 GiB KV cache per `time_candidates.py:250`), plus an
303|  exact gate that only removes a divergence the brief's end-to-end G2 would
304|  catch anyway. Divergence is then bounded to noise + hardware drift, and the
305|  [min–max] medians make "within the noise" checkable as range overlap. This
306|  is the ultimate test and the design makes it a comparison of two ranges,
307|  not two stories.
308|
309|Goodhart accounting (brief §Failure modes): the pinned check cannot become a
310|*cheaper* proxy because it is the objective's procedure, not a new proxy —
311|gaming it means gaming G3 itself, which Claude re-runs independently. Each
312|known gaming move is closed by construction: flag-tuning (no flags; repeat
313|audit fails non-G3 runs — proven on the 3-repeat handoff log in
314|`test-results/check_submit-tests.txt` test 1), `--variant` escape/crash (no
315|such flag), selective median quotes (checker accepts verdict keys and
316|median+[min–max]+n only), plain-engine zeros (not a citable source),
317|`--baseline` shopping (both bars fixed), noise-hunting re-runs (forbidden;
318|every run committed, latest cited), lock bypass via `breakdown.py`
319|(claim-sourcing requires wrapper-produced files, so a bypass run distorts
320|only its own author's timings). Residual: overfitting to the 4 workloads —
321|named in Unverified, not solved (§9).
322|
323|## 5. What remains unchanged; migration/compatibility
324|
325|- **Unchanged tools:** `check_candidate.py` (same 6 sizes, same sign test,
326|  same verdict keys), `time_candidates.py` (the wrapper imports it; the G3
327|  rule lives in exactly one place), `slots.py` (attempt format, `max_rows`
328|  hand-off semantics), `gpu_lock.py`, `check_sizes.py`, `engine_table.py`
329|  (submission logs keep the `muse-vllm.jsonl` shape, so judges' tables still
330|  render), `start.sh` (no new flags; capacity 12 covers the checker).
331|- **Unchanged skill machinery:** explorer/verifier/boundary cards and the
332|  verifier's exploration loop (P14 — the checker that works keeps its narrow
333|  job), checkpoints and versioning, compete/collect/harden flow except the
334|  ledger row and the two gates, one-run-one-attempt, limitless attempts,
335|  lead-only commits, authorship separation (all swarm writes stay in
336|  `<round>/`, including `evals/` and `grade.json`), frozen rounds and tags,
337|  G2 bit-exactness and token checks, and Claude's exclusive authority to name
338|  baselines.
339|- **Unchanged data:** all committed verdicts, logs and round documents keep
340|  their meaning. Round-2-era claims are not restated (rounds are frozen); the
341|  starting-point step already compares "G3 effect against its prediction"
342|  (`SKILL.md:67`) and now also seeds each lineage's first residual.
343|- **Migration:** purely additive. One skill commit (v8: edited cards +
344|  `checker.md` + claim-schema section) and one tool commit
345|  (`check_submit.py`), both on main before round 3; `grade.json` appears in
346|  attempt folders from round 3 on (the checker's R2 expects it — old attempts
347|  without one simply predate the contract). The `check_candidate.py`
348|  docstring line "It never writes into the attempt folder" (`:11-12`) stays
349|  true in intent (the grader doesn't litter inputs there); the builder's
350|  explicit `--out` is the documented mechanism, and the file travels with the
351|  attempt it verdicts. Docs: one ADR (skill v8; also records the one-run rule
352|  that today lives only in skill text — the traceability gap the findings
353|  report flags), plus `muse-swarm.md`/glossary touch-ups.
354|- **Compatibility risk:** negligible. The wrapper's only coupling to
355|  `time_candidates.py` is `main` + constants + `attempt_arg`; if those move,
356|  the wrapper fails loudly at import, never silently.
357|
358|## 6. Failure handling, data integrity, security, operational concerns
359|
360|- **Check fails (target `g3` false or exact false).** Hypothesis: back to
361|  hardening with the request-level evidence appended to the ledger, or drop.
362|  Submission (`muse-all` fails): the combination is not submitted; lead
363|  re-checks a passing subset or submits nothing. An empty submission is an
364|  honest round, not a failed one — the checker still stamps the summary (no
365|  measured request numbers claimed, Unverified present).
366|- **Check crashes / partial round.** `submit.json` is written only after the
367|  repeat audit passes, so a half run never sources a claim. Eval folders are
368|  committed per checkpoint like attempts; a resumed session carries on from
369|  the READMEs' last versions (`SKILL.md:52`) with ledger and evals intact.
370|- **Noise.** Faster/slower stay range-non-overlap in both tools; the [min–max]
371|  medians travel with every measured request number so Claude's comparison is
372|  range overlap. 1-request whole-request `same`-passes are listed as noise in
373|  Unverified, never presented as gains. `prompt_ms: null` cells (a run with
374|  no prefill-0 step) fail the audit loudly rather than timing prefill at zero.
375|- **Memory.** vLLM checks run strictly sequentially (the lock serialises
376|  them); the wrapper adds no process beyond what `time_candidates.py` already
377|  runs. `machine_before/after` rows are already in the jsonl for Claude to
378|  discount paged runs; the checker does not gate on them (no flaky gate).
379|  Existing mitigations (Docker quit, `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` default
380|  in `breakdown.py:54`) stand.
381|- **Data integrity.** Verdicts are content-addressed by citation (file + key);
382|  the checker compares verbatim. Every check run is committed under a new
383|  eval folder — the same "history shows every try" safeguard as one-run-one-attempt
384|  (ADR 0006:29-31), extended to request runs. The wrapper never edits attempt
385|  folders or round docs; it writes only its out dir.
386|- **Security.** No credentials (the wrapper reads no `.env`, makes no network
387|  calls), no sandbox/hook changes per the simplicity preference, no new
388|  privileged path: the swarm could already run `time_candidates.py`; it now
389|  runs a narrower subset of it. Lock-file deletion and hold-forever DoS are
390|  pre-existing voluntary-lock limits, unchanged by this design and out of
391|  scope to harden.
392|- **Operational fit.** Round-2 shape (2 ready + 1 submission) costs ~3 checks
393|  ≈ 40 min serial on top of a ~63 min round — inside the evening's budget
394|  with Claude's hour. Worst-case subset bisection over ≤3 slots is bounded
395|  (~7 runs) and each run is visible in the log; realistically 1–2 extra runs.
396|
397|## 7. Credible alternatives considered and their trade-offs
398|
399|- **A: skill-only fix (prediction rules + a second verifier pass, no
400|  in-round check).** Cheapest on GPU time and simplest to write. Rejected: it
401|  leaves the objective unmeasured in-round, so request-level numbers stay
402|  arithmetic by necessity — behaviour 2's mechanism (demand a number, forbid
403|  the measurement) survives, and criterion 6 has no in-round counterpart to
404|  compare. The brief already decided the swarm may run the check; refusing
405|  the tool concedes the root cause.
406|- **B: extend the verifier instead of a new checker.** Fewer roles. Rejected:
407|  the verifier's loop, done-condition and write-ownership are all
408|  exploration-scoped (`verifier.md:9-25`); bolting implementation checks onto
409|  it complicates the one checker that works, and its invocations happen at
410|  different times (exploration end vs per-hypothesis close + finish). A narrow
411|  second card copies a proven shape (`boundary.md`) and keeps both loops
412|  checkable by the contributor model.
413|- **C: flags on `time_candidates.py` ("run vLLM with --repeats 5 ...")
414|  instead of a wrapper.** Smaller diff. Rejected: free flags are gameable by
415|  the agent they constrain (`--repeats 1` collapses ranges to points;
416|  `--settings` subsets shrink "every setting" and change KV bytes per
417|  `:250`; `--tokens 9` reweights decode/prompt), and the exact gate plus the
418|  repeat audit would have to live in prose. Pinning belongs in the tool when
419|  no human watches (ADR 0012:33). The wrapper also fixes the invocation for
420|  judges and Claude to audit.
421|- **D: ship the claim validator (`check_claims.py`) as an enforced tool.**
422|  Tempting — it is mechanical. Rejected for the required path: claims live in
423|  prose tables, so a validator needs a machine-readable claim file the swarm
424|  must also maintain — a second source of truth that can drift from the docs
425|  judges read, plus new validator-gaming surface. It stays design scaffolding
426|  (it proved the contract is checkable); the checker agent is the mechanism.
427|  Revisit if round 3 shows checker misses.
428|- **E: require `check_sizes.py` (25 in-between row counts) for `ready`.**
429|  Would shrink Unverified honestly. Deferred, not rejected: its GPU cost was
430|  never measured, and the boundary agent already reports those counts as
431|  unverified. Cheap follow-up once timed.
432|- **F: family counter on "same cause" prose instead of lead-assigned family +
433|  same size/phase.** Matches criterion 5's wording most literally. Rejected:
434|  cause sameness is not mechanically checkable — renaming the cause dodges
435|  the rule. Size/phase loss comes from verdicts (mechanical), family from one
436|  auditable owner (the lead); cause prose stays as the row's explanation,
437|  not its trigger.
438|
439|## 8. Implementation handoff
440|
441|Dependency order (each step states where; total ≈2–3 h per the brief's budget):
442|
443|1. **`bench/grader/check_submit.py` (new, ~120 lines).** Copy the prototype
444|   (`prototypes/check_submit.py`), delete the prototype header. Depends on
445|   nothing new. CPU-test with `prototypes/test_check_submit.py` (5 tests;
446|   last green run: `test-results/check_submit-tests.txt`).
447|2. **Live acceptance run (one GPU job, ~15 min, through the lock).** Claude
448|   (or a smoke session — never a paid round) runs the pinned check on round-2
449|   routing-4 + combine-1 and compares the `submit.json` ranges against
450|   Claude's post-round G3 medians for range overlap. Proves the live path the
451|   prototypes could not (designer-b ran **no** GPU job — siblings held the
452|   lock and every addition over the already-exercised `time_candidates` path
453|   is CPU-testable). Required before round 3.
454|3. **Skill v8 text (all in `.agents/skills/muse-round/` + brief).** Apply
455|   P1–P15 from `prototypes/skill-patch.md` verbatim (new `checker.md` from
456|   `prototypes/checker.md`, claim contract from `prototypes/claim-schema.md`);
457|   bump `SKILL.md:10` and `CHANGELOG.md` to v8; fix the stale v6 stamps the
458|   skill explorer found (`SKILL.md:80`, `tracking.md:33`). Commit on main
459|   before round 3 starts.
460|4. **Docs.** One ADR (skill v8: the claim contract, the check, the checker,
461|   the ledger; also records one-run-one-attempt for the first time);
462|   `claude/muse-swarm.md` swarm/ready description; glossary `Improvement`
463|   already encodes the rule — no change. Judges read the ADR + `checker.md` +
464|   one `submit.json`.
465|5. **Dry-run checklist (no paid Muse run — all re-runnable now).**
466|   - `test_check_submit.py` (5/5) + `check_claims.py` recast-fails (8
467|     defects) / conforming-passes + `ledger_replay.py` (trigger at experts
468|     attempt-3, silent for routing). Commands and outputs:
469|     `test-results/check_submit-tests.txt`,
470|     `test-results/check_claims-tests.txt`, `test-results/ledger_replay.txt`.
471|   - Post-edit re-read of the v8 skill for internal consistency (version
472|     stamps, card cross-refs, P6 vs `tracking.md:152` agreement).
473|   - The live run from step 2.
474|6. **Round-3 success read (criterion 6 operationalised).** Every `ready` has
475|   a `submit.json` + `check: pass`; every *Ready to test*/summary number has
476|   kind+level+source; Unverified lists present; ledger triggers or why-nots
477|   visible; Claude's post-round G3 ranges overlap the in-round ranges.
478|
479|- **Acceptance tests:** steps 2 + 5 (all must pass pre-round-3).
480|- **Regression tests:** round-3 transcripts show one grader run per attempt
481|  still holds; `tools/provenance_check.py` clean; finished-round tags
482|  untouched; `engine_table.py` still renders the in-round `muse-vllm.jsonl`.
483|- **Monitoring:** eval-folder count per round (check runs), checker fail
484|  count (contract friction), queue waits (transcript "waiting for the GPU"
485|  lines), round wall time vs the ~2 h envelope.
486|- **Rollback:** skill v8 is one commit — revert to v7 and round 3 runs the
487|  old rules (losing only the new gates); `check_submit.py` is additive —
488|  delete the file. A mid-round abort leaves `evals/` + ledger committed and
489|  versioned, resumable under either version.
490|
491|Prototype/test inventory (all under `design-lab/designer-b/`): 
492|`prototypes/check_submit.py` + `test_check_submit.py` (pinned wrapper; live
493|path reuses `time_candidates.main`, CPU-tested incl. real handoff log);
494|`prototypes/check_claims.py` + `claims-round2-recast.json` (fails, 8 defects)

502|## 9. Unverified assumptions, risks, decisions requiring the user
503|
504|- **Assumptions (explicit, each cheap to verify):** (a) the contributor model
505|  follows the checker card as reliably as it followed one-run-one-attempt —
506|  same shape (explicit, countable), but unverified until round 3; (b) a
507|  ~40-min check overhead fits round 3's evening — follows from the
508|  tool-explorer's 13–14 min extrapolation, which is itself a prediction from
509|  one log, not a fresh run (step-8.2 replaces it with a measurement);
510|  (c) builders tolerate writing `notes.md` predictions with inputs+miss —
511|  small addition to an existing ritual; (d) `muse-all` subset bisection
512|  terminates in 1–2 extra runs in practice.
513|- **Risks:** (a) **4-workload overfitting** — the pinned check and Claude's G3
514|  share workloads, so both can miss the same out-of-workload loss; carried in
515|  Unverified, mitigated only by `check_sizes.py`-style breadth later (E
516|  above). (b) **`--tokens` unaudited** — output tokens are pinned by argv but
517|  not recorded per run, so the repeat audit cannot re-verify them; fix is a
518|  one-line `tokens` field in `repeat_fixes.time_variants` (proposed, not
519|  required). (c) **In-round vLLM paging** under 16 GB + agent processes could
520|  widen in-round ranges vs Claude's; ranges make this visible, not fatal.
521|  (d) **Lead-assigned families** could be gamed by over-splitting (every
522|  attempt its own family); the history shows every assignment, and Claude's
523|  findings can call it out — no mechanical fix proposed, by the simplicity
524|  guardrail. (e) **Checker–lead collusion** is out of scope: both are the same
525|  model; the backstop is Claude's independent G3 plus committed, citable
526|  files.
527|- **Decisions for surucuonur:** (1) K=3 for the ledger trigger (2 is twitchier,
528|  4 spends more; replay supports 3). (2) Ship `check_claims.py` as an optional
529|  helper or leave it as scaffolding (recommended: scaffolding). (3) Whether
530|  the step-8.2 live acceptance run happens before round 3 (recommended: yes —
531|  it is the one untested path) and who runs it. (4) Whether to add the
532|  `tokens` audit field (E/b above) now or after round 3.

1|"""The in-round request-level check (DESIGNER-B PROTOTYPE — not the repo tool).
2|
3|Pinned wrapper around bench/grader/time_candidates.py's vLLM + G3 path:
4|
5|* engine is always vllm; repeats, settings and tokens are pinned to the G3
6|  values (5 / 1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024 / 256); there is no --variant flag,
7|  so every measured slot combination (muse-all) is judged and nothing escapes
8|  judgment or crashes G3's bar lookup;
9|* after the run it composes ONE verdict file, submit.json, holding the G3
10|  verdict, the end-to-end token-exact gate (which time_candidates.g3 ignores),
11|  a per-cell repeat audit, the invocation record, and the static UNVERIFIED
12|  list of what this check never covers.
13|
14|Usage (live; takes the GPU lock through time_candidates):
15|  .venv/bin/python check_submit.py <out-dir> SLOT=FOLDER [SLOT=FOLDER ...]
16|
17|CPU-only entry points used by the tests:
18|  compose_submit(log_path, g3_path, attempts, out_path, invocation=None)
19|"""
20|
21|import argparse
22|import copy
23|import datetime
24|import json
25|import sys
26|from pathlib import Path
27|
28|REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
29|sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "bench" / "grader"))
30|
31|import time_candidates as tc  # noqa: E402  reuse, never a fork of the G3 rule
32|
33|ENGINE = "vllm"
34|REPEATS = tc.G3_REPEATS          # 5
35|SETTINGS = tc.G3_SETTINGS        # "1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024"
36|TOKENS = 256
37|CHECK_ROWS = (1, 32)             # rows at which greedy tokens must equal base's
38|
39|# What this check never covers (ADR 0011:51 residual + documented noise).
40|UNVERIFIED = [
41|    "prefill chunks of other sizes (only the first chunk at 127/1,016/2,048 rows is graded; G3 runs 128/1,024-token prompts)",
42|    "decode steps with row counts other than 1/8/32",
43|    "request counts and prompt lengths outside the four workloads",
44|    "1-request whole-request time: repeats spread 6-41%, verdicts there are mostly `same` (ADR 0011:52)",
45|    "kernels outside the submitted slots; pairing with future submissions re-measures the combination",
46|]
47|
48|
49|def parse_settings():
50|    return [tuple(int(n) for n in s.split("x")) for s in SETTINGS.split(",")]
51|
52|
53|def expected_names(attempts):
54|    """muse-* variants a run of *attempts* must judge: per slot, plus muse-all."""
55|    names = [f"muse-{slot}" for slot, _ in attempts]
56|    if len(attempts) > 1:
57|        names.append("muse-all")
58|    return names
59|
60|
61|def load_records(log_path):
62|    records = [json.loads(line) for line in Path(log_path).open()]
63|    checks = {(r["variant"], r["rows"]): r for r in records if r["kind"] == "check"}
64|    runs = [r for r in records if r["kind"] == "run" and r["engine"] == ENGINE]
65|    return checks, runs
66|
67|
68|def exact_gate(checks, names):
69|    """{variant: {rows: bool}} for the judged variants; base is exact by definition."""
70|    exact = {}
71|    for name in names:
72|        exact[name] = {}
73|        for rows in CHECK_ROWS:
74|            rec = checks.get((name, rows))
75|            exact[name][str(rows)] = bool(rec and rec.get("exact"))
76|    return exact
77|
78|
79|def repeat_audit(runs, names, settings):
80|    """run counts per (variant, rows, prompt) cell; the pin is 5 everywhere."""
81|    cells = {}
82|    for name in ["base"] + [f"compiled-{n.removeprefix('muse-')}" for n in names
83|                            if not n.endswith("-all")] + names:
84|        for rows, prompt in settings:
85|            n = sum(1 for r in runs
86|                    if (r["variant"], r["rows"], r["prompt"]) == (name, rows, prompt))
87|            cells[f"{name}@{rows}x{prompt}"] = n
88|    # compiled-all exists exactly when muse-all does
89|    if "muse-all" in names:
90|        for rows, prompt in settings:
91|            cells[f"compiled-all@{rows}x{prompt}"] = sum(
92|                1 for r in runs
93|                if (r["variant"], r["rows"], r["prompt"]) == ("compiled-all", rows, prompt))
94|    return cells
95|
96|
97|def medians(runs, names, settings):
98|    """median + [min-max] per judged variant/setting/measure, for MEASURED citations."""
99|    out = {}
100|    for name in names:
101|        out[name] = {}
102|        for rows, prompt in settings:
103|            cell = [r for r in runs
104|                    if (r["variant"], r["rows"], r["prompt"]) == (name, rows, prompt)]
105|            out[name][f"{rows}x{prompt}"] = {
106|                m: {"median": statistics_median([r[k] for r in cell if r.get(k) is not None]),
107|                    "min": min_max([r[k] for r in cell if r.get(k) is not None])[0],
108|                    "max": min_max([r[k] for r in cell if r.get(k) is not None])[1],
109|                    "n": len(cell)}
110|                for m, k in tc.MEASURES.items()
111|            }
112|    return out
113|
114|
115|def statistics_median(xs):
116|    import statistics
117|    return statistics.median(xs) if xs else None
118|
119|
120|def min_max(xs):
121|    return (min(xs), max(xs)) if xs else (None, None)
122|
123|
124|def compose_submit(log_path, g3_path, attempts, out_path, invocation=None):
125|    """Build submit.json from a finished pinned run. No GPU. Raises SystemExit
126|    with a clean message (never a traceback) when the run cannot source a claim."""
127|    names = expected_names(attempts)
128|    verdict = json.loads(Path(g3_path).read_text())
129|    missing = [n for n in names if n not in verdict]
130|    if missing:
131|        raise SystemExit(f"submit: G3 verdict is missing {missing}; "
132|                         f"the combination was not measured as a combination")
133|    checks, runs = load_records(log_path)
134|    settings = parse_settings()
135|    exact = exact_gate(checks, names)

1|"""Claim-contract validator (DESIGNER-B PROTOTYPE — design scaffolding, not shipped).
2|
3|The shipped mechanism is the checker agent + the contract text; this script
4|exists to prove the contract is mechanical: every rule below is a file read,
5|a key lookup, or a string match a checklist can perform.
6|
7|Claim file schema (JSON):
8|  {"doc": "...", "candidate": {"attempt_dir": "...", "eval_dir": "..."},
9|   "claims": [{"id", "text", "kind": "measured"|"predicted",
10|               "level": "piece"|"request"|null, "slots": [...],
11|               "value": number|string, "source": {...}, "inputs": [...],
12|               "formula": "...", "residual": "..."}],
13|   "unverified": ["..."], "required_unverified": ["keyword", ...]}
14|
15|Rules (each returns defect strings; no defects = pass):
16|  R1 level integrity: measured/request cites only submit.json (+ its jsonl);
17|     a grader verdict file can never source a request-level claim.
18|  R2 measured/piece: cites a grader verdict file (--out JSON) + existing key;
19|     the value equals the file's (verbatim, 1e-9).
20|  R3 measured/request: cites submit.json verdict key (value match) + a jsonl
21|     cell (variant, setting) with exactly 5 runs.
22|  R4 predicted: has inputs[], formula, residual; every file input resolves to
23|     the candidate's own attempt dir or eval dir (own measured effect only).
24|  R5 combination: a measured claim spanning >1 slot cites muse-all.
25|  R6 unverified: every required keyword appears in some bullet; no claim text
26|     says free/neutral/invisible about an unmeasured cost.
27|"""
28|
29|import json
30|import sys
31|from pathlib import Path
32|
33|
34|def getpath(doc, dotted):
35|    cur = doc
36|    for part in dotted.split("."):
37|        if not isinstance(cur, dict) or part not in cur:
38|            return None, False
39|        cur = cur[part]
40|    return cur, True
41|
42|
43|def is_grader_file(doc):
44|    return isinstance(doc, dict) and "timing_us_per_layer" in doc and "g1" in doc
45|
46|
47|def is_submit_file(doc):
48|    return isinstance(doc, dict) and doc.get("check") == "submit"
49|
50|
51|def check_claim(c, candidate, repo):
52|    d = []
53|    kind, level = c.get("kind"), c.get("level")
54|    slots = c.get("slots", [])
55|    src = c.get("source", {})
56|
57|    if kind == "measured" and level == "piece":
58|        f = repo / src.get("file", "")
59|        if not f.exists():
60|            d.append(f"R2 {c['id']}: no verdict file {src.get('file')} "
61|                     f"(builder must grade with --out)")
62|            return d
63|        doc = json.loads(f.read_text())
64|        if not is_grader_file(doc):
65|            d.append(f"R2 {c['id']}: {src.get('file')} is not a grader verdict")
66|            return d
67|        v, ok = getpath(doc, src.get("key", ""))
68|        if not ok:
69|            d.append(f"R2 {c['id']}: key {src.get('key')} not in verdict")
70|        elif isinstance(c.get("value"), (int, float)) and abs(v - c["value"]) > 1e-9:
71|            d.append(f"R2 {c['id']}: value {c['value']} != file {v}")
72|
73|    elif kind == "measured" and level == "request":
74|        f = repo / src.get("verdict_file", "")
75|        if not f.exists():
76|            d.append(f"R1/R3 {c['id']}: no submit file {src.get('verdict_file')}")
77|        else:
78|            doc = json.loads(f.read_text())
79|            if is_grader_file(doc):
80|                d.append(f"R1 {c['id']}: LEVEL VIOLATION — a grader verdict "
81|                         f"cannot source a request-level claim")
82|            elif not is_submit_file(doc):
83|                d.append(f"R3 {c['id']}: {src.get('verdict_file')} is not a submit.json")
84|            else:
85|                v, ok = getpath(doc, src.get("verdict_key", ""))
86|                if not ok:
87|                    d.append(f"R3 {c['id']}: key {src.get('verdict_key')} not in submit")
88|                elif v != c.get("value"):
89|                    d.append(f"R3 {c['id']}: value {c['value']!r} != file {v!r}")
90|        log = repo / src.get("log_file", "")
91|        if "variant" in src and "setting" in src:
92|            if not log.exists():
93|                d.append(f"R3 {c['id']}: no log {src.get('log_file')}")
94|            else:
95|                rows, prompt = src["setting"]
96|                n = sum(1 for line in log.open()
97|                        if (lambda r: r.get("kind") == "run" and r.get("engine") == "vllm"
98|                           and (r.get("variant"), r.get("rows"), r.get("prompt"))
99|                           == (src["variant"], rows, prompt))(json.loads(line)))
100|                if n != 5:
101|                    d.append(f"R3 {c['id']}: cell {src['variant']}@{rows}x{prompt} "
102|                             f"has {n} runs, want 5")
103|        if len(slots) > 1 and "muse-all" not in json.dumps(src):
104|            d.append(f"R5 {c['id']}: COMBINATION — a measured {len(slots)}-slot claim "
105|                     f"must cite a muse-all row")
106|
107|    elif kind == "predicted":
108|        for req in ("inputs", "formula", "residual"):
109|            if not c.get(req):
110|                d.append(f"R4 {c['id']}: prediction needs {req}")
111|        if not c.get("inputs"):
112|            return d
113|        own = [candidate.get("attempt_dir", ""), candidate.get("eval_dir", "")]
114|        for i in c["inputs"]:
115|            if "claim" in i:
116|                continue  # chained to another checked claim in this doc
117|            p = i.get("file", "")
118|            if not any(p.startswith(o) for o in own if o):
119|                d.append(f"R4 {c['id']}: BORROWED input {p} — predictions count "
120|                         f"only the candidate's own measured effect")
121|    else:
122|        d.append(f"{c['id']}: kind/level must be measured+piece, measured+request, "
123|                 f"or predicted (got {kind}+{level})")
124|
125|    low = c.get("text", "").lower()
126|    if any(w in low for w in (" free", "neutral", "invisible")) and kind == "measured":
127|        d.append(f"R6 {c['id']}: assumption language about an unmeasured cost")
128|    return d
129|
130|
131|def check_doc(path, repo):
132|    spec = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
133|    defects = []
134|    for c in spec.get("claims", []):
135|        defects += check_claim(c, spec.get("candidate", {}), Path(repo))
136|    bullets = " ".join(spec.get("unverified", [])).lower()
137|    for kw in spec.get("required_unverified", []):
138|        if kw.lower() not in bullets:
139|            defects.append(f"R6 unverified: missing '{kw}' (never assume free/neutral)")
140|    return defects
141|
142|
143|if __name__ == "__main__":
144|    repo = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "."
145|    defects = check_doc(sys.argv[1], repo)
146|    print("\n".join(defects) if defects else "pass: every claim resolves")
147|    sys.exit(1 if defects else 0)

1|"""Failure-ledger replay (DESIGNER-B PROTOTYPE): apply the proposed K=3 rule to
2|round 2's own tracker lines, parsed — never transcribed — from
3|muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md.
4|
5|Rule replayed: within one hypothesis, when 3 graded, timed attempts of one
6|lead-assigned family lose at the same size or phase, the next attempt must
7|use a different family or the log records why not (with evidence).
8|
9|Signal substitution (explicit): round 2 predates paired per-size verdicts in
10|committed files, so loss = candidate median slower than compiled median from
11|the README tracker. Under skill v8 the signal is the same run's `vs_compiled`
12|(row of grade.json), which is stricter (sign test, not medians).
13|"""
14|
15|import re
16|import sys
17|from pathlib import Path
18|
19|REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
20|README = REPO / "muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md"
21|
22|ATT = re.compile(
23|    r"(\d+): (pass|fail)(?: \(G1\))?, (pass|fail|—)(?: \([^)]*\))?, "
24|    r"(?:—|([\d.]+) / ([\d.]+) / ([\d.]+) \(([\d.]+) / ([\d.]+) / ([\d.]+)\))")
25|
26|
27|def parse_tracker(slot_row):
28|    """{attempt: {'g1':..,'g2':..,'cand':(3 medians),'comp':(3 medians)} }."""
29|    out = {}
30|    for m in ATT.finditer(slot_row):
31|        n, g1, g2 = int(m.group(1)), m.group(2), m.group(3)
32|        a = {"g1": g1, "g2": g2}
33|        if m.group(4):
34|            a["cand"] = tuple(map(float, m.group(4, 5, 6)))
35|            a["comp"] = tuple(map(float, m.group(7, 8, 9)))
36|        out[n] = a
37|    return out
38|
39|
40|def ledger(hyp, attempts, family_of):
41|    rows, losses = [], {}
42|    trigger = None
43|    for n in sorted(attempts):
44|        a = attempts[n]
45|        fam = family_of(n)
46|        if a["g1"] != "pass" or a["g2"] != "pass" or "cand" not in a:
47|            rows.append((n, fam, "ungraded/ungraded-timed", ()))
48|            continue
49|        lost = tuple(s for s, (c, b) in zip((1, 8, 32), zip(a["cand"], a["comp"]))
50|                     if c > b)
51|        for s in lost:
52|            losses[(fam, s)] = losses.get((fam, s), 0) + 1
53|            if losses[(fam, s)] >= 3 and trigger is None:
54|                trigger = (n, fam, s)
55|        rows.append((n, fam, "lost at " + str(lost) if lost else "no loss", lost))
56|    return rows, losses, trigger
57|
58|
59|def main():
60|    lines = README.read_text().splitlines()
61|    hyp1 = next(l for l in lines if "hyp-1-experts-exact" in l)
62|    hyp2 = next(l for l in lines if "hyp-2-routing-exact" in l)
63|    a1, a2 = parse_tracker(hyp1), parse_tracker(hyp2)
64|    assert len(a1) == 7 and len(a2) == 4, (len(a1), len(a2))
65|
66|    # Lead-assigned families for the replay. hyp-1: every attempt keeps the
67|    # per-pair fused structure ("Stay in attempt-1's fused single kernel",
68|    # round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-4/notes.md:16; hyp-1 Decision "Six
69|    # attempts across four packings", hyp-1-experts-exact.md:493) -> one family.
70|    # hyp-2: attempt-2 (scalar sums, G2 fail) and attempt-3 (unstaged) are
71|    # declared different families by the lead; 1 and 4 share "staged-fused".
72|    rows1, losses1, t1 = ledger("hyp-1", a1, lambda n: "fused-per-pair")
73|    rows2, losses2, t2 = ledger("hyp-2", a2,
74|                                lambda n: {2: "scalar-sums", 3: "unstaged"}
75|                                .get(n, "staged-fused"))
76|
77|    for hyp, rows, losses, t in (("hyp-1-experts", rows1, losses1, t1),
78|                                 ("hyp-2-routing", rows2, losses2, t2)):
79|        print(f"## {hyp}: failure ledger (family, loss sizes vs compiled median)")
80|        for n, fam, what, _ in rows:
81|            print(f"  attempt-{n} [{fam}]: {what}")
82|        print(f"  loss counts: {dict(sorted(losses.items()))}")
83|        if t:
84|            print(f"  TRIGGER after attempt-{t[0]}: 3 losses of family '{t[1]}' "
85|                  f"at size {t[2]} -> attempt-{t[0] + 1} must change family or log why not")
86|        else:
87|            print("  no trigger: losses never reach 3 at one size for one family")
88|        print()
89|
90|    assert t1 == (3, "fused-per-pair", 1), t1
91|    assert t2 is None, t2
92|    print("ledger replay: trigger fires for experts after attempt-3; "
93|          "routing correctly untriggered")
94|
95|
96|if __name__ == "__main__":
97|    main()

Read text file `design-lab/designer-b/prototypes/checker.md`.
1|# Checker (DESIGNER-B PROTOTYPE — new role card for skill v8)
2|
3|*Prototype of `.agents/skills/muse-round/checker.md`. Mirrors `boundary.md`'s
4|two-task shape. The checker never runs GPU work: it reads result files others
5|wrote, like the boundary agent's "no new grader run" precedent.*
6|
7|You are `checker-<n>`, the checker of hypothesis `<n>` — or `checker-submit`
8|for the round's submission. A speed number is trusted only when you have tied
9|it to the run that produced it. The lead's prompt names your task: *check a
10|hypothesis* or *check the submission*. [tracking.md](tracking.md) describes
11|the documents and the rules; its *Claim contract* section defines the three
12|claim kinds you enforce.
13|
14|## Task: check a hypothesis
15|
16|The lead sends you when a hypothesis is ready to close `ready` (and only
17|then — dropped hypotheses need no check). Inputs: the hypothesis entry, its
18|best attempt's `grade.json`, and its `submit.json` with the `muse-vllm.jsonl`
19|behind it.
20|
21|1. **Every measured piece number resolves.** For each row marked *measured /
22|   piece* in the entry's tables: open the cited `grade.json`, find the cited
23|   key (`timing_us_per_layer.<size>.<column>`, `vs_compiled`,
24|   `phases_vs_compiled`, `beats_compiled`), and compare verbatim. A number
25|   from any other file is not a measured piece number.
26|2. **Every measured request number resolves.** For each row marked *measured /
27|   request*: open the cited `submit.json`, find the cited `g3` verdict or
28|   `medians` row (median with its [min–max] and n=5), and compare verbatim;
29|   confirm the cited jsonl cell exists. A request-level number citing a
30|   grader file fails — piece timing never sources a request claim.
31|3. **Every prediction is labelled and owned.** For each row marked
32|   *predicted*: it shows its formula, every input is the candidate's own
33|   `grade.json`/`submit.json` (never another variant's gain, never a sum
34|   across slots), and it stands next to its measured value with the miss
35|   (or "unvalidated: first of its kind"). A prediction borrowing another
36|   variant's measured gain fails.
37|4. **Nothing unmeasured is free.** The entry's *Unverified* list names every
38|   cost this hypothesis did not measure: at least the boundary's can't-see
39|   items, prefill chunks of other sizes, decode row counts other than 1/8/32,
40|   and 1-request whole-request noise. A missing item fails. The words *free*,
41|   *neutral* or *invisible* about an unmeasured cost fail.
42|5. **The ledger adds up.** Recompute the hypothesis's failure ledger from the
43|   cited `grade.json` verdicts (`vs_compiled` per size): three timed losses of
44|   one family at one size or phase must show the family change or the logged
45|   why-not. A missing trigger fails.
46|6. **Stamp it.** Append to the entry's **Checks** section: `check: pass`, or
47|   `check: fail` with each defect as file + line + what is wrong. Log it and
48|   return. `ready` needs your `pass`; on `fail` the lead fixes the entry (or
49|   the attempt) and sends you again.
50|
51|## Task: check the submission
52|
53|The lead sends you once, when the implementation README's *Ready to test* and
54|`summary.md` are drafted. Inputs: those two documents plus every submitted
55|hypothesis's `submit.json` and the submission `submit.json` (with `muse-all`
56|when more than one slot is submitted).
57|
58|1. Run steps 1–4 above over both documents. The expected G3 change is a
59|   *measured / request* table from the submission `submit.json` (median with
60|   [min–max], verdict per setting); any other number there is marked
61|   *predicted* with its formula, own inputs and miss.
62|2. A *measured* number spanning more than one slot cites a `muse-all` row.
63|   A cross-slot sum without one fails.
64|3. The submission's *Unverified* list covers every hypothesis's list. A
65|   dropped cost fails.
66|4. Stamp both documents (`check: pass` / `check: fail` with defects), log it
67|   and return. The round finishes only on your `pass`. If no hypothesis
68|   closed `ready`, there is no submission check: verify the documents claim
69|   no measured request numbers and still carry Unverified.
70|
71|## What you write
72|
73|The hypothesis entry's **Checks** section, the `check:` stamps on the README
74|and the summary, and log lines. You change no number you check.

1|# Claim contract + table schemas (DESIGNER-B PROTOTYPE — new tracking.md section)
2|
3|*Prototype text for skill v8. Replaces the second half of tracking.md:153
4|("Every number has a source...") for speed numbers; other numbers keep that
5|rule unchanged.*
6|
7|## Claim contract (speed numbers only)
8|
9|Every speed number in a hypothesis entry, the implementation README, or the
10|summary is exactly one of:
11|
12|- **measured / piece** — a number from a `grade.json` the builder wrote with
13|  the grader's `--out`: a per-size time, a `vs_compiled` verdict, a phase
14|  verdict, `beats_compiled`/`beats_baseline`. It cites file + key, and the
15|  value matches the file verbatim.
16|- **measured / request** — a number from a `submit.json` the submission check
17|  wrote: a `g3` verdict (`faster`/`same`/`slower` per setting, `pass` per
18|  bar), or a median with its [min–max] over the 5 repeats. It cites
19|  `submit.json` + key and the jsonl cell (variant, setting). **Level
20|  integrity:** a grader file never sources a request-level claim.
21|- **predicted** — anything else with a number: it shows its formula, every
22|  input is the candidate's own measured number (never another variant's gain,
23|  never a sum across slots), and it stands next to its measured value with
24|  the miss once measured (or "unvalidated: first of its kind").
25|
26|Anything the swarm did not measure is listed under **Unverified**, never
27|assumed free or neutral. At least: the boundary's can't-see items, prefill
28|chunks of other sizes, decode row counts other than 1/8/32, and 1-request
29|whole-request noise.
30|
31|## Table schemas
32|
33|Decision (hypothesis entry), one row per number that matters:
34|
35|| Claim | Kind | Level | Value | Source (file + key / formula) | Measured vs predicted |
36||---|---|---|---|---|---|
37|| decode @1 row vs compiled | measured | piece | faster, 49.8 vs 65.1µs | `.../attempt-4/grade.json : timing_us_per_layer.rows 1` | — |
38|| request decode @1x128 vs base | measured | request | faster, −0.48 [−0.51,−0.44]ms | `.../evals/submit.json : g3.muse-routing.base + medians` | — |
39|| request delta if prefill matched | predicted | — | −0.55ms | own piece delta × layers (formula); inputs: rows above | miss +0.07 |
40|
41|Ready to test (implementation README): the same columns, one row per
42|slot and one for the submission. With more than one slot, the submission row
43|is measured and cites a `muse-all` row; without a `muse-all` row there is no
44|measured submission number — a sum is a prediction and is labelled one.
45|
46|Summary: the expected G3 change repeats the Ready-to-test measured rows (same
47|sources); predictions repeat with their misses. Unverified bullets travel
48|with every table.

Read text file `claude/findings/muse-round-2.md`.
1|# Round 2 of the Muse agent, measured
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|In round 2 (2026-11-04, 03:13 to 04:16 UTC), the Muse agent (Muse Wonder, `muse-wonder-1.0`, at `max` effort) ran skill version 5. It started from [Claude's measurement of round 1](muse-round-1.md), under the stricter grader of [ADR 0010](../adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md):
6|- G2 asks for outputs bit-exact with MLX's reference, at decode and prefill sizes;
7|- the piece timing chains the 20 layers.
8|
9|Its summary, [muse-spark/round-2/summary.md](../../muse-spark/round-2/summary.md), submits two kernels for G3:
10|- **routing:** `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/routing/attempt-4`;
11|- **combine:** `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1`.
12|
13|For experts it keeps MLX's reference. Its best experts kernel, attempt-7, was bit-exact and faster with 8 and 32 rows, but it was dropped for being slower with 1 row. The summary predicted the submission would shorten the decode step by 0.84 ms at 1, 8 and 32 requests.
14|
15|This is Claude's independent measurement, on main after merging round 2 (`4033cae`):
16|- **re-grading** the two submitted kernels and experts attempt-7;
17|- **checking all three at 25 row counts** that G2 doesn't test;
18|- **checking tokens end to end and timing the decode step (G3),** in plain MLX and vLLM.
19|
20|G3 timed each kernel alone, the submission, experts attempt-7 added to it, round 1's three kernels and the compiled references, all in the same run. A last run timed every pairing of round 2's three kernels, to find where they interfere.
21|
22|**Where everything is.** The raw data is in [results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/](../../results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/), with the pairings in [results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2-pairs/](../../results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2-pairs/) and the whole-request comparison in [results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/](../../results/runs/2026-11-04-engine-comparison/). The scripts are:
23|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py`, the grader;
24|- `bench/grader/check_sizes.py`, G2's checks at the extra row counts;
25|- `bench/grader/time_candidates.py`, the end-to-end check and G3.
26|
27|**The machine.** The same M1 Pro, with Docker quit. 19.5 to 20.6 GB of 20.5 to 21.5 GB of swap were in use (`machine-*.txt`). vLLM ran with `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0`.
28|
29|## Summary
30|
31|- **Every kernel round 2 graded is correct.** The two submitted kernels and experts attempt-7 are bit-exact with MLX's reference:
32|  - at the grader's six sizes;
33|  - at 25 more row counts, from 2 to 1,500 rows, on either side of MLX's switches at 16 and 60 rows, and inside each of routing's row-count regimes;
34|  - end to end, where the model's greedy tokens are identical in plain MLX and in vLLM, at 1 and 32 requests, for every round-2 variant.
35|
36|  Round 1's kernels, timed in the same runs as a control, still change the tokens with 32 requests.
37|- **routing attempt-4 passed G3 as it stood, on decode steps.** It is faster than both the unchanged model and the compiled reference at 1, 8 and 32 requests, in both engines. In vLLM it saves 0.47, 0.43 and 0.54 ms per step (8.7%, 3.0% and 1.8%). It is the project's first Muse kernel that passed every rule of its time. Over whole requests its gain is smaller, since it processes prompts 7–10% slower: throughput rises 10.2% with 1 request and 1.8% with 8, is flat with 32 and falls 3.5% with 32 requests of 1,024-token prompts ([section 5](#5-whole-requests-prompts-and-throughput)). Under the rule set after this measurement, that an improvement must hold in both phases ([ADR 0011](../adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)), it fails, so it is no baseline for round 3 ([For round 3](#for-round-3-baselines-and-starting-points)).
38|- **combine attempt-1 fails G3.** The grader timed it faster than the compiled reference at every row count. In the model it is slower than the unchanged step with 32 requests (+1.05 ms in vLLM, +1.17 ms in plain MLX), and no faster than the compiled reference with 8.

148|## 6. How round 2 worked
149|
150|- **Time:** 63 minutes; the lead and 34 helpers; 983 model calls. 981 were `muse-wonder-1.0`, and 2 were Muse Code's reminder agents on `muse-spark-1.3` (`muse-spark/transcripts/01a1a48b-e027-7462-898f-0b01290c8c9a.summary.json`).
151|- **Tokens:** 125.6M input, of which 121.1M were cached, and 0.77M output. At Muse Wonder's prices that is about $58: $18 uncached input, $24 cached input and $15 output. It would be about $65 if the 0.36M reasoning tokens are billed on top of the output.
152|- **Attempts:** one grader run per attempt, 13 in total, as the skill asks. Every graded attempt is committed.
153|- **What it got right:** it read round 1's measurement, made exactness its first goal, and met it in every slot. Its explorers found that routing's reference changes its matrix-product strategy in row-count regimes, and its builder copied each regime exactly. Those regimes are what section 2 tests.
154|- **What it missed:** its prediction for combine (−0.35 ms) and for the submission at 32 requests. The chained piece timing still doesn't show combine's cost in the step.
155|
156|## For round 3: baselines and starting points
157|
158|**The rule,** from round 3 ([ADR 0011](../adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)): a slot's baseline is its best attempt so far that passes the current G2, has `beats_compiled` true in the grader, and passes G3. Both of those now judge two phases, decode and prefill: faster in one, slower in neither, and in G3 no whole request slower, against the unchanged model and the compiled reference. An attempt that passes G2 but not the rest is a starting point, not a bar: making it the bar would ask a fix to beat it where it already wins.
159|

165|| `combine` | none | `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1` | 0.86 / 0.85 / 0.93, faster | 0.95 / 0.83 / 0.52, faster | Its decode step in G3 was 1.05 ms slower than the unchanged model's with 32 requests, for a reason the grader doesn't show (section 3). |

171|1. **experts with 1 row.** attempt-7 keeps its 8- and 32-row speed and loses at 1 row, as every fused design in round 2 did (92 to 110 µs per layer chained, against 73 to 87 for the compiled reference, in round 2's runs). 172|2. **Why combine attempt-1 costs 1 ms in the step with 32 requests** and not in the grader.
173|3. **Why all three slots replaced at once lose 2.8 ms with 8 requests,** when every pair adds up (section 4).

1|"""One GPU job at a time: the exclusive lock every grader entry point takes.
2|
3|Muse Spark's builder agents and Claude run these scripts on the same M1 Pro
4|GPU, and two runs at once distort each other's timings. A run that finds the
5|GPU busy says so and waits its turn, so runs queue and never overlap. The lock
6|file is in /tmp, so the main checkout and the Muse Spark worktree share it, and
7|the operating system releases it when the process ends, however it ends.
8|"""
9|
10|import fcntl
11|import os
12|import sys
13|
14|LOCK = "/tmp/mobilemoe-gpu.lock"
15|_held = []  # keeps the locked file open for the life of the process
16|
17|
18|def hold(job):
19|    """Take the GPU for this process, waiting while another run has it."""
20|    f = open(LOCK, "a+")
21|    try:
22|        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
23|    except BlockingIOError:
24|        f.seek(0)
25|        holder = f.read().strip() or "another run"
26|        print(f"{job}: waiting for the GPU ({holder})", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
27|        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
28|    f.seek(0)
29|    f.truncate()
30|    f.write(f"pid {os.getpid()}: {job}\n")
31|    f.flush()
32|    _held.append(f)

76|    wrap = {"routing": as_routing, "combine": as_combine, "experts": as_experts}
77|    return {p: wrap[p](fn) for p, fn in parts.items()}
78|
79|
80|def attempt_arg(value):
81|    """SLOT=FOLDER -> (slot, folder)."""
82|    slot, sep, folder = value.partition("=")
83|    if not sep or slot not in slots.SLOTS:
84|        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
85|            f"{value!r}: give SLOT=FOLDER, SLOT one of {', '.join(slots.SLOTS)}"
86|        )
87|    return slot, Path(folder)
88|
89|
90|def variant_arg(value):
91|    """NAME:SLOT=FOLDER[+SLOT=FOLDER...] -> (name, [(slot, folder), ...])."""
92|    name, sep, spec = value.partition(":")
93|    if not sep or not name:
94|        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(
95|            f"{value!r}: give NAME:SLOT=FOLDER[+SLOT=FOLDER...]"
96|        )
97|    return name, [attempt_arg(a) for a in spec.split("+")]
98|
99|
100|def implementations(attempts):
101|    """make_moe_call keyword arguments for (slot, folder) pairs; `compiled` is the reference."""
102|    fns = {}
103|    for slot, folder in attempts:
104|        if str(folder) == "compiled":
105|            fns |= {p: mx.compile(slots.REFERENCE[p]) for p in parts(slot)}
106|        else:
107|            fns |= implementation(load(folder, slot))
108|    return fns
109|
110|
111|class Variants:
112|    def __init__(self, attempts, extra=()):
113|        """*attempts*: (slot, folder) pairs whose slots share no part; *extra*:
114|        (name, attempts) pairs, each its own variant."""
115|        self.original = mobilemoe.MoE.__call__
116|        self.calls = {"base": self.original}
117|        compiled, muse = {}, {}
118|        for slot, folder in attempts:
119|            ref = {p: mx.compile(slots.REFERENCE[p]) for p in parts(slot)}
120|            fns = implementation(load(folder, slot))
121|            self.calls[f"compiled-{slot}"] = slots.make_moe_call(**ref)
122|            self.calls[f"muse-{slot}"] = slots.make_moe_call(**fns)
123|            compiled |= ref
124|            muse |= fns
125|        if len(attempts) > 1:
126|            self.calls["compiled-all"] = slots.make_moe_call(**compiled)
127|            self.calls["muse-all"] = slots.make_moe_call(**muse)
128|        for name, more in extra:
129|            if name in self.calls:
130|                raise SystemExit(f"--variant {name}: that name is taken")
131|            self.calls[name] = slots.make_moe_call(**implementations(more))
132|        self.names = list(self.calls)
133|
134|    def apply(self, name):
135|        mobilemoe.MoE.__call__ = self.calls[name]
136|
137|
138|def plain_checks(model, variants):
139|    """Greedy tokens over TOKENS steps and one step's kernel count, per variant."""
140|    from mlx_lm.models.cache import make_prompt_cache
141|
142|    out = {}
143|    for rows in (1, 32):
144|        tokens = {}
145|        for name in variants.names:
146|            variants.apply(name)
147|            mx.random.seed(rows)
148|            ids = mx.random.randint(0, 100000, (rows, 128))
149|            cache = make_prompt_cache(model)
150|            seq = [bd.prefill(model, ids, cache)]
151|            for _ in range(TOKENS - 1):
152|                seq.append(bd.greedy(model(seq[-1], cache=cache)))
153|                mx.eval(seq[-1])
154|            tokens[name] = mx.concatenate(seq, axis=1).tolist()
155|            out[(name, rows)] = rf.count_ops([model(seq[-1], cache=cache)])
156|        for name in variants.names[1:]:
157|            out[(name, rows)]["exact"] = tokens[name] == tokens["base"]
158|            out[(name, rows)].update(rf.divergence(tokens[name], tokens["base"]))
159|    variants.apply("base")
160|    return out
161|
162|
163|def against(c, b):
164|    """Two (min, max) ranges of a time: "faster" when c's lies below b's, "slower" above."""
165|    return "faster" if c[1] < b[0] else "slower" if c[0] > b[1] else "same"
166|
167|
168|def g3(log, names, settings, out):
169|    """Each muse-* variant against base and its compiled-* counterpart, from *log*'s vLLM runs."""
170|    runs = [r for r in map(json.loads, log.open()) if r["kind"] == "run" and r["engine"] == "vllm"]
171|
172|    def ranges(name, rows, prompt):
173|        rs = [r for r in runs if (r["variant"], r["rows"], r["prompt"]) == (name, rows, prompt)]
174|        return {m: (min(r[k] for r in rs), max(r[k] for r in rs)) for m, k in MEASURES.items()}
175|
176|    verdict = {}
177|    for name in [n for n in names if n.startswith("muse-")]:
178|        verdict[name] = {}
179|        for bar in ("base", "compiled-" + name.removeprefix("muse-")):
180|            settings_v = {
181|                f"{rows}x{prompt}": {
182|                    m: against(c, b)
183|                    for (m, c), b in zip(ranges(name, rows, prompt).items(), ranges(bar, rows, prompt).values())
184|                }
185|                for rows, prompt in settings
186|            }
187|            phases = {
188|                m: "faster" if all(v[m] == "faster" for v in settings_v.values())
189|                else "slower" if any(v[m] == "slower" for v in settings_v.values())
190|                else "not slower"
191|                for m in MEASURES
192|            }
193|            passes = "faster" in (phases["decode"], phases["prompt"]) and "slower" not in phases.values()
194|            verdict[name][bar] = {"pass": passes, "phases": phases, "settings": settings_v}
195|            print(f"G3 {name} vs {bar}: {'pass' if passes else 'fail'} {phases}")
196|        verdict[name]["g3"] = all(v["pass"] for v in verdict[name].values())
197|    out.write_text(json.dumps(verdict, indent=1) + "\n")
198|
199|
200|def main():
201|    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
202|    ap.add_argument("engine", choices=("plain", "vllm"))
203|    ap.add_argument("out", type=Path)
204|    ap.add_argument(
205|        "attempts", nargs="+", type=attempt_arg, metavar="SLOT=FOLDER",
206|        help="the Muse agent's attempt folder per slot",
207|    )
208|    ap.add_argument(
209|        "--variant", type=variant_arg, action="append", default=[],
210|        metavar="NAME:SLOT=FOLDER[+SLOT=FOLDER...]",
211|        help="another set of attempts to time, outside muse-all",
212|    )
213|    ap.add_argument("--tokens", type=int, default=256, help="output tokens per run")
214|    ap.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=G3_REPEATS, help="shuffled repeats per variant and setting")
215|    ap.add_argument(
216|        "--settings", default=G3_SETTINGS, metavar="ROWSxPROMPT,...",
217|        help="request counts and prompt lengths to time (G3: the default)",
218|    )
219|    args = ap.parse_args()
220|    settings = [tuple(int(n) for n in s.split("x")) for s in args.settings.split(",")]
221|    taken = [p for slot, _ in args.attempts for p in parts(slot)]
222|    if len(taken) != len(set(taken)):
223|        ap.error(f"two attempts replace the same part: {sorted(taken)}")
224|    gpu_lock.hold(
225|        f"time_candidates.py {args.engine} "
226|        + " ".join(f"{s}={f}" for s, f in args.attempts)
227|    )
228|    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
229|    log = args.out / f"muse-{args.engine}.jsonl"
230|
231|    if args.engine == "plain":
232|        from mlx_lm.utils import load_model
233|
234|        model, _ = load_model(Path(bd.MODEL))
235|        mx.eval(model.parameters())
236|        variants = Variants(args.attempts, args.variant)
237|        checks = plain_checks(model, variants)
238|        run = lambda r, p, s: bd.run_plain(model, r, p, args.tokens, s)  # noqa: E731
239|    else:
240|        from vllm import LLM
241|
242|        bd.install_vllm_step_hooks()
243|        llm = LLM(
244|            model=bd.MODEL,
245|            trust_remote_code=True,
246|            max_model_len=2048,
247|            max_num_seqs=32,
248|            max_num_batched_tokens=2048,
249|            # 32 rows x 384 tokens need 240 MiB; 32 x 1,280 need 800 MiB
250|            kv_cache_memory_bytes=(1 << 30) if max(p for _, p in settings) > 128 else 512 << 20,
251|            enable_prefix_caching=False,
252|            generation_config="vllm",
253|        )
254|        run = lambda r, p, s: bd.run_vllm(llm, r, p, args.tokens, s)  # noqa: E731
255|        run(1, 16, 0)  # warm-up; captures the runner
256|        variants = Variants(args.attempts, args.variant)
257|        checks = rf.vllm_checks(llm, variants)
258|
259|    rf.time_variants(args.engine, variants, checks, run, log, settings, args.repeats)
260|    if args.engine == "vllm":
261|        g3(log, variants.names, settings, args.out / "g3-vllm.json")
262|
263|
264|if __name__ == "__main__":
265|    main()
