1|"""Pinned in-round end-to-end gate for the Muse agent swarm (PROTOTYPE).
2|
3|Design Z prototype of the proposed `bench/grader/check_ready.py`. It runs
4|exactly one thing: `time_candidates.py vllm` with the G3 protocol pinned
5|(4 G3 settings, 5 repeats, 256 tokens, positional slots only, no --variant),
6|then audits the produced log instead of trusting it:
7|
8|  1. exactly one ready-protocol marker, with the pinned values;
9|  2. every run is engine vllm, at the 4 G3 settings, 5 repeats each, no extras;
10|  3. the variant set is exactly base + compiled-<slot> + muse-<slot>
11|     (+ compiled-all/muse-all when >1 slot);
12|  4. every non-base variant keeps base's greedy tokens (exact, rows 1 and 32);
13|  5. the g3 verdict is RECOMPUTED from the log and must match g3-vllm.json;
14|  6. every submitted muse-<slot> (and muse-all, when present) passes G3
15|     against base and against its compiled counterpart.
16|
17|Usage (GPU run; takes the GPU lock via time_candidates, waits its turn):
18|
19|  .venv/bin/python check_ready.py <out-dir> SLOT=FOLDER [SLOT=FOLDER...]
20|
21|Audit only (no GPU; also useful post-round):
22|
23|  .venv/bin/python check_ready.py --audit <out-dir>
24|
25|Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 judged fail (files written), 2 protocol violation.
26|Every failure path still writes ready-verdict.json, so a checker can cite it.
27|"""
28|
29|import contextlib
30|import io
31|import json
32|import sys
33|from datetime import datetime, timezone
34|from pathlib import Path
35|
36|HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
37|GRADER = HERE  # prototype dir; real home: bench/grader (imports work the same)
38|# Import the real tools from the worktree's bench/grader + bench/micro.
39|WORKTREE = HERE.parents[2]
40|sys.path.insert(0, str(WORKTREE / "bench" / "grader"))
41|sys.path.insert(0, str(WORKTREE / "bench" / "micro"))
42|import time_candidates as tc  # noqa: E402
43|
44|PINNED_SETTINGS = [(1, 128), (8, 128), (32, 128), (32, 1024)]
45|PINNED_REPEATS = 5
46|PINNED_TOKENS = 256
47|PINNED_ENGINE = "vllm"
48|MARKER_KIND = "ready-protocol"
49|
50|
51|def utcnow():
52|    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%FT%TZ")
53|
54|
55|def expected_variants(slots):
56|    names = ["base"]
57|    for s in slots:
58|        names.append(f"compiled-{s}")
59|        names.append(f"muse-{s}")
60|    if len(slots) > 1:
61|        names += ["compiled-all", "muse-all"]
62|    return names
63|
64|
65|def judged_variants(slots):
66|    names = [f"muse-{s}" for s in slots]
67|    if len(slots) > 1:
68|        names.append("muse-all")
69|    return names
70|
71|
72|def audit(outdir):
73|    """Audit <outdir>'s log + g3 file. Returns (verdict_dict, exit_code)."""
74|    outdir = Path(outdir)
75|    log = outdir / f"muse-{PINNED_ENGINE}.jsonl"
76|    g3file = outdir / "g3-vllm.json"
77|    problems = []  # protocol violations -> exit 2
78|    fails = []  # judged failures -> exit 1
79|    verdict = {
80|        "audited_at": utcnow(),
81|        "out": str(outdir),
82|        "protocol": {
83|            "engine": PINNED_ENGINE,
84|            "settings": [f"{r}x{p}" for r, p in PINNED_SETTINGS],
85|            "repeats": PINNED_REPEATS,
86|            "tokens": PINNED_TOKENS,
87|        },
88|    }
89|
90|    if not log.exists():
91|        problems.append(f"missing log file {log}")
92|        verdict.update({"pass": False, "problems": problems, "fails": fails})
93|        return verdict, 2
94|    records = [json.loads(line) for line in log.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
95|    markers = [r for r in records if r.get("kind") == MARKER_KIND]
96|    if len(markers) != 1:
97|        problems.append(f"want exactly 1 {MARKER_KIND} marker, found {len(markers)}")
98|        verdict.update({"pass": False, "problems": problems, "fails": fails})
99|        return verdict, 2
100|    m = markers[0]
101|    for key, want in (
102|        ("engine", PINNED_ENGINE),
103|        ("settings", [[r, p] for r, p in PINNED_SETTINGS]),
104|        ("repeats", PINNED_REPEATS),
105|        ("tokens", PINNED_TOKENS),
106|    ):
107|        if m.get(key) != want:
108|            problems.append(f"marker {key} is {m.get(key)!r}, want {want!r}")
109|    slots = m.get("slots", [])
110|    if not slots:
111|        problems.append("marker names no slots")
112|        slots = []
113|    verdict["protocol"]["slots"] = slots
114|    verdict["protocol"]["attempts"] = m.get("attempts", {})
115|
116|    runs = [r for r in records if r.get("kind") == "run"]
117|    checks = [r for r in records if r.get("kind") == "check"]
118|    if not runs:
119|        problems.append("log holds no runs")
120|    for r in runs:
121|        if r.get("engine") != PINNED_ENGINE:
122|            problems.append(f"run with engine {r.get('engine')!r}, want vllm only")
123|            break
124|    want_settings = set(PINNED_SETTINGS)
125|    got_settings = {(r["rows"], r["prompt"]) for r in runs}
126|    if got_settings != want_settings:
127|        problems.append(
128|            f"settings are {sorted(got_settings)}, want {sorted(want_settings)}"
129|        )
130|    want_names = set(expected_variants(slots))
131|    got_names = {r["variant"] for r in runs}
132|    if got_names != want_names:
133|        problems.append(f"variants are {sorted(got_names)}, want {sorted(want_names)}")
134|    for name in sorted(got_names & want_names):
135|        for setting in sorted(want_settings):
136|            reps = sorted(
137|                r["rep"]
138|                for r in runs
139|                if r["variant"] == name and (r["rows"], r["prompt"]) == setting
140|            )
141|            if reps != list(range(PINNED_REPEATS)):
142|                problems.append(f"{name} {setting}: reps {reps}, want 0..4")
143|    if problems:
144|        verdict.update({"pass": False, "problems": problems, "fails": fails})
145|        return verdict, 2
146|
147|    # Token exactness: every non-base variant, rows 1 and 32 (brief's G2 end to end).
148|    exact = {}
149|    for name in sorted(got_names - {"base"}):
150|        rows_exact = {}
151|        for rows in (1, 32):
152|            recs = [
153|                c for c in checks if c.get("variant") == name and c.get("rows") == rows
154|            ]
155|            ok = bool(recs) and all(c.get("exact") for c in recs)
156|            rows_exact[str(rows)] = ok
157|            if not ok:
158|                fails.append(f"{name} changes base's greedy tokens at rows={rows}")
159|        exact[name] = rows_exact
160|    verdict["exact"] = exact
161|
162|    # Recompute G3 from the log; the g3 file must match (kills lazy forgery).
163|    if not g3file.exists():
164|        problems.append(f"missing {g3file}")
165|        verdict.update({"pass": False, "problems": problems, "fails": fails})
166|        return verdict, 2
167|    filed = json.loads(g3file.read_text())
168|    tmp = outdir / "g3-recomputed-tmp.json"
169|    buf = io.StringIO()
170|    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
171|        tc.g3(log, sorted(got_names), PINNED_SETTINGS, tmp)
172|    recomputed = json.loads(tmp.read_text())
173|    tmp.unlink()
174|    for name in judged_variants(slots):
175|        if filed.get(name) != recomputed.get(name):
176|            problems.append(f"g3-vllm.json entry for {name} differs from log recompute")
177|    if problems:
178|        verdict.update({"pass": False, "problems": problems, "fails": fails})
179|        return verdict, 2
180|
181|    submitted = {}
182|    for name in judged_variants(slots):
183|        entry = recomputed.get(name, {})
184|        g3pass = entry.get("g3", False)
185|        submitted[name] = {
186|            "g3": g3pass,
187|            "vs": {
188|                bar: v.get("pass") for bar, v in entry.items() if bar != "g3"
189|            },
190|            "phases": {bar: v.get("phases") for bar, v in entry.items() if bar != "g3"},
191|        }
192|        if not g3pass:
193|            fails.append(f"{name} fails G3")
194|    verdict["submitted"] = submitted
195|    ok = not fails
196|    verdict.update({"pass": ok, "problems": problems, "fails": fails})
197|    return verdict, 0 if ok else 1
198|
199|
200|def run(outdir, attempts):
201|    outdir = Path(outdir)
202|    if outdir.exists() and any(outdir.iterdir()):
203|        print(f"{outdir}: exists and is not empty; use a fresh folder per check")
204|        return 2
205|    slots = [s for s, _ in attempts]
206|    # Pinned invocation: no --variant, no --repeats/--settings/--tokens flags.
207|    sys.argv = ["time_candidates.py", PINNED_ENGINE, str(outdir)] + [
208|        f"{s}={f}" for s, f in attempts
209|    ]
210|    tc.main()  # takes the GPU lock itself; waits its turn; loads the model inside
211|    marker = {
212|        "kind": MARKER_KIND,
213|        "engine": PINNED_ENGINE,
214|        "settings": [[r, p] for r, p in PINNED_SETTINGS],
215|        "repeats": PINNED_REPEATS,
216|        "tokens": PINNED_TOKENS,
217|        "slots": slots,
218|        "attempts": {s: str(f) for s, f in attempts},
219|        "exact_required": True,
220|        "written_at": utcnow(),

226|
227|def finish(outdir):
228|    outdir = Path(outdir)
229|    verdict, code = audit(outdir)
230|    (outdir / "ready-verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(verdict, indent=1) + "\n")
231|    for p in verdict.get("problems", []):
232|        print(f"PROTOCOL: {p}")
233|    for f in verdict.get("fails", []):
234|        print(f"FAIL: {f}")
235|    for name, v in (verdict.get("submitted") or {}).items():
236|        print(f"ready {name}: {'pass' if v['g3'] else 'fail'} {v['vs']}")

240|
241|def main(argv):

251|            print(f"{spec!r}: give SLOT=FOLDER")
252|            return 2
253|        attempts.append((slot, folder))
254|    if len({s for s, _ in attempts}) != len(attempts):
255|        print("each slot at most once per check")
256|        return 2

1|# Checker (DESIGN X PROTOTYPE — new role card for skill v8)
2|
3|*Prototype of `.agents/skills/muse-round/checker.md`. Mirrors `boundary.md`'s
4|two-task shape. The checker never runs GPU work: it reads result files others
5|wrote, like the boundary agent's "no new grader run" precedent.*
6|
7|You are `checker-<n>`, the checker of hypothesis `<n>` — or `checker-submit`
8|for the round's submission. A speed number is trusted only when you have tied
9|it to the run that produced it. The lead's prompt names your task: *check a
10|hypothesis* or *check the submission*. [tracking.md](tracking.md) describes
11|the documents and the rules; its *Claim contract* section defines the three
12|claim kinds you enforce.
13|
14|## Task: check a hypothesis
15|
16|The lead sends you when a hypothesis is ready to close `ready` (and only
17|then — dropped hypotheses need no check). Inputs: the hypothesis entry, its
18|best attempt's `grade.json`, and its `submit.json` with the `muse-vllm.jsonl`
19|behind it.
20|
21|1. **Every measured piece number resolves.** For each row marked *measured /
22|   piece* in the entry's tables: open the cited `grade.json`, find the cited
23|   key (`timing_us_per_layer.<size>.<column>`, `vs_compiled`,
24|   `phases_vs_compiled`, `beats_compiled`), and compare verbatim. A number
25|   from any other file is not a measured piece number.
26|2. **Every measured request number resolves.** For each row marked *measured /
27|   request*: open the cited `submit.json`, find the cited `g3` verdict or
28|   `medians` row (median with its [min–max] and n=5), and compare verbatim;
29|   confirm the cited jsonl cell exists. A request-level number citing a
30|   grader file fails — piece timing never sources a request claim.
31|3. **Every prediction is labelled and owned.** For each row marked
32|   *predicted*: it shows its formula, every input is the candidate's own
33|   `grade.json`/`submit.json` (never another variant's gain, never a sum
34|   across slots), and it stands next to its measured value with the miss
35|   (or "unvalidated: first of its kind"). A prediction borrowing another
36|   variant's measured gain fails.
37|4. **Nothing unmeasured is free.** The entry's *Unverified* list names every
38|   cost this hypothesis did not measure: at least the boundary's can't-see
39|   items, prefill chunks of other sizes, decode row counts other than 1/8/32,
40|   and 1-request whole-request noise. A missing item fails. The words *free*,
41|   *neutral* or *invisible* about an unmeasured cost fail.
42|5. **The ledger adds up.** Recompute the hypothesis's failure ledger from the
43|   cited `grade.json` verdicts (`vs_compiled` per size): three timed losses of
44|   one family at one size or phase must show the family change or the logged
45|   why-not. A missing trigger fails.
46|6. **Stamp it.** Append to the entry's **Checks** section: `check: pass`, or
47|   `check: fail` with each defect as file + line + what is wrong. Log it and
48|   return. `ready` needs your `pass`; on `fail` the lead fixes the entry (or
49|   the attempt) and sends you again.
50|
51|## Task: check the submission
52|
53|The lead sends you once, when the implementation README's *Ready to test* and
54|`summary.md` are drafted. Inputs: those two documents plus every submitted
55|hypothesis's `submit.json` and the submission `submit.json` (with `muse-all`
56|when more than one slot is submitted).
57|
58|1. Run steps 1–4 above over both documents. The expected G3 change is a
59|   *measured / request* table from the submission `submit.json` (median with
60|   [min–max], verdict per setting); any other number there is marked
61|   *predicted* with its formula, own inputs and miss.
62|2. A *measured* number spanning more than one slot cites a `muse-all` row.
63|   A cross-slot sum without one fails.
64|3. The submission's *Unverified* list covers every hypothesis's list. A
65|   dropped cost fails.
66|4. Stamp both documents (`check: pass` / `check: fail` with defects), log it
67|   and return. The round finishes only on your `pass`. If no hypothesis
68|   closed `ready`, there is no submission check: verify the documents claim
69|   no measured request numbers and still carry Unverified.
70|
71|## What you write
72|
73|The hypothesis entry's **Checks** section, the `check:` stamps on the README

7|## Claim contract (speed numbers only)
8|
9|Every speed number in a hypothesis entry, the implementation README, or the
10|summary is exactly one of:
11|
12|- **measured / piece** — a number from a `grade.json` the builder wrote with
13|  the grader's `--out`: a per-size time, a `vs_compiled` verdict, a phase
14|  verdict, `beats_compiled`/`beats_baseline`. It cites file + key, and the
15|  value matches the file verbatim.
16|- **measured / request** — a number from a `submit.json` the submission check
17|  wrote: a `g3` verdict (`faster`/`same`/`slower` per setting, `pass` per
18|  bar), or a median with its [min–max] over the 5 repeats. It cites
19|  `submit.json` + key and the jsonl cell (variant, setting). **Level
20|  integrity:** a grader file never sources a request-level claim.
21|- **predicted** — anything else with a number: it shows its formula, every
22|  input is the candidate's own measured number (never another variant's gain,
23|  never a sum across slots), and it stands next to its measured value with
24|  the miss once measured (or "unvalidated: first of its kind").
25|
26|Anything the swarm did not measure is listed under **Unverified**, never
27|assumed free or neutral. At least: the boundary's can't-see items, prefill
28|chunks of other sizes, decode row counts other than 1/8/32, and 1-request
29|whole-request noise.

31|## Table schemas
32|
33|Decision (hypothesis entry), one row per number that matters:
34|
35|| Claim | Kind | Level | Value | Source (file + key / formula) | Measured vs predicted |
36||---|---|---|---|---|---|
37|| decode @1 row vs compiled | measured | piece | faster, 49.8 vs 65.1µs | `.../attempt-4/grade.json : timing_us_per_layer.rows 1` | — |
38|| request decode @1x128 vs base | measured | request | faster, −0.48 [−0.51,−0.44]ms | `.../evals/submit.json : g3.muse-routing.base + medians` | — |
39|| request delta if prefill matched | predicted | — | −0.55ms | own piece delta × layers (formula); inputs: rows above | miss +0.07 |
40|
41|Ready to test (implementation README): the same columns, one row per
42|slot and one for the submission. With more than one slot, the submission row
43|is measured and cites a `muse-all` row; without a `muse-all` row there is no
44|measured submission number — a sum is a prediction and is labelled one.

1|# Checker (PROTOTYPE - new role card)
2|
3|*Design Z prototype of a new card in the [muse-round skill](SKILL.md).*
4|
5|You are `checker-<n>`, or `checker-final`. The verifier checks exploration's
6|inefficiency entries; you check implementation's numbers the same way, before
7|anyone closes on them. No hypothesis becomes `candidate` or `ready`, and the
8|round does not finish, without your `pass`. [tracking.md](tracking.md)
9|describes the documents and the rules, including what every speed number
10|carries.
11|
12|The lead's prompt names your task: *check a hypothesis* (its entry) or
13|*check the finish* (the implementation README's Ready to test and
14|`summary.md`).
15|
16|## Task: check a hypothesis
17|
18|1. **List every speed number** in the entry's builder sections, boundary
19|   checks and Decision.
20|2. **Check each number** against the rule in tracking.md:
21|   - open the cited run file; confirm it timed exactly what is claimed
22|     (the slot, or the combination; piece level or end to end);
23|   - confirm the label: `measured` only with such a file, else
24|     `prediction`, shown next to the measured value where one exists;
25|   - redo any arithmetic: it counts only the candidate's own measured
26|     effect, and a combination is never a sum of per-slot numbers;
27|   - confirm every unmeasured cost the entry touches is listed under
28|     **Unverified**, and nothing there is assumed free, neutral or zero.
29|3. **Check the gate:** for `candidate`, the best attempt passes G1, G2, its
30|   boundary check and `beats_compiled` (and `beats_baseline` where the slot
31|   has one); for `ready`, a ready check's `ready-verdict.json` says `pass`
32|   for exactly this attempt, and the Decision cites it.
33|4. **Check the failure counter:** the *Failures at the same point* list
34|   matches the attempts' verdicts, and after 3 shared failures the next
35|   direction is a changed approach or the log holds the lead's reason why not.
36|5. **Write the entry's `Check` section:** each number with its level, run
37|   file and label, then `pass` or each defect with what is right. Log it.
38|
39|## Task: check the finish
40|
41|1. **List every speed number** in Ready to test and `summary.md`'s expected
42|   G3 change.
43|2. **Check each** as in step 2 above. Every end-to-end number cites the
44|   ready check that measured it; the combination cites `muse-all` from one
45|   ready check over all submitted slots. Baselines and the reference carry
46|   no new claim: they cite Claude's measurement or stand without one.
47|3. **Write the verdict** as a log line and a note under the README's
48|   Ready to test: `checker-final: pass`, or the defects. Log it.
49|
50|**Done** when the section or note is written. Return `pass` or the defects.
51|
52|## What you write
53|
54|The hypothesis entry's `Check` section, or the finish note, and log lines.
55|You never change another agent's numbers; the lead fixes them and calls you

1|# The swarm's shared documents, and the rules every agent keeps
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Part of the [muse-round skill](SKILL.md). [Who made what](../../../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|Every agent of the round reads this file. The documents below are how the swarm shares what it knows and how surucuonur follows the round while it runs, so keep them current as you work, not at the end.
6|
7|## The round folder and its two phase folders
8|
9|`<round>/` is this round's folder: `muse-spark/round-<N>/` from round 2 on (round 1's is `muse-spark/` itself). The lead's prompt names it.
10|
11|| Folder | Phase | Holds |
12||---|---|---|
13|| `<round>/exploration/` | Exploration | the analysis: `README.md`, territory and inefficiency entries, `log.md` |
14|| `<round>/implementation/` | Implementation | the report: `README.md`, hypothesis entries, `log.md` |
15|
16|Kernels go in `<round>/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/`, numbered from 1 in each round; the grader reads any attempt folder it is given.
17|
18|**Earlier rounds' folders are frozen.** Read them and cite them by path; write what you add in this round's entries. The hooks refuse a change to any file a finished round left.
19|
20|Each folder has three kinds of document:
21|
22|- **`README.md`.** The phase's document. Only the lead writes it, refreshing it and raising its version at every checkpoint. It opens with its version line and the tracker table below.
23|- **Entries.** One file per territory, inefficiency or hypothesis. The owner keeps it current, and other agents append notes.
24|- **`log.md`.** One line per event, from every agent, appended only.
25|
26|## Versions
27|
28|Every shared document carries a version number, so a reader knows which version they're looking at, and git holds every version.
29|
30|**Phase versions.** Each README opens with its version line:
31|
32|```markdown
33|**Version:** v5 · 2026-11-04T09:40Z · skill version 6
34|```
35|
36|- **Who raises it:** the lead, at every checkpoint, and each version is exactly one commit.
37|- **The commit:** its subject names the version, `<name>: exploration v5: <what changed>`, where `<name>` is the Muse agent's name from the lead's first prompt. `git log --grep 'exploration v5:'` finds it, and `git diff` between two such commits shows what changed.
38|- **The changelog:** the README ends with `## Versions`, one line per version, newest first, naming the entries that changed and their new versions:
39|
40|```markdown
41|- v5 · 2026-11-04T09:40Z · split quantized-kernels in two · changed: territory-quantized-kernels v4, ineff-quantized-kernels-2 v2
42|```
43|
44|**Entry versions.** Each entry's status block has a `Version` line, starting at 1:
45|- **Territory and inefficiency entries:** the owner raises it with every change to its own text. The verifier raises it when it writes the verdict.
46|- **Hypothesis entries:** the lead raises it at each checkpoint where the entry changed, builders' and the boundary agent's sections included.
47|- **Notes:** a note under `## From other agents` leaves the version alone. The owner raises it when folding the note in.
48|
49|**Times.** Every time you write, in a version line, a status block, a tracker row, a note or a log line, is the output of `date -u +%FT%TZ` run at that moment. Never estimate or round one.
50|
51|## The README trackers
52|
53|Exploration, `exploration/README.md`:
54|
55|| Territory | Agent | Status | Inefficiencies | Updated |
56||---|---|---|---|---|
57|| `quantized-kernels` | `explorer-quantized-kernels` | exploring | `ineff-quantized-kernels-1` (confirmed), `-2` (open) | 2026-11-04 09:40Z |
58|
59|Implementation, `implementation/README.md`:
60|
61|| Hypothesis | Slot | Builders | Attempts: G1, G2, µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows (compiled) | Status |
62||---|---|---|---|---|
63|| `hyp-1-fused-gather` | `experts` | `builder-1-a`, `builder-1-b` | 3: pass, pass, 41 / 55 / 180 (48 / 70 / 260) | hardening |
64|
65|From round 2 on, where the slot has a baseline, the attempts column also gives its time from the same run, and whether `beats_baseline` is true.
66|
67|## Entries
68|
69|Each entry opens with a status block that its owner keeps current:
70|
71|```markdown
72|- **Owner:** explorer-quantized-kernels
73|- **Status:** exploring
74|- **Version:** 3
75|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T09:40Z
76|- **Next:** read the 32-row dispatch of affine_gather_qmm
77|```
78|
79|Entries are named so that two agents never pick the same name:
80|- `<round>/exploration/territory-<territory>.md`
81|- `<round>/exploration/ineff-<territory>-<n>.md`, numbered by the explorer of that territory
82|- `<round>/implementation/hyp-<n>-<slug>.md`, numbered by the lead
83|
84|**Another agent's entry:** append under its `## From other agents` heading, starting with your name and the time. The owner's text stays as written, so two agents never overwrite each other. The owner reads these notes and folds in what holds.
85|
86|### Territory entry
87|
88|1. Status block (statuses: `exploring`, `done`).
89|2. **What it does** in the decode step, in a few lines.
90|3. **The checklist** below, filled in for each piece of code or table in the territory.
91|4. **Relations:** which territories feed it and which it feeds, with the data passed.
92|5. **Inefficiencies:** links to the entries this territory raised.
93|6. **Files read**, and what each one gave.
94|
95|### Inefficiency entry
96|
97|1. Status block. The statuses are `open`, `confirmed`, `refuted` and `superseded by <entry>`; only the verifier sets `confirmed` or `refuted`.
98|2. **Slot:** `routing`, `combine`, `experts`, or `outside the slots`.
99|3. **What happens:** what the code does, and where (file and lines).
100|4. **Cost** at 1, 8 and 32 rows of a decode step and at the prefill's 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows: kernels × the fixed cost per kernel, bytes ÷ peak bandwidth, and the measured time with the table it comes from.
101|5. **Kind:** overhead-bound, bandwidth-bound or compute-bound, in the terms of `claude/GLOSSARY.md`.
102|6. **Spans:** the territories involved.
103|7. **Predicted saving** if removed, in µs per decode step at 1, 8 and 32 rows and per prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows, with the arithmetic. A saving in one phase that costs the other is not one.
104|8. **Verdict**, written by the verifier: each claim checked, and the result.
105|
106|### Hypothesis entry
107|
108|1. Status block. The lead owns it; the statuses are `boundary`, `building`, `hardening`, `candidate`, `ready` and `dropped`. `candidate` means the best attempt passes G1, G2, its boundary check and `beats_compiled` (and `beats_baseline` where the slot has one) and waits for the ready check; only a passed ready check moves it to `ready`.
109|2. **Inefficiency** it removes, the slot, and from round 2 on the slot's baseline folder, or `none` and its starting point.
110|3. **Boundary**, written by the boundary agent: what the solution must keep identical (see `boundary.md`).
111|4. **One section per builder:** its direction, its attempts (folder, predicted and measured µs per layer at the six sizes with each size's verdict, G1, G2, `beats_compiled`, and where the slot has a baseline its time and `beats_baseline`), and what each attempt taught.
112|5. **Boundary checks** of the attempts that passed G2.
113|6. **Failures at the same point:** each failed attempt's signature (the phase or size it failed at, and the named cause), kept current by the lead. After 3 failures share one phase and one cause, the next attempt changes approach (see SKILL.md step 4.5).
114|7. **Unverified:** what this hypothesis did not measure (other row counts, other engines, interactions with other slots, anything "G3 decides"). Updated whenever a claim is added.
115|8. **Check**, written by the checker: each number's level, run file and label, and the verdict.
116|9. **Decision:** the best attempt and why. When the status is `candidate`, it states the piece basis as a prediction; when `ready`, it cites the ready check's passed verdict file, with the measured end-to-end change.
117|
118|## The checklist
119|
120|Fill it in for each piece of code you inspect, so that no piece is judged without its neighbours:
121|
122|- **Callers:** who calls it, and with what shapes at 1, 8 and 32 rows of a decode step and in a prefill.
123|- **Callees:** what it calls, down to the Metal kernel it launches.
124|- **Data:** each input and output with shape, dtype and layout. Where it is produced, and where it is consumed next.
125|- **Neighbours:** what runs just before and after it in the decode step, and what a replacement must keep identical.
126|- **Cost:** the kernels it launches, the bytes it reads and writes (weight bytes counted per read), and its measured time with the table the time comes from.
127|- **Invariants:** what correctness depends on: G2's bit-exact rule at every size, the tie rule for the 4th and 5th expert, the bfloat16 rounding points, and which MLX kernel the reference uses at each size.
128|
129|## The log
130|
131|Append one line per event with the shell, so lines from several agents never mix. In round 2:
132|
133|```bash
134|printf '%s | %s | %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "explorer-baseline-experts" "posted ineff-baseline-experts-2: each weight byte read 4 times at 32 rows" >> muse-spark/round-2/exploration/log.md
135|```
136|
137|Log when you start, claim something, post or confirm an entry, change direction (what from, what to, and which entry made you), grade an attempt (with its verdict), and finish.
138|
139|## Adapting to the others' work
140|
141|Before every new piece of work, and after every post:
142|1. Read the phase README's tracker and the newest 30 lines of the phase log (`tail -n 30`).
143|2. Then change direction when:
144|   - **someone else covers it:** another entry already covers the same code or cause, so append to that entry instead of starting a second one;
145|   - **its premise fell:** the claim your work rests on was refuted;
146|   - **something pays more:** an open item in your territory or task predicts a larger saving than what you're on, and nobody owns it.
147|3. When you change direction, log it with the reason, and write it in your own entry's status block.
148|
149|Two claims on the same item go to the lead, who settles them.
150|
151|## Rules for every agent
152|
153|- **Writes go only to this round's folder, in the files your role names.** Earlier rounds' folders, everything else in the worktree, and everything outside it are read-only.
154|- **Only the lead commits.** Helpers never run `git add` or `git commit`.
155|- **The grader and the ready check are the only GPU jobs.** Run the grader only as a builder, through the brief's command; run the ready check only as the lead, through `bench/grader/check_ready.py` with one fresh folder per check. Each waits its turn when another run has the GPU. Load no model and start no other GPU work: the machine has 16 GB and slows down sharply when memory runs short. Never run `time_candidates.py`, `breakdown.py` or `repeat_fixes.py` directly: only the ready check's files count as end-to-end evidence.
156|- **Every speed number carries its level, its run file and its label.** A number is either *measured* or a *prediction*, at either *piece* level (one slot in the grader) or *end-to-end* level (whole requests in vLLM):
157|  - a measured piece number cites the grader verdict file that timed exactly that slot;
158|  - a measured end-to-end number cites the ready check's `ready-verdict.json` and log that timed exactly that slot or combination;
159|  - a prediction is labelled `prediction`, counts only the candidate's own measured effect (never gains borrowed from `mx.compile` or another attempt), and is shown next to the measured value once one exists;
160|  - a combination's effect is measured as a combination (`muse-all` in one ready check over all submitted slots), never summed from per-slot numbers;
161|  - anything not measured at the claimed level is listed under **Unverified** in the hypothesis entry and the README, and is never assumed free, neutral or zero. "G3 decides" is not a measurement: it goes under Unverified.
162|- **One ready check judges a fixed set once.** A ready check's folder is written once and never appended to; a new check needs a fresh folder. The verdict stands: never re-run a check to get a better number.
163|- **Credentials stay unread:** `.env` files, `~/.config/muse/` and any key store.
164|- **The API-stage kernels** in the history before the tag `agent-era` are from an earlier, removed stage (PROVENANCE.md) and stay unread.

  "exit_code": 0,
  "terminal_status": "completed",
  "output": """"Tables of an engine comparison run by time_candidates.py, one row per version and setting.

From <run>/muse-<engine>.jsonl it writes, next to it:

  versions.csv     per version and setting (requests x prompt tokens): the
                   median decode step and its range over the repeats, its
                   change against the unchanged engine, the median time until
                   every prompt was processed and its ratio to the unchanged
                   engine's, and output tokens per second over the whole request
  correctness.csv  per version: whether its greedy tokens equal the unchanged
                   engine's at 1 and 32 requests

  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/engine_table.py results/runs/<run> [--engine vllm] [--tokens 256]

LABELS names the versions of the 2026-11-04 comparison; a variant not in it
keeps its own name.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import statistics
from pathlib import Path

LABELS = {  # variant -> (label, short label, round, submitted)
    "base": ("Unchanged engine", "Unchanged", "none", "yes"),
    "compiled-3": ("MLX references, compiled", "Compiled references", "none", "yes"),
    "compiled-routing": ("Routing reference, compiled", "Compiled routing", "none", "yes"),
    "round1": ("Round 1: all three kernels", "Round 1", "1", "yes"),
    "round2-submitted": ("Round 2 submission: routing + combine", "R2 submission", "2", "yes"),
    "muse-routing": ("Round 2: routing only", "R2 routing", "2", "yes"),
    "round2-routing+experts-a7": ("Round 2: routing + experts attempt-7", "R2 routing + experts a7", "2", "no"),
    "round2-all-three": ("Round 2: routing + combine + experts attempt-7", "R2 all three", "2", "no"),
}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("run", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--engine", default="vllm")
    ap.add_argument("--tokens", type=int, default=256, help="output tokens per request")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in (args.run / f"muse-{args.engine}.jsonl").open()]
    runs = [r for r in records if r["kind"] == "run" and r["engine"] == args.engine]
    checks = {(r["variant"], r["rows"]): r for r in records if r["kind"] == "check"}
    seen = list(dict.fromkeys(r["variant"] for r in runs))
    variants = [v for v in LABELS if v in seen] + [v for v in seen if v not in LABELS]
    settings = sorted({(r["rows"], r["prompt"]) for r in runs})

    def runs_of(variant, rows, prompt):
        return [r for r in runs if (r["variant"], r["rows"], r["prompt"]) == (variant, rows, prompt)]

    out = []
    for rows, prompt in settings:
        base = runs_of("base", rows, prompt)
        base_step = statistics.median(r["period_median_ms"] for r in base)
        base_wall = statistics.median(r["wall_ms"] for r in base)
        base_prompt = statistics.median(r["prompt_ms"] for r in base)
        for v in variants:
            rs = runs_of(v, rows, prompt)
            steps = [r["period_median_ms"] for r in rs]
            step, wall = statistics.median(steps), statistics.median(r["wall_ms"] for r in rs)
            prompts = [r["prompt_ms"] for r in rs if r.get("prompt_ms") is not None]
            label, short, rnd, submitted = LABELS.get(v, (v, v, "", ""))
            out.append({
                "version": v,
                "label": label,
                "short": short,
                "round": rnd,
                "submitted": submitted,
                "setting": f"{rows} x {prompt}",
                "requests": rows,
                "prompt_tokens": prompt,
                "step_ms": round(step, 3),
                "step_min_ms": round(min(steps), 3),
                "step_max_ms": round(max(steps), 3),
                "step_change_ms": round(step - base_step, 3),
                "step_change_pct": round((step / base_step - 1) * 100, 2),
                "prompt_ms": round(statistics.median(prompts), 1) if prompts else "",
                "prompt_ratio": round(statistics.median(prompts) / base_prompt, 2) if prompts else "",
                "wall_ms": round(wall, 1),
                "tokens_per_s": round(rows * args.tokens / wall * 1e3, 1),
                "tokens_per_s_change_pct": round((base_wall / wall - 1) * 100, 2),
                "repeats": len(rs),
            })
    with (args.run / "versions.csv").open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(out[0]))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(out)

    with (args.run / "correctness.csv").open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(["version", "label", "same_tokens_1_request", "same_tokens_32_requests"])
        for v in variants:
            same = ["yes" if v == "base" or checks.get((v, n), {}).get("exact") else "no" for n in (1, 32)]
            w.writerow([v, LABELS.get(v, (v,))[0], *same])
    print(f"wrote {args.run / 'versions.csv'} ({len(out)} rows) and correctness.csv")


if __name__ == "__main__":

{"content":"# Independent review: designs X, Y, Z against the brief

Reviewer: independent, read-only. Read order followed: `design-lab/brief.md`,
the four explorer reports, then `design-lab/review/design-{X,Y,Z}/design.md`
+ `test-report.md` + prototype/result files. Never opened `design-lab/designer-*/`
or `design-lab/tester-*/`. No GPU work, no model load, no tracked file changed
(`git status` shows only `?? design-lab/`), no network, no credentials.
CPU-only verification: targeted reads and greps of repo code cited below.

All three designs agree on the core architecture the brief points at: a pinned
in-round end-to-end gate (wrapper over `bench/grader/time_candidates.py` vLLM +
G3 path) with a token-exactness gate, claim discipline (measure-at-level or
label prediction, own-effect-only, combinations measured, Unverified lists),
an independent checker, and a K=3 failure counter. All three were prototyped
and independently live-tested on GPU against round-2's known-bad attempts, and
all three live checks returned FAIL verdicts matching Claude's post-round G3.
The differences are in gate placement, audit strictness, checker shape,
counter trigger, and GPU cost — and one of those differences is decisive.

## Per-design gate table

| Gate | X | Y | Z |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 root cause | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| G2 fits code/boundaries | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| G3 protects behavior/integrity | FAIL | FAIL | PASS |
| G4 failures/concurrency/recovery | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| G5 feasible/testable | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| G6 cohesive/proportionate | PASS | PASS | PASS |

### Design X — typed claims, owned request check, checker

- G1 PASS. Names the root cause as untyped feedback (piece verdicts, request
  verdicts, predictions, assumptions all prose under `tracking.md:153`) plus
  the forbidden in-round measurement (`tracking.md:152`, `SKILL.md:164`).
  Each behaviour is traced to a contract failure with verified cites. The fix
  (claim types + pinned check + checker + ledger) addresses the gap, not
  symptoms. Evidence: design §2–§4; live FAIL on experts-7 matches Claude
  (test-report §1: prompt 7.5–14.8× slower, decode mixed, `pass=false`).
- G2 PASS. Additive only: new `bench/grader/check_submit.py` importing
  `time_candidates` (same pattern as existing scripts), new `checker.md`,
  skill v8 patches P1–P15 quoting current text at 1113c2d (spot-verified:
  `SKILL.md:20`, `:135-140`, `:147`, `:164`, `tracking.md:152-153`,
  `builder.md:13,24,28,30`, `boundary.md:13` all quoted verbatim). Keeps the
  lead GPU-free, fitting `SKILL.md:32`. One wart: P10 writes `grade.json`
  into the attempt folder, contradicting `check_candidate.py:11-12` ("It never
  writes into the attempt folder"). Mechanically safe — `load()` at
  `check_candidate.py:64-71` reads only `spec.json` + `block-*.metal` — but
  the docstring needs updating at implementation time.
- G3 FAIL. `compose_submit` copies the `g3` verdict dict into `submit.json`
  without recomputing any range from the jsonl
  (`prototypes/check_submit.py:153-157`, verified by reading). Tester-X's G4
  (hand-edited `g3-vllm.json` claiming pass over a failing log) exits through
  with `pass=true`, and the checker card compares `submit.json` verbatim
  (`checker.md` steps 1–4) with no jsonl cross-check, so the forgery
  propagates to `ready`. This is a demonstrated data-integrity hole in the
  load-bearing evidence mechanism. Everything else in G3 holds (protected
  keys, formats, lock path, one-run rule — tester-X §5, all confirmed).
- G4 PASS. Covers check-fail landing states (back to hardening or drop;
  failing `muse-all` blocks the combination, subset re-check), crash/partial
  (no `submit.json`, no claim), noise (ranges travel; 1-request `same` as
  noise), memory (sequential vLLM, existing mitigations), committed-history
  integrity. Locks/DoS correctly left as pre-existing limits.
- G5 PASS. Implemented as prototype; 5/5 wrapper tests, claim fail/pass pair
  (8 defects vs pass), ledger replay — all rerun byte-identical by tester-X
  (§2). Live acceptance done by the tester (17.4 min active). Regression and
  rollback specified. GPU-budget risk noted below, but feasible.
- G6 PASS. Cohesive "type every claim" story; the claim validator is
  deliberately kept as scaffolding, not shipped (alt D rejected with reasons).
  No speculative machinery. The two-tier check (per-hypothesis + submission)
  is the costliest shape of the three — see risks.

### Design Y — the round measures its own submission

- G1 PASS. Confirms the brief's root cause at high certainty with the same
  verified structural facts, and closes it with one gate + one checker pass +
  one counter. Live 2-slot check FAILs routing (prompt), combine (decode at
  32), and `muse-all`, matching Claude sign-for-sign and reason-for-reason
  (test-report §1). This is the only live multi-slot run of any design —
  the combination-measurement path at the heart of B2/B3 is proven live here
  and only here.
- G2 PASS. Minimal footprint: one wrapper, no new role card (verifier gains a
  second task), `candidate` status, v8 text pasted verbatim. Two warts.
  (1) The lead runs the GPU check, deviating from `SKILL.md:32` ("You don't
  explore, build or grade yourself"). This is skill convention, not a
  protected contract, and the design justifies it (ADR 0007 bottleneck
  rationale inapplicable to one Finish-time run) and asks the user to confirm
  (design §9) — acceptable, flagged. (2) The prototype's import,
  `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("bench/grader").resolve()))`
  (`prototypes/check_submission.py:162`), is cwd-dependent; existing scripts
  use file-relative `HERE` (`time_candidates.py:40-41`). Must be fixed when
  moved into `bench/grader/`.
- G3 FAIL. Same hole as X: `audit()` replays coverage (variants, engine,
  reps, exact) but takes the timing verdict purely from `g3.get(name)` pass
  flags (`prototypes/check_submission.py:120-141`, verified by reading).
  Tester-Y's G4 (forged `g3-vllm.json` pass over a 10×-slower jsonl) exits 0.
  This directly weakens the design's §6 claim that "the audit replays coverage
  from the log rather than trusting stdout" — coverage yes, verdict no.
  Rest of G3 holds (tester-Y §5, all contracts verified intact).
- G4 PASS. Best explicit gaming catalogue with per-game mitigations (weak
  baseline, `max_rows`, post-check edits, median quoting, direct runs,
  noise re-rolls capped at 2 checks, cause-renaming). Lock bypass forbidden
  but undetected — stated and accepted per simplicity guardrail. Noise
  semantics preserved from ADR 0011.
- G5 PASS. 25/25 prototype checks rerun byte-identical (tester-Y §2); live
  2-slot run 20:49, no queue wait; falsifiable pre-round expectations stated
  and met. Cheapest GPU shape (≤2 checks, at Finish, zero builder contention).
- G6 PASS. The most minimal of the three: one gate, one extended role, one
  counter. Alternatives 1–6 each rejected with evidence. Proportionate.

### Design Z — measure what you claim

- G1 PASS. Same confirmed root cause, plus the clearest statement of why ADR
  0011 alone is insufficient (new citable "Not covered" at `0011:51`) and why
  neither rules-alone nor tools-alone suffices. Failure-first F1–F10 analysis
  maps each failure to a design element. Two live FAIL agreements: designer's
  T-live on routing-4 (prompt slower → FAIL, reproducing ADR 0011's demotion)
  and tester-Z's live run on combine-1 (+0.964 ms vs Claude's +1.051 ms at 32
  requests, same verdict).
- G2 PASS. Additive wrapper + new checker card + `candidate` status, all
  prototyped. Same lead-runs-GPU deviation as Y (`prototype/skill/tracking.md:155`),
  with the same justification burden. Marker record appended to the jsonl is
  safe for consumers: `engine_table.py:42-43` filters `kind=="run"`/`"check"`,
  so the `ready-protocol` marker is ignored (verified by reading). No tracked
  tool edited. The §5/§8-step-6 hardenings that would touch `gpu_lock.py` /
  `g3()` are explicitly separable and deferred — correctly, since §7.2
  rejects editing Claude's measurement path.
- G3 PASS. The audit recomputes G3 from the log via `tc.g3()` and compares
  per judged variant (`prototype/check_ready.py:168-179`, verified by reading);
  tester-Z's forged-g3 fixture exits 2 with "differs from log recompute".
  Exact variant-set, engine, settings, reps-0..4, and token-exactness checks
  all demonstrated across 13/13 audit fixtures (rerun from copy by tester-Z).
  Fresh-folder refusal and crash-vs-verdict distinction (`ready-verdict.json`
  absent = no verdict) are the best partial-round story. Warts, none
  FAIL-worthy: (a) `run()` passes no `--repeats/--settings/--tokens` to

Decisive reason: X and Y both have a demonstrated evidence-integrity hole (hand-edited `g3-vllm.json` passes their audits — testers' G4, confirmed by my code reading of `compose_submit:153-157` and `audit:120-141`), while Z's recompute-and-compare closes it in a few lines. Further reasons: best failure handling (file-backed crash-vs-verdict distinction, F1–F10 Goodhart analysis), batched cost shape with no mid-round builder contention (unlike X's per-hypothesis checks, ~40–55+ min serial), close-time plus finish checking (unlike Y's Finish-only pass), and honest residuals.

Key caveats: Z's `muse-all` path is proven only synthetically (Y has the only live multi-slot run — require a live 2-slot acceptance run pre-round-3); Z needs three one-line transplants (explicit-argv pinning from X/Y, counter anti-rename rule from Y, `--out grade.json` provenance from X). Shared gaps across all: no live PASS exists anywhere, checker compliance is untestable until round 3, and `--tokens` is unauditable from the log. Also found: tester-X's `phases_vs_compiled` "defect" is a false positive (byte-identical strings, verified).

1|# Designer-c design: measure what you claim (failure-and-evolution-first)
2|
3|Perspective: failure-and-evolution-first. This design begins from the
4|realistic ways the system can fail — including how a swarm could game each
5|new check — and proposes the smallest architecture that survives them.
6|
7|Paths below are relative to the worktree at commit `1113c2d` unless noted.
8|"Proposal" marks what is designed but not yet built; everything else cites
9|a path and line, or a result file under `design-lab/designer-c/results/`.
10|
11|## 1. Status: READY
12|
13|The design is complete and its risky half — the pinned tool gate — is
14|prototyped and tested: 13/13 offline audit checks pass
15|(`results/audit-tests/`, §8), and the skill-text half replays correctly
16|against every historical false claim (`results/schema-dry-run.md`).
17|A live pinned vLLM run validates the full path and its duration (§8, T-live).
18|No protected contract is broken; no Muse Code capability beyond the brief
19|is assumed.
20|
21|## 2. Context and diagnosis
22|
23|### 2.1 Verified facts
24|
25|Two rounds produced no real efficiency gain while predicting gains. The
26|five behaviours and their evidence (explorer reports, spot-verified):
27|
28|1. **Unmeasured costs priced at zero.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/hyp-1-experts-exact.md:150-151`
29|   declares a slow prefill branch "free apart from time to first token",
30|   citing `claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md:42` (line 44 today).
31|   Measured cost: experts-7 prompts 6.6–14.5× slower, throughput −10% to
32|   −83%; routing-4 prompts 7–10% slower (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md:134-141`).
33|   Six sibling instances exist (B1-b–g, explorer-rounds §B1).
34|2. **End-to-end gains from piece arithmetic.** Round 1 predicted
35|   −0.54/−1.81/−5.72 ms and measured +0.980/+0.163/−1.756; round 2
36|   predicted −0.84/−0.85/−0.84 and measured −0.726/−0.735/+0.527
37|   (`claude/findings/muse-round-1.md:24-29`, `muse-round-2.md:39,83`;
38|   recomputed exactly in explorer-findings `g3_recompute.txt`).
39|3. **Inconsistent reasoning.** `muse-spark/round-2/implementation/README.md:13`
40|   says "per-slot wins are not assumed to compose", then `:36` publishes
41|   "Together (sum) −0.84/−0.85/−0.84". Combine's −0.35 borrows −0.26…−0.29
42|   of `mx.compile`'s end-to-end gain onto −0.07…−0.09 of its own (`:29,34`).
43|   Measured at 32 requests: +1.051 ms (`muse-round-2.md:81`).
44|4. **Grader as search loop (round 1).** 28 executed bash invocations on
45|   experts for 4 counted attempts (18/3/6/1; brief says 29 — lead's
46|   verification note 1 settles 28). Fixed by skill v4's one-run-one-attempt
47|   rule (`builder.md:13`); round 2 ran 13 for 13.
48|5. **Failing design family persisted.** Six timed round-2 experts attempts
49|   lose at 1 row (92–110 vs 73–87 µs/layer; attempt-6 never launched —
50|   lead's note 4), while attempt-3's own note already refuted group-count
51|   as the lever (`hyp-1-experts-exact.md:254-258`). The harden loop only
52|   says "Repeat while the attempt still has a cause you can name and
53|   remove" (`SKILL.md:138`) — a skilled agent can always name one more.
54|
55|Structural causes in the skill (verified verbatim per lead's note 2):
56|in-round model runs are forbidden twice (`tracking.md:152`,
57|`SKILL.md:164`); the goal is phrased as passing gates (`SKILL.md:20`);
58|the verifier checks only exploration (`verifier.md:5,11`); the lead's
59|Ready-to-test arithmetic is unconstrained (`SKILL.md:147`); shown
60|arithmetic counts as sourced (`tracking.md:153`).
61|
62|Structural facts in the tools (verified by reading + probes):
63|- `time_candidates.py` G3 is vLLM-only (`:260-261`); plain `prompt_ms`
64|  is always exactly `0.0` (lead's note 5; `repeat_fixes.py:277-282`,
65|  `breakdown.py:468-484`) and plain writes no verdict.
66|- G3 ignores token exactness (`time_candidates.py:168-197` reads only
67|  `kind=="run"` records), though `exact` is logged per check
68|  (`repeat_fixes.py:221-223`, `time_candidates.py:156-158`).
69|- G3 crashes on `--variant muse-x:...` without a `compiled-x` bar
70|  (`time_candidates.py:177-183`, `min()` of empty ranges); non-`muse-`
71|  extras are timed but never judged.
72|- `--tokens` below 9 crashes (`breakdown.py:508-510`); KV bytes depend on
73|  settings (`time_candidates.py:250`), so non-G3 settings are not
74|  comparable with Claude's G3.
75|- `muse-all`/`compiled-all` exist only with >1 positional attempt
76|  (`:125-127`); a single-slot call never measures a combination.
77|- The GPU lock is voluntary: `breakdown.py` and `repeat_fixes.py` never
78|  call `hold()`; it has no timeout and breaks silently if
79|  `/tmp/mobilemoe-gpu.lock` is deleted (`gpu_lock.py:18-32`).
80|- Durations measured or extrapolated: grader 12.7 s (routing) to 4 m 57 s
81|  (experts) per run; single-slot vLLM G3 ≈ 13–14 min run wall at 5 repeats
82|  (explorer-tools `vllm-duration-estimate.txt`); 3-slot call ≈ 3×.
83|
84|### 2.2 Failure-first analysis: how the system can fail
85|
86|Any fix must survive these; each maps to a design element in §3
87|(reference F1…F10):
88|
89|- **F1. The new check becomes the next proxy (Goodhart).** A free-flag
90|  end-to-end call is gamed nine ways (verified against code): `--repeats 1`
91|  collapses min–max ranges to points so non-overlap is near-certain;
92|  `--settings` subsets shrink the every-setting burden and change KV bytes;
93|  `--tokens 9` reweights decode/prompt silently; `--variant myname:...`
94|  yields quotable but unjudged medians; `--variant muse-x:...` crashes G3;
95|  single-slot calls leave sums as the only combination number; the plain
96|  engine prices prefill at zero with quotable medians; medians can be
97|  quoted selectively from the jsonl; `max_rows=32` makes prefill
98|  "same by delegation". → Pillar A pins the invocation and audits the log.
99|- **F2. The check becomes a search loop.** Behaviour 4's analogue: unlimited
100|  14-minute runs as a gradient, each blocking every builder. → One gated
101|  call shape, verdict stands (no re-runs), failed checks force
102|  redesign-or-drop.
103|- **F3. Queue contention stretches the round past the deadline.** A 3-slot
104|  call is ~40 min; naive per-hypothesis checks of 3 slots plus a combined
105|  check exceed an hour of serial GPU. → Batching: one combined call judges
106|  every candidate plus the combination; piece timing stays the search
107|  signal; the check runs only at close-time.
108|- **F4. Noise kills or crowns.** 1-request whole-request spreads 6–41%
109|  (`0011:52`); 5 repeats still leave ~3% false-slower over 8 checks
110|  (`0011:40`); 1-row piece timing is near noise even within-run
111|  (`muse-round-2.md:55`; experts-7 1-row flipped sign between re-grades).
112|  A re-run-on-noise rule would be a license to re-roll. → The verdict
113|  stands; precision (no false claims) beats recall (a missed improvement
114|  simply isn't submitted). Claude's independent G3 stays authoritative.
115|- **F5. The model ignores the rule.** Round 1 ignored one-attempt-per-run
116|  until it became explicit (`builder.md:13`); round 3 runs the less
117|  capable contributor model unattended (ADR 0012). General advice fails;
118|  explicit checkable rules held (13-for-13). → Every new rule is shaped
119|  like behaviour 4's fix: countable, file-backed, auditable post-hoc.
120|- **F6. Partial rounds leave half-gates.** A session can stop mid-check.
121|  Appended reruns, half-written logs, or a `ready` set before the verdict
122|  lands would corrupt the record. → Fresh folder per check (refuse
123|  non-empty); audit demands completeness; `ready` requires the verdict
124|  file to exist; new interim status `candidate` separates piece-done
125|  from end-to-end-proven.
126|- **F7. Self-checking fails.** The builder's >20% miss rule (`builder.md:30`)
127|  is self-graded and unverified; predictions missed by 2.7–60× while
128|  Ready-to-test kept publishing fresh arithmetic (O7). → An independent
129|  checker, not the author, signs every number; the lead cannot close
130|  without that signature.
131|- **F8. Forgeries and bypasses.** Hand-edited verdict files; direct
132|  `time_candidates.py` runs quoted as evidence; `breakdown.py` direct runs
133|  bypassing the lock and distorting concurrent timings. → The audit
134|  recomputes G3 from the log and compares (kills lazy forgery); only
135|  marker-bearing logs count (direct runs have none); a re-entrant-safe
136|  lock plus entry-point coverage closes the bypass.
137|- **F9. Docs drift and "Not covered" repeats.** ADR 0010's "Not covered:
138|  prefill speed" was cited to justify behaviour 1; ADR 0011 has its own
139|  "Not covered" (`:51`) in the same citable form; the one-run-one-attempt
140|  fix never reached any ADR; `SKILL.md:80` stamps "skill version 6" while
141|  `:10` declares v7. → Rephrase every coverage gap as "unverified: assume
142|  nothing"; record the fix in an ADR; repair the version stamp.
143|- **F10. Evolution.** More slots, other engines, rounds 4+, other models.
144|  A fix wired to "vLLM, 3 slots, 4 workloads" rots. → The pinned protocol
145|  lives in one audited place (the wrapper + marker); the skill cites the
146|  wrapper, not flag values; the glossary holds the shared definitions.
147|
148|### 2.3 Root cause and certainty
149|
150|**Cause (high certainty — five independent behaviour chains converge):**
151|inside a round the swarm never observes the real objective. Its only
152|feedback is per-slot piece timing, while the real measurement (G3 over
153|whole requests) arrives post-round; and its end-to-end claims pass from
154|hypothesis to README to summary with no recorded check step (verifier
155|verdicts appear in every exploration entry and nowhere in
156|`implementation/`). Behaviour 2 is directly *mandated* by this structure:
157|`SKILL.md:147` requires an end-to-end number while `tracking.md:152` and
158|`SKILL.md:164` forbid the only measurement that could produce one.
159|
160|**Why behaviour 1's specific fix (ADR 0011) is not enough (high
161|certainty):** it closes the prefill gap but leaves the general habit —
162|"anything outside the measurement is free" — unaddressed, and adds a new
163|citeable "Not covered" (`0011:51`).
164|
165|**Why rules alone are not enough (medium-high certainty):** behaviour 4
166|shows rules work when explicit and checkable — but an end-to-end call with
167|free flags has nine gaming vectors (§2.1), several undetectable from the
168|verdict alone. The flags must be mechanically pinned, not merely
169|listed. Conversely, tools alone are not enough either: no tool sees
170|unwritten assumptions, borrowed arithmetic, or design-family persistence —
171|those need the checker and the counter.
172|
173|## 3. Recommended design: measure what you claim
174|
175|One principle, three pillars. **Every speed claim in a round is either a
176|measurement of exactly what is claimed, at the level claimed, citing its
177|run file — or a labelled prediction shown next to the measured value.**
178|Proposal in full; prototypes live in `prototype/`.
179|
180|### Pillar A — a pinned in-round end-to-end gate (tool)
181|
182|**New entry point `bench/grader/check_ready.py`** (proposal; prototype:
183|`prototype/check_ready.py`, 13/13 audit tests pass). It is the only
184|end-to-end evidence the swarm may cite. It does exactly two things:
185|
186|1. **Runs one pinned invocation** — `time_candidates.py vllm` with the G3
187|   protocol fixed in code: 4 G3 settings (`1x128,8x128,32x128,32x1024`),
188|   5 repeats, 256 tokens, positional `SLOT=FOLDER` only. There are no
189|   `--repeats`, `--settings`, `--tokens`, `--variant` or engine flags to
190|   game (F1: six vectors removed by pinning, two more by the audit below;
191|   the ninth, `max_rows` delegation, is piece-level and contained by G2 +
192|   the boundary agent + `check_sizes.py`). It takes the GPU lock
193|   through `time_candidates.main()`'s existing `hold()` (no second hold:
194|   a same-process re-hold would self-deadlock on `flock`, F8 note), loads
195|   the model inside the run, and appends a `ready-protocol` marker record
196|   to the jsonl pinning what ran.
197|2. **Audits the log instead of trusting it** — exactly one marker with
198|   pinned values; every run vLLM at the 4 settings × 5 repeats; the exact
199|   variant set (`base`, `compiled-<slot>`, `muse-<slot>` per slot, plus
200|   `compiled-all`/`muse-all` when >1 slot, so a combination is always
201|   measured as a combination); every non-base variant keeps base's greedy
202|   tokens at rows 1 and 32 (the brief's end-to-end G2, which G3 itself
203|   ignores — §2.1); the G3 verdict **recomputed from the log** and
204|   compared with `g3-vllm.json` (kills lazy forgery, F8); every submitted
205|   `muse-<slot>` and `muse-all` passing G3 against base and its compiled
206|   counterpart.
207|
208|**Contract.** CLI: `check_ready.py <out-dir> SLOT=FOLDER [...]`, plus
209|`--audit <out-dir>` (no GPU; re-audits any folder — also useful to
210|Claude post-round). Refuses a non-empty out-dir (F6: no appends, one
211|folder per check). Writes `muse-vllm.jsonl`, `g3-vllm.json`,
212|`ready-verdict.json` (schema: `pass`, per-variant `g3`/`vs`/`phases`,
213|`exact` table, `protocol`, file paths). Exit 0 pass / 1 judged fail /
214|2 protocol violation; every path writes `ready-verdict.json` so the
215|checker can cite even failures. Prints one `ready <variant>: pass/fail`
216|line each plus `ready check: PASS/FAIL`.
217|
218|**Scheduling (F3).** Piece timing stays the search signal; the ready
219|check runs only at close-time. The lead batches: hypotheses converge on
220|piece timing to the new `candidate` status, then **one combined call**
221|over all submitted slots judges every `muse-<slot>` and `muse-all`
222|together. Typical cost: one vLLM run per round (~14 min for 1 slot,
223|~25–40 for 2–3). A failed check returns the hypothesis to building only
224|with a changed approach, else drops it (F2: bounded by genuine
225|redesigns, never a loop). The verdict stands — no re-runs (F4).
226|
227|### Pillar B — claim discipline with an independent checker (skill)
228|
229|**Number rule rewrite** (`tracking.md:153`; prototype:
230|`prototype/skill/tracking.md`). The old rule accepts shown arithmetic as
231|a source — the letter that blessed behaviours 2–3. The new rule: every
232|speed number carries level (piece/end-to-end), run file, and label
233|(measured/prediction). Measured piece numbers cite the grader verdict
234|that timed exactly that slot; measured end-to-end numbers cite the ready
235|check that timed exactly that slot or combination; predictions count
236|only the candidate's own measured effect and sit next to the measured
237|value; combinations are measured as combinations, never summed;
238|everything unmeasured goes under **Unverified** and is never assumed
239|free, neutral or zero — "G3 decides" is an Unverified entry, not a
240|measurement. GPU rule (`tracking.md:152`) becomes "the grader and the
241|ready check are the only GPU jobs", run only as builder / only as lead
242|respectively, with direct `time_candidates.py`/`breakdown.py`/
243|`repeat_fixes.py` runs explicitly not evidence (F8).
244|
245|**New `candidate` status + `ready` gate** (prototype:
246|`prototype/skill/tracking.md` hypothesis schema). `candidate` = passes
247|G1, G2, boundary check, `beats_compiled` (+ `beats_baseline`) on piece
248|timing, checker-signed, awaiting the ready check. `ready` = the ready
249|check's `ready-verdict.json` says `pass` for exactly this attempt. The
250|Decision at `candidate` states the piece basis as a prediction; at
251|`ready` it cites the verdict file with the measured change. Ready to
252|test names only `ready` attempts (or kept baselines / the reference,
253|which carry no new claim). This is AC2 made mechanical (F5: file-backed).
254|
255|**New role: checker** (proposal; prototype card:
256|`prototype/skill/checker.md`). The verifier's implementation-phase
257|counterpart — same method (open the cited file, redo the arithmetic),
258|because that method is proven. `checker-<n>` signs each hypothesis
259|before `candidate`/`ready`; `checker-final` signs Ready to test and the
260|summary. It checks levels, run files, labels, own-effect-only arithmetic,
261|Unverified completeness, the failure counter (§3C), and the ready-gate.
262|The lead cannot close without its `pass` in the `Check` section / log.
263|Like the verifier it never edits others' numbers; the lead fixes and
264|re-calls. One agent per check keeps it cheap; post-round, Claude audits
265|that the signatures exist (F7, §8).
266|
267|### Pillar C — a design-family switch rule (skill)
268|
269|**Failure signatures + count of 3** (proposal; schema in
270|`prototype/skill/tracking.md`, rule text for `SKILL.md` step 4 in §8).
271|The lead logs each failed attempt's signature — the phase/size it failed
272|at plus the named cause. After **3 failures sharing one phase and one
273|cause**, the next attempt must be a **changed approach** (different
274|kernel structure, parallelisation or dataflow — not tuning), named in
275|`notes.md` as "approach change: from X to Y", or the log holds the
276|lead's reason why not. The checker verifies the counter. A failed ready
277|check logs an end-to-end-level signature under the same counter.
278|Why 3: round-2 experts' attempts 1–3 share decode/1-row + "fused-structure
279|1-row latency", and attempt-3's own note refuted the lever — the rule
280|fires exactly where the record says it should (`results/schema-dry-run.md`),
281|while allowing genuine iteration (F5: countable, not advisory).
282|
283|### Data flow and integration points
284|
285|```text
286|builder → grader (piece) → hyp entry → boundary check → checker-<n> pass
287|  → candidate ─┐
288|               ├→ lead: ONE check_ready.py over all candidates (+muse-all)
289|candidate ─────┘         → ready-verdict.json pass → ready (per slot)
290|                       → fail → redesign (approach change) or dropped
291|ready set → Ready to test + summary → checker-final pass → commit → Claude's G3
292|```
293|
294|Integration points: `check_ready.py` imports `time_candidates` (calls
295|`main()` with a pinned argv, reuses `g3()` for recompute) and needs no
296|change to it; skill changes touch `SKILL.md` (goal line, step 4–5,
297|role table, `:164` ownership line), `tracking.md` (rules + schema),
298|new `checker.md`, `builder.md` (notes gain an Unverified line),
299|`boundary.md` ("can't see" list becomes Unverified entries),
300|`claude/muse-agent-brief.md` (`:213-215` end-to-end ownership),
301|`CHANGELOG.md` (v8), glossary (`Ready check`, `Candidate`,
302|`Prediction`, `Unverified`), `muse-swarm.md` + diagrams, and a new ADR
303|(§8). `tools/muse-agent/start.sh` needs no change.
304|
305|## 4. Why it solves the underlying problem and meets each acceptance criterion
306|
307|The root cause (§2.3) has two halves — no in-round observation of the
308|objective, and no check on self-reports. Pillar A closes the first
309|(the swarm sees G3-protocol end-to-end numbers before it claims them);
310|pillars B and C close the second (an independent agent verifies every
311|number; a counter forces design change). The three pillars are one
312|mechanism: the ready check produces the only admissible evidence, the
313|checker enforces admissibility, the counter bounds persistence. None

390|## 6. Failure handling, data integrity, security, operations
391|
392|**Failure handling (in-round).** Every failure has a defined landing
393|state, and every landing state is a committed document, so a partial
394|round resumes cleanly from step 0's "carry on from its READMEs":
395|- ready check fails → hypothesis back to `building` (approach change
396|  required) or `dropped`; the verdict file is cited either way.
397|- ready check crashes mid-run (OOM, killed) → folder holds a partial
398|  log with no marker; audit reports protocol violation; hypothesis
399|  stays `candidate`; the lead re-runs into a fresh folder (a crash is
400|  not a verdict, so "verdict stands" does not apply — the distinction
401|  is file-backed: no `ready-verdict.json`, no verdict).
402|- checker finds defects → lead fixes the numbers, re-calls the checker;
403|  close is blocked until `pass`.
404|- counter hits 3 with no approach change and no logged reason →
405|  checker defect; close blocked.
406|- GPU lock contention → runs queue (existing behaviour); builders keep
407|  waiting per `builder.md:28`. The lead schedules the ready check when
408|  few builders are active (end of implementation) and starts no new
409|  helpers until it lands, to bound swap pressure on 16 GB.
410|- swap/OOM during vLLM → same as any vLLM run today (Docker quit,
411|  `VLLM_METAL_KV_COMMIT_PROBE=0` default in `breakdown.py:54`); no new
412|  mitigation, and the crash path above keeps the record consistent.
413|
414|**Data integrity.** One folder per check, never appended (tool-refused);
415|audit demands exact settings/repeats/variants/marker; G3 recomputed
416|from the log and compared (forgery of `g3-vllm.json` alone is caught —
417|verified `results/audit-tests/game-forged-g3`). Residual: a fully
418|hand-fabricated jsonl (60+ coherent runs + checks) would pass the
419|audit. Contained, not closed: fabrication at that scale must also match
420|Claude's independent post-round G3 (AC6), which it cannot predict;
421|transcripts show whether `check_ready.py` actually ran. This matches
422|the brief's "simple over airtight" guardrail — proportionate, stated.
423|
424|**How the swarm could still game it (Goodhart audit, F1/F10).**
425|1. Tune to the 4 G3 workloads (e.g. `max_rows` edges placed just
426|   outside them). Contained: G2 still tests 6 sizes; the boundary agent
427|   checks off-size rows; `check_sizes.py` exists for Claude's audit.

429|   ready check has no `--baseline` flag; bars are fixed (base + compiled).
430|3. Time-of-day gaming (run when the machine is quiet). Inherent to all
431|   timing here; paired repeats (piece) and shuffled repeats (G3) bound it.
432|4. Quote piece medians as end-to-end. Killed by the level+label rule +
433|   checker + marker requirement.
434|5. Skip the checker (lead closes without calling it). The signature is
435|   file-backed and Claude's post-round audit checks presence (§8, M3);
436|   transcripts record helper starts. A lead that forges a signature is
437|   visible in the same audit. Residual accepted (see §9).

439|   The checker judges the notes' from-X-to-Y statement; weak but
440|   auditable. AC5's "or log why not" already concedes this boundary.
441|
442|**Security.** No new surface: no network, no credentials (rule stands),
443|no sandbox change, no hook change. The wrapper runs the same local
444|binaries the swarm already runs. The marker is provenance, not trust —
445|Claude's independent measurement stays the authority.

447|**Operations.** Round duration grows by typically one vLLM run
448|(§3A: ~14 min/1 slot, ~25–40/2–3; measured live in §8 T-live) plus
449|checker agents (minutes, no GPU). Cost stays ~$1/round (contributor
450|model). Memory: schedule the check late; the lead pauses new helper
451|starts while it runs. Monitoring: §8 M1–M4.

453|## 7. Credible alternatives considered and their trade-offs
454|
455|1. **Skill rules only (no tool change).** "Run `time_candidates.py vllm`
456|   with these exact flags." Rejected: nine gaming vectors (§2.1), and
457|   the contributor model follows explicit rules but cannot self-police
458|   flag discipline against its own incentive to show gains. Behaviour 4
459|   cuts the other way — but that rule was countable post-hoc (runs ==
460|   attempts), while flag values evaporate unless audited. The wrapper
461|   makes the protocol countable.
462|2. **Pin by editing `time_candidates.py` (remove flags / add a `--g3`
463|   mode).** Rejected: it changes Claude's own measurement path (risk to
464|   the authority), and any flag the script accepts stays available to
465|   the swarm. The additive wrapper leaves the authority untouched (§5).
466|3. **Plain-engine in-round check (fast: seconds, not minutes).**
467|   Rejected: plain `prompt_ms` is always 0.0 and writes no verdict

470|   disqualifying. (If plain ever gains real prompt timing + verdict,
471|   the wrapper can pin it as a pre-gate — evolution path, F10.)
472|4. **Extend the verifier instead of adding a checker.** Rejected
473|   narrowly: the verifier is exploration-scoped and returns before
474|   implementation (`verifier.md:25`); re-tasking it mid-round muddies
475|   its proven remit and its Done condition. A sibling card with the

477|   ever binds, merging the cards is a safe refactor (same method).

479|   Rejected: AC5 explicitly allows "or the log records why not", and a
480|   hard cap risks killing a slow-converging real improvement (round-2
481|   routing improved across 4 attempts). The approach-change rule bounds
482|   cost while preserving the escape hatch, file-backed.

484|   Rejected (F4): any re-roll rule is a license to re-roll, and "marginal"

490|   hardening; "simple over airtight"). The recompute-and-compare +
491|   independent-G3 pairing gives two independent observations of the same
492|   protocol, which is the proportionate integrity story.

160|## Verdict: Z is the strongest passing design
161|
162|Z is the only design that passes all six gates. The deciding difference is
163|tool-evidence integrity: X and Y both fail G3 on a demonstrated forgery hole
164|(hand-edited `g3-vllm.json` sails through), while Z's recompute-and-compare
165|closes it in a few lines — within the simplicity budget, proven by test.
166|Beyond that, concrete reasons to prefer Z:
167|
168|1. Strongest audit: recompute, exact variant-set/engine/settings/reps checks,
169|   token gate, fresh-folder refusal, exit 0/1/2 semantics, plus `--audit` for
170|   CPU-only re-checks (also useful to Claude post-round). 13/13 fixtures,
171|   independently rerun.
172|2. Best failure handling: the crash-vs-verdict distinction (no
173|   `ready-verdict.json` = no verdict = re-run allowed; judged FAIL = stands)
174|   is the only file-backed answer to partial rounds, and the F1–F10 analysis
175|   is the most thorough Goodhart accounting.
176|3. Batched cost shape: one combined call judges every slot plus `muse-all`
177|   (no per-hypothesis mid-round GPU jobs competing with builders, unlike X),
178|   while piece timing stays the search signal.
179|4. Per-hypothesis checking at close time plus a finish check (unlike Y's
180|   Finish-only pass), so Decision errors surface before the deadline rush.
181|5. Honest residuals: fabrication, skipped signatures, noise-killed
182|   candidates, and the untested-until-round-3 compliance assumption are all
183|   stated with containment, not buried.
184|
185|Caveat: Z's combination path is proven only on synthetic logs (`pass-2slot`,
186|`game-noall`); Y is the only design with a live multi-slot `muse-all` run.
187|The implementation should therefore include a live multi-slot acceptance run
188|before round 3 (routing-4 + combine-1, ~21 min measured by tester-Y) — cheap,
189|and it closes Z's one evidence gap with Y's evidence.
